author: By Dingane Xaba, Unicorn Riot
title: Seven of the Minnesota 15 Defendants Speak on Indictments
content:
Minneapolis, MN — In June of 2026, 15 Minnesota-based activist organizers were

indicted

 by the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) on charges of conspiring to “impede or injure” federal officers during mass protests against the deadly deportation surge led by the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).


Unicorn Riot interviewed seven of the

Minnesota 15

 —

Isaac Sant

,

Emmett Doyle

,

Cam Kennedy

,

Cal Robinet

,

Gabriel Van De Water

,

Treasure Thoreson

, and

Mac Stewart

 — over the course of the Summer to hear about their involvement in the historic immigrant-defense movement that led to them becoming political

targets of the federal government

.


The indicted include teachers, professors, union workers, electricians, and wildlife managers, among other careers. All are Minnesota residents and most of them have a longtime experience in local community activism; a common thread that defense lawyers stress is the real reason for the indictments.


The

prosecution claims

 that the accused were part of two local organizations known as Direct Action Minnesota (DAMN) and the Black Cat Workers Collective that “emphasize a violent, militant approach to politics and are highly critical of non violent peaceful protest.” This is according to Trump’s U.S. Attorney for Minnesota Daniel Rosen who announced the charges during a

June 16 press conference

.


Rosen went on to claim that the defendants were being charged “not for what they said, but what they did,” and that his office will introduce “video and eyewitness accounts” as primary sources in court.


Federal Indictment on Minnesota 15 Peddles DOJ ‘Antifa’ Conspiracy Angle After Raids


Dragnet Surveillance


Court documents from only a fraction of the government’s evidence already reveal that

ICE is running Operation Puppet Master, likely the largest surveillance operation in U.S. history

. See

Unicorn Riot’s deep-dive video

 on some of the initial court documents made public.


A large amount of

encrypted text message data is also being disseminated by the prosecution team

 and expected to be used in court. Much if not all of this data appears to have been gleaned from undercover HSI agents who joined the myriad of public Signal text groups created by local community organizers to coordinate protests against the ICE-led

Operation Metro Surge

.


Government surveillance of the defendants extended beyond Minnesota as it was recently reported that Chicago-area cops assisted Homeland Security in monitoring a multi-state organizing tour attended by some of the defendants and sponsored by the Anarchist collective Crimethinc. The same report by Wired reveals that

Homeland Security agents monitored other tour events in Michigan and Seattle

.


Mass surveillance utilizing artificial intelligence in facial recognition cameras has also been

deployed against protesters

. A photo that defendant Isaac Sant uploaded to a Signal group depicting his wounds after being struck in the face by a crowd-control munition was used to build a dossier on him. Said photo was run through a Clearview AI search and falsely linked his identity to a completely unrelated person. It isn’t the first time that said technology has produced false results, increasing calls from privacy advocates to ban the technology all together.


Deep Dive: Minnesota 15 Case Reveals Range of Pervasive Surveillance


DHS Facial Recognition Software Used Against Minnesota 15


Government Says Terabytes of Signal Chats are Central to the Case Against Minnesota 15


What the Defendants Say


Out of the hundreds of thousands of people involved in anti-ICE protests, the government has taken particular aim against prominent local left-wing organizers it perceives as leaders of a grand political conspiracy against the state.


One of the Minnesota 15 and a special education teacher, Treasure Thoreson, elaborated to UR: “I think this is meant to be chilling. Pretty much everyone who was arrested is someone involved in labor organizing … This was a threat to the federal government who does not want to see us getting along and supporting each other.”


Emmett Doyle, also a co-defendant and a union organizer added, “the most powerful thing that people in Minneapolis did to oppose Operation Metro Surge was the general strike, and they [the government] needed to try to get rid of the people who they think helped organize it … I think that’s why they worked so hard to construct this narrative around …

author: Unknown
title: The Hot Potato Changes Hands Again : On the 2026 Midterm Elections
content:
Ultimately, the Democrats are no more capable of addressing the root causes of popular anger than the Republicans. State power will continue to swing back and forth more and more wildly between different parties until our rulers consolidate an autocracy or we manage to effect revolutionary change.


As we anticipated

in April

, the death knell of the Trump era has rung. Despite being

historically unpopular

, Democratic politicians won a sweeping victory in the November 2026 midterm elections. Many are describing the rout as an “

extinction-level event

” for the Republican Party.


All this should feel familiar. Only two years ago, when Democrats lost the 2024 elections, pundits across the political spectrum rushed to declare the collapse of the Democratic Party. Summarizing a widespread perception, one

expert

 claimed that


“Fundamental shifts are occurring in the body politic that have left Democrats on the wrong side of the popular vote, congressional races, and the country’s shifting demographics.”


Two years later, people are saying the same things about the Republican Party. The backlash against Republicans in this year’s election eclipses the gains they made in 2024. Yet the pendulum has been swinging wildly back and forth between parties for over a decade now—and it could be that the wildest swings have yet to come.


For all the talk of political polarization, loyalty to political parties is at its

lowest

 in decades. Since at least 2016, anger at the status quo has been the most powerful force in politics; Democrats like Hillary Clinton and Joe Biden who attempted to present themselves as its defenders have learned that the hard way. Likewise, Donald Trump has only able to win elections when he is not in office. Whenever Trump represents the ruling order, he draws the same backlash that he once managed to channel.


Since 2014, we have argued that state power itself has become a hot potato that burns whoever holds it. In a globalized economy, in which governments can no longer mitigate the impact of capitalism on their citizens without investors taking their money elsewhere, no party is able to hold state power for long without losing credibility with voters. Similarly, the challenges of maintaining position as a waning imperial power inevitably undercut the legitimacy of whoever controls the state: just as the genocide in Gaza damaged the Biden administration’s support, Trump’s

war with Iran

 has contributed to driving away voters.


Similar things are taking place all around the world.

British politicians

 have also seen rapid reversals in fortune. The centrist parties that have long ruled Germany and France are in precipitous decline. One Latin American government after another has swung to the far right, but that hardly indicates a

social consensus

 in favor of

any political camp

.


Only countries under continuous autocratic rule, such as Russia, Belarus, China, and North Korea, are excepted from the hot potato pattern. Donald Trump has made no secret of his desire to establish a similar state of affairs in the United States. Yet even in Hungary, which Republicans took as a model for their illiberal aspirations, the long-running autocratic government ultimately lost control. The same has occurred in Poland and, more recently, Serbia. Wherever voters have an opportunity—however narrow—to demand change, they do so—however arbitrarily and capriciously.


With no prospect of improving life for his rank-and-file supporters, Trump’s solution was to

inflict violence

 on their behalf, offering them the vicarious thrill of watching the state cause harm to others as an outlet for their frustration.

Less bread, more circuses

.


Republicans and Democrats—trash and recycling.


It might have worked—if ordinary people had not courageously taken the streets to interfere. We owe Trump’s failure to those who assembled at

Tesla dealerships

 in spring 2025, who

rose up

 against federal agents and the National Guard that June, who confronted Immigration and Customs Enforcement mercenaries in

Chicago

,

Minnesota

, and elsewhere. As we previously saw in

the movement against police and white supremacy

, when people take risks in solidarity with others, this makes it possible for more people to experience empathy where previously, they only felt dissociation and apathy.


The grassroots resistance that emerged in response to the Trump administration stands in stark contrast to the way that …

author: CNT Galiza
title: Nueva victoria para la CNT en La Galletería
content:
Leer en

Castellano

Galego


Castellano

Nueva victoria para la CNT en La Galletería: la acción directa y la presión sindical redoblan sus esfuerzos contra Álvaro Cernuda


La lucha en las calles, el apoyo mutuo y la acción directa demuestran una vez más ser las herramientas más eficaces para defender la dignidad de la clase trabajadora. Tras una campaña de presión y movilización impulsada por la CNT, logramos una importante victoria contra la empresa tras el despido injustificado de dos de nuestros compañeros.


El resultado de esta batalla sindical es contundente: los despidos fueron declarados infundados, se otorgó la indemnización correspondiente y uno de los trabajadores fue reincorporado. Este triunfo no surgió por arte de magia ni de buenas intenciones: se logró gracias a la presión constante del sindicato y su firme presencia en las calles.


Álvaro Cernuda, reincidente en abusos laborales y antiguo conocido de la CNT por conflictos anteriores, pretendía marcharse con un escándalo tras acumular un historial de impago de horas extras, falta de pago de preaviso y denegación de vacaciones pendientes. Pero la respuesta no se hizo esperar. Los piquetes sindicales frente a su negocio, La Galletería, en Ribadeo, denunciaron públicamente la injusticia y dejaron claro que ningún ataque contra los trabajadores queda impune.


Esta victoria confirma que los trabajadores nos organizamos y que las victorias se consiguen gracias a la unidad de todos y a la lucha sindical. Cuando llevamos la lucha a las calles, cuando practicamos la acción directa y cuando nos centramos en la solidaridad de clase, los empresarios tienen que ceder y reconocer nuestros derechos.


Ante los abusos laborales, las amenazas y la precariedad, la organización sindical es nuestro mejor escudo y nuestra mejor arma. Cuando nos unimos en el sindicato, el miedo cambia de bando.


Galego

Nova vitoria da CNT en La Galletería: a acción directa e a presión sindical dobregan de novo a Álvaro Cernuda


A loita na rúa, o apoio mutuo e a acción directa volven demostrar que son as ferramentas máis efectivas para defender a dignidade da clase traballadora. Tras unha campaña de presión e mobilización desenvolvida pola CNT, acadamos unha importante vitoria fronte ao empresario tras o despedimento inxustificado de dúas das nosas compañeiras.


O resultado desta batalla sindical é rotundo: logrouse a declaración de improcedencia dos despedimentos, a correspondente indemnización e a readmisión dunha das traballadoras. Este triunfo non caeu do ceo nin veu da man de despachos nin de boas palabras: acadouse grazas á presión constante do sindicato e á presenza firme nas rúas.


Álvaro Cernuda, reincidente nos abusos laborais e vello coñecido da CNT por conflitos anteriores, pretendía marchar de rositas tras acumular un historial de impagos de horas extras, non abonar os días de preaviso e negar o pagamento das vacacións pendentes. Pero a resposta non se fixo esperar. Os piquetes sindicais ás portas do seu negocio, La Galletería, en Ribadeo, sinalaron publicamente a inxustiza e deixaron claro que ningún ataque contra as traballadoras queda sen resposta.


Esta vitoria confirma que as traballadoras nos organizamos e as vitorias conséguense grazas á unidade de todas e á loita sindical. Cando levamos a loita á rúa, cando practicamos a acción directa e cando poñemos o foco na solidariedade de clase, a patronal ten que ceder e recoñecer os nosos dereitos.


Fronte aos abusos laborais, ás ameazas e á precarización, a organización no noso sindicato é o noso mellor escudo e a nosa mellor arma. Cando nos xuntamos no sindicato, o medo muda de bando.


La entrada

Nueva victoria para la CNT en La Galletería

 se publicó primero en

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

author: Rory Mir
title: Google Forcing AI on Students Is BS
content:
Google is rightfully facing blowback for forcing K-12 schools to enable AI if they wanted to keep using Google search. The company quickly backtracked and decoupled and turned off the services by default, but made it clear search will continue to be just another AI chatbot. This mandate forces an ultimatum on educators: accept generative AI or de-google your school.


Students, teachers, and parents across the U.S. are now years into an argument about how schools should respond to the growth of AI-enabled tools. Google decided to skip this debate and take this choice from schools. In August it activated AI chatbot Gemini

for 150 million K-12 students

 on Google Classroom, leaving educators

scrambling to respond

. A few months later, Google introduced a new way to turn it off — but now administrators

would also be turning off Google search

.


Google

walked this back

 somewhat, clarifying that Gemini, Gemini notebook, and Search will have their own controls and will be off by default. But because of Google’s broader approach to force AI on all search users, this change is still an example of a tech monopolist pushing unwanted changes into the classroom.


Tying AI to Search


It’s no secret that the biggest companies in AI  are

operating at a huge loss

, in the hope they can follow


Uber’s enshittification playbook

. Offer a cheap convenience

at a major loss

 until old systems atrophy, then flip the script to reduce wages and raise consumer costs—whether that’s paying with cash or with data. 


This puts Google in the odd position of an incumbent, with around

90% of search traffic

. It needs to not only make good on its own AI investment, but protect its dominance from new AI tools. It’s not just enough to offer its own AI mode, it needs to turn search into AI mode, while engaging in

clumsy self-preferencing

 that is

eating its own ad revenue

.


The problem with this approach is the public is split on AI, to put it mildly. Some users will welcome these changes, but the rest are stuck in an all-or-nothing bargain. Anyone concerned 

about the accuracy of AI overviews

 or their

impact on click-through rates

 for

online communities

 and

small publishers

 can just

deal with it

. The bet is any inconvenience in switching to an alternative is enough to keep you trapped.


Google can and should offer a way to disable AI overviews. Smaller services like DuckDuckGo* and Brave search have simple and persisting AI settings which don’t require login. These services also don't mince words and make a distinction between generated AI summaries, suspected AI results, and the backend use of AI to curate links. 


It’s not enough to point to

opaque workarounds

, either. Adding “-ai” to your Google search will usually remove AI Overview, but so will “-unicorn”. This trick isn’t meant to be an AI off-switch, it’s a quirk of how AI Overview was implemented and can change at any time. These tricks also don’t generalize well to

settings for system administrators

. Hacks might work for now, but everyone—including administrators—deserve clear set-and-forget controls for the tools they rely on.


Pushing AI on Schools


De-googling your life isn’t easy, and for schools it can be even more difficult. For decades Google has gone after schools to foster life-long Google users—resulting in many institutions being deeply entrenched in its ecosystem

despite data privacy concerns

. That’s because schools face major

switching costs

 when moving to a competitor. It takes more than flipping a setting—it means a lengthy contract process, staff retraining, and a cumbersome migration of past work. 


The difficulty of switching makes granular controls even more essential, particularly for a hot-button issue like generative AI. Few parents would send their kids to

AI-driven schools

, but they may want their kids to learn tools like search as they exist outside of the classroom. However, many parents and teachers concerned with AI disrupting learning are pushing

major school districts

 to implement temporary

AI moratoriums

 for young students. These pauses are meant to make sure any introduction of AI 

fits the needs of students


and is done in a way that actually makes sure educators are prepared. 


But in either camp, this is a choice that must be made by schools, not Google. Teachers know more about what their students need than a trillion-dollar tech company, and this expertise should be respected in their …

author: David Swanson
title: World BEYOND War Asia Responds to Statement by U.S. Embassy to Philippines
content:
By World BEYOND War Asia, November 6, 2026


A response to

this statement

.


U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth’s visit to the Philippines for the ASEAN Defense Ministers’ Meeting-Plus signifies the continuing effort of the U.S. to use the country as a pawn for its war and militarism in the region, using the Philippines to encourage other ASEAN nations to enter partnerships and align with U.S. interests.


For 75 years under the Mutual Defense Treaty (MDT), the Philippines has remained a loyal subordinate to U.S. wargames in the region and across the globe, while many Filipinos and their communities suffer atrocities and human rights violations at the hands of U.S. military forces. The MDT was and remains an unequal relationship, alongside related agreements such as the Visiting Forces Agreement (VFA) and the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA). Now, with the Philippines entering Pax Silica initiatives and the Luzon Economic Corridor, the government has further opened the country to exploitation.


Our message is also clear:


The U.S. is the primary reason why the Philippines and the Filipino people do not enjoy genuine sovereignty.


We call on all peace-loving people to denounce this continuing alliance between the Philippines and the U.S., and we call on other ASEAN governments to refuse to let the U.S. use them to advance its militaristic agenda.

World BEYOND War Asia Responds to Statement by U.S. Embassy to Philippines

 appeared first on

World BEYOND War

author: Sophia Sheera
title: UK Government to Extend Palantir’s NHS Contract by Two Years
content:
The government is planning to extend spytech firm Palantir’s £330m deal with the NHS despite pressure from Labour MPs, medical unions and activists to cut ties with the company. 


Ministers had the option of triggering a break clause in the contract in February. However, a review concluded that removing Palantir and switching providers within four months would be too disruptive,

the FT reported

, with ministers drawing up plans to potentially replace it with a British alternative in two years’ time instead. 


Tech justice campaign group

Foxglove said

 this decision showed “a serious ignorance” of Palantir’s contract, which “specifically requires the firm to provide bridging support for up to 24 months if the contract is ended” to ensure continuity of service.


“The reported claim that it would not be ‘practical to replace Palantir within the next four months’ is, frankly, nonsense,” said Foxglove’s head of communications Tom Hegarty.


The decision comes amid growing opposition to Palantir’s involvement in British public services. The firm has faced criticism over its work with the Trump administration and the Israeli military, while its co-founder Peter Thiel has previously attacked the NHS.


Last week, it was revealed that dozens of UK hospitals reportedly benefitting from a platform built by Palantir are

not even using it

.


Novara Media also revealed a fortnight ago that British MPs who have criticised Palantir in parliament

received intimidating letters

 from the firm. 


Amnesty International’s UK crisis campaigner Tom Guha said: “Patients, healthcare workers and campaigners have pushed ministers to look for a way out of this contract. Ministers must show Palantir the door now, not give it two more years to bed in further.


“Palantir has publicly acknowledged supporting Israel’s military in ‘war-related missions’,” he added. “Any company linked to genocide has no place in our NHS.”

author: Ellen David Friedman
title: Steward’s Corner: Rethink the Scripted ‘Ask’
content:
You’re having a conversation with a co-worker, but inside you’re feeling icy dread. You’re talking through a script that ends with asking them to do a specific thing: sign a union card, wear a button, come to a meeting, vote for a strike. And sure enough, when you ask, a wall comes down.


The co-worker looks away, makes an excuse, and pins you as someone who is after something. You’re disappointed, confused about why it didn’t work, and afraid you’re not going to meet your goal.


Many of us feel nervous or awkward about asking a co-worker to do something. Sometimes we just need to push ourselves to do it. But if you’re being pressured to follow the script and get to a particular “ask” without finding out who this person is and moving at their pace, that’s a problem.


A co-worker you don’t yet have much of a relationship with may be turned off that you’re pressuring them to take an action that has already been decided on by others.


What can you do instead? Replace the “ask” (to take some predetermined action) with an invitation: “Hey, some of us are getting together to talk about this. You want to join us?” “Can we figure out how you can be part of the solution to this problem that you’re posing?”


People are happy to be asked to do something they want to do, or that they’re good at, or that they’re confident about. People like to be asked to do things when it reflects your respect for them: “You’re asking me to do this because you’re confident in my ability. You know I like this task, or that I’m good at it.” Think how different that is from simply complying with what the organizer wants them to do.


A NEW APPROACH


A young worker in a chemical factory in Massachusetts was trying to interest his co-workers in a union. After many frustrating weeks of trying to approach people with an ask—to come to a meeting with a union organizer—he was about to give up.


But then he opened his eyes to other possibilities and changed his approach: “What I’m really trying to do is build real relationships,” he said. “I decided to see what happened if I gave up the ask.”


With this new approach, in a matter of just two or three weeks, he met his goal to connect with co-workers in a dozen departments where he had not previously had any contact. He found that it was so much easier to make contact when that was the only goal.


What had been holding him back from contacting these people before? “I didn’t know what the ask was. And what do they owe me? They’re going to feel bad if they don’t do what I ask. They might avoid me.”


TRUST TAKES TIME


Instead, his co-workers started to approach him with questions, concerns, and ideas about workplace problems. It emerged that the boss was providing very different retirement packages to different employees. Pretty soon a group came together to document the problem, propose a fix, and bring it to the boss.


Of course organizers are asking people to do things all the time—our organizing is about action, not just talk.


And there are times when making a specific ask, even pushing hard, makes sense—asking people to commit to a strike, for instance, or  to vote yes to join the union.


But such urgency should be grounded in strong relationships and discussions that have built trust over time, helping people overcome fear.


Any hard “ask” should stem from inclusive discussion and collective decisions. People should be coming up to you to say, “Is that petition what I think it is? Give me that, I want to sign it.”


[Do you have a different take on "the ask" or the organizing conversation? Write to

editors[at]labornotes[dot]org

]


Excerpted from

Keep Going: A Guide to Organizing When It’s Hard

 by Ellen David Friedman, a retired organizer for Vermont NEA and a member of the Labor Notes board.

title: I think the left completely failed to form an effective covid-safety strategy.
content:
queeranarchism

:

chronicbitchsyndrome

:

queeranarchism

:

I think the left completely failed to form an effective covid-safety strategy.

First they failed by putting far too little effort into winning systematic changes (access to health care, access to paid sick leave, ventilation of work- and public spaces, etc) and putting most of the focus on individual behaviors that they could judge individuals for (vaccines and above all masking).

Their second failure was to then primarily rely on punitive pressure and scolding people to achieve that behavior. Which meant that this strategy only kind of worked a little when they had enough people to keep up that pressure. The moment that pressure wasn’t enough anymore, most people stopped masking because they’d only even done it because of external pressure.

This left us with nothing. No systematic changes and no group safety.

At that point, the third failure was to change nothing once it became abundantly clear that these tactics weren’t working. People wrote comics and long reads and video essays about the lack of solidarity of people who stopped masking, and while there was truth there, that didn’t change anything.

Yet at no point did people take stock, re-assess and change strategy. To this day people are just doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results. In fact, people seem to just double down. Where they talked about a range of safety measures in the past they’ve switched to only talking about masking. Where they used a range of tactics in the past, they’ve switched to only scolding.

And when you challenge them, the response is something like “But I am right, this is unjust, so people

should

 change when I tell them it is unjust”. But that’s not a strategy. Creating societal change doesn’t require being right, it requires having an effective plan on how to actually achieve real change.

And I don’t have a full draft of what would make an effective strategy. I think unions could play a big role in achieving things paid sick leave and proper ventilation. But I don’t have all the answers either. I think there needs to be an acknowledgement that what’s currently happening isn’t working, and that a new strategy is long overdue.

ventilation and air filtration are the most important, and its exhausting to be constantly screaming this from the rooftops every day.

organizers have the power to make community events covid-safer and accessible for the at-risk disabled via two simple tracks: hold events outside, and purchase air purifiers to run at indoor events. (advertise on your literature that the air at your indoor events will be purified, otherwise disabled people will assume it’s not and we can’t come.)

stand-alone air purifiers run from around $200 to the $1000 range, depending on size and efficiency, and purchasing a single one should be doable for a fundraising event and/or collective purchase by most organizations with more than a handful of organizers (at least, in north america and europe, which is unfortunately the only economies i have knowledge about organizing within and so is all i am talking about right now).

the things that do not work, as said above, are guilting, shaming, or bullying individuals into taking individual mitigations. this does not make your community space safe for disabled individuals. on top of that, if you are indoors, requiring masks doesn’t make it safe for us anyway unless you are also purifying the air. mask-required events in poorly ventilated indoor areas without filtration end up mostly serving groups of abled people and people who are otherwise not at high risk from viral infections, who are well meaning, but failing to achieve what this accommodation should be targeting.

this has been something i have been agitating for locally for over two years now, to very little avail, because i am fighting against a veritable nonprofit industrial complex pushing the “guilt people for not masking and do nothing else” party line. there isn’t even any publicly available educational literature locally on why masking does and doesn’t work and why air filtration is a significantly more useful accommodation. i am doing my best to compile some information into a database, but designing effective propaganda is outside of my wheelhouse, and it feels like a losing battle at times.

Everyone else: please stop focussing on the ‘scolding’ part. We don’t …

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Peter Gelderloos: Breathing Room
content:
Woodcut by Frans Masereel


from Peter Gelderloos’ substack page,

Suviving Leviathan

, 05/11/2026


Breathing Room


from the apocalyptic, fascistic Right to the insufficient, hypocritical, quietly genocidal Left


In the recent elections in Brasil, one of the largest countries in the Global South, leftwing darling Lula beat Flavio Bolsonaro, the fascistic dynast supported by the country’s plantation owner class. In Israel, the extreme Right lost the elections to the far Right (not a typo). And in the US, a “blue wave” has given the Democrats an ample margin of control in both chambers of Congress as well as a strong majority of governorships (for non-US readers, for whatever weird-ass reason related to our especially amnesiac, isolationist culture, in the US blue is the color of the Left and red is the color of the Right). In once Republican-held or toss-up states like Texas, North Carolina, and New Jersey, Democratic candidates won by double digits while conservatives won in what were, until yesterday, solidly Republican states like Florida or Louisiana by only 1 or 2%.


A high level Republican operative connected to Trump admitted to the press that these elections were just “too big to rig,” casually acknowledging how common it is to redraw electoral maps or send the precise vote-counting machines to the friendly districts and low quality, high-failure-rate machines to the unfriendly districts, in order to win an extra percentage point and tip elections.


Brasil


In Brasil, where former far Right president Jair Bolsonaro serves a sentence of house arrest in his mansion for launching a failed coup attempt after he lost the 2022 elections, his son Flavio Bolsonaro carried the first round of the elections in early October but failed to attain a majority. In the second round, held October 25

th

, voters turned to the Left and re-elected the incumbent, Lula, off the Workers’ Party. Wealthy investors punished the country for their vote, with the Brasilian stock market taking a plunge after the election even though Lula is a very business-friendly politician who has overseen a large deal of growth and “development” in the Brasilian economy. In practice that means he promotes oil drilling and mining in the Amazon, he subsidizes the intertwined beef-soy industry causing so much destruction in the south and west of the country, and he also supports manufacture and higher tech industry.


Brasil’s stock market index, with the big crash on the right-hand side occurring on October 25.


If Bolsonaro’s son Flavio had won this past 25

th

 of October, the death squads that work for the ranchers, soy plantation owners, miners, loggers, or directly for the state, would have had free rein. Several of my friends and many of the

Ecco una breve intervista con il neonato gruppo

Le Donne del Vallo di Diano

andata in onda sulle libere frequenze di

Blackout

Siamo in Campania, più precisamente in provincia di Salerno. Il contesto è quello delle mobilitazioni degli auto trasportatori: è in questi presidi che prendono parola anche diverse giovani mamme, sul tema del carovita, del lavoro, ma anche dei diritti che vengono loro sottratti e che rivendicano, come quello alla sanità pubblica ed accessibile.

author: Benji
title: Grossdemo gegen Tönnies
content:
Grossdemo gegen Tönnies

Wir demonstrieren am 21.11. in Kellinghusen

Ihr seid wütend auf Tönnies? Wir auch! Wir haben

dokumentiert

, was Schweine bei Tönnies wirklich erleiden müssen. Wir haben bei Tönnies in Rheda-Wiedenbrück protestiert. Doch Tönnies tötet weiter. Deshalb fahren wir jetzt nochmal groß auf und demonstrieren an dem Schlachthof, aus dem die Aufnahmen unserer Aufdeckung stammen: Kellinghusen.


Bist du dabei?


Samstag, 21.11.2026

14:00 – 17:00 Uhr

Unterer Marktplatz, 25548 Kellinghusen

Hintergrundinfos


Rideshare-Tool

Damit möglichst viele Menschen zur Demo gegen Tönnies kommen, wollen wir euch bei der Planung eurer Anreise unterstützen. Daher haben wir ein cleveres Rideshare-Tool entwickelt, mit dem ihr Fahrgemeinschaften bilden könnt. So wird die Anreise für euch günstiger, einfacher und spaßiger.


Jetzt einsteigen!

Warum demonstrieren wir?

Anlass für die Großdemo am 21. November ist unsere aktuelle Veröffentlichung „Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies“. Tönnies ist Deutschlands größter Schlachtkonzern und gilt als eines der mächtigsten Unternehmen der europäischen Fleischindustrie. Als Marktführer tötet Tönnies jedes Jahr 16 Millionen Schweine. Unsere Aufdeckung zeigt den grausamen Erstickungskampf der Tiere in der CO₂-Anlage. Die Schweine schreien vor Angst und versuchen zu fliehen.


Was wir bisher getan haben

Gewalt im Schlachthof aufgedeckt

Verstöße dokumentiert

Tönnies angezeigt

Eine große Welle an Presseberichten ausgelöst

Zahlreiche Interviews geführt

Eine politische und gesellschaftliche Debatte angestoßen

Bei der Tönnies-Zentrale in Rheda-Wiedenbrück protestiert

Hintergrundinfos

Und jetzt?

Die Gewalt im Schlachthaus geht unvermindert weiter! Wir sind wütend. Deshalb fahren wir jetzt nochmal ganz groß auf, bündeln unsere Kräfte an einem Termin und demonstrieren gemeinsam mit euch an genau dem Schlachthof, aus dem die Aufnahmen unserer Aufdeckung stammen:

Kellinghusen!


Unsere Forderung: Der Betrieb muss schließen!


Ablauf und Programm

14:00 Uhr: Auftakt


Wir starten mit einer Auftaktkundgebung mit Redebeiträgen auf dem Unteren Marktplatz.

Demozug


Als großer und lauter Demozug ziehen wir mit Schildern, Bannern und Fahnen durch Kellinghusen, skandieren lautstark und setzen ein starkes Zeichen.

Zwischenstopp am Schlachthof


Die Demoroute führt uns bis zum Schlachthof. Dort gibt es weitere Redebeiträge.

Abschlusskundgebung


Gemeinsam laufen wir zurück zum Unteren Marktplatz, wo die Demo nach einer Abschlusskundgebung endet.

So kannst du mithelfen

Du willst mithelfen, dass die Demo richtig groß wird? Dann unterstütze uns bei der Mobilisierung: Bring deine Freund*innen mit zur Demo, teile unseren

Content auf Social Media

 oder poste selbst unser Sharepic:


Demoregeln

Bitte beachtet unsere allgemeinen Demohinweise, damit sich alle wohlfühlen. Danke für euer Verständnis und eure Mithilfe!


1. Antispeziesistisch und abolitionistisch

Einen Ansatz, die Ausbeutung der Tiere zu reformieren und somit im Grundsatz beizubehalten, verfolgen wir nicht. Unsere Forderungen sind grundsätzlich antispeziesistisch und abolitionistisch. Wir bitten deshalb ausdrücklich darum, auf der Demo vermeintliche „Zwischenschritte“ oder „Reformen“ (z. B. Biofleischkonsum oder Verbesserung der Haltungsbedingungen) nicht als Ziel zu kommunizieren.

2. Kein Platz für Menschenfeindlichkeit

ARIWA lehnt alle Formen allgemeiner und gruppenbezogener Menschenfeindlichkeit (wie zum Beispiel Ableismus, Antisemitismus, Homo- und Trans*feindlichkeit, Rassismus oder Sexismus) sowie verschwörungsideologische Denkmuster ab. Personen mit solchen Hintergründen sind bei der Demo ausdrücklich nicht erwünscht. Mehr Infos:

ariwa.org/selbstverstaendnis

3. Keine Kleidung tierischen Ursprungs

Bitte tragt nach Möglichkeit keine Kleidung tierischen Ursprungs und achtet darauf, dass sie auch nicht so aussieht. Denn Produkte wie Kunstpelz oder Kunstleder können missverstanden werden und für Außenstehende einen falschen Eindruck erwecken.

4. Keine Partei- oder Religionswerbung

Parteiwerbung, Werbung für religiöse Gruppierungen sowie Holocaust-Vergleiche sind nicht erwünscht.

5. Bitte keine Tiere mitbringen

Aufgrund von Lärm, Hitze und Enge bitten wir euch, keine Tiere mit zur Demo zu bringen.

Grossdemo gegen Tönnies

author: Jana Hoger
title: Update: Polizeihund bei Demo misshandelt – Staatsanwaltschaft stellt Ermittlungen ein
content:
Symbolbild


Bei einer Demonstration gegen den AfD-Parteitag am 11. Januar 2025 in Riesa kam es zu

gewaltsamen Einsätzen

 der sogenannten Polizeihunde. Wir von PETA Deutschland kritisieren dies scharf, erstatten Strafanzeige gegen die Verantwortlichen und fordern, dass der Einsatz von Polizeihunden endlich beendet wird. Erfahren Sie hier, was bei der Demonstration vorgefallen ist und warum Gewalt gegen „Polizeihunde“ kein Einzelfall ist.


Update vom 7. November 2026


Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden stellt Verfahren ein


Nachdem im Januar 2026 ein Video für einen medialen Aufschrei sorgte, das zeigt, wie ein sogenannter

Polizeihund

 bei einer Demonstration gewaltsam gegen einen Demonstranten eingesetzt wurde, erstatteten wir von PETA Deutschland Strafanzeige gegen die Verantwortlichen.


Im August 2026 wurde bekannt, dass die Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden in dem Fall nicht weiter ermittelt – angesichts des traurigen Videos mit absurden Begründungen. Die Staatsanwaltschaft erklärt diese Entscheidung in dem Einstellungsbescheid damit, dass ein „Verstoß gegen das Tierschutzgesetz […] nur vorliegen [würde], wenn man einem Tier ohne vernünftigen Grund aus Rohheit erhebliche Schmerzen zufügen würde.“ Der im Video dokumentierte Umgang des Beamten mit dem Hund sei keine „Rohheit“ im Sinne des Tierschutzgesetzes, da die ergriffene „Maßnahme […] zum Aufrechterhalten der öffentlichen Sicherheit und Ordnung erforderlich war […]“ und der Hund „nur kurz eingesetzt“ worden sei.


Die Staatsanwaltschaft begründet die Entscheidung darüber hinaus damit, dass „Diensthunde […] legal bei der Polizei als Hilfsmittel auch in Stresssituationen eingesetzt […]“ werden. Die Tiere würden dabei automatisch Belastungssituationen ausgesetzt. Die Interessen und das Wohl der Hunde rückten jedoch im Verhältnis zu den polizeilichen Interessen der Gefahrenabwehr in den Hintergrund, da die „Diensthunde“ zu diesem Zwecke ausgebildet würden. Der den Hunden zugeschriebene „Nutzen“ rechtfertigt laut Ansicht der Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden, dass die Tiere bewusst in Gefahrensituationen gezwungen werden.


PETA kritisiert Entscheidung der Staatsanwaltschaft: Gesetz erlaubt Gewalt gegen Diensthunde


Die Einstellung unserer Anzeige ist ein weiteres Beispiel dafür, dass das Gesetz die „Diensthunde“ nicht vor einem gewaltsamen Umgang und Missbrauch schützt. Hunde sind keine Einsatzmittel, sondern fühlende Lebewesen, die einen respektvollen, liebevollen Umgang verdient haben – nicht die missbräuchliche Verwendung  als Waffe oder Schutzschild.


Wir vertreten die Ansicht, dass moderne Polizeiarbeit ohne Tiere auskommt und fordern daher Politik und Behörden auf, „Diensthunde“ zu verbieten.


Originaltext vom 13. Januar 2025


Gewalt gegen Polizeihunde bei einem Einsatz gegen Demonstranten in Riesa


Videos von der Demonstration zeigen deutlich wie gewaltvoll einige Diensthundeführer:innen mit den „Polizeihunden“ umgehen. Einer der

Hunde

 wurde von einem der Beamten am Hals gepackt und gegen eine Leitplanke und einen Demonstranten gedrückt. Dadurch sollte der Hund offensichtlich dazu gebracht werden, den Demonstranten zu beißen. Der Hund zeigte hierbei unübersehbare

Anzeichen

 von massivem Stress, Überforderung und Meideverhalten. Ein weiterer völlig überdrehter Hund verbiss sich in den Arm eines anderen Polizisten.


https://www.instagram.com/p/DExO_Z1Mcvv/?hl=de


PETA erstattet Strafanzeige und fordert den Einsatz von Polizeihunden zu beenden


Dieser gewaltsame Umgang der Einsatzkräfte mit den Hunden ist tierschutzwidrig. Hunde sind nicht dazu da, für die Arbeit der Polizei ausgenutzt zu werden. Wir fordern deshalb, den Einsatz von Hunden bei der Polizei endlich einzustellen. Zudem erstatten wir bei der Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden Zweigstelle Meißen Strafanzeige gegen den verantwortlichen Polizisten. Ferat Kocak, Abgeordneter der Linken war als parlamentarischer Beobachter vor Ort und hat sich bereit erklärt in der Strafanzeige als Zeuge aufzutreten.


„Die aktuellen Aufnahmen aus Riesa zeigen eindeutig, dass Hunde bei Polizeieinsätzen nichts zu suchen haben. Wir hoffen, dass es den betroffenen Hunden gut geht und sie keine körperlichen Schäden von dieser grausamen Behandlung davontragen. Die Psyche der Hunde leidet nach solch einem Einsatz ganz sicher. author: OAG
title: Picturing the bandits
content:
In June, the

Guardian

 published

“Brutal and Emboldened: How Nigeria’s Bandit Crisis Spun Out of Control,”

 a report from Katsina State in Nigeria’s northwest, where communities in local government areas such as Batsari have struck peace deals with the armed groups that have terrorized them for years. The photographs were taken by Terna Iwar, an Abuja-based photographer and artist who traveled with the

Guardian

’s West Africa correspondent, Eromo Egbejule, and a local stringer — without a security escort — to meet one of those groups under a neem tree near the border with Niger.

On the latest episode of the

Africa Is a Country

 podcast, the Nigerian Scam talks to Terna about that encounter: why he kept his camera in plain sight from the moment he arrived, how the group saw itself (as protectors of their communities, not bandits or terrorists), and what the peace deal actually gives them. Access to shops and medicine, and an end to their families’ shame, are on the table; disarmament is not, since other armed groups are still out there. Terna describes a landscape of abandoned towns and clinics, electricity poles without cables, and border posts that barely function. He also reflects on the central dilemma of conflict photography: how to portray people as more than one-dimensional without losing sight of the horrific acts they have committed.

Listen to the show below, and

subscribe

 on your favorite platform.

Sa’eed Husaini

Well, look, I guess we should talk banditry and photography, which are some of the key words for the day. So yeah, we’re talking about banditry and shooting the bandits, quote, unquote, today. And the conversation is with a longtime comrade, collaborator, or friend, Terna Iwar, who’s also a well-known photographer, artist, and creative. So, Terna, thanks for coming on the show, man.

Terna Iwar

Thank you for having me.

Sa’eed Husaini

Homecoming in some ways, right?

Terna Iwar

In many ways, yes.

Sa’eed Husaini

We hope. So feel free to raid the fridge. You don’t need to take your shoes off. The normal protocol. So, this is inspired by a recent article,

“Brutal and Emboldened,”

 a

Guardian

 article about how Nigeria’s bandit crisis is spinning out of control. We want to talk about banditry, but not necessarily only about the dynamics and history and stuff. We’ve had part of that conversation previously with James Barnett, and we’ll have more of that kind of more historical, if you will, conversation going forward. But I think part of what we want to dive into is a bit of the experience, right, of encountering this camp, going to the camp, and shooting, or photographing, the bandits — and then, of course, your assessment, based on that experience, of what the hell is going on with banditry in Nigeria. I’m sure there’ll be elements of the conversation maybe you don’t want to get into right now. We’ll respect that, but of course, as detailed or as granular as you want to get, there’s space for that. And so, just by way of a little bit more background, Terna was part of a team that went up to Katsina, if I’m not mistaken, and had an exclusive interview with at least one camp of AK-47-wielding bandits. Got their perspective, but also kind of hung out with them. They seem pretty relaxed in the photos, and I guess it’d be interesting to get your take on how you got them to be so chilled out in the photos, and what they thought of you as well, shooting at them from the camera. So I don’t know, man. Maybe by way of intro, you could just talk a little bit about how you got into this and what that was about, and how freaked out were your parents hearing that you. . . .  However you want to get into it.

Terna Iwar

Well, again, thank you for having me. Talking about the work I do is not something I often get to do, so I think this might even help me metabolize what that was like. So Eromo, the West Africa correspondent for the

Guardian

, reached out. We’d been talking back and forth for a while about potential stories and stuff that I was working on, what I was interested in doing, and when this came up, he thought that it would be a great fit, since a lot of the work that I’ve been doing in photojournalism revolves somehow around conflict. I just kind of found myself shooting a lot of conflict stuff, banditry, the aftermath of people’s lives changing in the most horrific, drastic ways. author: Abdulbagi Mohammad
title: Formalising the RSF: EU Policies and Sudan’s Search for Funds
content:
The Rapid Support Forces (RSF) are one of the two armed parties in the current war in Sudan. Despite their historic collaborations with multiple domestic and external actors, everyone is washing their hands of them. In this piece, I will try to make sense of the RSF and conclude by associating its institutionalisation with the convergence of goals between Sudan and the EU in the 2010s.


It depends on where you stand to identify the root causes of the formalisation and institutionalisation of the RSF. In 2003, when the war broke out in Darfur, Sudan’s western region, the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) received a

humiliating shock

. The Sudanese government then mobilised Darfurians, who know the geography of the area and who were mobile enough to cope with the insurgents’ tactics. The rebel groups were mostly from non-Arab ancestries, while the bulk of the counterinsurgent militias were Darfurian Arabs including Mohammad Hamdan Dagalo ‘Hemedti’ (the current leader of RSF) and others. The counterinsurgency campaign was successful militarily, but against the backdrop of this ‘‘succes’’ the campaign left damaging results. The International Criminal Court (ICC) issued an arrest warrant,

in March 2009

, for Al-Basheer, then the president of Sudan,  for war crimes and crimes against humanity during the counter insurgency. What is relevant here is the governmental admiration for this model received despite the associated ethical and reputational costs. The informal militias were deployed outside of Darfur and grew in size, and in 2013 they were given an official identity as the ‘RSF’ and attached to the National Intelligence and Security Service (NISS).


The RSF was considered by many as a

coup-proofing

 tool. Al-Basheer was an army officer and seized power through a military coup. As an insider, he knew what a strong army could do for a dictator’s throne. The NISS received better treatment than the army, elevating it to a

rival status

 with the SAF, something that caused angst within SAF ranks. In November 2012, authorities foiled a coup that had the former chief of NISS,

Salah Goush

, as the putschist. Again, the playbook was revisited and this time the rising player was RSF. Hemedti would subsequently

quip

 that

‘Sudan has no army but us.’


Making Sense of the RSF


The key decisions leading to the formulation of the RSF took place between 2013 and 2014 in Sudan and Europe.  In Sudan, Al-Basheer’s regime was experiencing a difficult time. On the 27

th

 of January 2014, Al-Basheer

addressed the nation

 in what was known as the ‘National Leap Speech’.  He considered

four prerequisites

 for the country to leap forward: Peace, free and rule-abiding political community, lifting the Sudanese from poverty into prosperity, finally reviving the ‘Sudanese Identity’. In addressing poverty, Al-Basheer zeroed in on sanctions as a major hindrance in the alleviating poverty in Sudan.


To the north, Europe was facing what it described as a ‘Migration Crisis’. In November 2014, the EU-Horn of Africa Migration Route Initiative, known as the

Khartoum Process

, was established.  It was meant to be a platform for political cooperation between Horn of Africa and Europe regarding migration routes.  In November 2015, the Valletta Summit action plan was issued.  This plan served as a marriage of convenience between the Sudanese government and the EU. The latter wanted to address migration, while the former was keen to achieve the leap goals through partnering with a global power like the EU.


The government started drafting and amending acts eagerly to prove itself as a reliable partner in the addressing migration. In January 2014, it issued the

Asylum Regulating Act

 2014, repealing

The Regulation of Asylum Act 1974

.  The new act imposed more restrictions on the movement of refugees in Sudan.  They were not allowed to move outside their registered residence without permission. The law vested authority in the Minister of Interior to establish, close or transfer any refugee camp.


18 months later, the

Sudan’s Passports and Immigration Act 2015

 was passed.  Harbouring aliens who are not eligible to reside in Sudan was now considered a crime. Those found guilty were subject to two years imprisonment and a fine. The same act considered involvement in human trafficking an offense resulting in imprisonment for between five to ten years, and the court had the right to confiscate any property used in trafficking.  None of …

author: Willy Mutunga
title: Book Review: From Mau Mau to Ruto-Must-Go: A Scrapbook of Essays on Kenya’s Struggle Against Imperialism
content:
I recently read a review of the book, 

From MAU MAU to RUTO-MUST-GO: A Scrapbook of Essays on Kenya’s Struggle Against Imperialism,

 

by Teddy Odira, a young lawyer in Nairobi who published in The Platform for Law, Justice, and Society. I shared the review with one of the co-editors of the book, Shiraz Durrani, and asked him what he thought. This is was his response via a WhatsApp text:


It’s a brilliant review, I think. He understands the undercurrents that the book explores and identifies key issues, like land, that have driven resistance. He also sees resistance as an on-going, incomplete struggle. Very well done!


What is well said by another is mine. In this review, I want to glorify the work of the artist movements in Kenya for breathing life into the Constitution of Kenya, 2010, particularly

Article 33

 that decrees freedom of expression. This freedom of expression has limitations. It is the freedom of artistic creativity that is glorified in two of the articles in the book. They glorify cartoonists and Social Justice Theatre (SJCCTT). Freedom of artistic creativity in Kenya is valued by others, including the two mentioned. The others include: poets, spoken word artists, graffiti artists, songwriters, singers, comedians, filmmakers, and others. Freedom of artistic creativity has been a radical site of struggle in the implementation of the Constitution of Kenya, 2010. Freedom of expression under the Constitution has been the subject of a recently published scholarly work.


This Constitution has been described as progressive and transformative because of the process of its making, its texts on objectives, purpose, and vision to reform, by non-reformist reforms, which maintain the status quo in Kenya. While the ruling elite find the Constitution inconvenient and abstract, these sites of struggle have used provisions of the Constitution to craft political demands, breathe life into these sites through uprising, robust public participation, mass action, and public interest litigation. The quest for an authentic patriotic alternative political leadership is a continuous struggle anchored in these constitutional sites of struggle that the ruling elite has refused to implement. It is argued that such an alternative political leadership that is authentic and patriotic will implement the Constitution by consolidating gains made, and rescuing the weaknesses that are encountered during the process of its implementation.


Glorification


A: In Praise of Cartoonists: Ruo Kimani-Ruo


Ruo Kimani-Ruo praises the cartoonists in words that should not be paraphrased:


…,

there has emerged an unprecedented form of political cartoons artwork which has been launched in Kenya with sizzling, scorching, blistering cartoon editorials and other graphics and caricatures of public figures that express the artists’ opinions, with celebrated cartoon artists Celeste and Maddo


being joined by Yoko and others-all freely and fearlessly expressing their opinions on public issues and the individuals in government and thereby shedding light on the public mood on issues.…


With these political cartoons, the artists have had a field day and typically combined artistic skills, hyperbole and satire to question authority. The cartoons have drawn attention to, among other things, corruption, electoral inequalities, political abductions and other social ills including violence- and the Consolidated Fund at Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) where billions of shillings are being ‘siphoned and stashed in offshore accounts in the West; and suspicions of embezzlement.


The genius of the cartoonists that I have encountered over decades lies in the interpretation of their work for the powers that be, and the citizens themselves. They are always armed with many interpretations of their cartoons. They use those interpretations to either stay safe when confronted by elites and their machinery of violence, or to mobilize the citizens around the key messages. They invariably keep their mouths shut and let their work engage both the enemy and the friend. Their work requires great critical thinking, taking ideological and political positions in breathing life into the provisions of the Constitution to energize non-reformist reforms.


B: In Praise of Theatre Artists:


Zachary J Patterson

title: Polls close and the counting of votes has begun
content:
The Western Cape electoral officer, Michael Hendrickse told reporters that there were more people who voted in this year’s local government elections compared the previous poll in 2021. By 18h00, over 1.5 million people had voted. “Its clear that the number of voters is going upwards and will surpass the number of voters in the local government elections in 2021. But, there were fewer registered people in 2021 compared to this year. So, I’m not comparing the turnout as a proportion but looking at the numbers of people who voted,” he said.


Hendrickse said that there were still people waiting to vote at around 21h45 as they were in the queue by 21h00.


In Cape Town


Elitsha


reported earlier

 that voters in Khayelitsha and Mitchells Plain said that youth unemployment and lack of basic services are some of the issues that the next council should prioritise. Zine Malusi from ward 89 in Khayelitsha pleaded with political parties to work together to improve the lives of the poor even if they end up in coalition governments.


Her views were echoed by Fiona Jacobs from Portlands who said there was a need for the media to play an educational role in the elections to make sure that voters are clear who to vote for.


In Johannesburg


In Alexandra, unemployment and poor municipal services featured prominently in the concerns of young voters.


Bonang Makola, a first-time voter, said unemployment and the deteriorating state of Johannesburg influenced her decision at the ballot box. She had followed interviews in which political parties outlined their plans to reduce unemployment over the next five years, and their proposals helped shape her choice.


“As a young person, unemployment is one of the biggest issues. Some parties said they would reduce it by 0%, while others said they would reduce it by 2% every year. That influenced my decision on which party to vote for,” she said.


Makola said residents in her community continue to experience electricity problems, water interruptions and poor refuse collection. The accumulation of rubbish in Alexandra, she added, had become a serious health concern.


Thato Couch, a resident of Tsutsumani in Alexandra and a first-time voter, believes that the growing dissatisfaction with political parties has contributed to voter apathy. She said some residents no longer saw the point of voting because they felt that elections had brought little improvement to their circumstances. “People choose not to vote because they think it’s useless. There’s no change, no progress and nothing is actually moving. We just keep voting for the same thing,” she said.


Municipal workers fixing a blocked drain outside ward 89 voting station in Khayelitsha

.


Meanwhile, Rene, a Sandton resident, said Johannesburg’s deteriorating infrastructure requires urgent intervention, regardless of whether the next administration was formed by a single party or a coalition. She supports coalition governments provided political parties cooperate and share a commitment to fighting corruption and improving service delivery. “Johannesburg is falling apart. There has to be a party, whether it’s a coalition or a single party, that fixes this wonderful city because it’s broken through neglect,” she said.


Rene argued that political disagreements and leadership disputes should never take precedence over residents’ basic needs. “We’re the people. We pay our taxes and rates, yet our streets are full of potholes, we have no water, no electricity and the garbage isn’t being collected,” she said.


She also highlighted the dangers posed by poorly maintained roads, particularly for elderly motorists navigating streets without adequate lighting and road markings.


Across the interviews, voters expressed different perspectives on political parties and coalition government but shared a common expectation: those elected must demonstrate accountability and deliver tangible improvements. For Johannesburg residents, the real test of the elections will not simply be who wins political power, but whether that power translates into jobs, functioning infrastructure and reliable basic services.


In KuGompo City


Mdantsane residents, in Buffalo City Metropolitan Municipality, said that youth unemployment and service delivery should be one of the key things that the next council should focus on.

author: Abahlali_3
title: We mourn the loss of Des D’sa
content:
30 October 2026 Abahlali baseMjondolo press statement

We mourn the loss of Des D’Sa, father, uncle, grandfather, and a comrade to many

The death of Desmond D’Sa has plunged many people on the left in Durban and beyond, across numerous organisations, into shock and despair. Siyakhala ngo Des.

Comrade Des was a stalwart in the struggle against apartheid and was a well-known organiser who formed the South Durban Community Environmental Alliance (SDCEA), an environmental organisation that raised the concerns of families living in the oil- and gas-affected areas of Wentworth and the Bluff.

His activism and the fight against injustices did not end with environmental issues and it definitely did not end in Wentworth and the Bluff. Comrade Des fought against all forms of oppression and injustice, including gangsterism and the mining companies in rural areas, and supported everyone from fisherfolk to migrants and poor people, whether living in flats, hostels or shacks. He did not back down when struggle became dangerous. Comrade Des spoke fluent isiZulu and engaged everyone with the same respect.

He joined the first march against ANC councillor Yacoob Baig organised from Kennedy Road in 2005, which became part of the process towards the formation of our movement. He stood with our movement from the beginning, and was one of the few who never wavered in his support even when we were under severe attack and isolated.

Comrade Des was one of the founders of the Right to Know Campaign that fought fought against secrecy while promoting the right to information. He was also one of the founders of The Durban Coalition, which was first formed in response to the devastating floods of 2022. The Coalition, which unites community organisations across the city in a united front, is thriving today and is an important formation in the city.

We will miss Comrade Des so much. He was always on the side of the people. He was always so warm and kind. We always laughed when he was around.

We wish to thank his family for him. And wish to express our heartfelt condolences to his family, friends and comrades.

It is so sad and devastating that you have left us. Till we meet again.

Hamba kahle Comrade Des D’Sa. Ubuyiqhawe.

author: WoMin
title: From Mombasa to Yaoundé, the vision and the demand is for reparative justice
content:
Through WoMin’s work alongside African women organising against extractivism, against the drivers of the climate crisis and its impacts, the destruction of the commons through false solutions, unjust energy transitions (and generally a world order that serves a minority over the global majority), we have been asking: what is the full range of impacts and costs in the face of environmental and climate impacts? Who and whose work absorbs these impacts and costs? And what would repair mean from the perspective of women, their communities and the ecosystems they care for and are cared for at the frontline of the climate crisis, where centuries of continued systems of accumulation by dispossession and destruction meet?


Our experience shows us that reparations cannot simply be another form of compensation. They must confront the very systems producing the harm – extractivism, odious and illegitimate debt, colonial legacies, patriarchy, racism, and corporate power promoting more false solutions whose aim is not climate justice but profit. Reparations must indeed offer us all a real chance to build Pan African feminist futures that centre care, including the restoration of the commons, and the conditions that make life possible.


Connecting the “c-words” – colonialism to climate reparations


The recent

African Symposium on Climate Reparations

 in Mombasa, Kenya, started on that same note: “there is no “c-word” that we cannot bring into conversations on climate reparations”, argued a comrade in his opening remarks. And indeed, the current

climate disorder

1

 is a historical process, and Colonialism (the c-word that in other climate justice spaces some shy away from) is part and parcel of it. As is, we argue at WoMin, capitalism. What is more, not only do climate reparations need to address colonialism and neocolonialism, but also the solution to the climate crisis will not be found within capitalism. Or as Audre Lorde put it, “… the master’s tools will never dismantle the master’s house. They may allow us temporarily to beat him at his own game, but they will never enable us to bring about genuine change.”


Not only we need our own tools, but also a broad alliance, as broad, yet united in principles and analysis, as broad and urgent is the task ahead. And the symposium offered an important space to bring together many working for reparations across the continent and in the diaspora, in conversations navigated along four main tracks: rights of nature and ecosystems stewardship; finance, debt and tax justice; law and human rights; and lived realities from frontline communities.


And the timing matters. We are entering the Decade of Justice and Reparations for Africans and People of African Descent, while the debt crisis in Africa continues to exponentially grow and deepen climate vulnerability, false climate solutions continue to expand, further threatening the commons millions of Africans depend upon for their everyday subsistence, and the African Court considers an Advisory Opinion on States’ obligations in the climate crisis.


As powerful expressed in an

open letter

 which emerged from the symposium, a Pan African position and action plan for climate reparations is urgent, but it cannot be constructed only through states, legal and financial tools. Those at the frontlines absorbing the costs of extractivism, ecological destruction and climate disruption have to shape what counts as harm, what constitutes repair, and what must stop. And importantly, we need to organise at all levels the collective power to make repair possible.


African women united for climate justice and reparations


This was the task of the 4th

Women’s Climate Assembly

 (WCA) in Yaoundé, Cameroon, held in early October under the theme, “Our lands, our voices: African women united for climate justice and reparations!”. The Assembly convened over 75 women community leaders, activists, feminist organisations, civil society groups and allies from twelve countries including Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Guinea-Conakry, Liberia, Namibia, Niger, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Senegal, and Zambia.


Oh ancestors, watch over Africa and let everything return to Africa! If we are coveted today, if there are wars, it is because our ancestors bequeathed this land to us. They did not abuse its riches. They used them sustainably. So we ask our ancestors to guide us during this Assembly, so that peace and food …

author: Mada Masr
title: Lina Attalah in custody after court issues LE3 mn fine, orders Mada Masr’s closure
content:
Mada Masr Editor-in-Chief Lina Attalah was fined LE3 million by the New Cairo Misdemeanor Court, which convicted her on charges of managing an unlicensed website, issuing an order for the website’s closure. Attalah was taken into custody after the issue of the ruling.


Tuesday’s session at the ninth circuit of the New Cairo Misdemeanor Court, presided over by judge Mohamed Mubarak, was temporarily suspended for deliberations after Attalah’s defense counsel requested time to review the case file.


After the court returned from deliberations, the judge ordered the courtroom cleared of everyone except Attalah and her defense counsel, the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights’ executive director Hossam Bahgat, who was also present, told Mada Masr. The room then filled with plainclothes officers and guards, with a National Security Agency officer in attendance, he added.


The presiding judge and a Supreme State Security Prosecution representative returned to the session and the judge announced that the court has decided to stand by its rejection of all the procedural arguments presented by the defense, including requests to bring in any documentation or hear any witnesses.


The judge then asked the defense team to present its plea. The counsel insisted that it would not submit a plea as long as its requests were unanswered by the court.


The judge then abruptly asked for a lawyer unknown to any member of the defense counsel to be brought in, “in a move that astonished all those present,” said Bahgat, and announced that the court decided to appoint a lawyer for Attalah.


At that point, all members of the defense counsel cried out to reject the court’s appointment of a lawyer when the eight chosen lawyers were present. Attalah herself spoke to say she did not accept the court-appointed lawyer acting on her behalf, an objection the judge refused to have recorded in the session’s minutes.


“In an even more shocking move,” said Bahgat, the judge himself began to log down the requests of the court-appointed lawyer, without the lawyer having said a word. The judge then read out the conviction amid shouts and protests from the defense counsel.


The judge sentenced Attalah to the maximum possible penalty: a LE3 million fine, the closure of Mada Masr’s website and the confiscation of its property.


Security personnel then surrounded Attalah, lifted her off the ground and took her out of the courtroom, where she remains in custody in the courthouse.

The post

Lina Attalah in custody after court issues LE3 mn fine, orders Mada Masr’s closure

 first appeared on

Mada Masr

author: AfricanFeminism
title: Morocco’s First Woman Prime Minister and the Terms of Freedom
content:
Something changes when a woman occupies an office men have treated as their natural inheritance. Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri’s

appointment

 on 29 September 2026 makes that change visible in Morocco. For women whose competence is routinely scrutinised, the pleasure is neither naïve nor trivial.


But the woman forming a government and the woman labouring in the fields, raising children without pay and denied an equal share of her inheritance encounter power differently. Representation changes who governs; emancipation changes what all women have the power to do. That distinction shifts our attention from PM Mansouri’s gender to the politics of the centre-right

 Party of Authenticity and Modernity (PAM

)

, which she leads. Will its programme redistribute the resources and rights on which women’s freedom depends?


The history beneath the headline


Calling women’s leadership foreign to Morocco requires forgetting its history. Historian Osire Glacier

documents

 women’s authority long before the contemporary premiership. Kenza al Awrabiya, the Amazigh mother of Idris II, helped secure the Idrisid dynasty, founded in the late eighth century in what is now Morocco. Zaynab al Nafzawiyya influenced eleventh-century Almoravid politics around Aghmat, near Marrakech. Sayyida al Hurra governed Tétouan, a city in northern Morocco, during the sixteenth century. Khnata bint Bakkar intervened in eighteenth-century dynastic politics.


Across the region,

Dihya

 is remembered as an Amazigh queen who led resistance to the Arab conquest in the Aurès, in present-day Algeria, during the late seventh century. Tuareg oral tradition remembers

Tin Hinan

 as a queen and founding ancestress of noble lineages in the Ahaggar, in present-day southern Algeria.


These histories expose how male authority is made to appear natural. Fatima Mernissi’s

The Forgotten Queens of Islam


challenges that selective memory. Colonialism also reorganised authority: French Protectorate administrators

reshaped

 customary courts around imperial priorities. What survives as tradition can carry the history of political intervention. 


Religious interpretation can give exclusion another claim to permanence. Islamist and other conservative opponents invoke this

hadith

 against women’s political authority:


«لَنْ يُفْلِحَ قَوْمٌ وَلَّوْا أَمْرَهُمُ امْرَأَةً»


Usually translated as saying that a people governed by a woman will not prosper, it becomes a prohibition irrespective of her competence. Asma Lamrabet, a

Moroccan Islamic feminist thinker

, questions turning a

narration linked

 to Persia’s dynastic succession into a universal ban. She reads it against the Qur’anic Queen of Sheba, whose judgement demonstrates capable leadership. Her argument contests male authority’s claim to divine necessity.


PAM’s promises and its record


Women have long contested how authority is distributed within the family. Fatima Sadiqi

documents

the Union de l’Action Féminine’s 1992 million-signature campaign to reform the Moudawana, Morocco’s family code. The 2004 reform abolished wives’ duty of obedience but retained unequal inheritance and exceptions to the marriage age of eighteen. Proposals announced in December 2024 left fundamental equality demands unresolved. In October 2025, more than sixty civil society organisations and public figures

joined to call for comprehensive reform

. Rights in Morocco have advanced through organised demands, not the gender of an officeholder.


PAM, a centre-right party founded in 2008,

advocates

 social modernisation and positions itself against the Islamist Justice and Development Party (PJD). It entered government in 2021 alongside the National Rally of Independents and conservative nationalist Istiqlal. Opposition to Islamist conservatism, however, does not itself entail reforming the laws and economic conditions that subordinate women.


PAM’s

2026 programme

 promises improved widow pensions, childcare, safe transport, a women’s enterprise fund and labour inspection. The commitments leave inheritance equality, abortion reform and decriminalisation of consensual same sex relations unaddressed. Mansouri called for

banning child marriage

 without exceptions in 2024, yet PAM’s electoral programme

omits that commitment

. Employment can support independence, but a wage does not cancel criminalisation or unequal property rights. The programme leaves those constraints intact.


Even PAM’s narrow promise to increase …

author: Branko Marcetic
title: The left can defeat reactionaries
content:
The United States left has been so conditioned in the Trump era to look aghast and horrified at election results that it is still hard to fully believe the outcome of the November 3 midterms. Yet those historic events really did happen: Donald Trump and Republicans suffered a historic rebuke from voters, handing Democrats wins up and down the ballot all across the country, flipping both chambers of Congress in their favor, and handing them the largest congressional majorities they’ve had since Barack Obama’s election.

In many ways, the result is simple. Across poll after poll leading into the election and exit poll after exit poll leading out of it, the message from voters was the same: they think the economy sucks, they think prices are too high, and they’re angry at Trump and blame him squarely for this entire situation. To send this message, voters turned out in droves to hand power to a Democratic Party that these same polls show they have very little love for, sometimes viewing the Dems even more dimly than they do Trump.

Democrats were expected to take the House. They were

not expected

 to win a majority of more than 250 seats in it, as estimates at the time of writing had them winning. Nor were they expected to win a Senate majority, let alone a Senate majority of at least 54 seats. And they were not expected to flip deep red seats across the country, to sweep Republicans from control of Texas at nearly every level of power, and to win a

majority of the country’s governorships

, achieving

wins and trifectas

 in states they’ve been practically locked out of, sometimes for decades. Obama referred to his 2010 midterms rout as a “shellacking.” These midterms were an annihilation.

This is not just good news for Democrats. For the US left, which operates within these Democratic majorities at both the state and federal levels, the results present a historic opportunity to turn its political priorities from words into tangible reality across the country, further building the power it has patiently and, for a long time, quietly been constructing from the ground up these past

10 years

.

That includes at the federal level. Even though Trump has two more years in the White House, and Democrats are threatening to zealously turn their powers of oversight on the vast record of abuse and criminality he’s racked up during that time, there is some, extremely slim reason to believe something could actually get done.

Trump

phoned

 Politico on election night to make clear he was open to working with the Democrats and didn’t “want to be just sitting there for two years vetoing everything.” The last time Trump was in the White House with a Democratic-controlled House, during the pandemic, the United States saw the largest expansion of the welfare state in decades. Trump’s ideological malleability and the fact that he is currently looking at a legacy as a historic failure presents at least the possibility of an opening for something better to happen.

It’s an opening the left will be able to take advantage of, too. The left will enter this new Congress with far more formidable numbers than it’s had in decades: at least seven members of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), creating the historic opportunity to form, for the first time, a distinct

socialist caucus

 in Congress and a Squad-like progressive “

Bloc

” that could have as many as 20 members.

The massive Democratic House majority means “the Bloc” will not have the expected leverage of being able to block House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries’s bid for Speaker, or to hold up legislation Freedom Caucus–style. But it will have influence. Much of the generous pandemic policies of 2020, including both Trump and, later, Joe Biden’s stimulus checks, originated with the public demands of socialist and progressive members of Congress that later found their way into legislation on the back of their clear public need and popularity.

This time, the left will be making these arguments in a world in which socialists have already transformed the way even centrist Democrats talk about politics. The party’s years-long obsession with “norms” and rescuing democracy having largely faded into the background in favor of the affordability-focused and anti-billionaire rhetoric

popularized

 by, respectively, New York’s socialist mayor, Zohran Mamdani, and the socialist duo of Sanders and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez on their “Fighting Oligarchy” tour.

Just as importantly …
