author: Savanna Craig
title: Akwesasne community members fighting the opening of a Hyperscale data center
content:
A few minutes’ drive outside the borders of Akwesasne Mohawk Territory, industrial sites line the perimeter.


One aluminum reduction and smelting site now operates as a digital currency mining facility.


The facility is set to expand, opening the doors to a new hyperscale data center. The center will be another facility on the list of many that border Akwesasne, Kanienʼkehá꞉ka territory.


A truck with three Kanienʼkehá꞉ka women drive past the facility. As they pass, a group of men nail up “no trespassing signs” along the facility.


“You’re on native land,” Dana Leigh Thompson shouts from the driver’s window. Thompson has been fighting to protect Akwesasne’s land, water and people for decades from outside corporate industry.


“We don’t care how many signs they put up [saying] no trespassing,” says Thompson. “This is our land. This is the land of the Kanienʼkehá꞉ka. Period.”


Three industrial and commercial sites are located near Akwesasne. In the United States these are known as Superfund sites.


Johnson-Zafiris and Sunday plan for future MUSH events in Dana Leigh Thompson’s library. Photo: Savanna Craig/APTN.


The digital currency mining facility once operated as Reynold’s Metals. For decades, the aluminum reduction and smelting site released high amounts of toxic polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) into the environment.


A significant amount of U.S. Superfund sites are located on or near Indigenous land. Indigenous communities in North America are disproportionately exposed to environmental contaminants, including PCBs, according to a

study from 2012

.


“There are 1,373 Superfund sites on or adjacent to indigenous communities in the United States,” says Thompson.


Two other Superfund sites line the border of Akwesasne.


The defunct

General Motors site leaked

 aluminum die casting contributing to PCB contamination.


Thompson stands on her land, neighbouring the former General Motors site.


“What happens when a boat passes, all the water goes out, pulls it out, then it acts like a suction cup,” she explains, explaining that the pollutants are pulled from the site where PCB contamination is buried in the ground.


The third Superfund site, Alcoa Grasse River, discharged PCBs on the land and neighbouring wetlands from the 1950s to the mid 1970s.


An anti-data center sign sits across from a digital mining facility, owned by the same company set to open the data center. Photo: Savanna Craig/APTN.


‘Ranatakárias’


In July 2025, U.S. President Donald Trump signed an

executive order

 to accelerate federal permits of data center infrastructure. Within it, it states environmental reviews should be expedited to turn Superfund sites into data centers.


His efforts to expedite the conversion of Superfund sites into data centers, like the ones that line Akwesasne, has granted him the name “Ranatakárias” in Akwesasne.


“What that translates into is ‘town destroyer,’” says Thompson.


Now one of these sites will be expanding to develop a 1.5 million square foot hyperscale data center.


New York Digital Investment Group operates a digital mining facility on the old Reynold’s Metals site. The group has partnered with North Country Collocation Services to open the data center.


Wetlands surround the proposed three buildings that will inhabit the new hyperscale data center.


APTN News reached out to both New York Digital Investment Group and North Country Collocation Services for an interview request but didn’t receive a response.


Thompson is a mentor for the next generation. The next generation leading the fight against industrial and commercial sites from opening along Akwesasne are a group that calls themselves MUSH.

author: Nehaa Bimal
title: International Inuit Day celebration set to return to Ottawa’s Annie Pootoogook Park
content:
Isaruit Inuit Arts, an Ottawa-based organization, will host its sixth annual International Inuit Day celebration Saturday at Annie Pootoogook Park in the Sandy Hill neighbourhood. 


The event runs from noon to 4:30 p.m. and will feature musical performances, a feast, family games and cultural activities. It is free and open to the public. 


Performers include Pangnirtung singer-songwriter Joey Nowyuk, Ottawa-based drum dancer Donovan Gordon Tootoo, who is originally from Rankin Inlet, and the Nunavut Sivuniksavut students’ performing group.


Inuit arts and crafts vendors will also sell their work at the event.


The schedule includes a qulliq lighting at 1:30 p.m., performances from 1:40 p.m., a feast at 2:30 p.m. and community games at 3:15 p.m. 


An Inuit cultural activity tent will offer a qulliq making activity and photo opportunities featuring Inuit clothing.


International Inuit Day, observed annually on Nov. 7, was established by the Inuit Circumpolar Council in 2006 to celebrate Inuit culture and amplify Inuit voices across the circumpolar world.


The date honours Greenlander Eben Hopson Sr., founder of the first Inuit Circumpolar Conference in 1977.

author: Matt Simmons
title: Inside the Big House connecting generations to Haíɫzaqv knowledge
content:
Photos by Matt Simmons


This story was produced in collaboration with


The Narwhal

.


As smoke rises from the fire at the centre of a Haíɫzaqv Big House raised two decades ago on a beach crowded with cedar, the song begins.


The dancers emerge and circle the floor, their feet tracing stories in the sand. Drummers seated at the log drum hold the beat and their voices carry the song. Around the room, from among all the people here to witness the ceremony, women stand. Swaying like kelp

in tidal currents, their movements and hand gestures mirror those of the dancers, protecting them.


Leading this ceremony, dancing life into the walls and the world around, are children. This is

Kvai

, a place where

Haíɫzaqv

 kids come to connect with song and story, language and ceremony. Received by the lands and waters, this is their lineage, their inheritance.


Standing next to the log drum, leaning on the talking stick, Thomas Dixon extends a welcome.


“The name of this Big House is λáλix̌sístala,” he says. “λáλix̌sístala in our language translates to ‘complete the circle’ — and the circle we’re referring to is the circle of knowledge, because of the amount of knowledge that gets passed on here, from generation to generation.”


Hear ‘Cúagilákv Jess Housty say the name of the Big House, “λáλix̌sístala”


Inside the λáλix̌sístala Big House, cultural leader Thomas Dixon welcomes young people to Kvai, a camp for Haíɫzaqv Youth.


Like many of his peers, Dixon came here as a Youth and learned from the land and from the stories. Now, as a cultural leader, he’s passing on the teachings he received, completing the circle.


“These songs and dances are very sacred,” he says, asking guests not to share photos or videos on social media. “When we were given permission to teach these songs and dances, we promised the chiefs and Elders we wouldn’t put it out publicly like that.” 


He pauses. In the space between his words, the snapping of the fire. 


“

W̓álas ǧiáxsix̌a

,” he says, sitting down at the log. The drumming begins.


Patterns in the sand.


In 2008, Opaskwayak Cree scholar Shawn Wilson, said: “When listeners know where the storyteller is coming from and how the story fits into the storyteller’s life, it makes the absorption of the knowledge that much easier.” 


These are not my stories — but I am part of it because I was there.


​’Cúagilákv Jess Housty


invited me, extending the welcome to my seven-year-old daughter. I was invited to witness, given permission to share a story of this place and what it means to many Haíɫzaqv. This place also holds deep meaning for Wuìk̓inux̌v people and the watershed is an area of shared importance. Gently warned about past harms done by well-meaning journalists, I am walking lightly, honouring the trust.


I listen to my recordings while I write: the sound of the waves, ravens squawking, an eagle chittering. A light wind.


Inside, a couple of teenagers add logs to the flames, sending a burst of sparks through the hole in the roof. Outside, a grizzly bear walks the beach with her cubs under sheets of rain while salmon jump from the bay, their silver backs glistening against a grey ocean.


Dixon stands, again holding the talking stick, and speaks in Haíɫzaqvḷa: “Yáu sásṃ, sas húmíɫṇƛa?”


As one, the kids respond with an affirming ‘mm-hmm.’ 


“I want to explain what I just asked the kids,” he says. “I asked the kids: ‘Sas húmíɫṇƛa?’ — ‘Did you hear me?’ [Are you listening?] I asked them that because I want to make sure that they’re listening before we tell the story. At every practice, after every dance, I would ask them that before I tell them the story. I would tell the story behind each dance so the stories get told over and over and over again and hopefully it gets embedded in their heads.”


A Haíɫzaqv youth hands out gifts at the potlatch in λáλix̌sístala.


“This was an old teaching we got from

Thistalalh Ed Martin

, when he was our camp Elder out here,” he continues. “When I was a camper, that’s what he used to say to us. So when I say, ‘Sas húmíɫṇƛa?’ you guys can say ‘mm-hmm,’ to make sure you are all paying attention.”


The sounds of the rain and the fire are one and the song begins again.


Sunset reflections on the ocean.


Haíɫzaqv have always been here, caring for w̓áxv:w̓uísax̌v. W̓áxv:w̓uísax̌v is the land, ocean, submerged land, surface water, groundwater, subsurface and air space as defined by the boundaries of the five tribes which make up the Haíɫzaqv …

author: William D. Hartung
title: The Democrats have a mandate for peace — here are 4 urgent priorities
content:
This article

The Democrats have a mandate for peace — here are 4 urgent priorities

 was originally published by

Waging Nonviolence

.


Voters in the midterm elections dealt a decisive blow to Trump’s war agenda and have created new possibilities for challenging militarism and ending the debacle in Iran. The blue tsunami that swept across the country was driven by

many issues

, including tariffs, corruption and higher prices, but voter discontent was rooted in opposition to the war against Iran and the high fuel costs and inflation that resulted. 


The election outcome presents an opportunity for activists to intensify pressures to end the war, reverse excessive arms spending, restore necessary funding for vital social and environmental priorities, and protect democracy. We need to elect a government that will build the foundations for a forward-looking, progressive foreign policy by expanding essential diplomatic capabilities and restoring U.S. support for global cooperation.


The current electoral realignment can be compared to the dramatic political transformation that occurred in the 2006 midterm elections. That year, the Iraq war was the

decisive issue

 in helping Democrats pick up 31 seats in the U.S. House of Representatives and six in the Senate. Then as now, affordability and immigration were important issues, but the dominant concern was war in the Middle East. As analysts argued at the time, Iraq was the “

Archimedean lever

” that shifted voters toward Democrats. 


But when the new Congress assembled in 2007, Democratic Party leaders equivocated. Speaker of the House Nancy Pelosi and Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid proposed a legislative agenda for the new Congress that ignored Iraq. 


Embed from Getty Images


As Tom Hayden wrote in  “Ending the War in Iraq”, antiwar activists were furious. Constituents bombarded Democratic leaders with demands to prioritize withdrawal from Iraq. Protesters gathered outside Pelosi’s San Francisco home. An estimated 100,000 people marched in an antiwar rally in Washington, D.C. 


Democratic leaders quickly got the message and agreed on a legislative strategy to establish a timetable for withdrawal, which Congress subsequently adopted. 


We may need to exert similar pressures now to ensure that the new Congress fulfills its political mandate to end the Iran war and takes action to reverse other elements of Trump’s dangerous foreign policies. 


The threats to peace have grown significantly in recent years, and they are enormous and multifaceted. An unending, illegal war in Iran and related carnage throughout the Middle East; the arming of repressive regimes, up to and including enabling genocide in Gaza and occupation and ethnic cleansing in Lebanon; the skyrocketing of military-related spending (proposed at more than

$1.5 trillion

 this year) and an accelerating nuclear arms race. All of this is occurring while the Pentagon is

moving

 rapidly towards the deployment of AI-driven weapons systems that can operate without human pilots or human control.


Sign Up for our Newsletter


We’ll send you a weekly email with the latest articles.


The threat or use of force has taken precedence over diplomacy, economic development and peacebuilding programs. The White House has rebuked democratic allies in Canada and Europe while coddling authoritarian regimes in Russia and Saudi Arabia. 


The human, economic and environmental consequences of these militarist policies have been disastrous —

trillions

 of dollars wasted,

hundreds of thousands

 of lives lost and

tens of millions

 of people driven from their homes.      


The pursuit of peace abroad depends on the defense of democracy at home. Legislators must protect democracy by removing obstacles to the exercise of basic rights, including the right to vote, the right of assembly, freedom of speech and an end to discrimination based on race, gender, religion and sexual preference. We need to create an America where every person is cherished, and every person is treated with the dignity they deserve — and then we need to extend that ethos to the rest of the world.


For cooperation, not confrontation


On the foreign policy front, we must demand congressional and executive action on the following major goals:

: Prohibit the use of funds for military hostilities over, in, or off the shores of Iran. Work through the United Nations to reach a comprehensive diplomatic agreement to open …

author: Chad Nelson
title: La Guerra dei Politici contro gli Immigrati è un Diversivo
content:
Di

Chad Nelson

. Originale.

The Political Class’s War on Immigrants is a Diversion

, del 30 gennaio 2015. Traduzione italiana di

Enrico Sanna

.


Al dibattito sulla nomina a ministro della giustizia di Loretta Lynch, il 28 gennaio scorso, i repubblicani erano ansiosi di chiederle fino a che punto avrebbe spinto la sua politica amica di quella categoria di persone che il governo definisce “immigrati clandestini”. In un

confronto di idee

,

Jeff Sessions

, repubblicano, severo in materia di immigrazione, chiedeva chi, secondo la Lynch, ha il diritto di lavorare in America. In particolare, chi ne ha “più diritto”: un immigrato in regola, un cittadino o qualcuno entrato illegalmente nel paese? La Lynch ha saggiamente ignorato le tre ipotesi e ha risposto che vorrebbe che tra i lavoratori americani ci fosse anche chi non ha documenti.


Il modo di porre la domanda di Sessions, e le risposte implicitamente suggerite, dicono molto sul modo di pensare distorto della classe politica. Secondo il pensiero antiimmigrazione bipartitico, il Congresso avrebbe, come nota Sheldon Richman, “il diritto di concedere il permesso di lavorare”. Cosa che purtroppo è diventata legge comune. Oggi, chi ha diritto ad un posto di lavoro lo decidono perlopiù i burocrati di Washington e gli interessi particolari che si giocano così il diritto di

vendere

 i loro servizi in monopolio. Tu pensi di essere libero di svolgere un lavoro che hai scelto, in realtà gli innumerevoli requisiti imposti dallo stato limitano drasticamente quella tua scelta. E se sei abbastanza fortunato da superare tutti gli ostacoli, la possibilità di mantenere l’attività è spesso impedita dalla palude normativa.


I politici confidano in questo enorme potere per tenere al giogo i loro soggetti. Il diritto di dare un lavoro, con tutti gli annessi e connessi che accompagnano il potere di offrire un privilegio, permette alla classe politica di arricchirsi nel modo più efficiente possibile. Quando il lavoro, che si tratti di immigrati irregolari o afroamericani, diventa lavoro in nero, i politici perdono la capacità di intercettarlo e estorcere tributo. Non rispettare quell’intrico fatto di tasse e norme amministrative e professionali, per non dire del sistema di licenze che imbriglia intere professioni, può significare la fame. Si tratta di una struttura falsamente fatta passare per protezione di produttori e consumatori.


I burocrati non temono l’immigrazione clandestina. Temono l’impossibilità di sfruttare il lavoro degli immigrati irregolari. Sessions e gli altri come lui al Congresso nascondono le loro paure dietro la retorica del “noi contro loro”, in un’astuta messinscena al servizio di importanti fini politici. Con questo trucchetto i politici vogliono far credere di essere preoccupati non per la perdita del loro guadagno personale, ma per il “vostro” posto di lavoro, la “vostra” sanità, la “vostra” pensione. A chi è in norma (e paga le tasse) dicono che sta svolgendo un compito patriottico. Non bisogna odiare la scrematura dei loro stipendi, al contrario c’è da esserne fieri perché così si contribuisce al benessere generale. Il nemico è chi lavora senza permesso, chi distrugge il nobile impiego di chi è in norma. “Voi” siete i buoni e “loro” i cattivi. Gli immigrati senza documenti, politicamente impotenti, sono un facile bersaglio di Washington, servono a nascondere la finta isteria dei politici dietro una maschera umanitaria come neanche la peggiore agenzia pubblicitaria potrebbe fare.


Questa isteria, è bene dirlo, è rivolta a: 1) i disoccupati e i precari americani e 2) i pensionati. Il “noi contro loro” si rafforza quando ti dicono che se non si ferma l’immigrazione puoi perdere qualcosa. Chi ha un buon lavoro sicuro ed è relativamente indipendente dallo stato ha poche ragioni per preoccuparsi per qualcosa che riguarda il lavoro e i meccanismi retributivi altrui. Sono i vecchi, molti dei quali immigrati o discendenti di immigrati, che generalmente sono poco tolleranti verso la nuova ondata migratoria dal sud. Questa alterizzazione fa facile presa sui vecchi, i quali difficilmente conoscono gli immigrati e finiscono per credere che la loro presenza porta alla disintegrazione della cultura americana.


È lo stato, vera fonte di insicurezza e rovina culturale, a derubare i lavoratori e le persone oneste. Sondare le ragioni dietro l’interesse dei politici per l’immigrazione, svelarne i veri motivi, e allo stesso tempo riconoscere l’umanità dei nostri …

author: Victoria Valenzuela
title: Incarcerated Los Angeles Youth Fought for the Right to Hug Their Parents — and Won
content:
This story was co-published with


Truthout

.


Mercedes Maradiaga sat across from her 19-year-old son in the Los Padrinos Juvenile Hall in Los Angeles in complete devastation. Her son had at that point been incarcerated at the prison for two years and she had visited him every weekend. But that day in September 2024 was especially hard because it was their first visit since he had been beaten by officers earlier that week in a space in the jail where there were no cameras. The guards had jumped on and kicked him, and he needed surgery for a torn ACL. All she wanted was to give him a hug and reassure him that she was there. However, because of the no-contact visit policies at Los Padrinos, she was unable to give him that comfort.


Even during birthdays and holidays, they weren’t allowed to embrace. The boy endured the jail’s horrible living conditions — including rat infestations and flooded toilets — but couldn’t hug his mom for a moment of escape.


“I couldn’t even let him know I’m here just with the little hug,” Maradiaga said. “It would have meant everything to him. It was sad, and I did that for four years.”


Los Padrinos had

reopened a year earlier

 in 2023, after being shut down in 2019 due to conditions that violated the Board of State and Community Corrections (BSCC) standards, including abuses by staff. Six officers were criminally charged with

assault and child abuse

 for using pepper spray on several teenage girls. Reports

also cited a decreasing youth population

 as a factor for closure, yet staff

claimed to feel “outnumbered.”

 When Los Padrinos closed, youth were shuffled to another facility called Central Juvenile Hall — and then in 2023, that facility was closed down due to similar issues. Los Padrinos reopened, and just months later, the abuses restarted. In 2025,

30 officers were criminally charged

 by the California Attorney General with child endangerment and abuse, conspiracy, and battery for encouraging “gladiator fights” that pit youth against each other.


Olivia Shields, a justice transformation policy coordinator at Urban Peace Institute, described the constant closing and reopening of BSCC facilities as a “cycle of noncompliance.” Shields said the Los Angeles County Probation Department has ultimately failed with these maneuvers to address the core issue: unmet youth needs — which won’t be addressed through incarceration but through coordinated care in the form of individualized, robust support systems and resources.


“Rather than decarcerate these populations of young people and find community-based alternatives or step-downs for as many of them as possible, they basically shift the youth around from facility to facility to avoid noncompliance,” Shields said.


Long before the closing of Los Padrinos in 2019, the facility had a bad reputation among Angelenos. Maradiaga recalled hearing disturbing stories about the facility in the ’80s when she was a kid.


“I think it needs to be shut down,” Maradiaga said. “I think that there needs to be a better way for the youth. I don’t think locking them away from their family is the answer.”


The Appeal in Your Inbox


Subscribe to our newsletters for regular updates, analysis and context straight to your email.


          Sign Up


Barred From Basic Human Contact


When Ilana Parach, executive director and co-founder of

Hoops 4 Justice

, went inside Los Padrinos with a basketball and mentorship program, she quickly learned about what youth were facing inside. She felt it was important to give them a platform to express their needs directly, so she pivoted to working with them on legislation.


“They made a list of specific programs they wanted — resources for their families, reentry support,” Parach said. “At the bottom of that list, they wrote, ‘We want to hug our moms.’”


Incarcerated youth directly told her that one parent who hugged her son during a visit on his birthday then had her visit terminated and future visits suspended for two weeks. She said another youth was incarcerated for three years and had no choice but to watch his mother cry during the visits because she couldn’t hug him.


Contact visitation policies vary across California and are often left at the discretion of correctional officers. Parach said youth and staff both told her that Los Padrinos stopped allowing contact visits after the pandemic. Parach said that during meetings of the board of supervisors, she heard officers citing staffing shortages …

title: In the Crosshairs of the Far-Right Advance : An Update on Anti-Fascists and Anarchists in Greece
content:
Anarchist graffiti from Athens, Greece (2026)


The anarchist movement in Greece faces a new wave of repression. Urged on by the US and its obsession with combatting “far-left extremism,” the Greek state has targeted anti-authoritarians with new legal charges and attacked demonstrations, while fascists carry out street attacks and plot their return to the halls of power. Amidst a landscape of ongoing austerity, terrorism designations, lethal prisons, and ferocious wildfires, anarchists nonetheless continue to forge a combative culture of revolutionary solidarity.


In this article, we present an interview with an anarchist comrade in Athens assessing the current situation among anarchists and anti-fascists in Greece, along with analysis of the US’s role in advancing state repression and fantasies of Western supremacy.


The US and Greece: A Right-Wing Alliance to Defend “The West”


Earlier this month, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio delivered a speech at the Pnyx in Athens. With the historic Acropolis and the Parthenon—that ancient symbol of Western democracy, constructed with slave labor—in the background, he delivered a warning message to Greece’s political and business elite.


“The course we take will determine whether the West maintains its place at the head of the world or resigns itself to a future of atrophy and servitude and decline,” Rubio cautioned. “We will either choose to act now or lose the choice to act at all.” Lamenting how “nationalism became a dirty word,” he called for renewed militarism, praised Christian faith and martyrdom, and announced a new counterterrorism information-sharing program between the two countries. His statements were calculated to reinforce the colonial legacy of Western dominance over the rest of the world, while urging the worst of Greek society to imitate America’s current political trajectory.


US Secretary of State Marco Rubio constructs an elaborate photo op for his defense of nationalism, militarism, and “the West” (October 7, 2026).


The speech came in the wake of a conference Rubio convened in July that aimed to coordinate intensified repression against “far-left extremism.” The following month, the US government imposed a “global terrorist” designation on the Italy-based

Autistici/Inventati (A/I) tech collective

, which operated the free publishing platform NoBlogs.org.


Greece’s right-wing politicians and business leaders benefiting from the country’s endless austerity measures are heeding Rubio’s call to preserve the hubris of the so-called West. Meanwhile, governments are collaborating to escalate repression against any truly revolutionary movements that challenge the world’s current status quo.


Greece’s strategic importance to Western powers is rooted in its symbolic status as the birthplace of “Western Civilization,” as well as its strategic location in the world today. The country offers the US access to four military sites, including a dedicated Navy base in Crete’s Souda Bay. Those with a longer memory have not forgotten how the US supplied napalm to Greece’s fascist forces, who worked with the Nazis during World War II and later with the British and US in a Cold War anti-communist alliance. Fascists dropped American napalm on Greek partisan resistance fighters during the civil war from 1946 to 1949, scorching bodies and charring forests, leaving the countryside scarred to this day.


More recently, the Greek people were pummeled by the 2008 global economic crisis, brought on in part by Wall Street firms such as Goldman Sachs that raked in immense profits while destabilizing the world’s economy and immiserating millions. The US then contributed to the austerity measures imposed on Greece in 2010 by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), leading to years of ferocious resistance to neoliberal capitalism and government complicity.


Today, Greece’s current New Democracy regime upholds

the legacy of the brutal military junta

 of 1967-1974, promoting the image of Greece as a symbol European supremacy as invoked by Rubio. Despite its nationalist rhetoric, the government continues to lick the boots of the US, crushing opposition in the streets and enforcing a never-ending precarity on the majority of Greece’s increasingly exhausted and numb population.

Al llegar a Tribunales se realizó una clase pública de Derecho Constitucional, a cargo del profesor Christian Cao y del abogado constitucionalista Pablo Luis Manilli.


Al concluir el encuentro, los participantes cantaron el himno nacional y dejaron sus velas encendidas frente al Palacio de Justicia.


Antes de las 20.30, cuando la plaza ya estaba vacía, el personal de seguridad de la Corte Suprema las apagó y las retiró.


La Ley de Financiamiento Universitario fue aprobada por el Congreso y ratificada por los dos tercios de ambas cámaras, cuando anularon el veto presidencial inicial. Sin embargo, el Poder Ejecutivo la incumple: al promulgarla en octubre de 2025 mediante el Decreto 759, le introdujo un condicionante ilegal para su ejecución, que el Parlamento estableciera las fuentes de financiamiento y asignara las partidas presupuestarias correspondientes.


Sin embargo, la Justicia declaró inconstitucional el decreto del Ejecutivo que frena la aplicación de la ley y ordenó su cumplimiento inmediato para la actualización salarial de docentes y no docentes, además del refuerzo de becas estudiantiles.


A pesar de los fallos en contra por parte del Fuero Contencioso Administrativo, el Gobierno Nacional presentó recursos de apelación para no aplicar la norma.

author: Ed Wanderley
title: Imposto do pecado: Governo alivia para indústrias e adia proteção popular, alma da reforma
content:
Após quase dois anos de espera, o governo federal enfim definiu as alíquotas do Imposto Seletivo (IS), mas, na prática, adiou a incidência das medidas de proteção à população que inspiraram parte da reforma tributária, ao desidratar o chamado “imposto do pecado”. Além disso, deixou para 2027 a definição do real impacto na indústria, além de colocar a questão, na prática, nas mãos de um Congresso Nacional onde a oposição tem maioria, o que, por enquanto, beneficia indústrias como a das bebidas açucaradas.


Desde janeiro de 2025, quando da publicação da Lei Complementar nº 214, o Ministério da Fazenda tinha que publicar as referências do substitutivo do Imposto sobre Produtos Industrializados (IPI), que será zerado em janeiro. Na reforma tributária, cinco impostos, incluindo o IPI, foram condensados e apenas dois, para unificar as cobranças e modernizar o processo de forma mais transparente – uma demanda que vinha sendo discutida há três décadas. A

Medida Provisória 1.399/26

 foi finalmente publicada nesta quarta-feira (4) e trouxe uma proposta de neutralidade fiscal provisória – em outras palavras, não é agora que as indústrias vão sofrer qualquer baque.


Gradativamente, os impostos no país estão sendo adequados para existirem apenas três. Os dois que afetam todos os setores já estão desenhados são o IBS, Imposto sobre Bens e Serviços (que reúne o que antes eram ICMS e ISS) e a CBS, Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (unificando PIS, Cofins e IPI).


O último e mais polêmico elemento dessa tríade é o IS, que reúne indústrias cujos produtos representam custos sociais, ambientais ou à saúde pública – daí o nome “imposto do pecado”. Por que cigarros e refrigerantes estão lá? Porque causam doenças que aumentam a despesa com o Sistema Único de Saúde. Por que incluir veículos automotores? Dado a emissão de CO² e a necessidade de investir em transportes coletivos. E por aí vai.


O que o imposto do pecado muda no seu cotidiano? O exemplo máximo é o cigarro. Essa é uma indústria que mantém público mesmo tendo publicidade proibida e fumo em locais públicos restrito há anos. De toda forma, os números de fumantes caíram. Em outras palavras, o poder público dificulta o acesso. Você continua tendo liberdade para fumar, desde que arque com os custos disso. No caso da reforma tributária, esse custo incide sobre o que beneficia pouca gente e/ou prejudica milhares todos os anos.


A inspiração central do dispositivo é o de desincentivar o consumo de produtos que gerem custos elevados ou sejam prejudiciais ao próprio consumidor, dificultando o seu acesso, logo, o protegendo. Há quem discorde – e apresente o argumento da liberdade de escolha –, especialmente

as próprias indústrias

, mas o IS passou e foi aprovado.


“Ele [o IS] vai incidir sobre exclusivamente sobre bebida alcoólica, refrigerante, bebida açucarada, tabaco, carro, embarcação. Então, são alguns poucos itens. Com o fim do IPI para a indústria como um todo, a indústria fica desonerada, e a gente passa a ter o imposto seletivo sobre esses poucos setores”, disse o ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, em entrevista coletiva nesta quinta (5).


A definição do imposto do pecado era bastante esperada porque definiria o nível de desestímulo aos produtos listados e poderia ajustar a versão final da reforma pelo legislativo, cuja influência do lobby industrial criou distorções tributárias, como a baixa distinção entre veículos automotores entre os de combustão e elétricos ou de produtos de consumo, como os refrigerantes produzidos na Zona Franca de Manaus, que poderiam pagar menos impostos que a água mineral, como

já mostrou a

Agência Pública

.


Elas por elas?


Mas o que fez, na prática, o governo agora? Publicou uma lista com alíquotas baixas, para apenas equiparar o que a maior parte das indústrias já pagavam com o IPI, que será zerado a partir de janeiro e jogou o início da progressão tributária apenas para 2028. Os refrigerantes, por exemplo, ficaram limitados a 2,6% – na prática, não haverá progressão das taxas cobradas em 2027. Durigan, no entanto, negou adiar os efeitos da reforma tributária.


Para o cientista político e coordenador de advocacy da ACT Promoção da Saúde Marcello Baird, a alíquota de 2,6% sobre bebidas açucaradas iguala o mesmo

patamar de tributação já praticado

 hoje sobre a indústria, o que beneficia os fabricantes desses produtos nocivos e a gente não consegue ter os impactos na redução de adoecimentos e mortes na população, em especial a mais …

author: Andrés
title: Patricia Walsh deja abierto el camino para construir otro futuro
content:
Patricia Walsh en su escuela primaria


Llevaba más de una semana internada. La habían operado de un pulmón. Ayer a la mañana supe que había muerto. Patricia Walsh fue periodista, diputada, legisladora, dos veces candidata a presidente. Un cuadro político de peso que luchó por los derechos humanos y bregó todo lo que pudo por la unidad de la izquierda. «Bajaba a la calle a pelearse con la policía que estaba asediando a un pibito vendedor de paltas.» me relató

su yerno

hace unas horas, en el velorio. «

Ni un paso atrás, era su lema y tal cual, hasta el último día» agregó. «Me pidió disculpas por mover unas plantas que le había regalado, me dijo la última vez que estuve en su casa, es fea, no me gusta pero la salvé porque la habían tirado en un volquete, ¿podés creer?.», me contó el hermano del yerno. Lucidez y ternura, coraje y tosudez fueron las palabras que le arrancaron lágrimas a los y las presentes en el salón blanco del Congrrso, donde fue velada esta tarde. Su

muerte nos toma por sorpresa, cuando el futuro todavía d

ura para siempre. Por Andrés Manrique, ANRed.


No imaginé que podía pasar esto. Pocas veces estuve cerca. Una tarde la iba a conocer, me pondría a conversar con ella. La muerte es un hecho para después. Y la de Patricia Walsh me deja con la culpa de poder haberlo hecho mucho mejor. Ojalá fuera culpa solamente, porque es más. Una mezcla de culpa e impotencia que busco aplastar con rabia para que no me gane la frustración.


¿Cómo ser la hermana de una mujer a la que el Estado persiguió hasta su muerte? ¿Cómo tolerar la figura de un padre, Rodolfo Walsh, cuadro, escritor y periodista fundamental de la historia Argentina, también asesinado y desaparecido por el aparato represivo del Estado?


Myriam Bregman despide a su colega y amiga íntima


¿Qué decía Patricia de la tibieza para la oposición de nuestra época? ¿Cómo continuaba sus luchas dentro de este generalizado clima de apatía? ¿Cómo hacer para dejar de administrar la miseria y pasar a la delantera? La de veces que se  habrá hecho estas preguntas desde sus variados roles y puestos políticos.


Patricia vivió la muerte de su hermana, Victoria. Leyó la carta que su padre Rodolfo escribió para ella al enterarse de su muerte. Vivió la muerte y desaparición de su padre. Leyó la carta que había dejado Rodolfo a la Junta Militar poco después de que las Fuerzas Armadas emboscaran a Victoria. Nunca recuperó el cuerpo del padre.


Patricia, además de referente de izquierda, legisladora, diputada, dos veces candidata a presidente. Además de hija y hermana, fue mamá y abuela. Compañera y suegra. Su entorno la quiso, la admiró y la admira. Su hija la recuerda con amor y humor negro: «Si no me hago problema, ¿que hago?», cuenta que decía. Sus compañeras se acuerdan con sentido orgullo de ella.


Patricia llenó de cariño y capricho a sus nietos. Peleó con las herramientas de la época. Fue autora y propulsora de la nulidad de las leyes de Obediencia Debida y Punto Final cuando todo el mundo le decía que una ley no podía anularse, contó Bregman emocionada hasta las lágrimas. Avanzó a fondo contra los militares culpables por delitos de lesa humanidad. En 2005, la Corte declaró la inconstitucionalidad de las normas. Desde entonces, más de 1250 represores fueron condenados. Pero ella murió sin poder enterrar a su padre.


Textos de su nieta dedicados a Patricia Walsh


Fue incansable militante de los derechos humanos, participó de Proyecto Sur y del MST. Buscó y persiguió hasta el último día a los asesinos de su hermana. Quería que le devolvieran la casa de San Vicente, en la que su padre se había recluido clandestinamente. Esa casa que los militares habían bombardeado, para luego cedérsela a una familia de policías. Por esas vueltas que tiene la justicia en este país, con sus demoras y atropellos, la expropiación para declararla sitio de memoria se firmó ayer mismo (05/11/26). Patricia tampoco llegó a conocer la noticia.


Al día de su muerte seguía detrás de los juicios de la calle Corro, donde había resistido su hermana María Victoria Walsh con cuatro compañeros de la dirección política de Montoneros, a 150 militares con armas pesadas, un tanque y un helicóptero. En mayo de este año había estado declarando en Comodoro Py contra el Estado, con una lucidez que te invito a ver aquí.

Así declaró ella el pasado 19 de mayo de este año.


“Pudo haber elegido otros caminos sin ser deshonrosos, pero el que eligió era el más justo, el más generoso, el más razonado …

author: Darío Aranda
title: La salud no es lo primero: en Argentina se utilizan 167 agrotóxicos prohibidos en otros países
content:
Por Javier Souza Casadinho*


Los plaguicidas autorizados en Argentina que están prohibidos o no autorizados en otros países alcanzan la cifra de 167 productos, y 35 de ellos son Plaguicidas Altamente Peligrosos (PAP) según los criterios establecidos por la FAO (organismo de Naciones Unidas para la agricultura y la alimentación) y la Organización Mundial de la Salud (OMS). Entre las

empresas responsables sobresalen


Syngenta, Bayer, Adama, Corteva y Atanor

. En Argentina, cada año, su utilizan 580 millones de litros de venenos del agro.


Incremento en el uso de plaguicidas


El

modelo productivo agrícola en la Argentina

 ha experimentado una profunda transformación en las últimas décadas, caracterizada por la expansión de la frontera agropecuaria y la adopción consolidada de paquetes tecnológicos dependientes de fertilizantes sintéticos y agroquímicos, mal denominados "fitosanitarios".


En este contexto cobran especial relevancia los Plaguicidas Altamente Peligrosos (PAP). En Argentina, la problemática adquiere dimensiones críticas debido a los volúmenes de aplicación y a la cercanía de las zonas de cultivo con núcleos poblacionales. Los casos más frecuentes y documentados de exposición e impacto ambiental, que en ocasiones derivan en

demandas judiciales

, involucran a principios activos de amplio uso

como el glifosato, el paraquat, la atrazina, el 2,4-D y la cipermetrina

.


Lejos de limitarse a un único sector, estas sustancias se emplean de manera intensiva y extensiva en distintas matrices productivas que configuran el mapa productivo del país, abarcando

desde la agricultura extensiva de cereales y oleaginosas hasta economí

as regionales como el cultivo de tabaco y la horticultura

. Un informe del Instituto Nacional de Tecnología Agropecuaria (INTA) señala que “la Argentina se caracteriza por tener un importante consumo anual de productos fitosanitarios, los cuales son de origen nacional por síntesis o formulación y muchos son importados. En los 36 millones de hectáreas cultivadas,

se utilizan 230 millones de litros de herbicidas y 350 millones de litros de otros productos

 fitosanitarios”.


Una comparación entre la superficie sembrada de cereales y oleaginosas y el consumo de plaguicidas desde 1990 hasta la actualidad muestra que el aumento en el uso de plaguicidas ha sido muy superior al incremento en la superficie cultivada. En las últimas tres décadas, la superficie sembrada con cereales y oleaginosas creció de 19.000.000 de hectáreas en 1990 a 41.182.000 hectáreas en 2023, lo que representa un aumento del 117 por ciento. En el mismo período, la producción pasó de 38.200.000 toneladas a 140.893.000 toneladas, un incremento del 269 por ciento.


Entre 1990 y 2022, el uso de plaguicidas en Argentina se incrementó de manera exponencial: pasó de 35 millones a 580 millones de kg/litros, lo que representa un aumento del 1.657 por ciento.


Existen diversos factores de índole económica, productiva y ambiental que pueden incidir en el incremento en la utilización de plaguicidas tales como: aumento de las especies de hierbas resistentes a herbicidas, mayor presión de los patógenos (hongos y bacterias)

,

 incremento en la superficie agrícola de alimentos y de biocombustibles, baja de aranceles a la importación de determinados principios activos precursores de plaguicidas, reducción en el precio de ingredientes activos cuyas patentes han caducado, alta demanda de insumos por parte de la horticultura y fruticultura para mantener la calidad formal de los productos, el

cambio climático

 junto a modificaciones en las legislaciones que regulan el registro, uso y comercialización de estos insumos.


Foto: Nicolás Mendiola – Greenpeace


Los Plaguicidas Altamente Peligrosos (PAP)


Según el Código de Conducta sobre Manejo de Plaguicidas (adoptado por la FAO y la OMS en 2013) y de las Guías sobre PAP, los Plaguicidas Altamente Peligrosos pueden definirse como:


Los que presentan niveles particularmente altos de peligro agudo o crónico para la salud o el ambiente, conforme a los sistemas de clasificación aceptados a nivel internacional, como los de la OMS o del SGA (Sistema Globalmente Armonizado).


Por estar incluidos en acuerdos o convenios jurídicamente vinculantes.


Aquellos que aparecen como causantes de daño grave o irreversible a la salud humana o al ambiente, en las condiciones de uso en un país, pueden ser considerados y tratados como altamente peligrosos.


Desde la

Red Internacional de Acción …

author: La Zarzamora
title: La Chilean Horror Story, nuevas temporadas
content:
El mal sigue aquí. 56 engendros, extorsionadores de mujeres, violadores, pedófilos y torturadores de la DINA-CNI, responsables de marcar a sus víctimas con cuchillos de combate, amarrarlos a rieles y tirarlos vivos al mar, de violar y abusar sexualmente, fueron liberados por la Kasta gobernante y están listos para reincidir.

En este thriller maldito, la Kasta está siendo coherente con sus siniestras convicciones y su maligna esencia blancona. Es la Chilean Horror Story, en la que calzan perfecto: dictadura, “Colonia Dignidad”, Paul Schäfer, Spiniak, “los coroneles” de la derecha, los decretos de libertad a criminales, y el alienado proyecto de ley de la escalofriante Vanessa Kaiser contra las víctimas.

Son crímenes inmortales de la continuación del horror político de “los nuevos padres fundadores” de los años 70 y 80, coordinados por el funesto subsecretario general de Pinochet, Jovino Novoa, el psicópata serial Paul Shäfer y los demonios de la DINA-CNI, que usaban como cuartel general de violaciones y otras torturas, la pedófila “Colonia Dignidad”.

No es casual que 20 años más tarde, en 2002, se inaugurara el siglo XXI con el sacrificio de niños y niñas de clases pobres, una nueva temporada de horror pedófilo por el mismo protagonista de la anterior, Jovino Novoa, esta vez acompañado por los libertinos vejadores Carlos Bombal de la Unión Demócrata Independiente y Nelson Ávila del Partido Radical; y dirigidos por el escatófilo Spiniak (pedófilo invitado).

El sacrificio fue quitada de cartelera informándose que Novoa, Bombal y Avila habrían sido “falsamente” acusados. Sin embargo, fue una generación que también en los años 90 albergó demonios torturadores y pedófilos organizados en el estado, especialmente los perturbados “Amigos de la Colonia Dignidad”. Algunos ya están muertos vivos como el asesinado, pero no menos maligno, ideólogo de la dictadura Jaime Guzmán; también, los “malditos Sergios”: dos ministros del interior de Pinochet, Sergio Onofre Jarpa y Sergio Fernández, y el grotesco delegado en la ONU, Sergio Diez. Y siguen vivos muchos “vampiros amigos” del Paul Schäfer” que traspasan siglos: Hernán Larraín Fernández, ministro de justicia y “derechos humanos” del piñerismo2 junto al conspirador Andrés Chadwick Piñera, ministro del interior de la misma masacre, el piñerismo2, ambos responsables de mutilaciones y violaciones a manifestantes del estallido.

Chadwick además, integra los “coroneles”, pilares del poder de los fundadores de la derecha, junto a Juan Antonio Coloma, quien fuese base “juvenil” de la dictadura, y también junto a Pablo Longueira, el mismo que habla con espectros. No hay que olvidar a las estrellas femeninas como la implacable -ya desaparecida- Mónica Madariaga, ministra de justicia y de educación de la dictadura, que dio el visto bueno a la constitución de Pinochet junto a Guzmán, ni debemos dejar fuera a la ambiciosa -y muy viva- Evelyn Matthei, reciente ex candidata presidencial, candidateándose otra vez, y defensora -solapada- de la criminal junta de gobierno, del golpe de estado y de la dictadura en que participó su padre. Todas y todos son villanos políticos, fríos y calculadores, además de grandes amigos de la pedófila “Colonia Dignidad” de Schäfer.

Nueva temporada: “La liberación”

La línea de la historia chilena del horror que continúan los padres fundadores-Generación Z, es innegable. En este inolvidable octubre 2026 de la Kasta, Fernando Rabat Celis, ministro de Justicia, Luis Silva Irarrazaval, vicepresidente del partido republicano y ahora ex subsecretario de Justicia, y Pablo Mira Hurtado, subsecretario subrogante, firmaron los decretos de liberación de sus engendros y mintieron diciendo que estaban “obligados” por una doctrina inexistente de la Corte Suprema, misma institución judicial que, apurada, mediante un fallo, los desmintió.

Ninguno de los criminales liberados por ellos había presentado individualmente un recurso de amparo porque los pedófilos están informados de sus derechos. La opción de salir en libertad se terminó en 2022 cuando Piñera2, el mismo que gobernó con los “amigos de la Colonia” pedófila, los excluyó, justo a ellos, pero no a los violadores en general, en su Ley N°21.421.

Antes del piñerismo2, habiendo tantas “comisiones de género”en los partidos de la Concertación,los pedófilos no habían sido excluidos de las rebajas de condenas, y los violadores de mujeres, menos. La ley anterior de rebajas de condenas, la N°19.856 de 2003, fue enviada por …

author: Administrador
title: Wir werden gehen. Ob sie es wollen oder nicht, wir werden gehen.  Denuncia der Gemeinschaftlichen Regierung der zwölf zapatistischen Caracoles.
content:
Musik: »Poblanas« der Gruppe La Surada. Sie sind Teil der Jarana-Gitarrist*innen (mehr als 40 Musiker*innen, die gemeinschaftlich spielen), welche beim »Konzert für eine Umarmung« im Metroplitan-Theater [in Mexiko-Stadt] am 18. November teilnehmen, wo auch Meme, Kevin Kaarl, Vivir Quintana, Ely Guerra und die Caifanes auftreten werden – um so die Kohle für den Transport der Familien Sucherinnen zusammenzubringen. Ticketmaster wird ebenfalls seine Gebühren für diesen Zweck übergeben. Aufnahmen, Zusammenstellung, Produktion: Terci@s Compas Zapatistas.

Wir werden gehen. Ob sie es wollen oder nicht, wir werden gehen. Denuncia der Gemeinschaftlichen Regierung der zwölf zapatistischen Caracoles.

Compañeras, Compañeros und Compañeroas.

Schwestern*Brüder, Schwestern und Brüder.

Dieses Jahr im Juli haben wir unsere Absicht bekanntgegeben, nach Mexiko-Stadt zu reisen, um uns mit den Gruppen, Kollektiven oder Gruppenlosen der Familien Sucherinnen zu treffen. Nicht für Vollversammlungen, nicht um neue Netzwerke und Koordinierungen zu schaffen, sondern um ihrer Geschichte und der Geschichte ihrer Vermissten zuzuhören: Gruppe für Gruppe, Familie für Familie. Und auch, wenn sie es akzeptieren, um ihnen eine Umarmung zu geben, welche die zapatistischen Gemeinschaften senden.

Wir haben Mexiko-Stadt als zentralen Ort benannt, um für Euch, die Familien mit Vermissten, Erschöpfung und Kosten zu vermeiden, die es bedeuten würde, bis zum zapatistischen Gebiet zu reisen.

Seitdem [der Ankündigung der Reise nach Mexiko-Stadt] haben die Bundesregierung, die Bundesstaatenregierung von Chiapas sowie verschiedene Landkreis-Regierungen eine Serie von Aktionen umgesetzt, die nicht nur die Menschenrechte verletzen (nicht nur die der Zapatistas, sondern auch der Partei-Anhänger*innen und Parteilosen), sie widersprechen auch der Rede von Frieden, Glücklichsein und Wohlergehen, welche die da oben predigen.

Wir geben Euch jetzt die Details; jedoch möchten wir Euch zuvor informieren: Diese Provokationen zwingen uns nicht, die Reise zu Ende November, den Aufenthalt in Mexiko-Stadt im Dezember sowie der ersten Januar-Woche, die sich konkretisierenden Besuche in Oaxaca, Veracruz, Puebla, Jalisco und Querétaro während dieses Zeitraums, abzusagen.

Somit müssen die da oben, auf Landes-, Bundesstaaten- und Landkreis-Ebenen begreifen, dass wir nach Mexiko-Stadt gehen werden (gut möglich, dass eine*r von uns bereits dort ist). Wir werden uns mit den Familien Sucherinnen, die das wollen und können, in Mexiko-Stadt, in Veracruz, Puebla, Jalisco, Oaxaca und Querétaro treffen. Wir werden der Geschichte ihres Schmerzes zuhören; wir werden sie umarmen; wir werden ihr Wort in unseren Web-Taschen [morraletas] bewahren; wir werden bei der Rückkehr ihre Geschichten mitbringen und werden sie bewahren, damit nicht das Vergessen und die Gleichgültigkeit sie beflecken.

Jegliche Provokation wird mit Entschiedenheit und Mobilisierung beantwortet werden. Sie müssen entscheiden, ob sie diese Tatsache akzeptieren und sich damit abfinden, dass wir unser Wort erfüllen werden. Oder sie können mit ihren Stumpfsinnigkeiten weiter fortfahren (darin sind das gesamte Kabinett der Bundesregierung, der Bundesstaatenregierung sowie Landkreis-Präsidenten involviert) – und [damit] unserer Initiative einen anderen Charakter geben. Wir wollen keinen Aufruhr machen, wir können es jedoch.

1.- Im Ejido La Culebra, offizieller Landkreis Ocosingo (regiert von der PVEM, der Grünen Ökologischen Partei Mexikos) fahren sie fort, Familien der [zapatistischen] Unterstützungsbasen zu schikanieren, zu bedrohen und einzuknasten. Diejenigen, die provozieren sind Mitglieder des Kartells von Mario Delgado, Staatsminister für öffentliche Bildung. Der Haupt-Auftragskiller ist Eusebio Cruz Ruiz, der sich als Lehrer präsentiert und sagt, er erhält von Mario Delgado direkte Anordnungen.

Nun haben sie einen Schritt weiter getan: Sie verbieten allen, in den Kooperativ-Laden der Compas zu gehen, ansonsten droht Gefängnisstrafe. Und auch jeder*jede Anwohner*in des Ejido und der nahen Gemeinden, welcher*welche die Gemeinschaftsklinik aufsucht (die Zapatistas, Partei-Anhänger*innen sowie Parteilose versorgt), wird eingesperrt und erhält eine Geldstrafe. Wer nicht gehorcht, wird inhaftiert.

Wir erfinden das nicht. Hier ist der Beweis (darauf klicken, um die beiden Fotos zu vergrößern):

author: Rizomatica
title: Maestras en Isla Lemuy: un podcast para reconocer los aportes de las maestras rurales en la educación pública de Puqueldón
content:
El podcast presenta un recorrido histórico a través de seis capítulos donde se entrelazan las memorias de maestras normalistas, universitarias, jubiladas y en ejercicio.


Durante el año 2026, la comuna de Puqueldón ubicada en Isla Lemuy, Archipiélago de Chiloé, experimenta dos hitos históricos en materia de Educación Pública. Por un lado, el Liceo Puqueldón realizará la ceremonia de egreso de la primera generación de 4to medio, saldando una brecha de desigualdades que, hasta el año 2023, posicionaba a Puqueldón como la única comuna de la Región de Los Lagos carente de enseñanza media. Por otro lado, la Escuela San Juan de Lincay, con una trayectoria de 99 años, despedirá a los únicos dos estudiantes que cursan 6to básico y cerrará sus puertas a finales del año.


Estos dos acontecimientos constituyeron una motivación para que Revista Territorio Sur elaborara una propuesta al Fondo de Fomento de Medios de Comunicación Social de la SEGEGOB – Los Lagos. De esa manera, fue posible obtener financiamiento para ejecutar la iniciativa de conversar con seis maestras de Isla Lemuy; dos maestras normalistas (jubiladas) que ejercieron sus funciones como profesoras en la Escuela Puqueldón (actual Liceo Puqueldón), dos maestras universitarias (jubiladas) que ejercieron funciones en la Escuela Rural de Detif, Chulchuy, Aldachildo y Puqueldón y, finalmente, dos maestras universitarias (en ejercicio) que cumplen labores en la Escuela Rural Santa Rosa de Liucura y San Juan de Lincay.


A través de los seis episodios del podcast se logran apreciar elementos característicos de distintas épocas, describiendo aspectos como por ejemplo: conectividad, transporte, tecnologías, relaciones sociales y comunitarias entre las escuelas y las familias de sectores rurales, así como también, las transformaciones que experimentaron las escuelas públicas y rurales a lo largo de la historia. El podcast recorre episodios de la vida antigua, desde la década del 70 hasta la actualidad, donde por un lado se reconocen los aportes de la enseñanza media y por otro lado se lamenta el cierre de escuelas por falta de matrícula.


Finalmente, el podcast permite reflexionar sobre los desafíos actuales que presenta la Educación Pública y a su vez, proyecta futuras oportunidades para una educación con perspectiva e identidad territorial.

author: Kodao Productions
title: IBON to Marcos: Explain worst inflation rate in 18 years
content:
IBON Foundation executive director Sonny Africa dared the Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to explain why the Philippines has the highest inflation rate in Southeast Asia.


Reacting to Malacañang’s claim Marcos is “doing something” about soaring prices of commodities, Africa said the president’s inaction is behind the people’s worst poverty and hunger in decades.


“It’s because Malacañang’s ‘doing something’ is just enough for a press release, and far less than what’s needed and what it can do,” Africa said.


The Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) announced his week that the country’s inflation rate worsened further in October at 7.8 per cent, up from September’s 7.2 per cent.


Marcos in late September assured his government is doing everything it can to keep the economy stable despite heavy pressures from external factors, , including rising global oil prices.


“Do not take it with alarm. Don’t panic,” Marcos said in September.


All images from Africa’s Facebook post.


But Africa asked if Malacañang doing enough, reminding government that the poorest and most vulnerable are ever the ones hit the worst.


“But then these figures probably really are just numbers and nothing to panic about for those like the president, his Cabinet, the economic managers, BSP officials, and trapo allies. It’s a little different if you’re earning millions of pesos annually, and have wealth running into the billions,” he said.


Marcos and wife Liza Araneta are reportedly worth nearly P1.5 billion.


Try living on P96 a day


The Kilusang Magbubukid ng Pilipinas (KMP), meanwhile, challenged Marcos and fellow officials to live on P96 a day, the poverty threshold set by government.


The group said that officials should experience firsthand what it is like to make ends meet with the very amount they deem sufficient to keep a Filipino from being classified as poor. “Let them try to cover food, transportation, and other essential needs with just P96 before claiming that it is sufficient for survival,” KMP said.


The group said government’s P14,634 per month threshold is far removed from IBON Foundation estimate that a five-member family requires P1,277 per day to afford a decent standard of living .


KMP cited that food inflation has hit 6.4%, while rice inflation has reached 20.7%, impacting poor families by as much as 9.4 per cent food inflation rate.


“The Filipino masses are forced to tighten their belts, while those in power live in comfort. Our challenge to Marcos and his officials is this: Try living on P96 a day, without dipping into your massive salaries, allowances, and privileges. Let’s see if you can endure the kind of life you impose upon the poor,” said KMP chairperson Danilo Ramos. #

(Raymund B. Villanueva)

author: Unknown
title: Bafel Talabani: We are withdrawing from this government
content:
The Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) Executive Council convened with the participation of its President, Bafel Talabani. Following the meeting, Talabani released a video statement in which he commented on political developments in the Kurdistan Region and the process of forming a government.


Talabani stated that they had held several meetings with officials in Erbil (Hewlêr), but despite progress in the discussions, no agreement had been reached and parliament had been unable to convene. “On every occasion, progress was made in the discussions, but no results were achieved, and parliament could not convene. It has been demonstrated that the KDP does not know how to govern. We had previously warned that such a situation would arise. We do not recognise this session,” Talabani said.


‘We are withdrawing from this government’


Stating that the PUK Executive Council had authorised him to make the decision, Talabani announced the party's withdrawal from the government in the following terms: “Today, the PUK Executive Council authorised me, and we declare that we do not recognise this session. This government has failed. Therefore, our decision is to withdraw from this government. We are prepared to make any sacrifice. We are concerned with resolving the Rojava issue, the peace process, and our brothers and sisters in Rojhilat.”


‘Do not intimidate the people’


Addressing the KDP, Talabani called on the party to abandon any attempts to use force, saying: “I have a message for you: you have made an unjust decision. I am telling you, do not intimidate the people. Abandon your attempts to use force. We do not recognise this session or the government that will be formed as a result of it. I ask that you do not force us to take action in response. Whatever position you appoint in Erbil, we will appoint an equivalent position in Sulaymaniyah.”

title: Bernie Sanders: Winning the Midterms Is Not Enough. Here’s What We Must Do
content:
The American people understand that the economy today is rigged and that we cannot continue the ‘same old, same old’ establishment politics and establishment policies.


 


Bernie Sanders


Nov 05, 2026


Common Dreams


 


On Tuesday, Trump told us to vote as if he were on the ballot. And that is exactly what the American people did.


 


Together, we stood up to

authoritarianism

 and a president who does not believe in the Constitution or the

rule of law

. And we won.


 


With Democratic control over the Senate and the House, we will now—finally—be able to hold

Donald Trump

 accountable.


 


The American people have had enough. They are demanding real change and bold policies that will dramatically improve their lives.


 


That is a big deal. But as important as it is, it is not enough. We have got to do more.


 


Whether we like it or not, we are living in an unprecedented moment in American history where our country faces extraordinary crises. We cannot and must not run away from them when Democrats assume power in January.


 


These crises must be dealt with.


 


It is no secret that in the

United States

 and all over the world, people are giving up on

democracy

. Now, why is that?


 


And the answer is that—all over the world, not just in America—working families are struggling to put food on the table and pay for basic necessities while the very richest people become much richer. And, throughout our country and in many other countries, ordinary people are saying, ‘Does their government even know that they exist?’ Or are elected officials too busy worrying about the needs of the rich and the powerful?


 


This is an American issue, but, in fact, an international issue.


 


And in my view, the American people have had enough. They are demanding real change and bold policies that will dramatically improve their lives.


 


In the richest country on Earth, the American people want a government that stands for working families, not billionaire campaign contributors. And that is not just

Bernie Sanders

 talking.


 


According to a recent AP poll, 80% of registered voters want either “complete and total upheaval” or “substantial change” in how this country is run. And that includes 97% of Democrats, 90% of independents, and 58% of

Republicans

.


 


In other words, the American people understand that the economy today is rigged and that we cannot continue the ‘same old, same old’ establishment politics and establishment policies.


 


The American people want change. Real change. And the midterm election confirms just that.


 


Let me give you some examples of what I mean and the issues that we have got to deal with.


 


In our country today, income and

wealth inequality

 has reached unprecedented levels. The top 1% now owns more wealth than the bottom 93%. One man,

Elon Musk

, owns more wealth than the bottom 53% of American households. In my view, that is insane. And I think that’s how most Americans feel.


 


Democrats, when they gain control, in January, of the House and the Senate, cannot ignore this grotesque

inequality

. We must take on the greed of the very, very rich and their incredible wealth.


 


We must enact a 5% wealth tax on billionaires so that we can provide every working-class family in the country, a family of four, with a $12,000 direct payment.


 


And that means a Democratic Congress must pass a wealth tax on billionaires.


 


At a time when billionaires pay a lower effective tax rate than truck drivers or nurses, we must enact a 5% wealth tax on billionaires so that we can provide every working-class family in the country, a family of four, with a $12,000 direct payment. In other words, if you’re a working-class family of four, that’s $3,000 for every man, woman, and child—$12,000.


 


Furthermore, with that tax on billionaires, we can build 7 million units of low-income and

affordable housing

, we can make public colleges and universities tuition-free, and we can provide universal free child care for 13 million

children

. That is what a wealth tax on billionaires can do.


 


But taxing the oligarchs means more than just taking on their wealth.

It means ending their stranglehold over our political system.


 


Elon Musk

 and his billionaire friends have poured a record-breaking $2 billion into the recent election. That is absurd.


 


The American people want Congress to overturn

Citizens United

, abolish

super PACs …

author: Jian Sanz
title: Art exhibit vs Pax Silica as visualizing resistance
content:
As the Marcos Jr. administration flexes the upcoming visit of U.S. President Donald Trump for the ASEAN summit, Filipino artists decide to use art to take a stand.

Cultural group Sama-samang Artista para sa Kilusang Agraryo (SAKA) and the Artists Unite Against Pax Silica (AUPAX) network launched “ALL CAPS: Art, Land, and Labor” at the Sampaguita Project in Quezon City. The anti-Pax Silica and anti-imperialist exhibit which ran from September 6 to September 11 challenged the U.S.-led initiative that threatens to displace around 20,000 Aeta in Tarlac to clear land for technology and artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure hubs.

Featuring works from member creators and independent cultural workers, the exhibit exposed the deadly cost of imperialist plunder and expansion disguised as technological progress.

What began as a localized digital campaign transformed into a broader physical movement. Ivan Pasion of SAKA and convenor for AUPAX said that the exhibit started as an online art protest by the Bulacan Collective and SAKA. “We noticed so many artists joined because AI itself is already a very polarizing topic. But beyond that, it is a much wider issue.”

Pasion said that during SAKA’s general assembly, they realized the massive reach of the protest and how deeply artists were affected. They saw this as an opportunity to build the ALL CAPS exhibit and integrate artists into a broader societal movement.

For Pasion, standing against Pax Silica is inseparable from the struggle against foreign domination. “Historically, artists have always played a huge role in society. We often view art as a mirror reflecting truth, but we cannot remain passive observers of history—we must be active participants.” Pasion said in an interview with Bulatlat.

He connected this to the idea that generative AI is already a uniting issue for artists as resisting Pax Silica is not an isolated issue but an ongoing fight against imperialism. “Even if you claim your art isn’t political, everything down to your subjects and materials is inherently political.”

Artist for Just Peace (AFJP) member Kart Mabato, one of the exhibit artists, brought this critique into physical form through visual symbolism, as expressed in an interview with Bulatlat. His featured piece titled “Bonk” focuses on the grotesque realities of U.S. hegemony disguised as tech expansion.

“In my artwork, I depicted a modernized, suit-wearing Uncle Sam carrying a scroll that lays out the destruction expected in the Philippines—land grabbing, labor exploitation, and environmental degradation. Opposite him, a giant hand holding a sledgehammer strikes Uncle Sam’s head, symbolizing the Filipino workforce resisting Pax Silica,” Mabato said.

When asked about the title of his artwork, Mabato said that it refers to the sound made when hitting metal. “As artists, our works are reflections of our ideology shaped by social conditions. We don’t just draw for the sake of drawing; we draw with a purpose—and at this point, that purpose is fighting back against U.S. land grabbing and imperialism.”

Both artists stressed that individual creation is insufficient when dismantling a rotten system. For them, collective organization remains the primary key to turning art into a force capable of dismantling broken systems.

“Whenever I lead educational discussions on art and society, I challenge the common belief that art is merely a mirror reflecting reality. Art can also be a hammer—an active instrument to reconfigure, reform, and revolutionize societal ills,” Pasion said. “We will only reach a point where we can truly live off our craft if we take action now to critique these ills. Simply voting isn’t enough when the framework itself is broken; art is a vital component in driving cultural revolution.”

Mabato urged unorganized creators to join collective fronts. “To fellow artists who are unorganized or working independently: it is crucial to organize. Being in a collective gives you comrades and creates a far greater impact against these issues.”

“The government claims Pax Silica displaces no one and promotes national progress. But no innovation exists in a nation where people, especially Aeta communities and farmers, are exploited,” Pasion said. (DAA)

title: Miss X Versus Late Rekha Waghmare: The Selective Outrage of Telangana Civil Society
content:
In Telangana, the term “civil society” evokes images of principled activism: women’s groups marching for justice, human rights organisations amplifying marginalised voices, and political parties channelling public anger into demands for accountability. Yet this activism reveals a troubling selectivity when the victim belongs to a Scheduled Caste (SC) community, especially a vulnerable migrant labourer. The stark contrast between the high-profile handling of the Miss X POCSO case and the alleged gang-rape and murder of Late Rekha Waghmare exposes what can only be described as caste-driven hypocrisy. Telangana’s so-called civil society functions less as a beacon of universal justice and more as a caste society indifferent, even complicit, when atrocities target SC “untouchable” communities.

The Miss X Case: Swift Action, Political Storm, and Current Legal Position

In May 2026, Bandi Sai Bhageerath, son of Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay Kumar, faced serious criminal allegations under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The complaint, lodged on May 8, 2026, by the mother of Miss X, a 17-year-old girl, accused him of repeated sexual harassment, assault, emotional manipulation, and coercive acts over several months at various locations, including a farmhouse in Moinabad.

Despite his father’s prominent political standing, the initial state machinery moved with noticeable readiness. Following an intense police manhunt and the issuance of a lookout notice, Telangana police arrested Bhageerath on May 16, 2026. He was remanded to judicial custody, subjected to custodial police interrogation, and the investigation proceeded swiftly amidst massive public scrutiny. Protests erupted across Hyderabad and throughout the state; women’s groups, student organisations, and opposition parties (including BRS, CPI, and others) staged aggressive dharnas and demonstrations demanding accountability and an impartial Special Investigation Team (SIT) probe. The media covered every twist and turn relentlessly, ensuring that political patronage could not quietly bury the case.

Regarding the latest position in the case, after spending over 50 days in judicial detention, Bandi Sai Bhageerath approached the Telangana High Court seeking regular bail. On July 9, 2026, Justice K. Sujana of the Telangana High Court granted him regular bail subject to strict conditions. Following his release on bail, Bhageerath moved the High Court seeking orders to restrain social media platforms and mainstream media outlets from publishing defamatory content or reporting prejudicial material concerning the POCSO case, in which the High Court subsequently passed interim restraining directions and sought counter-affidavits from the respondents. While the prosecution’s trial process and chargesheet proceedings continue under the statutory oversight of the special POCSO court, the case stands out as a prime instance where public mobilisation, political contention, and intense civil society pressure forced law enforcement to register the FIR promptly, arrest a powerful minister’s son, and hold custodial interrogation.

The Late Rekha Waghmare Case: Systemic Silence, Cover-Up, and Institutional Apathy.

At roughly the same time, an appalling horror unfolded in Donkeshwar village, Nandipet Mandal, Nizamabad district. Late Rekha Waghmare, a 32-year-old Scheduled Caste woman and migrant agricultural labourer hailing from Patoda Khurd village in Dharmabad Taluka, Nanded district, Maharashtra, was found dead under highly suspicious circumstances on the afternoon of February 13, 2026.

Since 2021, Rekha and her husband, Devidas Waghmare, along with their two young daughters (Jeevika, aged 10, and Sona, aged 8), had been living in a small shed on the agricultural land of a local influential landlord, Barla Narsing Reddy, working on a salaried labour basis. According to the consistent representations submitted by Rekha’s brother-in-law, Sri S. Sanjeev, the landlord had repeatedly harassed Rekha and attempted to exploit her. On February 13, 2026, Narsing Reddy intentionally sent Devidas away to work at another distant agricultural plot with strict orders not to return until all work was finished. The children were away at school. Taking advantage of Rekha being completely alone, Barla Narsing Reddy and his associate, Vittal Empalwad (or Emphalwar), allegedly broke into the …

author: Daniel Aloc
title: Ganggang ni JL Burgos bilang salamin ng lipunan
content:
Natatangi ang karanasan ng mga batang lumalaki sa kanayunan, malayo sa kalunsuran na may madaling access sa teknolohiya. Sa pagitan ng pagpasok sa paaralan at paglalaro sa mga burol at parang—kabilang na ang paghahanap ng mga gagambang panlaban sa kapwa gagamba—unti-unti nilang natututuhan ang mga realidad ng mundong kanyang ginagalawan. May nananalo, may natatalo; may nambubully, at may napipilitan lumaban upang hindi na lamang manatiling api.

Ngunit paano kung ang mga larong kinalakihan nila ay naging daan upang maaga silang mamulat sa karahasang umiiral sa lipunan? Paano kung ang mga batang dapat sana ay malayang naglalaro ay maagang nahaharap sa dahas, takot, at pang-aabuso.

Ilan lamang ito sa mga tanong na sinisikap sagutin ng Ganggang, ang kauna-unahang full-length narrative film ni JL Burgos, na unang ipinalabas sa Cinemalaya noong Agosto. Nitong Oktubre 21 ko lamang ito napanood sa Cinematheque Centre Manila, na ngayo’y matatagpuan sa bagong tahanan nito sa Philippine Film Heritage Building sa Intramuros, bilang bahagi ng Pelikula ng Bayan: Cinemalaya 22.

Hindi na katakataka ang tema at paksang tinatalakay ng pelikula, lalo na’t ang gumawa nito ay isang filmmaker na matagal nang nakatuon sa usapin ng karapatang pantao. Bago ang Ganggang, nakilala na si Burgos sa mga dokumentaryong Portraits of Mosquito Press at Alipato at Muog (2024). Ang huli ay nagwagi ng Best Picture, Best Documentary, at Best Editing sa ika-48 Gawad Urian noong 2025.

Hindi isang bagong proyektong biglaang nabuo ang Ganggang kasunod ng tagumpay ng Alipato at Muog. Ayon kay Burgos, isinulat niya ang kwento noon pang 2019. Sa halip na talikuran ang mga isyung matagal na niyang tinalakay sa kanyang mga dokumentaryo, pinili niyang ilahad ang mga ito sa pamamagitan ng naratibo ng isang pelikula—sa lente ng mga batang hindi pa lubusang nauunawaan ang bigat ng mga puwersang humuhubog sa kanilang buhay.

Sa pelikula, sina Ilay (Kenneth “Butchoy” Vincent Mendoza), Ten-ten (Don Rishmond Cerbito), at Mel (Raine Dela Cruz) ay tatlong batang naging magkaibigan sa paghahanap ng gagambang panlaban sa gagamba ni Anton (Prince Nathaniel España), ang bully sa kanilang paaralan. May kanya-kanyang pinagmulan ang tatlong bata. Anak ng isang desaparecido si Ilay, anak ng magsasaka si Ten-ten, at anak na naman ng isang sundalo si Mel.

Sa unang tingin, ang Ganggang ay isang pamilyar na bahagi ng pagkabata sa maraming pamayanan sa bansa. May tuwa sa paghahanap ng gagamba at sa pananabik na makita kung alin ang mananaig. Ngunit isa itong alegorya ng isang lipunang tila nakondisyon nang maniwala na kailangang maglaban-laban ang mamamayan upang mabuhay.

Sa talkback at Q&A session matapos ang screening, ipinaliwanag ni Burgos ang kahulugan ng tunggalian ng mga gagamba. Hindi naman likas sa mga ito ang mag-away sa paraang nakikita sa laro; inilalagay sila ng tao sa sitwasyong kailangan nilang magpatayan. Katulad ng mga mamamayang napipilitang mag-unahan at maglaban sa isang sistemang pinaghaharian ng iilan.

Sentrong usapin ng pelikula ang militarisasyon sa kanayunan. Binabago ng presensya ng mga sundalo ang pang-araw-araw na buhay ng mga residente, kabilang ang mga guro at magsasakang itinuturing na mga miyembro o tagasuporta ng New People’s Army (NPA) dahil lamang sa kanilang mga paninindigan.

Bukod sa karahasan at paglabag sa karapatang pantao na iniuugnay sa estado, ipinakikita rin nito ang epekto ng karahasan sa mga bata at kanilang pamilya.

Mahalagang banggitin na ang ilan sa mga karakter at eksena sa pelikula ay hango sa mga tunay na tao at pangyayari.

Isa rito si Rebelyn, ang gurong karakter sa pelikula na hango kay Rebelyn Pitao, anak ni Leoncio Pitao, na mas kilala bilang Commander Parago ng NPA sa Davao. Noong 2009, dinukot si Rebelyn at natagpuan ang kanyang bangkay kinabukasan. Ayon sa ulat ng Commission on Human Rights, ang biktima ay may mga saksak sa dibdib at iba pang palatandaan ng matinding tortyur. Ang sinapit ni Rebelyn ay isang paalala na ang mga taong hindi naman aktwal na nakikidigma ay maaari pa ring maging target ng estado.

Ang plaka naman ng sasakyang ipinakikita sa unang bahagi ng pelikula ay kapareho ng plaka ng sasakyang ginamit sa pagdukot sa kapatid ng direktor na si Jonas Burgos sa isang mall sa Quezon City noong 2007. Hanggang ngayon, hindi pa natatagpuan si Jonas.
