author: chuang
title: “Every War Is a World War”: Interview with a Member of Taiwan Alliance for a Free Palestine
content:
The following is an interview with friends from Taiwan who have formed the umbrella coalition Taiwan Alliance for a Free Palestine (TWAFP). The interview includes an overview of the rifts in the Taiwanese left, and the frustration of TWAFP organizers carving out their place amid divisions between pro-unification and independence, or pro- and anti-American positions, in the contentious and highly polarized politics on the island.


The organizer recounts their efforts to confront Taiwan’s growing ties with Israel and direct support for the genocide in Palestine. They speak with sadness that, even as Taiwan is now the fourth-largest supplier of arms to Israel, surpassing mainland China, most Taiwanese care little for the distant genocide and the struggle in Palestine seems far away. And yet, TWAFP has led successful demonstrations, pulled together a broad coalition of disparate groups in support of Palestine, and conducted research to expose Taiwan’s complicity in the ongoing genocide.


Be sure to read their

report


from 2025, outlining specific pathways of material component support for Israel, including radar, armor, and an array of military hardware.


See also a recent

piece

 submitted to us, outlining Taiwan’s deepening ties with Israel under the DPP government.


–

Chuang


Q: To begin, let’s just set the stage. Over the last few years, the Taiwan Alliance for a Free Palestine (TWAFP) has helped to organize the largest mobilizations against the genocide in Palestine seen in Taiwan. Can you tell us a little about how TWAFP formed and maybe review some of the protests it has organized?


A:

Taiwan Alliance for a Free Palestine (TWAFP)

 was founded in April of 2024. Prior to this, Taiwan had already seen several groups doing Palestine advocacy work arise spontaneously, including Palestine Action Front, Taiwan Palestine Solidarity Network, and Parallel Government. As its name suggests, TWAFP is an “Alliance” that brings together groups that were already involved in initiatives related to Palestine. In addition to the three groups already mentioned, the alliance also includes a migrant worker organization, the

Taiwan International Workers’ Association (TIWA)

; the human rights organization, Taiwan Association for Human Rights; the cultural collective, Taiwan Rave & Punk Solidarity Front for Palestine; the gender issues group, Queer Margins; and the Christian group, Taiwan Olive Branch Peace Collective. From 2024 to today, we have organized one petitioning campaign, issued two open letters, held one candlelight vigil, hosted one book club meeting, staged five protest actions, held three press conferences, and organized three marches. In the future, we plan to engage in a number of other activities, many of which may be smaller in scale.


Q: TWAFP also did some very interesting research on material links between Taiwan and Israel. We can link to the report here, but can you briefly go over the main findings, and maybe go over any new information that you’ve found since that report was released? For example, have there been more details since then?

      


A: In September of 2025, we released our report,

Taiwanese Companies’ Complicity in Israel’s Ongoing Genocide

, which identified specific manufacturers assisting Israel in the production of military weapons, including via the production of components. For example: Gloria Material Technology Corp (GMTC) supplies superalloys and high-grade steel produced through electroslag remelting, while ADLINK Technology supplies embedded computing systems and industrial-grade computers. In another case, Transcom marketed its vertically integrated capabilities—spanning chip design to module production—to enter the Israeli defense supply chain and is now a key, long-term supplier of components for the EL/M-2084 multi-mission radar, which is a core element of the Israeli “Iron Dome” air defense system designed by Israeli defense company Elta.


Since the primary purpose of this report was to provide accurate information that could be used by media outlets and other organizations, who would ideally follow up with their own reporting and investigation, we were relatively restrained in our writing approach and did not engage in much interpretation or extrapolation. However, when I was conducting this research, I came across a number of findings that I want to share widely:

author: Odessa Bishop-McMurray
title: “If they won’t give us a future, we will build one right here” - why the French revolt should inspire high-schoolers everywhere
content:
As one of the organisers of the upcoming nationwide 

Students Say No to Hanson

 demonstration on 12 November, I’ve had to endure a lot of inanity from the media and the right. Amongst snide remarks about the stages of brain development and warnings of the mortal dangers of missing two periods of class, one accusation keeps coming up: that we’re plotting to bring “French-style riots” to Australian cities. 

Right-wing journalists seized on an Instagram post we made on 11 October, conveying the inspiration we draw from French student protesters fighting government austerity and the far right. 

Cue an avalanche of hysterical headlines and news segments: The Murdoch-owned Adelaide 

Advertiser

 warned readers to brace for “walkouts ‘inspired’ by violent French protests”. Pauline Hanson went on Brisbane’s 4BC Radio to rip into us:

“...They are saying they are inspired by what’s going on in France. What? The 

looting

? The 

burning

? The 

destruction

? They’re 

inspired

 by that?”

Well, we’re not sorry for being inspired by French students. Everyone who wants to see a better world should identify with their struggle. 

Young people everywhere are facing a dire future, and revolt is rightly spreading. It’s clear even to some in the establishment that what’s happening in France is part of a global wave of protest with deep roots. As former UK Prime Minister Gordon Brown wrote this week in 

The Guardian

: “A global youthquake is happening. Promises we made young people have been broken—and they know it.”

Both far-right governments and “sensible centrists” are taking us on the same trajectory: more racism, more militarism, and more austerity. 

When states aren’t attempting to re-introduce conscription, as in Germany, they’re funnelling billions into the military-industrial complex while schools crumble. In France, students endure classrooms infested with cockroaches, mould and overcrowding, sometimes numbering 35 students to a class. 

We’ll likely never be able to afford secure housing or sufficient healthcare. We’ve watched politicians choose fossil fuel companies over the habitability of our planet. For many of us, the establishment’s unanimous endorsement of Israel’s genocide in Gaza was the final nail in the coffin.

It’s obvious that the journalists’ and politicians’ pearl-clutching about a few broken Parisian shop windows is a means of avoiding discussion of these issues. And their condemnation of violence rings hollow when they decline to comment on the vastly greater violence that the system inflicts on people daily. 

There’s the violence that is inherent in running such an unequal society. French youth linger without a future in the slums while the richest 500 families own nearly half the country. Schools and hospitals in France are crumbling, but the latest budget announcement includes 54 billion euros in further cuts to public spending. The police systematically brutalise Black and Arab working-class migrants. The high-profile killing of 17-year-old Nahel Merzouk, which sparked a nationwide revolt in 2023, is part of a long history of racialised policing. 

When these injustices generate resistance, there’s one public service the government can guarantee: the bludgeoning of protestors, tear gas, and potentially lethal stun grenades; exploding a student’s hand, breaking another’s jaw and leaving two 16-year-olds blinded for life. 

This is an inherent admission that the ruling class has no genuine plan to improve society. They just want resignation from ordinary people, and when that fails, tear gas is their backup plan.

But French students have shown that resignation gets us nowhere; Our power comes from the streets, and that’s a lesson the ruling class desperately does not want students to learn.

Already, France has shown small glimpses of how these movements can win real gains. While still hoping to crush the movement, the government has already been forced to make concessions. They’ve announced plans to cap class sizes, hire more teachers, and create more university places. This is a tiny fraction of what the movement is demanding, but it proves a timeless truth: a month of rebellion can win more change than decades of asking nicely.

A grassroots student movement in Serbia just ended the 14-year rule of the repressive Vučić regime. In Brazil, thousands of students flocked to the streets to successfully halt the advance of far-right presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro.

It seems like …

author: Sagar Sanyal
title: Emergency and autocracy in Modi’s India
content:
The far-right government in India led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been increasingly repressive and anti-democratic over recent months. Commentators are asking if the country is in the grip of an ‘

undeclared Emergency

’, a reference to the 1975-77 period of ‘Emergency rule’ by then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi in which activists and trade unionists were simply rounded up and jailed. 

The current repression is a response to the student and youth protests that erupted in the capital, New Delhi, in late July. They were sparked by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), a satirical movement that began on social media a couple of months earlier. The scale and intensity of the protests surprised the regime, as did the mocking anti-Modi tenor of popular chants. While the protest demand was for the resignation of the education minister over exam leaks, the protesters were motivated by visceral opposition to Modi, who has ruled since 2014. The police lashed out using the sort of 

force

 that they typically use in repressed regions like Kashmir. Police fired pellet guns, used nail-studded batons and sexually assaulted women protesters. 

Despite the repression, tens of thousands mobilised daily for five days—high school and university students, middle-class and working-class youth. Not only in Delhi, but in dozens of cities around the country. Alongside clips of police brutality circulating on social media, there are clips of youth chasing police off the streets with their sheer numbers and bravado. There are clips of cheeky middle-class youth approaching police who are away from the heat of the action to ask mocking questions like “Dear Mr. Officer, are you planning to tear gas protesters today?” The government is tracking down incriminating and embarrassing recordings of those events and asking social media platforms to 

remove them

.

Public opinion has turned strongly against Modi’s repression. Among the Hindi-speaking, middle-class, upper-caste Hindus who have been the most secure vote base of the BJP, parents now saw their own children being beaten—just for demanding a fair opportunity in college exams! Ultimately, the administration conceded the protest demand to sack the education minister, a humiliating 

defeat

 for Modi. It gave the lie to the “unstoppable strongman” image of him so carefully crafted by pro-Modi big media. 

Less than three months after the July protests, a new protest movement gripped the nation. It demands the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner of India, Gyanesh Kumar, who has been highly partisan to Modi and his 

Hindu nationalist

 Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and, according to some parties, rigged state elections in Bihar (May 2025) and West Bengal (April 2026). In West Bengal, the BJP won for the first time due in part to the chief election commissioner disqualifying millions of names from the eligible voters list. Deletions disproportionately targeted Muslims, who are an ideological enemy of Hindu nationalists, and who were also an important vote base of the party the BJP displaced—the Trinamool Congress (TMC). 

Following a late September 

expose,

 which revealed that the chief election commissioner had overruled the protestations of even his fellow election commissioners, the CJP and left student groups took up vote-rigging as a national campaign to channel the energy from the July student movement. Demands for the chief election commissioner to resign have been taken up by all opponents of the BJP. 

When a large protest was called for 

10 October

, the state responded by locking down New Delhi. Around 40,000 paramilitary and police laid siege to a sizeable area around the “designated protest site” of Jantar Mantar in the centre of the city. They blocked roads and shut down local internet mobile services (India is 

among the worst

 states for this). They closed over 40 metro train stations in Delhi and stopped over 200 inter-city trains from reaching Delhi. They threatened activists in their homes on the night before the march, this coming on top of regular arbitrary detention of prominent leaders of the protest movement (from the CJP and the left parties). 

Undeterred

, protestors appeared in their tens of thousands and were again met with batons and tear gas, and thousands were detained.

Sizeable protests have continued sporadically since 10 October, some called by the CJP or student organizations of the left, 

others

author: Rick Kuhn
title: Unemployment: a feature of capitalism, not a bug
content:
Today more than one in ten workers can’t find enough paid labour to live a decent life. And that’s only workers actively looking for a job or for more hours of employment. It doesn’t count those who have given up on finding a job, even though they want one, and survive thanks to friends, family or a measly government payment that isn’t an unemployment benefit.

In September

 the seasonally adjusted

un

employment rate was 4.7 percent;

under

employment was 6.3 percent. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, you’re not unemployed if you worked even an hour in the survey fortnight.

To get the Jobseeker Payment or Youth Allowance the un- and underemployed have to follow the Albanese government’s savage eligibility rules, inherited from its Liberal predecessors. If you earn more than a pitiful $75 a week, your payment starts to go down. You must follow the instructions of Workforce Australia and, if you’ve been directed to one, of an outsourced “employment services provider” agency, which profits from government funding.

That may mean applying for a certain number of jobs every “reporting period”, doing training they tell you to do, however meaningless courses about writing job applications or behaviour during an interview might be; or perform “work for the dole”, that would normally be done for much higher award wages. You have to “accept any offer of suitable paid work”, defined by the provider, whether the type of work or its location actually suits you or not.

If you’re single, without kids, the dole is

currently


a princely $413 a week. Certainly in Sydney, you’d be very lucky if less than half of that went on renting a room. And if you’re young, that’s unfortunate: unemployed aged 21 or younger are penalised and get less money than those over 21. Apparently young people don’t need as much shelter, food, clothing, etc. as older people.

Both the unemployment and underemployment rates are rising.

Unemployment is not a bug in capitalism, but a feature. The threat of un- and underemployment – descending into what Marx called “

the industrial reserve army

”—disciplines workers fearful of losing their jobs. The higher the level of unemployment, other things being equal, the less likely they are to take risks by fighting to defend or improve their pay and conditions.

The extent of the reserve army of labour changes in the course of economic cycles: lower during booms, higher in slumps.

Many central banks, like the Reserve Bank of Australia, are bumping up interest rates to slow their countries’ economies down. Their goal is not increased unemployment; that’s a side effect. Their main target is the rate of inflation. High inflation—lack of stability in the purchasing power of money—makes calculations by capitalists about their activities and especially investments more difficult.

In legislation

, the RBA has two goals: “price stability and the maintenance of full employment”. It says that “

[t]hese two objectives usually work together

”. In practice, the bank favours sacrificing jobs to keep a lid on inflation.

But today, high oil prices, due to the USA’s and Israel’s war on Iran, is the main driver of inflation. The RBA isn’t bumping up interest rates to discipline workers, although that’s a side-effect. Governor

Michelle Bullock

said at the end of September that “There is no wage price spiral going on in Australia. Rises in wages are not driving … cost pressures”.

In fact, it is workers who are mainly affected by inflation. Greg Jericho, in the

Guardian

, has illustrated how workers’ real pay has been falling since 2021, compared with the Consumer Price Index by 7 percent; compared with the more appropriate Employee Living Cost Index, by more than 12 percent.

The hostility of most union officials to leading their members in serious struggles to defend, let alone restore or improve their living standards, is mainly to blame.

In his 1972 report

Poverty in Australia

, Ronald Henderson, appointed by the Liberal government of Billy McMahon, calculated a poverty line, marking an “austere” standard of living below which people were in poverty. The Melbourne Institute of Economic Research frequently updates it.

JobSeeker

has consistently been below this line. Today that unemployment benefit is less than half the

Henderson poverty line

. Using 50, let alone 60 percent of median

household income

, common alternative international measures of poverty, the situation of people on JobSeeker …

author: John Mullen
title: Update from France: Towards an explosive general strike?
content:
The sharp upturn in class struggle continues in France, with school students and workers demanding more for ordinary people and far less for bankers and billionaires.

The Emmanuel Macron government is setting up ever more authoritarian institutions and practices, demanding harsh sentences for those arrested, and mutilating teenagers, while making minor concessions. The trade union leaderships are calling, mostly half-heartedly, for mass strike action this week. An explosion is possible.

The hundreds of demonstrations on October 24 and 31 were a major victory for the movement. The government's attempt to scare people off the streets failed. Despite bans and curfews and a solemn presidential speech ("we recommend that people do not demonstrate"), despite invented figures about injured cops and the cost of damage to public buildings, the movement is going forward.

Many were too frightened to go to these protests (two more people were mutilated by cops on the 24th), but more turned up, in an atmosphere of joyous revolt. Support is flooding in from very varied places: the magistrates' union, for example, has denounced the "brutality" of police action, a group of Catholic activists published an open letter to their right-wing bishops entitled "We are proud to take part in the uprising", and the Louvre museum was blockaded last week by Fine Arts students.

The repression was ratcheted up. For the 31st, demonstrations were banned in many city centres and peripheral routes were imposed. More than 100 towns and cities have been affected by curfews or restrictions on assembly.

This week, using the excuse of the rioting in mid-October, Macron is trying to push through parliament a new law. It increases penalties for looting, but would also impose heavy punishment for refusing to leave a demonstration when the police tell you to; it would give police the power to ban individuals from attending protests for up to three years, and allow the authorities to confiscate wages or social benefits of people "present in an assembly" where looting takes place (even if the individuals involved are not accused of any offence).

The far right, which hopes to win the presidency next May, applauds every new repressive measure.

The government seems to make additional minor concessions each week. We have seen 3000 replacement teachers hired, smaller classes (of 28 pupils) announced for 15-year-olds, 15,000 more student places promised in higher education, small increases in grants for poorer students, and more loans for regional governments to rebuild crumbling high schools.

This week Macron announced "a complete remoulding" of the hated Parcoursup platform, which controls who gets into which university … in 2028, long after the next elections! Some concessions answer student demands directly, but far more is needed.

Working-class combativity has long protected some aspects of French education from neoliberalism: enrolling in university costs less than €300 a year, for example. But this movement is not a defensive one. It is demanding more: 250,000 more places in higher education and €5 billion for school buildings, for a start.

As high schools and universities finished their autumn break on November 2, there was little sign of calm. A regional university student coordinating meeting, with representatives from a dozen universities, met for the second time on October 31: just one example of the important grassroots initiatives building the revolt.

That same day, almost all docks in France were closed as workers struck both against war and against proposed cuts in welfare being discussed in parliament. Their demands include an increase in the minimum wage for all workers.

As I write, the general strike for November 5 is being prepared, in support of the high schools and for increases in wages and hirings. It will be huge.

After a delay by union leaderships — which it is difficult not to describe as criminal — one month after the beginning of the movement, mass strike action has finally been called across the economy by five of the six biggest union confederations.

One of the biggest, the General Confederation of Workers (CGT), is asking strikers to organise workplace meetings and to "generalise the strike on the 5th November and afterwards". (The "renewable strike", re-voted in general meetings every couple of days, is an excellent tradition in the French workers' movement, but it can also be used as an excuse by leaderships to avoid …

author: Priya T.
title: Workers can overthrow capitalism
content:
Human beings are the most cooperative species that have ever existed. The expectation that we will live socially, with other people to help and guide us, is built into our biology. 

Compare a human baby with, say, crocodiles, which are born with as many as 60 teeth and use them to break through their eggshell, fending for themselves from their earliest moments. Or baby horses, who can walk within an hour of birth. Human babies can’t so much as lift their own heads

.

Our evolutionary survival instinct is to

cry

, the single purpose of which is to

alert others

 to needs or distress. This interdependence continues, in various ways, throughout our lives.

The fact that humans are not designed to make it alone is why capitalism feels so deeply wrong to so many of us. It is not geared towards meeting people’s needs, and the values it promotes—individualism, competition and greed—run counter to the social and collective instincts that are crucial to our survival as a species. 

The enormous resources and technologies that capitalism brings into existence are not used to provide for people or distributed to meet need. Instead, they are bought and sold to generate wealth for the tiny minority who control them. This gap between how things are, and how they could and should be, is one of the features of the system that perpetually cause people to turn against it. And it is becoming increasingly obscene. 

At the same time as the super-rich are getting on commercial space flights—at $70 million a ticket—the majority of the world’s population have never set foot on a plane. While the ultra-wealthy pour resources into the pursuit of immortality

for themselves,

wasting millions on cryogenic chambers, organ replacement, blood transfusions and uploading themselves to the cloud, millions of children die from diarrhea-related illnesses every year, and 3.4 billion people live without proper sanitation. Twelve billionaires hold more wealth than half of humanity. Abundance exists, but it is hoarded away from the masses. 

The rich would like us to think they earned and therefore deserve this wealth; that they are compensated in proportion to what they contribute to society. Australia’s richest person Gina Rinehart wrote a column expressing this view for the industry publication

Australian Resources and Investment

in 2012: “If you’re jealous of those with more money, don’t just sit there and complain; do something to make more money yourself—spend less time drinking, or smoking, or socialising, and more time working.” 

Leaving aside that Rinehart seems to spend heaps of time drinking and socialising, including at expensive Italian hotels with One Nation leader Pauline Hanson, nobody really thinks that a mining executive works harder than a garbage truck driver or early childhood educator. But the reality is that on average Australian salaries, it would take these workers about 650,000 years of “more time working” to earn the $40 billion Rinehart is worth. 

The truth is that the ruling class amasses their wealth not by working harder than everyone else, but by getting

other people to work for them

. Wealth is “created” when the value of the products other people produce is greater than what they are paid by their bosses in wages. This is called exploitation, and it is the basis of capital accumulation. 

Without the labour of workers, bosses wouldn’t have profits or power. Workers do the work to produce what we all need, while the “work” bosses do is to protect their control over this process, make it more profitable and manage the profits. This control gives bosses the ability to shape the lives of millions if not billions of other people—they decide what is made, who gets it and what it sells for. 

The majority, on the other hand, are oppressed: they are denied control over their own activity, as well as what happens to the products of their labour and, by extension, how their society is organised. This oppression is a prerequisite for exploitation—workers are conditioned from birth into accepting their subordinate place in society, and are expected to accept it throughout their working lives. Whether this is unadulterated, as in tyrannical dictatorships, or sanitised, as in parliamentary democracies, the underlying reality is the same. Bosses exercise dictatorial authority in the workplace. And their interests inform government policy. 

The majority of us get little to no say over what happens in our communities …

author: John Tully
title: Australia can build public housing, end homelessness
content:
I often walk my dog in Nipaluna/Hobart’s beautiful Rivulet Linear Park, which winds up from the city to the foothills of Mount Wellington. If you’re lucky, you can spot a platypus in the rivulet, there are flocks of gorgeously plumed parrots, and the marsupial population is thriving.

But that’s not all you’ll see, for half-hidden in the bushes there are tent encampments: places of last resort for some of Lutruwita/Tasmania’s homeless people. Others huddle on pieces of cardboard in shop doorways in the CBD or in other parks.

Sleeping rough exposes people to the vagaries of the elements, the threat of theft and violence and a constant battle to maintain good health and sanitation.

A fine line now separates countless numbers of working-class people from a similar fate. With the country’s median rents at $705 per week — an increase of 40.6% in the past five years — half of all people who live in rental accommodation are struggling to put food on the table and pay rent and other bills.

About 45% of families with children struggle to buy sufficient food — an estimated 3.6 million people, 69% of whom report they are facing food insecurity for the first time.

The link between the cost-of-living crisis and soaring rents is clear: 1.26 million households are forced to pay more than 30% of their disposable income on rent, which doesn’t leave much for food, utilities, education and medical care.

This crisis disproportionately impacts renters — though this is not to downplay the struggles of many to pay their mortgages with rising interest rates.

Unforeseen bills can send renters into a downward spiral of debt and homelessness. Elderly and middle-aged women, often with little savings to fall back on, can find themselves out on the street.

About 48% of 18–34-year-olds find themselves in precarious living circumstances.

While the United States/Israeli war on Iran turbocharged the cost-of-living crisis by forcing up the price of fuel and fertilisers, this conjunctural crisis only added to the existing pressures in a country where millions of people are priced out of home ownership and are reliant on the private rental market.

It doesn’t have to be this way. Australia is the third wealthiest country in terms of median wealth, and the fifth wealthiest in terms of average wealth.

However this wealth is not distributed evenly. The top 1% are wealthier than the bottom 50$ combined, and much of their wealth is in property and real estate.

With Labor, the Coalition and One Nation pushing politics further to the right, there is little challenge to the neoliberal dogmas that had led us to this crisis.

Those three parties are firmly wedded to the private rental market. Indeed, many politicians have a personal interest in maintaining it.

According to the Guardian, at least 55% of federal politicians own multiple properties, and between 50 to 92 are actively receiving rental income.

Meanwhile, public housing has declined to only 4% of housing stock.

This is an ideological choice with disastrous consequences. While Australia does better than the US, where less than 1% of households live in any form of social or public housing, we compare poorly with most OECD countries.

Countries like the Netherlands (29%), Austria (24%), Denmark (21%), Sweden (17%) and Britain (17%) have far greater percentages of public housing stock than Australia. In Vienna, and other city centres that have consciously prioritised public housing, that figure can rise to more than 50%.

Social housing is nothing new — at least to those who care to look.

I recently visited the oldest public housing project in the world, the Fuggerei, in the southern German city of Augsburg, founded in 1521. The project’s museum points out that “people have continuously been living in the Fuggerei for half a millennium”.

One of the early residents was Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart’s great-grandfather, the impoverished bricklayer, Franz Mozart. “When the project’s major donor, the banker Jakob Fugger, died in 1525, there were 52 houses in the complex. Today, the Fuggerei consists of 140 flats in 67 houses, with other buildings for administration, a museum and workshops.”

The Fuggerei is not a ghetto of poverty and despair. It is a beautiful place, with homes meeting modern living standards with heating, modern bathrooms, television and the internet.

It has some strict conditions for residence, designed for “Catholic Augsburg residents in need”, who must contribute three prayers a …

title: Francia en huelga: un malestar que cruza generaciones
content:
Sindicatos de trabajadores y de estudiantes, chalecos amarillos, convergieron en una jornada de huelga tras cinco semanas de movilización masivas que desafían las respuestas del gobierno de Macron. Actualmente, tres generaciones convergen en un mismo espacio, ya no privado, sino público, para expresar un descontento social articulado contra la cultura del trabajo precarizado y el consumo asfixiante. Los jóvenes ven su futuro hipotecado antes de empezar; los adultos, su presente consumido por el costo de vida y la carga impositiva; los jubilados, agotados tras una vida laboral, se enfrentan a reformas que recortan o postergan lo que legítimamente les corresponde. En el plano comunicacional, existe un contraste directo entre la narrativa oficial del Ministerio del Interior, que califica las marchas como jornadas transcurridas «sin problemas», y el registro de la ciudadanía. Cientos de registros audiovisuales difundidos por los propios manifestantes muestran cómo la intervención de las fuerzas policiales y de la gendarmería, en los momentos de dispersión, suele actuar como detonante de los enfrentamientos.

 Por Mario Daniel Villagra desde Francia, para Red Eco Alternativo.


(Mario Daniel Villagra desde Francia – Red Eco Alternativo) Francia – Las manifestaciones continúan, se intensifican, se organizan y pasan de la espontaneidad a la conciencia, pese a los intentos del gobierno de Emmanuel Macron de controlarlas, desviarlas y generar desinformación. Docentes hartos de las malas condiciones de trabajo y estudiantes secundarios, que se pusieron a la cabeza de un movimiento de imaginación y cólera, empujan desde hace semanas una protesta que hoy, 5 de noviembre, suma a estudiantes y trabajadores: el motor de todo pasado, presente y futuro. Según el sindicato SNES-FSU, el 52 % del personal de colegios y liceos está en huelga.


Actualmente, tres generaciones convergen en un mismo espacio, ya no privado, sino público, para expresar un descontento social articulado contra la cultura del trabajo precarizado y el consumo asfixiante. Los jóvenes ven su futuro hipotecado antes de empezar; los adultos, su presente consumido por el costo de vida y la carga impositiva; los jubilados, agotados tras una vida laboral, se enfrentan a reformas que recortan o postergan lo que legítimamente les corresponde.En el plano comunicacional, existe un contraste directo entre la narrativa oficial del Ministerio del Interior, que califica las marchas como jornadas transcurridas «sin problemas», y el registro de la ciudadanía. Cientos de registros audiovisuales difundidos por los propios manifestantes muestran cómo la intervención de las fuerzas policiales y de la gendarmería, en los momentos de dispersión, suele actuar como detonante de los enfrentamientos.


Las causas estructurales de la protesta


No sería justo atomizar el análisis y decir que esto es algo de actualidad. Hay hechos que indican que, desde hace una década, existe una presidencia atravesada por una retórica del diálogo, pero con falta de escucha y de canales de participación ciudadana reales.Las movilizaciones actuales no son un hecho aislado, sino la acumulación de un largo ciclo de conflictividad durante los mandatos de Macron. En esa cronología podemos enumerar la revuelta de los Gilets Jaunes (Chalecos Amarillos) en 2018-2019; las protestas masivas de 2023 contra la reforma de las pensiones, impuesta mediante el artículo 49.3 de la Constitución, que permite adoptar un texto sin votación parlamentaria; y, claro, la actualidad, con el descontento por el encarecimiento de la vida y el malestar en el sistema educativo y universitario, donde se denuncian el deterioro de la infraestructura escolar, la falta de reemplazo de docentes y la necesidad de mejores condiciones de trabajo y estudio.Es lógico mencionar también el factor económico, entre causas propias del gobierno y ajenas a él: la subida del precio de los combustibles, impulsada por la inestabilidad geopolítica en Oriente Medio, ha reducido severamente el poder adquisitivo.


El frente de estudiantes secundarios y la respuesta del Ejecutivo


A finales de octubre, tras una consulta que reunió más de 100.000 contribuciones de casi 3.000 liceos, el gobierno, con el primer ministro Sébastien Lecornu a la cabeza, presentó un paquete de medidas: un tope de 28 alumnos por clase (el primer año del liceo), 500 puestos docentes adicionales, 1.000 millones de euros para renovar las universidades, becas indexadas a la inflación …

content:
Η Γαλλία έζησε μία από τις μεγαλύτερες κινητοποιήσεις στην ιστορία της, καθώς υπολογίζεται ότι συμμετείχαν περισσότεροι από 1,6 εκατομμύριο διαδηλωτές, σύμφωνα με τους διοργανωτές. Τα γαλλικά συνδικάτα ένωσαν τις δυνάμεις τους στην πανεθνική απεργία της 5ης Νοεμβρίου στη Γαλλία για αυξήσεις στους μισθούς και για υποστήριξη του κινήματος διαμαρτυρίας των μαθητών, ασκώντας νέα πίεση στην πολιορκημένη κυβέρνηση του Μακρόν.  Σήμερα φοιτητές, εκπαιδευτικοί, εργαζόμενοι, εργατικά συνδικάτα και μέλη του κινήματος των Κίτρινων Γιλέκων ενώθηκαν για να απαιτήσουν αλλαγές.


Η απεργία διοργανώθηκε από την L’intersyndicale,  που εκπροσωπεί όλα τα κύρια συνδικάτα της Γαλλίας. Η εκπαίδευση, η υγειονομική περίθαλψη, οι δημόσιες συγκοινωνίες και άλλοι τομείς επηρεάστηκαν και πολλές υπηρεσίες παρέμειναν κλειστές.


Μετά από περισσότερο από ένα μήνα τακτικών και μεγάλων διαμαρτυριών σε όλη τη Γαλλία, μεγάλες συγκεντρώσεις πραγματοποιήθηκαν στο Παρίσι, τη Λυών και τη Μασσαλία. Η

author: Unknown
title: Fransa: Öğrenci ve işçi grevleri birleşti, yüz binler ücret ve sosyal haklar için sokakta
content:
İşçi sendikalarının ücret artışı, emeklilik haklarının korunması, kamu hizmetlerinin güçlendirilmesi ve sosyal harcamalardaki kesintilerin durdurulması talepleriyle başlattığı Fransa çapındaki grev, lise ve üniversite öğrencilerinin katılımıyla perşembe günü geniş bir toplumsal gösteriye dönüştü. 


Paris, Marsilya, Lyon, Toulouse ve Nantes başta olmak üzere ülkenin birçok kentinde yürüyüşler düzenlenirken, İçişleri Bakanlığı öğle saatlerinde Paris dışındaki 180 gösteriye 270 bin kişinin katıldığını bildirdi.


Liselilerin başlattığı hareket bu noktaya nasıl geldi?


Fransa'da toplumsal hareketlilik eylülün ikinci yarısında, Paris yakınlarındaki Créteil'de öğretmen açığını protesto eden lise öğrencilerinin başlattığı eylemlerle bir dönüşüm geçirdi. Kalabalık sınıflar, bakımsız okul binaları, öğretmen eksikliği ve eğitimdeki eşitsizlikler kısa sürede ülke çapında ortak talepler hâlini aldı. Öğrenciler, eşitsizlikleri derinleştirdiğini savundukları üniversiteye giriş sistemi Parcoursup'un da kaldırılmasını istedi.


Ekim başında okul işgalleri, blokajlar ve yürüyüşlerle büyüyen hareket, 17 Ekim'den başlayarak hayat pahalılığına karşı gösterilerle buluştu. 17, 24 ve 31 Ekim'de düzenlenen üç büyük eylem dalgasına öğrencilerin yanı sıra sendikalar, emekçiler ve yeniden harekete geçen Sarı Yelekliler katıldı. Polis müdahaleleri, gözaltılar ve gösterilere getirilen kısıtlamalar da protestoların gündemine yerleşti.


Hükümetin eğitim koşullarını iyileştirme kapsamında açıkladığı sınırlı önlemler, öğrencilerin taleplerini karşılamadı. Kasımın ilk günlerinde liselerde eğitim yeniden dururken, üniversite öğrencileri de eylemlere katıldı. Öğretmen açığı ve eğitimdeki eşitsizliklere karşı başlayan hareket, ücretler, emeklilik, sosyal güvenlik ve kamu harcamaları için mücadeleyle ortaklaşmaya başladı.


Beş büyük sendika konfederasyonu CFDT, CGT, FO, FSU ve UNSA, bir ay öncesinden, 5 Ekim'de 5 Kasım için ortak grev çağrısında bulunmuştu. Sonraki haftalarda CFTC, Solidaires ve CFE-CGC de çağrıya katıldı. Sendikaların gündemindeki ücret ve sosyal haklar mücadelesi öğrencilerin eğitim talepleriyle aynı eylem takviminde buluştu.


Yüz binler sokakta, ulaşım ve eğitimde aksama


Sendikaların önceden açıkladığı takvime göre ülke genelinde yaklaşık 260 gösteri planlandı. İçişleri Bakanlığı ise 220'den fazla sokak eylemi beklediğini duyurdu.


Bakanlığın Fransa saatiyle 13.00 itibarıyla verdiği bilgiye göre Paris dışındaki 180 yürüyüşte 270 bin kişi bulunuyordu. CGT ise aynı saatlerde 73 kentte 250 binden fazla gösterici olduğunu açıkladı. Her iki veri de günün başındaki ilk katılım rakamlarıydı.


Başkent Paris'te yürüyüş, öğleden sonra République Meydanı'ndan Nation Meydanı'na doğru başladı. Sendika bayraklarının yanı sıra öğrencilerin eğitim hakkı taleplerini taşıyan pankartlar da kortejlerde yer aldı.


Grevin etkileri özellikle demiryolu ulaşımında ve eğitimde hissedildi. Ulusal demiryolu şirketi SNCF'nin dört büyük sendikası birlikte iş bırakma çağrısı yaparken, bazı bölgelerde tren seferleri aksadı. Sağlık çalışanları, posta emekçileri, hava ulaşımı personeli ve öğretmenler de grev çağrısının kapsamındaydı.


AP'nin haberine göre liselerin yaklaşık üçte birinde eğitim, öğrenci blokajları veya öğretmenlerin iş bırakması nedeniyle aksadı. Eğitim Bakanlığı ise devlet ilkokullarındaki öğretmenlerin yüzde 17,54'ünün greve katıldığını bildirdi. Paris'te Eyfel Kulesi de grev nedeniyle ziyarete kapatıldı.


Ücretler, emeklilik ve kamu hizmetleri


Sendikaların ortak talepleri arasında asgari ücretin yükseltilmesi, ücret pazarlıklarının derhal açılması, emekli aylıklarının korunması, istihdamın güvence altına alınması ve büyük servetlerin daha yüksek vergilendirilmesi yer alıyor.


Demiryolu sendikaları hükümetin bütçe tasarısının sosyal güvenlik harcamalarını azaltacağını, kamu çalışanlarının ücretlerini baskılayacağını ve yoksulluğu derinleştireceğini savunuyor.


Sendikalar ayrıca sanayide artan işten çıkarma planlarına ve kamu hizmetlerinin finansmanındaki daralmaya dikkat çekiyor. Hayat pahalılığı karşısında ücretlerin ve emekli aylıklarının geride kalması, öğrencilerle çalışanların ortak eyleminin başlıca nedenlerinden biri olarak öne çıkıyor.


CGT Genel Sekreteri Sophie Binet, grev öncesinde yaptığı açıklamada 5 Kasım'ın geniş bir toplumsal buluşma günü olması gerektiğini vurgulamıştı. Binet, bugün Paris'te yaptığı açıklamada da talepler karşılanmadıkça mücadelenin durmayacağını söyledi.

Dossier

Übersetzung aus der Hong Kong Free Press vom und am 17.5.2021 beim Forum Arbeitswelten

Vor der Freilassung in 2027: Hongkonger Aktivist und Gewerkschafter Joshua Wong zu weiteren zehn Jahren Haft verurteilt


„

Joshua Wong muss wegen eines weiteren Verfahrens noch lange im Gefängnis bleiben. Er soll mit ausländischen Mächten kollaboriert haben.


Der inhaftierte Hongkonger Demokratieaktivist Joshua Wong ist von einem Gericht in der chinesischen Sonderverwaltungszone wegen »Kollaboration mit ausländischen Kräften« zu weiteren zehn Jahren Haft verurteilt worden. Das Gericht habe gegen Wong »eine endgültige Freiheitsstrafe von zehn Jahren« verhängt, hieß es am Donnerstag in einer Pressemitteilung des Gerichts. Die Haftstrafe des Aktivisten wurde damit über die sechs Jahre hinaus verlängert, die er bereits verbüßt hat.


Wong musste sich in dem weiteren gegen ihn angestrengten Prozess verantworten. In dem neuen Verfahren wurde ihm zur Last gelegt, gegen das nationale Sicherheitsgesetz verstoßen zu haben. Der 30-Jährige hatte sich im September schuldig bekannt. Zurzeit sitzt er bereits eine Haftstrafe wegen Subversion ab. Menschenrechtsorganisationen kritisieren, dass die neuen Anklagepunkte darauf abzielen, den Aktivisten so lange wie möglich hinter Gittern festzuhalten.


Wong ist eines der bekanntesten Gesichter der Hongkonger Demokratiebewegung, die von den Behörden mit massivem Druck zum Erliegen gebracht wurde. Er wurde durch die von Studenten angeführten Proteste bekannt und war auch an den Massenprotesten beteiligt, die zur Verhängung des nationalen Sicherheitsgesetzes führten. Er sollte eigentlich im kommenden Jahr freikommen

Am 8. März wird die Krankenhausgewerkschafterin Winnie Yu wieder ins Gefängnis geschickt. Im Februar 2021 in Untersuchungshaft genommen, wurde sie fünf Monate später auf Kaution freigelassen. Die entlassene Winnie Yu soll am 28. April zusammen mit 46 anderen AktivistInnenen aus dem gesamten Spektrum der Opposition vor Gericht erscheinen. Ihnen wird vorgeworfen, an einer „oppositionellen Vorwahl“ vor den Parlamentswahlen teilgenommen zu haben.


Unter den derzeit inhaftierten GewerkschafterInnen befinden sich auch Lee Cheuk-yan und Carol Ng, ehemalige Führer des aufgelösten HKCTU.

author: CMI Argentina
title: El Ueno Bank financió con dinero de jubilaciones a la red de desinformación ultraderechista de Cerimedo
content:
De Paraguay a Mar-A-Lago. El argentino detenido en Bolivia por el intento de asesinato de su amante recibió, junto a Javier Negre y Andy Rivas, financiamiento de la entidad financiera paraguaya, que con su colapso obligó a la renuncia del presidente Santiago Peña.


Fernando Cerimedo


Por El Ciudadano


El Ueno Bank, cuyo colapso derivó ayer jueves en la renuncia del presidente de Paraguay, Santiago Peña, deja al descubierto el desvío ilegal de cientos de millones de dólares de fondos públicos jubilatorios. La entidad sirvió como motor financiero para patrocinar eventos como el de Javier Negre en Mar a Lago, la residencia del mandatario también caído en desgracia Donald Trump, donde premiaron al consultor de toda la ultraderecha regional Fernando Cerimedo.


El principal socio de Cerimedo, detenido en Bolivia acusado de mandar asesinar a su amante, es Andy Rivas, quien trabajaba para Peña en la sombra. La empresa organizadora del evento junto a Negre también financia CPAC, eventos donde participa Santiago Peña y que trajo personalmente a Paraguay donde fue entrevistado por Javier Negre.


Durante el mandato de Peña, el Ueno Bank pasó de ser un actor marginal a un monstruo bancario hinchado artificialmente con más de 5 billones de guaraníes (unos 869 millones de dólares) de fondos públicos inyectados de manera irregular desde el Instituto de Previsión Social (IPS).


Fue un drenaje sistemático de las pensiones (jubilaciones) del Estado que sirvió, además, para financiar la agenda ideológica de la extrema derecha internacional en foros que van desde Mar-a-Lago en la gala latina organizada por Javier Negre donde le dieron un premio a Cerimedo y el Wall Street Latino, que a su vez financia CPAC, donde Peña tejió las alianzas geopolíticas con la ultraderecha española de VOX.


El empresario Javier Negre.


Ueno Bank fue patrocinador exclusivo y principal (Diamond Sponsor) de cumbres ultraderechistas continentales, como la Hispanic Prosperity Gala 2026 celebrada en Mar-a-Lago, en Palm Beach. Ese fue un evento con entradas VIP de 5000 dólares donde se dieron cita figuras como el brasileño prófugo en Estados Unidos Eduardo Bolsonaro –hijo del detenido Jair y hermano del derrotado Flávio–, el presidente argentino Javier Milei y la Presidenta de la Comunidad de Madrid, Isabel Díaz Ayuso, que participaron a través de un video.


La entidad financiera actuaba en la práctica como el brazo pagador de una red de influencia política conectada con los organizadores de eventos como la Conferencia de Acción Política Conservadora (CPAC) y las redes europeas ligadas a VOX. En esa red de patrocinios operan conocidos agitadores de la desinformación y la propaganda de extrema derecha, como el español Javier Negre, fundador de La Derecha Diario con Cerimedo. El argentino fue premiado como mejor consultor por sus victorias en las elecciones de Bolivia y Honduras. Uno de sus principales socios era, hasta que cayó detenido, Brad Parscale, estratega digital de Trump. Otro, Rivas, asesor de Peña.


 


Ver esta publicación en Instagram


 


Una publicación compartida por Camilo Soares (@camilosoaresm)


Rivas, socio de Cerimedo y un “Mago del Kremlin” paraguayo con actuación en Argentina


Andrés “Andy” Rivas, socio de Cerimedo, fue consultor sin cargo oficial ni figuración en las planillas del Estado paraguayo. Acompañó muchas veces al canciller Rubén Ramírez Lezcano y al propio Peña en sus viajes internacionales.


Rivas se sentó a la par de diplomáticos de carrera en cumbres de alto nivel en Washington y Asunción. Tuvo acceso privilegiado a reuniones con el Consejo de las Américas, la Fundación Heritage, el Instituto Republicano Internacional (IRI), el congresista estadounidense Mario Díaz-Balart, la Embajada de Israel y la OEA. Lo mismo que hizo Cerimedo en Bolivia. Y utilizando el financiamiento del Ueno Bank con las campañas de guerra sucia digital y la penetración geopolítica conservadora.


Junto a Cerimedo, se acercó al exmileísta Ramiro Marra. Y organizó en abril de 2024 el viaje a Taiwán de los diputados Álvaro Martínez (La Libertad Avanza) y Karina Bachey (PRO), costeado por el gobierno taiwanés. Fue en paralelo a la gira que la entonces canciller Diana Mondino realizaba por Beijing junto al presidente del Banco Central, Santiago Bausili, para renegociar el swap de monedas de US$6.000 millones con China.


Rivas también se vinculó con el procesado José Luis Espert y su ex compañero de fórmula Luis Rosales. Quedaron retratados …

author: Henry A. Giroux
title: After Electoral Victory, Let’s Dismantle the System That Breeds Authoritarianism
content:
The task now is to turn this moment of resistance into a sustained struggle against these structures of power.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

With the Democratic Party’s landslide victory, a day of reckoning appears to have arrived for Trump and the far-right, white nationalist forces that have turned cruelty into a governing principle and hatred into a political language. Something has broken in the machinery of fear. The old fascist ideas, the politics of racial hatred, and the relentless assault on human dignity have encountered a moment of resistance. Too much suffering, too much misery, too much authoritarian violence. Too much blood in the streets, too many deaths, screams, and a deafening silence. Enough is enough, at least for the moment. The Trump regime has exposed some of the darkest impulses of political life, resurrecting the ghosts of a past that should have taught us where the glorification of state violence, racial cleansing, the crushing of dissent, and organized cruelty inevitably leads. Its legacy is written in the expansion of the carceral state, the staggering investment in prisons and punishment, the unleashing of masked agents of repression across the country, and the unapologetic embrace of a language of racial cleansing that strips entire populations of their humanity and destroys lives and civil liberties.

Yet the celebrations now dominating liberal and mainstream media risk turning this electoral victory into an exercise in historical amnesia. Trump’s defeat is being hailed as a crushing repudiation of the far right, as though the political conditions that made his rise possible have suddenly disappeared. Missing from this triumphalist narrative is any serious reckoning with the Democratic Party’s own complicity in creating those conditions. From Clinton to Obama, Democratic administrations embraced neoliberal policies that deepened economic inequality, strengthened corporate power, weakened working-class institutions, and helped create the social and political landscape in which authoritarianism could flourish. Nor can the party’s leadership escape responsibility for its support of Israel’s genocidal war in Gaza, its exporting of horrendous military weapons, and its broader allegiance to a colonizing authoritarian order, sustained through violence and dispossession. A party so deeply implicated in the machinery of neoliberal capitalism cannot be entrusted with dismantling the very structures of power it has helped legitimate and preserve.

For a fleeting moment, democracy may be able to breathe again. But breathing is not liberation, and an electoral victory is no substitute for dismantling the gangster capitalist order that breeds authoritarianism, feeds on human suffering, commodifies every aspect of life, and makes fascism an enduring possibility. The forces that produced Trump did not emerge overnight, nor will they disappear with an election. They are embedded in institutions that concentrate wealth, manufacture fear, normalize inequality, and transform human misery into a source of profit and political power. Trump may be defeated at the ballot box, but Trumpism cannot be defeated without confronting the economic, political, and cultural foundations of a system that turns greed into virtue, cruelty into policy, racism into a badge of honor, and human disposability into a governing principle.

Unless those foundations are dismantled, the nightmare will return, perhaps wearing a different mask. The serpent’s egg, to invoke the haunting metaphor associated with Ingmar Bergman, has not been destroyed. It lies beneath the surface of seemingly democratic societies, nourished by the dark and volatile forces of a capitalist order that breeds inequality, authoritarianism, and organized cruelty. Brecht understood that fascism could not be confronted without exposing the capitalist relations of power that give rise to it. The serpent’s egg remains embedded in the political, economic, and cultural machinery of gangster capitalism, waiting for the conditions under which it can hatch again. Fascism may suffer an electoral defeat, but the serpent survives, sustained by the very system that gave it life.

There is another historical lesson that cannot be buried beneath the celebrations of an electoral victory: the need to recover the spirit of the Nuremberg trials. Nuremberg established a principle that must never be forgotten …

title: Συγκέντρωση ενάντια στη φασιστική επίθεση σε μαθήτρια και φοιτητές, Τετάρτη 4/11, στις 18.00, στη πλατεία Ταραμπούρας, Πάτρα
content:
Δολοφονική επίθεση εναντίον  μαθήτριας, μέλους της ΚΝΕ,

την οποία είχαν στοχοποιήσει εδώ και μέρες, και

εναντίον φοιτητών

, που βρέθηκαν στο πλευρό της για να την υπερασπιστούν, εξαπέλυσαν

 φασιστοειδή

 το βράδυ της Τρίτης στην

Πάτρα,

στην περιοχή της Νεάπολης Ζαρουχλέικων.


Συγκεκριμένα, σύμφωνα με την ανακοίνωση των οργανώσεων Αχαΐας του ΚΚΕ και της ΚΝΕ, εδώ και μερικές ημέρες, φασίστες απειλούσαν και έβριζαν

μαθήτρια του 8ου Λυκείου Πατρών

, μέλος της ΚΝΕ και της Συντονιστικής Επιτροπής Μαθητών της Πάτρας, σε μικρή πλατεία έξω από το σπίτι της, τις βραδινές ώρες.


Το βράδυ της Τρίτης και ενώ για ακόμη μία φορά επαναλαμβανόταν το ίδιο σκηνικό, μαθητές και φοιτητές στην παρέμβασή τους προς άτομα που βρισκόντουσαν κάτω από την οικία να σταματήσουν την απαράδεκτη συμπεριφορά τους, δέχθηκαν

τραμπούκικη βίαιη επίθεση από περίπου 40 φασίστες.


Το

 Εργατικό Κέντρο Πάτρας όπως και οργανώσεις και συλλογικότητες καλούν σε αντιφασιστική συγκέντρωση ενάντια στην φασιστική αυτή επίθεση, την Τετάρτη 4/11, στις 18.00, στη Πλατεία Ταραμπούρας, Πάτρα


Κάλεσμα/Αφίσες:


Εργατικό Κέντρο Πάτρας


Σε

συλλαλητήριο σήμερα Τετάρτη 4 Νοέμβρη

 στις

6 μ.μ.,

στην

 πλατεία Ταραμπούρα,

στην

 Πάτρα

, καλεί το

 Εργατικό Κέντρο Πάτρας

, καταγγέλλοντας την

απρόκλητη φασιστική επίθεση εναντίον πρωτοπόρας μαθήτριας και εναντίον φοιτητών

 στην περιοχή των Ζαρουχλέικων.


Το Εργατικό Κέντρο καλεί όλους τους φορείς της πόλης να καταδικάσουν την επίθεση των φασιστών και να συμμετάσχουν σήμερα το απόγευμα στο συλλαλητήριο.


Αναλυτικότερα, το ΕΚΠ με την ανακοίνωσή του «καταγγέλλει την απρόκλητη επίθεση που είχε στόχο νεολαία πρωτοπόρα μαθήτρια στην περιοχή των Ζαρουχλέικων από θρασύδειλους φασίστες-ναζί μαζί με άλλους εγκληματίες. Έστησαν καρτέρι κάτω από το σπίτι της και επιτέθηκαν με μαχαίρια και σιδερογροθιές σε φίλους και πρωτοπόρους νεολαίους που βρέθηκαν εκεί για να την υπερασπιστούν».


Με τον τρόπο αυτό, τονίζει το ΕΚΠ, «προσπαθούν να τρομοκρατήσουν τη νεολαία και τον λαό, αλλά και όποιον αντιστέκεται στην αντεργατική, αντιλαϊκή πολιτική της κυβέρνησης και των άλλων συστημικών κομμάτων».


Συνεχίζοντας αναφέρει:


«Δεν θα τους περάσει! Δεν τρομοκρατούμαστε!

 Οι φασίστες που βγήκαν από τις τρύπες τους για να χύσουν το φασιστικό τους δηλητήριο θα απομονωθούν και θα πάρουν την απάντησή τους από το οργανωμένο εργατικό και λαϊκό κίνημα. Η λαϊκή δυσαρέσκεια που γεννάται από τα ίδια τα προβλήματα που αντιμετωπίζει η εργατική – λαϊκή οικογένεια είναι φόβος και τρόμος για το σύστημα του κέρδους και των φασιστών που το υπηρετούν, ακριβώς γιατί είναι αυτή που μπορεί να μετατραπεί σε οργανωμένη απόφαση για ανατροπή αυτού του βάρβαρου συστήματος.


Οι δήθεν πατριώτες ναζί που πατρίδα τους είναι το κεφάλαιο

 και ορκίζονται μόνο σε αυτό και τα συμφέροντά του, θέλουν την εργατική τάξη και τη νέα γενιά να μένει αδιαμαρτύρητα στοιχισμένη πίσω από τους ματωμένους “εθνικούς στόχους” των επιχειρηματικών ομίλων, της πολεμικής εμπλοκής και των αμύθητων κερδών. 

Έχουν ορκιστεί να τσακίζουν κάθε προσπάθεια διεκδίκησης των σύγχρονων αναγκών μας! Γι’ αυτό επιτίθενται στους πρωτοπόρους!


Θα ξαναμπούν στις τρύπες τους, όσο και αν προσπαθεί η αστική τάξη και τα επιτελεία τους στα ΜΜΕ να τους διαφημίζουν

. Στις εργατογειτονιές δεν χωρούν οι υμνητές του Χίτλερ, οι δολοφόνοι του Παύλου Φύσσα και του Σαχζάτ Λουκμάν. author: Soligruppe um Henry aus Leipzig
title: Erklärung zum Tod von Henry
content:
CN: Suizid


Henry, Beschuldigter im Antifa-Ost-Komplex, ist am 24. Oktober 2026 an den Folgen eines Suizidversuchs gestorben.


Wir sprechen von Herzen der Familie, seinen Freund*innen, seinem Umfeld und (ehemaligen) Wegbegleiter*innen unser tiefes Beileid aus.


Unsere Gefühle wechseln zwischen Trauer, Erinnerungen an ihn und auch Wut.


Wut auf Journalist*innen, die der Familie und seinem Umfeld keine 24 Stunden der Trauer gelassen haben. Wut auf Neonazis, die auch nach seinem Tod ihn nicht in Frieden lassen können. Wut auf das Gericht, weil es ihm seine therapeutische und medizinische Unterstützung immer wieder erschwerte und zum großen Teil nicht gewährte.


Wir verstehen, dass (seine) Anwält*innen auf die Ungerechtigkeiten bis hin zu rechtswidrigen Taten von Behörden gegen Henry und andere Antifaschist*innen in Leipzig und Sachsen verweisen. Antifaschist*innen stehen seit jeher im Fokus der Repressionsbehörden (*). Die SoKo LinX hat die Kriminalisierung und Verfolgung antifaschistischen Engagements in Sachsen im Besonderen betrieben.


Dies haben Henry und seine Familie immer wieder zu spüren bekommen. Die letzten Jahre von Henry waren von Repression und öffentlichen Diffamierungen seitens Behörden und Neonazis gegen seine Person geprägt, was für ihn, seine Familie und sein soziales Umfeld sehr belastend war.


Aber neben diesen Tatsachen gibt es noch weitere. Wir sind auch wütend auf Henry. Doch können wir dies nicht mehr mit ihm ausmachen. Wir möchten nicht, dass seine Person und sein Leben in der Öffentlichkeit bewertet werden, deswegen werden wir das hier auch nicht tun. Wir wünschen uns, dass dies respektiert wird. Zumal die Strafverfahren gegen das Konstrukt einer angeblichen antifaschistischen kriminellen Vereinigung weiter geführt werden.


Die Verkürzung, die wir in den letzten Tagen öfter gelesen haben, dass der Staat ihn umgebracht habe, finden wir nicht richtig. Es geht uns dabei nicht darum staatliche Stellen von ihrer Mitverantwortung frei zu sprechen, doch so einfach, wie einige meinen, ist es eben nicht.


Bei aller Trauer und emotionaler Erschütterung ist es Teilen der Familie, jenen die ihn die letzten Jahre begleiteten, und uns wichtig, dass der Tod von Henry nicht instrumentalisiert wird. Wir bitten euch daher von öffentlichkeitswirksamen Aktionen abzusehen. Es fühlt sich als Antifaschist*innen, die seit Jahrzehnten in Sachsen von dieser Repression auf unterschiedliche Weise betroffen sind und waren, falsch an.


Für uns ist es gerade besonders wichtig jene zu unterstützen, die im Moment am meisten leiden: Henrys Familie, die diesen Verlust verarbeiten muss.


Wir möchten daher Spenden für die Familie sammeln, damit diese mit den Auswirkungen des Todes nicht alleine bleibt.


Spenden Information:


–

https://www.antifaostkomplex.org/erklarung-zum-tod-von-henry/


Wir wünschen uns, dass Henry nun in Frieden ruhen kann.

title: When the city is burning #60

«17 χρόνια μετά, στέλνουμε ένα σινιάλο αλληλεγγύης στα συντρόφια στη Χιλή, συνδέοντας τους αγώνες για μνήμη και εξέγερση. Τα μεσάνυχτα της Παρασκευής 22 Μαΐου, βάλαμε φλεγόμενα οδοφράγματα με κάδους σε κεντρικούς δρόμους των Εξαρχείων σε 8 διαφορετικά σημεία».

https://athens.indymedia.org/post/1641445/

«Το γεγονός αυτό αποσιωπήθηκε πλήρως απ’ την ΓΑΔΑ και δεν κυκλοφόρησε σε κανένα μέσο, κάτι που χει επαναληφθεί με επιθέσεις στα συγκεκριμένα δικαστήρια στο παρελθόν. Η συγκεκριμένη δράση πραγματώθηκε με την επιδίωξη να αποτελέσει μια πρώτη ελάχιστη-στοιχειώδη ένδειξη αλληλεγγύης στα 8 υπόδικα αναρχικά συντρόφια».

https://athens.indymedia.org/post/1641512/

«Aλληλέγγυα στον αγώνα της Κοινότητας Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών πραγματοποιήσαμε σε βραδινές ώρες επίθεση στο παράρτημα του Υπουργείου Πολιτισμού που βρίσκεται στο κέντρο της Πάτρας, στην οδό Υψηλάντου, προκαλώντας φθορές στο κτίριο».

https://athens.indymedia.org/post/1641769/

«Tα ξημερώματα της Τετάρτης 24/6/2026 επιλέξαμε να επιτεθούμε και καταφέραμε το σπάσιμο των καμερών που βρίσκονταν στο κτήριο διοίκησης. Πάνω από τα κεφάλια των security που βρίσκονταν στο φυλάκιο και για καλή τους τύχη επέλεξαν να μην εμπλακούν και μείναν κλεισμένοι στην τρύπα τους με κατεβασμένα τα ρολά».

https://athens.indymedia.org/post/1641831/

«Η μέθοδος και τα υλικά που χρησιμοποιήθηκαν είναι απλά, καθώς μόνο με την χρήση μιας ισχυρής κόλλας και μιας τηλεκάρτας ή και οποιασδήποτε άλλης κάρτας, μπλοκάρεται το ΑΤΜ και έστω και για μικρό χρονικό διάστημα διαταράσσεται η λειτουργία της τράπεζας και προκαλείται μια ελάχιστη ζημιά, με ασφαλή και γρήγορο τρόπο».

https://athens.indymedia.org/post/1641863

«Αναλαμβάνουμε την ευθύνη για την εμπρηστική επίθεση στη συμμορία της ομάδας ΔΕΛΤΑ επί των οδών Τσαμαδού και Τοσίτσα, το βράδυ του Σαββάτου στα Εξάρχεια. Ομάδα συντρόφων και συντροφισσών προσέγγισε την εν λόγω ομάδα και την έτρεψε σε άτακτη φυγή εν μέσω κραυγών πανικού. Ήταν ένας τρόπος από τη μεριά μας να δείξουμε οτι με οργάνωση, πειθαρχεία και κυρίως ΘΕΛΗΣΗ για δράση το δόγμα νόμος και τάξη ξεφτιλίζεται στην πράξη».

https://athens.indymedia.org/post/1641896/

«Η Αστυνομία είναι για όποιον και όποια έχει μάτια ένας κατοχικός στρατός. Κι αν κάποιοι μπάτσοι είναι ανοιχτά δολοφόνοι ρομά, αναπήρων, μεταναστών και αναρχικών, άλλοι επιτελούν τον ρόλο του μιζερόμπατσου, του μαλάκα της καθημερινής ζωής. Αυτόν τον ρόλο κατέχει η δημοτική αστυνομία. […] Γι’ αυτό και εμείς, για το καλωσόρισμα των 30 νέων τους συναδέλφων, ανακαινίσαμε την πρόσοψη του κτηρίου με τρόπο που πιστεύουμε ότι ταιριάζει καλύτερα στα συναισθήματα των δημοτών. Την Παρασκευή 24/07 πραγματοποιήσαμε φθορές στην είσοδο του κτηρίου της δημοτικής αστυνομίας, ασκώντας και εμείς με την σειρά μας το δικό μας «δικαίωμά στην πόλη». author: By L. Cam Anderson, Contributor
title: Hennepin County Charges Far-Right Influencers Following Election Fraud Stunt
content:
Minneapolis, MN – Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty

announced

 felony charges of identity theft and unlawful voting against far-right influencers James O’Keefe and Cam Higby

on Wednesday

, Oct. 28.


“Before the August 11 primary election this office was very clear that reports of unlawful activity related to the election would be investigated and charged if appropriate,” Moriarty said during a press conference held on Oct. 27.


The charges stem from a series of videos produced by the duo during the Minnesota primary election on Aug. 11, where the two attempted to document what they alleged was a flaw in the state’s voter registration system that allows voters to prove their residence by having neighbors vouch for them. 


In the videos, Higby and O’Keefe, representing O’Keefe’s Florida-based Citizens Justice League, provide the names of actual voters in the area to poll workers but stop short of signing the oath to receive the ballot.


“Minnesota law states clearly that no individual shall intentionally misrepresent their identity in applying for a ballot,” Moriarty said, addressing the fact that neither man actually received a ballot. “The charges filed today are appropriate to address the conduct of Mr. O’Keefe and Mr. Higby.”


Read the charging complaints at the end of the article or click the name:

Cam Higby

 /

James O’Keefe


The vouching system in Minnesota is rarely used, accounting for less than 0.6% of all votes cast during the 2024 election, according to Moriarty. The system is most often used among those who live in senior living facilities, where residents often do not obtain drivers licenses updated with the facility’s address.


Despite this, both men disguised themselves as Muslim women and visited polling locations across Minneapolis. 


In one video published Aug. 14 Higby made a clear case for election fraud against himself. In it, he appears dressed in a niqab, with the area around his eyes painted a shade of brown, while attempting to vote under his assumed aliases, all of which were the real names of registered voters.


Throughout the video, Higby repeatedly asks the poll workers if the potential voter being vouched for needs a form of identification. At the first polling location, the poll worker tells him the other person needs one.


“No,” Higby said in a forced accent. “We don’t have ID. We no have pocket.”


If a voter is being vouched for at a polling place, they still need to provide either their Minnesota driver’s license, an ID card number or the last four digits of their social security number,

according to the Secretary of State website

.


Poll workers immediately reported Higby and O’Keefe’s group after their visits,

Minnesota Secretary of State Steve Simon told KSTP News later that day

.


“Their apparent goal was to cast doubt on one or more Minnesota election laws that have been in force for over fifty years,” Simon said in a statement. “Instead, they revealed their ignorance of how those laws actually work – while putting themselves in legal jeopardy.”


O’Keefe defended his and Higby’s actions that day by citing his earlier work with Project Veritas “investigating” the 2012 and 2016 elections in New Hampshire.


Project Veritas, founded by O’Keefe in June 2010, was

described by the Southern Poverty Law Center

 in 2022 as a “hard-right propaganda group that engages in sting operations.”


Related – 2025:

Newly Revealed FBI Document Confirms Collaboration Between DC Police and Discredited Far-Right Group Project Veritas


In New Hampshire in 2012, O’Keefe’s group visited a polling location and requested the ballots for numerous dead people whose names had yet to be culled from voter rolls. The state opened a criminal investigation into O’Keefe and his group,

quietly dropping the charges the next year

.


The strategy used in Minneapolis in August of sending somebody into a polling location under false pretenses dressed in a burqa is not entirely new to O’Keefe. During the 2016 presidential election, a female Project Veritas journalist dressed in a burqa entered a New York City polling location and requested the ballot of Huma Abedin.


On Oct. 26, two days before Hennepin County announced the charges, the two attempted the same investigation in Florida, both still dressed as Muslims.


In 2010,

O’Keefe pleaded guilty

 to entering federal property under false pretenses, for which he was ordered to pay a $1,500 fine and placed on three years’ probation …

author: Unknown
title: Tuncay Yılmaz: We want to build a united front of resistance in Europe - Part Two
content:
ANF spoke to Tuncay Yılmaz, founding co-chair of the Socialist Refoundation Party (SYKP), about the outcomes of the Cologne meeting, the need for a common struggle, the situation of left-wing and democratic forces in the face of the rising far right in Europe, and the roadmap for the proposed alliance.


The first part of this interview can be read

here

. 


On 17 October, 25 organisations from different political traditions came together in Cologne. Similar attempts to build alliances have been made in Europe before. Why has the need to establish a common platform for struggle emerged again today? What distinguishes this meeting from previous initiatives?


Organisations from different political traditions and social groups in Europe have come together at various times. Previously, there was the European Assembly for Peace and Democracy (ABDEM). We then extended the organisation of the Peoples' Democratic Congress (HDK) in Turkey to Europe, establishing a broad organisation under the name HDK Europe. This organisation later became the European Democratic Forces Union (ADGB) and continued its activities under that name. Most recently, ahead of the NATO summit, a joint initiative called PANEV was established against imperialist aggression, wars and NATO.


All these initiatives emerged from efforts to find ways for the forces of democracy, peace, equality and freedom to become better organised in Europe and pursue more effective political action against the enormous aggressive power confronting us.


The alliances we established at different times sometimes lost their effectiveness, both because of changes in the objective conditions in which they were formed and, to speak frankly, because of our own shortcomings. This is a reality, and we are aware of it. Indeed, this was one of the issues on the agenda of our meeting. We want to learn from our previous experiences.


However, the mistakes we made in the past or the changes we have experienced should not prevent us from bringing democratic forces together again and carrying out a common struggle. And indeed, they are not preventing us. One of the main motivations that brought us together at this meeting was the growing hostility towards migrants in the European countries where we live, the rise of the right, fascist movements coming to power and increasing state violence. The fact that laws targeting asylum seekers have reached almost inhumane proportions is also deeply concerning to all of us. We want to build a united front of resistance against all of this.


At the same time, however, all our attention, thoughts and concerns are focused on developments in Turkey. Looking at Turkey, we see a totalitarian regime being built step by step. Everyone who opposes it becomes a target. Presidential candidates are arrested. Selahattin Demirtaş has been imprisoned for years, as has Figen Yüksekdağ. Ekrem İmamoğlu was subsequently arrested. The Republican People's Party (CHP), which prides itself on being the founding party of the state, is also under serious pressure. Attempts are being made to divide the party, and many of its representatives have been arrested.


Alongside all this, a negotiation process has begun. It has not yet reached the stage of a peace process. However, this negotiation process has the potential to generate a collective strength capable of pushing back attacks on democracy through the positive developments it could bring to the country's political life. Despite this, we see that the political authorities are acting with appalling arbitrariness in this process as well.


To speak frankly, this process has been made possible by the determination and goodwill of Abdullah Öcalan and the Kurdish Freedom Movement. After all, decisions were taken to lay down arms and dissolve the organisation. These decisions represent a profound transformation in the movement's historical existence.


Despite this, the state continues to display an extremely indifferent and unserious attitude towards taking steps on these issues, potentially jeopardising the process. Its actions could allow the anti-democratic practices it maintains throughout the country to continue in different forms in this area as well. We can all see that, for months, instead of implementing the legal arrangements brought onto Parliament's agenda with broad support, the authorities have merely continued saying, "We want this as well, and we want that too."
