title: Özgür Sevgi Göral: France’s dilemmas also exist in Turkey - Part Two
content:
ANF spoke to academic Özgür Sevgi Göral, who is currently in Paris and has participated in the demonstrations, about the historical foundations of the protests and their potential.


Part one of this interview can be read

here

. 


When you compare these protests with the history of social movements and youth activism in Turkey, what similarities or significant differences do you see? Is the possibility of their influence spreading to Turkey limited, or what factors might increase that possibility?


This is a very difficult question. Youth movements in Turkey constitute a very broad field, and although I try to follow them, they are not my primary area of research. Therefore, I do not think I am in a position to compare the two countries in this respect. Perhaps I can offer just a few observations. Turkey has witnessed powerful youth movements, although they have been heavily suppressed, particularly over the past decade. We can assume that the racialised capitalist regime in which we live, and its various manifestations, have also generated considerable dissatisfaction among young people in Turkey. Moreover, even under Turkey's extremely harsh political conditions, youth movements have repeatedly emerged and made themselves visible over the past ten years. However, we know that for particular grievances or isolated political revolts to develop into powerful political mobilisation, there must be an accumulated history and tradition of struggle capable of protecting and developing itself. There must also be different political organisations operating at various levels, sometimes reaching agreements with one another and sometimes coming into conflict. I do not know to what extent such conditions exist or are possible in Turkey today, although there are certain emerging centres of struggle.


On the other hand, I think that rather than speaking of the protests spreading from one country to another, we can speak of a certain "simultaneity". Simultaneity, a concept frequently used in the literature on political and social movements, suggests that movements in different parts of the world during the same historical period can inspire one another in terms of political programmes, repertoires of mobilisation and demands, and that revolutionary ideas can travel across geographical boundaries. This could also apply to Turkey at a moment when the repertoire of street protests has some room to expand. However, the state's security strategy and policies against the accumulated experience of the Kurdish struggle, particularly the rapid criminalisation of forms of political violence and their framing through the concept of "terrorism", have unfortunately also proved effective among different political and social movements. Therefore, I cannot determine whether this wave of protests might produce rapid consequences for youth movements in Turkey through an effect of simultaneity, or what possibilities might exist for such a development. I am sure that my colleagues who are active in this field and study these movements have much more to say on the subject than I do.


Do these protests offer the prospect of lasting social and political transformation?


I think this question is extremely important, not only in relation to these protests but also in terms of the situation that widespread mass protests and uprisings have faced for some time. The latest youth uprising began on a broader scale than previous ones. However, in France and many other countries, it is debatable how successful such uprisings have been in producing concrete political and social transformation, despite all their potential. This movement also faces the dilemma your question points to. The central issue here is the dual nature of the demands of the groups driving the movement. There is a tension between those who prioritise short-term problems concerning the existing education system and those who focus on how wealth and resources should be distributed and on the broader prospect of anti-capitalist transformation. For now, it is difficult to say that this uprising has a programme and organisational structure based on a broader emancipatory perspective extending beyond its concrete demands. The government currently appears to have taken a step back by announcing that it will abolish Parcoursup, the university admissions system, in 2028. However, unless a strong and sustained bloc of political struggle can be established, it could introduce essentially the same …

author: Nick Everett
title: Will Israel’s election outcome make life better for Palestinians? Not likely.
content:
In the lead-up to Israel’s 27 October election, media headlines declared this would be the most “consequential” in Israel’s history. At stake is the fate of Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, who faces corruption charges at home and an international arrest warrant for war crimes in Gaza.

Israeli politicians debated the cost of living, the independence of the judiciary, conscription of ultra-Orthodox Jews into the military, a state inquiry into security failings on 7 October and Israel’s growing isolation abroad. Not up for debate was Israel’s Gaza genocide, nor the massive expansion of Israeli settlements, settler violence and military invasions in the West Bank, nor Israel’s seizure of territory in southern Lebanon and Syria. 

This was a contest between two blocs, a pro-Netanyahu coalition of far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties against an alliance of centrist and right-wing Zionist parties seeking to depose him, led by retired General Gadi Eisenkot, the former military chief of staff. A third bloc, made up of the two Arab-majority parties, the Joint List and Ra’am, was initially barred from participation by Israel’s Central Elections Committee before the supreme court overturned the ban.

Right-wing parties Likud and Otzma Yehudit petitioned for their exclusion, accusing the Arab-majority parties and candidates of denying Israel’s existence as a Jewish and democratic state, supporting armed struggle against Israel or inciting racism. A ban was, however, upheld against Sami Abu Shehadeh, leader of the Palestinian nationalist Balad party and one of the Joint List candidates, on the grounds that he had supported armed struggle against Israel. 

The evidence? An opinion piece published in 

Alaraby

 on 8 October 2023, in which Abu Shehadeh described the previous day’s Hamas-led attack on Israel as a “significant historical event”. 

Accusations of “inciting racism” against Ra’am and the Arab List are of course rank hypocrisy coming from Netanyahu and his coalition partners who have 

called for

 the “total annihilation” of Gaza’s cities and the burning of Lebanon, as well as the death penalty for Palestinians accused of “terrorism” offences.

On the eve of the election, Netanyahu’s social media posts drew attention to long queues of Palestinian voters at polling stations and urged Likud supporters to come out and vote.

“If we don't wake up now, we'll find ourselves with a government of Mansour Abbas and Ahmed Tibi”, he said, referring to the leaders of the two Arab-majority parties.

Netanyahu’s coalition ally and Jewish supremacist Itamar Ben-Gvir described the level of Arab voter turnout—people exercising their democratic right to vote—as “crazy”. As national security minister, Ben-Gvir has armed Israeli settlers and established a paramilitary police force in the West Bank.

Basel Smotrich, another Jewish supremacist Netanyahu ally, and leader of the Religious Zionism party, announced he had suspended his election day campaigning to convene an emergency meeting to discuss what he described as unusually high turnout among Arab voters, alleging voter fraud. 

While Netanyahu failed to win this election, he remains far from defeated. His ruling coalition, dominated by Likud, will likely secure 53 of the Knesset’s 120 seats, a major drop from the 64 seats he won in 2022, and significantly short of a majority. However, the opposition bloc is trailing with 48 seats. The opposition’s only pathway to power is to govern with the support of the two Arab-majority parties, the Joint List and Ra’am, which together secured an additional 19 seats (nearly double the ten they secured in 2022).

This would not be unprecedented. In 1993, the Oslo Accords were signed by a minority Israeli government with the support of the Arab List parties.

In 2021, Ra’am leader Mansour Abbas broke with the Arab List to join an eight-party coalition, the first time an Arab-majority party had joined an Israeli government. For Abbas, this was an opportunity to secure some short-lived investment in Palestinian communities inside Israel, while turning his back on the elephant in the room: the Israeli occupation. The coalition collapsed within a year following defections from its right flank.

Abbas has declared his intention again to seek a coalition that can unseat Netanyahu. His Islamist Ra’am party put a Jewish former police chief in second position on its slate. However, such overtures have so far been rebuffed.  …

title: Fransa'da ırkçılık ve İslamofobi karşıtı gösteriler düzenlendi
content:
Fransa'da farklı sendika, dernek ve kitle örgütü kuruluşlarının çağrısıyla Paris, Strazburg, Roubaix, Stains, Nanterre, La Courneuve dahil farklı kentlerde ırkçılık karşıtları bir araya geldi.

Ülkede artan ırkçılığa ve İslamofobiye tepki verilen gösterilerde, 23 Ekim'de Yvelines ilinde düzenlenen terör saldırısında hayatını kaybeden Kongo asıllı Fransız Pengo Bossio Wangi anıldı.

Gösterilerde, söz konusu ırkçı saldırıda yaralanan 1'i çocuk olmak üzere 5 kişiye yönelik destek mesajları da dile getirildi.

Başkent Paris'te Stalingrad Muharebesi Meydanı'nda yerel saatle 19.00'da başlayan gösteriye yüzlerce kişi katıldı.

Göstericiler, "Irkçılık bir görüş değil, hayatları paramparça eden bir suçtur", "Paramparça olan hayatlardan ziyade kırılan vitrinlere şefkat gösteriyorlar" ve "Irkçılık öldürür" yazılı pankartlar taşıdı.

Göstericiler, ırkçı söylemleri yaymakla suçlanan CNews kanalında çalışan bir gazetecinin gösteriye katılmasına "CNews dışarı" ve "CNews katil, (Cumhurbaşkanı Emmanuel) Macron suç ortağı" sloganları atarak tepki gösterdi.

Irkçılıkla mücadele derneği SOS Racisme'in Başkanı Dominique Sopo, burada yaptığı konuşmada, birkaç yıldır ülkede ırkçı saikli suçların yeniden işlenmeye başlandığını söyledi.

Sopo, bazı medya organlarının bünyelerinde ırkçı söylemlerin sarf edilmesine izin verdiğini belirterek, bu söylemin son derece "ciddi" olduğuna dikkati çekti.

Yvelines'e bağlı Trappes kentindeki saldırıyı yapan teröristin "siyahilere ve Araplara saldırarak 17 Ekim'deki gösterilerinde, dükkanı yağmalanan esnafın öcünü almak istediğini" dile getirdiğini aktaran Sopo, terör saldırısından birkaç gün önce Fransız televizyon kanallarında eylemlerdeki yağma olaylarıyla ilgili ırkçı bir çerçeve kullanıldığını belirtti.

Trappes Belediye Başkanı Ali Rabeh ise Ulusal Birlik (RN) Partisi Başkanı Jordan Bardella'nın daha önce Trappes kentini "Paris'e 30 dakika mesafedeki Kabil'e" benzettiğini hatırlattı.

Rabeh, Trappes'a yönelik damgalayıcı sözler kullananları terör saldırısının failine silah vermekle suçlayarak, "Kanallarda durmaksızın aktarılan yabancılara, göçmenlere, Müslümanlara karşı sarf edilen nefret söylemleri, Fransızların bir kısmının insanlıktan çıkarılmasına neden oldu." dedi.

Bu durumun, bu kişilerin "iç düşmanlar" gibi gösterilmesine sebebiyet verdiğini kaydeden Rabeh, ırkçılık zehrinin tüm ülkeye bulaştığını dile getirdi.

Irkçılık Karşıtı Koalisyon'dan yapılan açıklamaya göre, Paris'te Cumhuriyet Meydanı'nda düzenlenmesi planlanan bir diğer gösteri, Paris Emniyet Müdürlüğünce yasaklandı.

Sosyal medyaya yansıyan görüntülere göre, bazı göstericiler, yasağa rağmen Cumhuriyet Meydanı yakınlarında toplandı.

Sokakta yere oturan göstericiler, Fransa'nın ulusal marşı La Marseillaise'i okudu.

Polis, eylemi dağıtmak için kalkanlarıyla göstericileri iterek bölgeden uzaklaştırmaya çalıştı.

Yvelines ilinde 23 Ekim'de bir kişi, bulunduğu araçtan etraftakilere ateş açmıştı. Saldırıda 1 kişi hayatını kaybetmiş, 5 kişi ağır yaralanmıştı.

39 yaşındaki saldırgan Kevin T, olay yerinde gözaltına alınmıştı.

Fransa Cumhurbaşkanı Emmanuel Macron, saldırının ırkçı nitelikte bir terör saldırısı olduğunu duyurmuştu.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: [Valladolid] Apertura de nuevo local de CNT
content:
Antifascistas, antirracistas, anticapitalistas, transfeministas e internacionalistas. En medio de una convocatoria de huelga general por la vivienda y contra todos los poderes que viven de desangrar a la clase trabajadora, CNT Valladolid inaugura un nuevo local en calle Merced, 6, de Valladolid, entre las plazas de Santa Cruz y Circular.


Hace más de dos años empezamos un proyecto muy ilusionante. Nuestro local se quedaba pequeño y teníamos que buscar otro. Hicimos un proceso de reflexión colectiva, para tener claras nuestras necesidades presentes y futuras. Una tienda de fontanería se ha convertido en un sindicato como el nuestro, con más salas donde reunirse, un salón amplio en el que convocar actos… Un nuevo espacio en Valladolid a disposición de todas las personas trabajadoras.


A pesar de que quedan retoques, el pasado 17 de octubre nos decidimos a abrir puertas en un acto en el que nos reunimos la afiliacIón con personas afines del presente y del futuro. Contamos con las actuaciones de Jesús Puebla Mimo, de Rubén Ruiz, Rosa Vicente y José Luis Alonso, de Chusma y de Juguillos, de Astrolabio, y tuvimos ocasión de mover el esqueleto con las aportaciones de Eva DJ. No faltaron el recorrido por el nuevo local, el picoteo hecho a mano en comida y bebida, y sobre todo las ganas de llenar de vida esta nueva casa para la rebeldía y la defensa frente a empresaurios y politicastros de todos nuestros derechos actuales y los que nos inventemos en el futuro. Para todo ello y más, contad con CNT, vuestra herramienta de lucha, vuestro sindicato de clase, vuestra alternativa sindical.


A continuación hemos puesto en marcha unas jornadas de inauguración de las que tenéis información en las redes y web de CNT.


Reproducimos a continuación el manifiesto que refleja esta nueva etapa:


Hoy, sábado, 17 de octubre, inauguramos una nueva etapa en CNT Valladolid.


Estrenamos un espacio más amplio. Un espacio donde pueda entrar más gente, donde podamos encontrarnos, organizarnos y construir juntas una respuesta colectiva a la realidad que vivimos.


Porque este local no es solamente un lugar nuevo. Es un espacio de encuentro para quienes entendemos que nuestros derechos no son concesiones, que la dignidad no se negocia y que nuestra fuerza está en la lucha obrera.


Y cuando decimos clase trabajadora, no hablamos solo de quienes tienen un contrato o un empleo. También hablamos de quienes trabajan sin derechos, de quienes sostienen los cuidados y de quienes encuentran las puertas cerradas al empleo por su identidad o su condición.


Porque si el sistema utiliza esas diferencias para dividirnos y para colocar a unas personas en posiciones de mayor vulnerabilidad, el sindicalismo tiene que hacer justamente lo contrario:

reconocernos como parte de una misma clase y organizarnos juntas.


Por eso abrimos este espacio.


Para que haya más gente, más organización y más lucha.


Porque somos CNT.


CNT tiene una historia profundamente ligada a la organización de la clase trabajadora y a la lucha por los derechos laborales y sociales.


Antes que este local, CNT tuvo varios, cada uno con su historia: desahucios, asaltos policiales, atentados… Desde la calle Francisco Zarandona multiplicó por diez su afiliación en tiempos de la segunda republica; desde los pactos de la moncloa, superando multiples dificultades, hemos crecido en varios locales en Valladolid que han ido abriendo cada vez más brecha en la provincia y en la ciudad. Hasta llegar a este en el que nos encontramos


Somos anarcosindicalistas. Entendemos que quienes vivimos de nuestro trabajo tenemos capacidad para defender nuestros derechos colectivamente y para construir otras formas de relacionarnos y organizarnos frente a la explotación.


Tenemos una memoria sindical fuerte y combativa. Pero no queremos convertir esa memoria en una fotografía, ni mirar hacia atrás únicamente para recordar lo que fuimos.

Nuestra memoria nos obliga a mirar hacia delante.


Porque el sistema contra el que se organizaron quienes nos precedieron no ha desaparecido. La explotación adopta nuevas formas. La precariedad se normaliza. Trabajar ya no garantiza unas condiciones de vida dignas. Y quienes acumulan riqueza siguen teniendo capacidad para decidir sobre nuestras vidas.


Por eso estamos aquí.


Porque la lucha sigue.


Y esa lucha sigue hoy en múltiples frentes que se complementan.


Una de ellas es la

lucha antifascista

.


Estamos viendo crecer discursos que alimentan el odio y el miedo …

author: mark
title: Bigger, Stronger, More Violent: The EU’s Plans for Frontex
content:
On 27 October 2026, the European Commission presented its proposal for a new Frontex Regulation. The proposal would massively expand Frontex’s powers, staff, budget and activities, both inside and outside the EU. At the same time, some of the already very weak Fundamental Rights safeguards will be further weakened.

We oppose this proposal of the new regulation and call for an International Action Day on 18 December 2026, asking groups in all countries to participate however they can.

 Find here the callout for the Action Day and below our analysis of the new regulation proposal. 


1. Tripling Frontex’s border force and massively increasing its funding


What are the planned changes?


The EU wants to increase Frontex’s standing corps from 10,000 to 30,000 officers by 2041. This includes creating a new European Border and Return Reserve, made up of national officers trained by Frontex.


Frontex officers would also receive more powers to act independently. They could intercept people at borders, search vehicles and belongings, identify people for deportation and carry out deportations by air, land or sea.


The proposal also removes the general requirement for national border guards to be physically present when Frontex officers use force. 


The rules on the use of force would also change. The specific requirement that handcuffs are used only on people who pose a danger to themselves or others would be removed and replaced by broader criteria. The same applies to the use of batons and pepper spray. The use of service dogs would be explicitly allowed, while several specific safeguards concerning the oversight of force would be removed from the annex.


The European Commission has proposed a budget of €11.9 billion for Frontex for 2028–2034. The reform adds additional possibilities for Frontex to access more funds, including a duty for the Commission to consider the Agency as a priority partner when engaging third parties in Union funded projects. 


Frontex would also be able to help determine priorities for EU research and innovation funding while receiving funding from the same programmes.


Why is this problematic?


This would mean a massive expansion of the EU’s militarised border regime, with more officers, more equipment and more powers to stop, detain and deport people on the move. For people on the move this will mean more violent and deadly borders. 


Billions of euros would be spent on strengthening border enforcement instead of providing housing, healthcare, education and support for people on the move.One year of Frontex’s proposed budget could instead fund: 


A year of schooling for 121,000 students (Germany 2024)


More than 5,000 energy-efficient social homes (Barcelona)


A year of healthcare for 3,800 people (EU average cost 2023)


EU resettlement support for more than 125,000 people 


More than 725,000 basic German language courses at Goethe institute 


More than 1,400 rescue ships like SOS Humanity


The expansion would also strengthen the border-industrial complex, including the arms and security industry that profits from border surveillance and enforcement.


2. Turning Frontex into the central EU deportation agency


What are the planned changes?


Frontex would become the central EU agency for planning, coordinating and carrying out deportations. It would be involved in practically every step of the deportation process, from identifying people and obtaining travel documents to organising deportation flights and so-called reintegration assistance. A new Return Coordination Centre would be established within Frontex to coordinate these activities.


A new SIRENE office would give Frontex access to additional information from the Schengen Information System concerning deportations and refusals of entry.


A new hit/no-hit system would allow Europol and Eurojust to check whether Frontex holds personal data relevant to their work, further conflating migration and security issues.


Frontex would be able to restrict people’s rights to access, correct or erase their personal data under certain conditions. The proposal would also facilitate systematic transfers of deportation-related personal data to third countries.


Under Articles 63 and 64, Frontex could support deportations starting from countries outside the EU. This includes deportations carried out under the laws of those countries, even when there is no deportation decision from an EU member state.


Member states would have to …

title: Study reveals 86.7% of Kurds in Munich report discrimination
content:
The Kurdish population living in Germany is estimated at approximately 1.5 million. An expert report published by Mediendienst Integration on 15 October 2026, titled Kurds in Germany: Between Asylum, Social Participation and Anti-Kurdish Racism, examines the demographic situation of Kurds in the country, asylum procedures, social participation and experiences of discrimination.


The expert study underpinning the report was prepared by Professor Çinur Ghaderi of the Protestant University of Applied Sciences Bochum (EvH Bochum). The study was supported by the Robert Bosch Foundation.


The Munich component of the research examined the living conditions of Kurds and their experiences of racism in detail. The study, prepared by Professor Çinur Ghaderi, Monique Kaulertz and Mary Lam, was conducted at the request of the Democracy Unit (Fachstelle für Demokratie) of the City of Munich.


183 out of 210 respondents reported experiencing discrimination


The Munich study, conducted in 2025 and published in January 2026, revealed the extent of discrimination faced by Kurds in the city. The research included a quantitative survey involving 210 participants, alongside 23 individual expert interviews and nine focus group discussions. Approximately 65 people participated in the focus group discussions.


Of the 210 survey respondents, 183 reported experiencing discrimination at least once in Munich during the previous 12 months. This represented 86.7 percent of participants.


Among respondents, 66.4 percent reported experiencing humiliating behaviour, while 64.4 percent encountered disrespectful or condescending attitudes. Half of the participants said they had experienced exclusion, 44.2 percent reported verbal abuse or insults, and 11.8 percent said they had been physically assaulted.


Among those who reported discrimination, 57.4 percent identified their Kurdish identity as a reason, while 56.8 percent cited their origin. The study noted that discrimination based on Kurdish identity could also occur in connection with other identities and affiliations.


The researchers emphasised that the findings reflected only the experiences of participants in Munich and should not be regarded as a nationwide survey representative of the entire Kurdish population in Germany.


Discrimination does not occur only on the streets


According to the research, Kurds experience various forms of discrimination in public spaces, within the education system, in workplaces and in their interactions with public institutions. The findings show that discrimination is not limited to overt insults and physical attacks but also manifests through condescending behaviour, exclusion and institutional barriers.


The report highlights that security-focused approaches towards Kurdish political and civil organisations can reinforce social mistrust and prejudice. It also notes that people with insecure residence status and stateless Kurds are in a more vulnerable position because of legal uncertainties and barriers to accessing social resources.


The researchers also emphasise that the Kurdish community should not be viewed solely through its experiences of discrimination. The report states that Kurds contribute to Munich's cultural, social and political life and engage in activities that strengthen social solidarity and support democratic participation.


The exact Kurdish population in Germany remains unknown


According to data published by Mediendienst Integration on 22 October 2026, approximately 1.5 million Kurds live in Germany. However, the country does not maintain official population statistics based on Kurdish ethnic identity.


One of the main reasons is that population records in Germany are based on criteria such as citizenship and country of birth rather than ethnic identity. Kurds may hold German, Turkish, Syrian, Iraqi or Iranian citizenship, while some are stateless.


According to data obtained by Mediendienst Integration from the German Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF), the number of asylum applications submitted by Kurds between 2010 and June 2026 reached 656,245. Of these, 607,896 were registered as initial applications. During the same period, 378,316 people were granted protection status.


However, these figures do not directly indicate the total Kurdish population living in Germany. Estimates of the Kurdish population must also take into account other forms of migration, family reunification, naturalisation and …

title: Perdió Trump y los demócratas recuperan el control de las Cámaras: velorio en la Casa Rosada
content:
Los demócratas dominarán el próximo Congreso. Consiguieron triunfos en estados en disputa como los de Iowa, Kansas, Maine, Carolina del Norte, Ohio, Carolina del Sur y Texas, que le permitirán controlar el Senado. La votación general donde superan a los republicanos por más de diez puntos le permitirán obtener una amplia mayoría que se expresará en la Cámara de Representantes (Diputados), que se renueva por completo. La derrota de Trump ha sido un golpe muy fuerte para el gobierno argentino, que se ató a su destino político, y que fue correspondido por el gobierno estadounidense con apoyos políticos y financieros en momentos clave.

Por Guillermo Cieza, para Huella del Sur.


En el Senado, según los últimos conteos, los demócratas habrían obtenido 54 curules y los republicanos apenas retienen 44. En la Cámara de Diputados la diferencia será aún más aplastante. Los demócratas obtendrían 231 representantes, contra 139 de los republicanos.


El deterioro económico de la mayoría de la población estadounidense y sus promesas incumplidas de acabar con las guerras, bajar el precio de los combustibles y publicar el archivo Epstein, parecen haber sido decisivas en estas elecciones. La marea azul (demócrata) parece haberse asentado en el fuerte apoyo del voto latino (una comunidad asediada por las deportaciones), en el cambio de voto de los jóvenes y en la ruptura de sectores rurales con la gestión (por razones económicas y morales).


Gina Hinojosa será la primera latina en gobernar Texas, un estado de fuerte ascendencia republicana. Lo mismo sucederá en California donde se impuso Xavier Becerra, por amplio margen. Otra de las sorpresas fue el triunfo de Abdul El Sayed que ganó en Michigan y se convirtió en el primer senador musulmán de EEUU.


También hay un crecimiento del ala izquierda del Partido demócrata. Janeese Lewis George, miembro del partido Socialista Democrático de América (DSA) ganó las elecciones a la alcaldía de Washington DC, la capital del país. El resultado fue abrumador. La candidata socialista democrática obtuvo el 84% contra su rival republicana, Rhonda Hamilton, que obtuvo el 10,3%.


La derrota del gobierno republicano que se estima en una cifra no inferior a 10 puntos, y la pérdida del Congreso, coloca al presidente Trump en una situación muy complicada, por las dificultades legislativas que tendrá en el futuro y porque estallará en su propio partido una feroz interna para sucederlo.


El gobierno de Argentina también ve agravar sus dificultades. Apoyó a Bolsonaro que perdió las elecciones en Brasil y después se fugó con ayuda de Milei, creando un importante conflicto con el principal socio comercial de nuestro país. Ahora advierte que su mentor y sostén en Estados Unidos se ha convertido en un “pato rengo”, que ha perdido carisma y poder. Finalmente advierte que en las elecciones estadounidenses el voto joven se volcó mayoritariamente a la oposición y que este fenómeno ya está empezando a producirse en la Argentina.


Para finalizar y reducir un poco el triunfalismo que se ha apoderado de distintos sectores de la oposición en la Argentina, habría que recordar que en Estados Unidos tanto demócratas como republicanos comparten los siguientes acuerdos.


1. El gran enemigo a derrotar es China. Debilitar y tratar de cortar la expansión de esta nueva potencia emergente es la prioridad. El tiempo juega a favor de China que crece mucho más rápido que Estados Unidos, y que está armando una política de alianzas que pueden deteriorar la vigencia del dólar como moneda rectora de los intercambios internacionales. La guerra, que es cada vez más impopular en Estados Unidos y lo empieza a ser en Europa, se les presenta a las elites occidentales como la única forma de evitar la pérdida de la hegemonía mundial.


2. author: Joshua Carroll
title: Home Office Unlawfully Blocks Gaza Children From Joining Families in UK
content:
The Home Office is refusing to allow mothers and their children trapped in Gaza to join family members in the UK, even after a judge said the government’s position is unlawful.


The two women, who have five children between them aged seven and under, were told to submit biometric information as part of a security check to obtain family reunification visas.


But the application centre where they would need to submit fingerprints and other information has been closed since the start of Israel’s genocide in October 2023.


On 30 September, a judge in the immigration and asylum chamber of the upper tribunal ruled that the Home Office, by refusing to waive the biometric requirement for these families, had unlawfully applied its unsafe journeys policy.


In her ruling, judge Fiona Lindsley said the mothers and children – who have been granted anonymity – “have too little food and are suffering from malnutrition. They dare not go to US aid collection points as they are aware that people have been killed by Israeli forces at these places.”


She said the children’s fathers, who are based in the UK, were also suffering severe psychological hardship. One has been diagnosed with PTSD due to his experiences in Gaza “coupled with the continuous threat” to the survival of his wife and children, she added.


The Home Office has appealed the judge’s decision and a hearing is set for 16 December. But the Greater Manchester Immigration Aid Unit (GMIAU), whic

h


represents the families,

 said th

at process will further delay reunification and put the families “in grave danger” in Gaza.


“The children are all traumatised,” said Decla Palmer, a lawyer from GMIAU. “They have gone to bed every night to the sound of bombs, suffering from nightmares, with rats and mice crawling around their tent. The mothers are completely exhausted and without hope.”


“Every day the families remain in Gaza, they are at risk of death,” said GMIAU.


Surgeons who have worked in Gaza have said Israeli forces

 deliberately and systematically

 kill children. Dutch newspaper Volkskrant last year

published testimony from doctors

 who had encountered at least 114 children with multiple bullet wounds in the head and chest.


A Home Office spokesperson told Novara Media that “enrolment of biometrics enables comprehensive checks… to identify individuals who may pose a threat to national security, public safety or immigration controls.”


Ghassan Ghaben of the British Palestinian Committee, an advocacy group, said the government was applying a double standard against Gazan families.


“The UK has shown in other situations that, when there is the political will, rules can be adapted to the realities of war – and in this case, genocide,” he said. “The Ukraine Family Scheme recognised that ordinary immigration procedures were not appropriate in the circumstances and enabled people to reunite with their families.”


Since the Russian invasion in 2022, Ukrainians and their children have been able to live and work in Britain under special temporary humanitarian visas.


“Palestinians have been asking for a similarly practical response since 2023, yet the response has instead been to maintain or introduce even stricter barriers,” said Ghaben.


He added there was “a real contradiction” between the shift in rhetoric about Gaza from Andy Burnham’s Labour government and its treatment of the families. 


“The home secretary has recently announced the reopening of the UK Resettlement Scheme, and spoken about creating safe and legal routes for people fleeing persecution,” he said.


“Yet at the same time, the Home Office is continuing to fight against the reunification of Palestinian mothers and young children with their fathers who are already in the UK.”


During the genocide in Gaza, the UK has

allowed weapons

 sales to Israel, flown spy flights over Gaza, allowed

military planes to depart

 from its bases bound for Israel and

refused to investigate British nationals

 who joined the Israeli military.


Home secretary Shabana Mahmood was accused last month of


giving people in Gaza “false hope”

 after announcing a new safe route to the UK for Palestinian refugees. The route only applies to those who have

already escaped to Lebanon or Jordan

 and will benefit only a few hundred people a year.


Last year, the government suspended a programme that allowed people granted asylum in the UK to bring their family members over.

author: Dyepeson Martins
title: Brasileiro eleito na Flórida diz que Trump ajuda quem foge da Justiça e deporta domésticas
content:
Mais do que um nome na política, Felipe Sousa-Lazaballet, 40, também quer ser símbolo de representatividade. Ele se tornou o primeiro brasileiro eleito representante (um deputado estadual, para nós) na Flórida, nos Estados Unidos (EUA). O estado é reduto político do Secretário de Estado norte-americano, Marco Rubio, principal responsável pela expansão do movimento nacionalista

Make America Great Again

 (MAGA) na América Latina. Na Flórida também está localizada a Mar-a-Lago, uma espécie de Casa Branca secundária utilizada por Trump como centro de deliberações políticas.


Filho de empregada doméstica, Felipe nasceu em Duque de Caxias (RJ) e, aos 14 anos, migrou para os EUA. É ativista comunitário, militante do movimento LGBTQIA+ e agora também é o primeiro imigrante abertamente gay a integrar a Florida House of Representatives (a Assembleia Legislativa da Flórida).


Em entrevista à

Agência Pública

, ele reforçou que teve a campanha pautada pela igualdade de direitos sociais e comentou a controversa política trumpista que, ao mesmo tempo, deporta imigrantes que fortalecem a economia americana, enquanto ajuda figuras como o Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). O senador deixou o Brasil dois dias depois de ser derrotado na eleição à Presidência da República apesar da determinação do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) para que ele entregasse o passaporte à Polícia Federal.


“Primeiro, queria dizer que, pra mim obviamente, o Brasil é um país soberano e a Justiça do Brasil deve ser respeitada. Pra mim não faz sentido nenhum que os Estados Unidos estão aceitando uma pessoa que está literalmente fugindo da Justiça no Brasil e, enquanto isso, está deportando uma empregada doméstica, ou seja, não faz sentido nenhum”, declarou o deputado eleito. Flávio Bolsonaro é investigado, entre outros crimes, por lavagem de dinheiro e organização criminosa.


Além de Felipe, outros seis brasileiros foram eleitos deputados estaduais nos EUA. Em Massachussets, foram quatro: Danillo Sena, Lorena Betts, Priscila Sousa e Rita Mendes. Em Connecticut, foi eleito Farley Santos e, em Nevada, Elaine Marzola.


A eleição americana representou uma grande derrota ao presidente Donald Trump com a vitória avassaladora de candidatos do partido Democrata, que agora tem a maioria no Congresso Nacional americano. Na Câmara, dos 435 membros votantes, haverá 231 democratas, 139 republicanos e 65 nomes ainda em definição devido às disputas acirradas em alguns estados, que podem levar semanas para contabilizar todos votos. Os Democratas também terão 54 das 100 vagas do Senado. Os republicanos garantiram 44. Duas vagas ainda estão em definição.


As eleições de meio de mandato são chamadas de “midterms” e marcam a metade da gestão de Donald Trump. Nos EUA, o sistema de votação e apuração dos votos ocorre de forma descentralizada e cada estado tem autonomia para definir as regras do pleito na região, diferentemente do modelo adotado no Brasil, onde as normas são regidas pelo Superior Tribunal Eleitoral (TSE).


“Por muito tempo, os democratas não estavam tão focados nos assuntos que realmente estão impactando mais a classe trabalhadora aqui, que é o custo de vida, ter oportunidade de poder ter um imóvel próprio, que é o caminho mais comum e tradicional de conseguir chegar ao sonho americano”, frisou Sousa-Lazaballet.


Confira os principais trechos da entrevista:


Como foi a sua inserção na política partidária americana?


Eu fiz parte de uma marcha que foi de Miami até Washington D.C., que foram 1.500 milhas [2,4 mil km] a pé até lá. E foi assim que a gente conseguiu, na época, mudar a maneira que o presidente Obama pensava sobre a instituição da imigração e quem deveria ou não deportar. E dessa maneira conseguimos conquistar grandes coisas para o movimento. Ao mesmo tempo, também batalhei bastante para o movimento LGBT+. E sempre tive essa atuação política mais no sentido do lado de fora.


Não do lado de dentro, não da parte partidária, como você mesmo disse. Mas, mais ou menos uns dois anos atrás, quando o presidente Trump foi reeleito pela segunda vez, eu lembro que eu estava no meu carro pensando “uau, a gente vai acabar vivendo nesse mundo com o presidente Trump e o governador DeSantis”, que é o governador daqui da Flórida – um governador muito anti-imigrante, muito contra a comunidade LGBT +, mas muito de direita, que tem realmente criado vários problemas para as comunidades que vivem aqui. E naquele momento eu pensei: “nossa, a gente tem que realmente se expandir …

author: Unknown
title: James Michael Yeoman - Salud y Anarquía desde Dowlais
content:
Author

: James Michael Yeoman

Title

:

Salud y Anarquía desde Dowlais

Subtitle

: The translocal experience of Spanish anarchists in South Wales, 1900–15

Date

: 2016

Source

: Yeoman, J.M. (2016) Salud y Anarquía desde Dowlais: The translocal experience of Spanish anarchists in South Wales, 1900–15. International Journal of Iberian Studies, 29 (3). pp. 273–289. ISSN: 1364-971X


Abstract


 In the early twentieth century a group of Spanish anarchists settled in the town of Dowlais, South Wales, as part of a wider migration to the area prompted by the town’s ironworks. Over the following fifteen years this community kept in constant contact with their comrades in Spain through the networks sustained by the anarchist press. Examination of these records reveals the dislocation experienced by these migrants, and their efforts to retain their identity and standing within the movement they had left behind. This study highlights the benefits of a translocal approach towards anarchist internationalism, which focuses on the experience of ordinary members of the movement and their struggles to overcome the challenges presented by international movement.


Keywords


 Anarchism Spain Wales internationalism translocalism migration


Introduction


 Studies of turn-of-the-century anarchist transnationalism are often framed around elite figures and propagandists (Bantman 2006: 961–62), such as Pyotr Kropotkin, Errico Malatesta and Fernando Tarrida del Mármol. Many of these figures lived truly fascinating lives, moving regularly through major cities on both sides of the Atlantic, driven by a combination of devotion to the cause and a need to stay one step ahead of the law. Influenced by the broader shift towards transnational labour history, some recent studies of anarchist internationalism have sought to flesh out the experience of these figures more fully (Levy 2010) while others have shifted their focus away from these exceptional, and largely atypical, individuals altogether. Far more attention is now directed at the experience of ordinary anarchists, whose reasons for movement were – like most migrants of the era – as much material as political, and who often had little time or resources to engage in extensive political activity (Goyens 2007; Bantman 2013). Of particular relevance for this study is the increasing number of works dedicated to transnational networks formed between radicals separated by geographic and political borders (Turcato 2007; Khuri-Makdisi 2010). The Spanish movement has not been entirely isolated from these historiographical trends. Anarchist migration and networks between Spain and Latin America have received some attention from scholars such as Moya (1998), Sánchez Cobos (2008) and Shaffer (2010), as have anarchist links between Spain and the Philippines (Anderson 2005). Nevertheless, the trans-Atlantic networks of Spanish anarchism remain understudied; a fact noted by Martha Ackelsberg elsewhere in this special issue. Likewise, the movement of Spanish anarchists within Europe has received little attention in recent scholarship.


 While the turn to transnational anarchist history is welcome and important, some questions about the premises of such studies remain. Many transnational studies focus on the period when the international anarchist movement was at its strongest, from the late nineteenth century up to the outbreak of World War I, which overlapped with one of the great periods of globalization. Capital flowed into and out of nation states, borders were relatively fluid and movement of people was both an opportunity and a compulsion for many. This situation presented internationalists with an unprecedented context in which to spread their message to the working class of Europe and the Americas. There is a risk, however, that transnational studies portray cross-border activity as a straightforward and ultimately positive activity, obscuring the difficulties and failures experienced by those engaged in transnational radicalism. For many, migration was an undesired and distressing experience, and even those of an internationalist outlook often maintained parochial or nationalistic ideas and practices (Bantman 2006: 961, 970). Likewise, states and borders continued to function in the increasingly globalized world, presenting huge and complex obstacles for those who wished to undermine them (Bantman and Altena 2015: 7–10).


 A further problem lies in the concept of transnationalism itself …

author: Chris Slee
title: Forum discusses corruption and inhumanity in offshore detention regime
content:
The Refugee Action Collective Victoria (RAC) held a public forum in Naarm/Melbourne on October 26 to discuss the Anthony Albanese government’s policy of sending refugees to detention centres on remote islands.

Despite Albanese’s promise to end the offshore detention regime, about 100 refugees are currently held on Naoero (formerly Nauru). Previously refugees had been sent to Manus Island in Papua New Guinea (PNG), before its Supreme Court ruled this illegal.

Keynote speaker Nik Feik, an investigative journalist who has uncovered details about the offshore detention regime, said the system was corrupt. He said contractors receive hundreds of millions of dollars to run these centres, yet the refugees do not receive sufficient food and other supplies. “Where does the money go?”, he asked.

Feik said aircraft safety problems, audit reports and money handling processes had been ignored.

He raised concerns about Nauru Airlines, which owns seven Boeing 737 planes paid for by Australia. Naoero has a population of 12,000 and receives only 200 visitors each year. He said the planes had been used to take the families of political leaders on holidays.

Australia is committed to paying Naeoro $2.3 billion over 20 years in return for holding refugees and others deported from Australia.

Kieran Magee from RAC said corruption damages Naoeroan society. He said the money goes to wealthy elites, not ordinary people and distorts the economy.

Atena Kashani, an Iranian refugee, spoke about her experiences arriving by boat as a nine-year-old after her family fled Iran due to fear of persecution.

She was detained on Christmas Island, and then at Melbourne Immigration Transit Accommodation detention centre in Naarm. She said detention felt "cruel" and that it was "horrible" to see guards with guns.

Eventually the family was allowed out of detention. Their work and study rights were granted and withdrawn, before being restored. Her family now has permanent residency.

Kashani has friends who were on Naoero. Some are still there. One man set himself on fire as a protest.

She said some refugees living in Australia have been threatened with being sent back to Nauru. They have also been pressured to return to Iran.

Magee said that up to 70,000 people are at risk of being deported. He urged people to get involved in campaigns for refugee rights.

He pointed to past victories, including the campaign to get children off Naoero. He pointed to the 100 day protest in which refugees on temporary visas camped outside the Department of Home Affairs and immigration ministers’ offices demanding permanent visas. Many have since been granted permanent residence.

[Chris Slee is a member of the Refugee Action Collective Victoria.]

author: Publicación Abierta
title: El capitalismo cree en el crecimiento infinito. El planeta, no.
content:
Un sistema sin freno en un planeta con fin.


El capitalismo está diseñado para crecer sin límite: fabricar más, consumir más, extraer más. Pero nada, absolutamente nada, es infinito. Se atribuye a Einstein aquello de que solo hay dos cosas infinitas: el universo y la estupidez humana, aunque de la primera no estaba tan seguro. Los recursos energéticos y materiales de nuestro planeta, desde luego, tienen un límite. Y un sistema que exige crecer cada año choca de frente con esa realidad.


El futuro de nuestros hijos, hipotecado.


Al capital le da igual el futuro de nuestros hijos, el de nuestros nietos e incluso nuestro propio presente. Aquí solo importa crecer, acaparar riqueza y ganar cada vez más. Se parece demasiado a un cáncer: una enfermedad que lo devora todo hasta que no queda nada y el cuerpo muere. Ese será el destino del planeta si seguimos por este camino.


Einstein y la necesidad del socialismo.


Einstein se declaró socialista y, en su ensayo «¿Por qué el socialismo?», denunció la anarquía económica del capitalismo y la concentración del poder en pocas manos. Su advertencia sigue vigente: necesitamos un sistema que piense en el futuro y no solo en la acumulación de riqueza por parte de unos pocos.


El mono que acapara plátanos.


Cuando un mono acapara más plátanos de los que necesita, los científicos lo estudian porque ese comportamiento no es normal. En el capitalismo, a quien hace lo mismo lo llamamos multimillonario y lo respetamos. Gente como Elon Musk, que ha llegado a ser el hombre más rico del mundo en más de una ocasión, o los dos o tres multimillonarios que siempre se alternan en esa lista, viven de acaparar.


Riqueza que se convierte en poder.Y no les basta con tener más y más. También quieren más poder: influir en las democracias e injerirse en otros países para imponer su forma de ver el mundo. Y esa forma de ver el mundo, si no la frenamos, será la que acabe con la humanidad.


Hay alternativa, y se llama organización, conciencia de clase y un sistema que ponga la vida por delante del beneficio.


¡Até á vitoria sempre!


André Abeledo Fernández

El capitalismo cree en el crecimiento infinito. El planeta, no.

title: Midterm USA: come sta la seggiola di Trump?
content:
A due anni dall’inizio del secondo mandato di Trump il tempo delle elezioni del Midterm è stato raggiunto in modo da rinnovare il Congresso intero e un terzo del Senato, come indicato dalla Costituzione statunitense. Trump è stato sconfitto in entrambi i casi, con i Dem vincitori in 22 Stati, di cui 5 precedentemente in mano repubblicana, e che ora contano 228 seggi alla Camera e 54 al Senato (dati parziali allo stato della scrittura dell’articolo).


Due anni passati anche troppo velocemente: intensificazione delle operazioni dell’ICE (con i conseguenti sommovimenti come a

Minneapolis

), stati di emergenza di carattere politico emanati in diversi Stati, guerra (persa) all’Iran, ruolo di principale sponsor del genocidio in Palestina, richiesta agli Stati Nato di aumentare la spesa militare senza sborsare un centesimo, guerra commerciale alla Cina (e non solo), aumento vertiginoso del debito, ma anche corruzione e aumento dei profitti per la famiglia di Trump, lo scandalo di Epstein… In poche parole, una fattuale caduta del soft power americano.


STRATEGIE 


Entrambi i partiti hanno messo in atto delle strategie per giocarsi la riconferma o il ribaltamento dei rapporti governativi tra Camere (in particolare il Senato) e la Casa Bianca. Il rischio di un ribaltamento in favore dei Dem era nell’aria e in questo senso la priorità da parte del GOP era quella di concentrarsi sul mantenere il controllo sul Senato, in particolare sul difendere i seggi contesi e cruciali in Stati come Texas, Ohio, Kansas, Maine e Alaska per garantire l’approvazione delle nomine giudiziarie e dei funzionari federali anche in caso di governo diviso. Ma non è andata come sperato, infatti alcuni di questi Stati hanno visto una vittoria Dem inaspettata come nel caso del Kansas che non eleggeva un democratico dal 1932.  D’altro canto la strategia del Partito Democratico ha puntato ad affermarsi come l’unico contrappeso istituzionale e di controllo nei confronti del secondo mandato di Trump. Il tema centrale ruota intorno all’economia domestica: i Democratici imputano direttamente alla Casa Bianca l’aumento del costo della vita, del carburante e dell’inflazione, dipingendo i dazi protezionistici come “tasse sui consumatori” e denunciando i tagli ai servizi sanitari (medicina di base e sussidi ACA). Sul piano internazionale, attaccano i rischi di escalation bellica nei conflitti esteri ed evidenziano presunti conflitti di interesse dell’amministrazione, promettendo di usare la maggioranza al Congresso per avviare commissioni di inchiesta e vigilanza.


L’ultimo elemento da considerare è un andamento particolare degli ultimi anni relativo ai Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) che si sono trasformati da movimento di nicchia a forza capace di influenzare gli equilibri della sinistra americana. Sfruttando il malcontento della cosiddetta Gen Z e Millennials su disuguaglianze e costo della vita, i DSA hanno canalizzato l’attivismo giovanile portando istanze radicali nelle istituzioni. I risultati di ciò si sono visti: nel macro l’elezione a sindaco di Mamdani a New York, seguito da oltre 250 membri dei DSA in diverse altre posizioni (minori) in più di 40 Stati.


Fino ad ora i DSA sono stati forti principalmente nei grandi centri urbani abitati, tuttavia dalla campagna elettorale emerge un altro fenomeno: la retorica alternativa all’establishment, impostata sulle condizioni di vita e di riproduzione delle persone, sta permettendo le prime penetrazioni nelle zone

rurals

 più prossime alle città; forse ancora in minoranza, ma tuttavia rimane un fenomeno interessante. 


La loro strategia per le

Midterms

 si è basata sul condizionamento interno al Partito Democratico: sfidando i candidati moderati alle primarie nei collegi urbani, l’organizzazione impone temi chiave come sanità pubblica, diritto alla casa e tutela dei lavoratori. Questo spinge l’agenda dem verso sinistra, garantendo altresì un’alta affluenza di elettori militanti. Questo soggetto introduce un discorso che significa la dialettica alto-basso non più nei termini di establishment-popolo, bensì con fattori nuovi più prossimi ad una dialettica di classe. author: ROAPE
title: What does Zambia’s Hakainde Hichilema tell us about democracy in Africa today?
content:
Perhaps the strongest hangover from colonialism is the relative lack of consent garnered by the ruling parties: the notion of them gaining “hegemony on a

shoestring

” in a context where rulers’ goals are to keep labour costs as low as possible in order to expand profits of exports. The strategy depended upon indirect rulers defined by “traditions” (flexible and changing) and regions and required brokerage among shifting alliances. Lacking the ideological means of gaining consent via domination of media and civil society institutions, rulers resort to state violence and intimidation.


In 2021 Hichilema inherited a state structure that had, according to

Amnesty International

, over the previous decade undertaken a “systematic crackdown on the right to freedom of expression”, criminalizing peaceful dissent and forcing the closure of independent media outlets. One consequence is that there are no reliable sources of information on the current political crisis. What fails to make international news is any analysis of the prominent regional and ethnolinguistic divisions that animate street-level politics. There is also no analysis of the striking absence of any clear differences in ideological or policy orientations between parties. The currently jailed opposition leader Brian Mundubile heads a coalition formed for the sole purpose of getting UPND out of power while contestation rests largely on respective judgements of character and regional and ethno-linguistic criteria. Questions revolved around

who

 gets to govern – rather than

why

 they should govern. Youtube and Facebook searches for elections information do not yield much more than pastors and self-appointed “prophets”, prophesizing elections results rather than actual political analysis.


The campaign period leading up to the national election on August 13

th

 was marred by street violence among

political supporters

, backed up with intimidation of opposition supporters by police and military. International observers have documented instances of voter intimidation, assaults, abductions, and arrest of hundreds of opposition supporters. Even worse has been the loss of life. A day after the election, security forces killed opposition member,Mutotwe Kafwaya, a former cabinet minister, and Lovemore Chishima, a polling agent. The UN Special Rapporteur, Gina Romero, has called for immediate international scrutiny. The EU parliament passed a near

unanimous resolution

 condemning the killings and the increase in political repression since the election and calling for an independent and impartial investigation. Hichilema has also cancelled the passports of at least six critics of his government, who include a

prominent academic

. When he was in opposition, Hichilema was a victim of the same repression he is inflicting on those who oppose his government.


For Tonga, Ila and Lenje ethnic groups (collectively referred to as ‘Bantu Botatwe’),  a stronghold of the ruling UPND, and where Hakainde and the rest of Southern Province belong, his election victory in 2021 was the culmination of a 75-year struggle of supporting opposition candidates who called for liberal nationalism. This dates back to 1951 when Hakainde’s fellow southerner, Harry Nkumbula launched the Northern Rhodesian African Congress (later renamed as African National Congress). With Nkumbula being eclipsed by Kenneth Kaunda and the United National Independence Party (UNIP) throughout the independence struggle, he remained the primary opposition figure until the banning of the opposition parties in 1973. Since then, Southern and Western regions had maintained deep grievances. With the UPND in power, today these grievances find expression through periodical street battles involving loyal cadres, most of who are lumpenproletarian, against their opposition counterparts. Unemployed and in poverty, these cadres hope for hand-outs in exchange for political support. Ruling party cadres are often the ones who kickstart the political disturbances targeting the opposition, which include disrupting campaign rallies. Thereafter, the police and military, join in, ostensibly to restore order by cancelling the opposition rallies altogether, which ultimately benefit the party in power. This dynamic also led to the suspension of the 2026 election ballot counting in some areas.


Back to Nkumbula, his politics continue to be misunderstood despite a brilliant

biography

 by Giacomo Macola that dispels much of the …

author: Unknown
title: Hope lies with young people
content:
Our generation grew up under the influence of the 1968 Youth Revolution. More precisely, we were forged in the fire of that historic revolution. The Revolutionary Youth Movement of 1968 was based primarily on university students. It was the most striking example of conscious, organised youth taking the lead in society as a whole. Through this revolutionary movement, university students proved themselves and passed the test of history.


The 1968 Youth Revolution was the most influential revolutionary wave since the 1917 Soviet Revolution, which emerged during the First World War. It aimed not only to overthrow the system of capitalist modernity, whose crisis was deepening, but also to transcend actually existing socialism, which had moved away from the principles of equality based on freedom and diversity. For various reasons, it undoubtedly failed to overthrow the system of capitalist modernity. However, it played a significant role in the collapse of actually existing socialism, which had proved incapable of correcting or renewing itself. Had actually existing socialism understood the revolution developed by intellectual university youth, and demonstrated the capacity to transform and renew itself on the basis of that revolution's characteristics, perhaps it would not have met the tragic end it did, nor disintegrated in that way.


The 1968 Youth Revolution first developed on the European continent, and its influence gradually spread. From that point onward, Turkish youth, inspired by the forms of organisation and struggle developed by their European peers, reached the peak of their revolutionary activity in 1970–71. The Revolutionary Youth Movement, which also knew how to draw on the Palestinian Resistance in practice, succeeded in leading the democratic revolution that Turkey experienced during the 1970s. New socialist and revolutionary formations in Turkey and Kurdistan also emerged from the fire of this movement. Undoubtedly, the most influential representative of this new wave was the PKK.


Today, under conditions in which the system of capitalist modernity has brought nature and society to the brink of destruction—going beyond even the peak of crisis and chaos—the breakthrough is once again coming from Europe, and once again from the youth. It is the youth who carry hope. This time, however, the spark is being ignited not by university students but by secondary-school students. Scientific and technological advances undoubtedly play an important role in this. It is clear that secondary-school students are using these advances more effectively.


As has so often been the case, the secondary-school youth movement that began in France has, this time too, spread across almost all of Europe in a very short period. It also appears to have succeeded in mobilising different sections of society. In a manner reminiscent of the “sans-culottes” of an earlier era—the so-called “ragged-trousered” masses—the movement of secondary-school students, who were dismissed as “just a few kids”, has already managed to shake the system of capitalist modernity very seriously, and right at its very centre. It is abundantly clear that these “few kids” are achieving extraordinary things and inspiring everyone's admiration. Indeed, the French government has introduced a partial curfew, while it appears that new measures are also being discussed at the European level.


The popular movement led by young people, which continued throughout October and has progressively developed and spread, is undoubtedly extremely intriguing. It demands close attention and a sound assessment. Although its underlying causes are largely understood, it remains difficult to predict how events will unfold, how the movement will progress, and where it will ultimately lead. It is also becoming clear that the movement cannot be easily dismissed or suppressed through simplistic approaches.


One particularly interesting and striking question is why secondary-school students, rather than university students or young people as a whole, are driving this movement. As noted above, secondary-school students appear to be using science and technology more effectively and organising themselves more rapidly. While this is one contributing factor, it cannot, of course, be regarded as the only one. Another possible factor is that a deliberate system of special warfare has been applied to university youth, with the result that this section of the younger generation has, to a …

LOVE Is Just a Four Letter Word

The Great Middle-Class Cultural Revolution

The Youth Culture: An Anarcho-Communist View

Counter-Culture or Counter-Revolution

Is the ideology of Hip Culture the essence of self-determination, of the universal right of the individual to control her/his everyday life; the harbinger of the end of domination, authoritarianism, hierarchy and power? Is Hip Culture making demands that cannot be accommodated by the system and will thus bring about the end of the capitalist era?

Is “do your own thing” the slogan of hip middle-class, white men who continue to do their thing, as their straight counterparts have always done, by dominating and exploiting women, the Third World and working people? Will today’s energy of discontent merely be channeled into the making of a groovy drug/rock sanctuary for the disenchanted inheritors of capitalism’s overabundance?

Stanzas of .... And I Danced in the Mud and the Blood and the Beer, a poem by Jon Grell, are interspaced throughout the essays.

well, it’s two days after i split from woodstock and the mud is still caked heavy on my boots and my pants below my knees are still shit brown, four days of constant tripping has still left an acid reality in my head and, yeah, goddamnit, i wish i was still the fuck up there instead of coughing my lungs out from too much carbon monoxide here in good old new york city.

To believe that revolution is possible in this country without destroying the psychological stranglehold of middle class culture upon the workers, as if revolution could be made by the 3rd World poor alone, is a delusion. The vast majority of Americans are indeed working class; but the whole thrust of their culture, which is capitalist, has been to repress that class identity. They think of themselves as white, American, taxpayer, home-owners—not as workers. To bring about real revolution, it has always been necessary to raise the consciousness of the greater mass of the people to the point where they see the need for the revolution and identify with it. This means that the worker’s middle class identity, and culture supporting that identity, must be seriously weakened before they can identify with the revolution.

To avoid this hard fact, many leftists are fond of arguing from the revolutionary experiences of Russia, China, or Cuba, that a capitalist ‘crisis’ will sooner or later reduce the middle class worker to poverty, forcing him into revolutionary consciousness. They ignore the concrete lesson of the Great Depression of the 1930’s, when workers’ struggles were contained by the middle class “liberalism” (and the CP. Popular Front), and channeled into purely economic reforms within the system. The people of Russia, China, or Cuba shared not only common poverty, but a common consciousness and folk culture that was quite distinct from the bourgeoisie …

 zu einem Herbst der Gegenwehr sah Vieles richtig voraus und doch kam es bis zum Sommer 2026 noch viel schlimmer, immer noch ohne ausreichende Proteste. Neben unserem

Dossier zur sozialpolitisachen Gegenwehr der Gewerkschaften

 werden hier Strategiedebatten und Aufrufe sowie

Terminübersichten

 der sozialen Bewegungen gesammelt (

GenZ-Proteste im gesonderten Dossier

):


Resolution der regionalen Aktionskonferenz von „Kürzen nicht mit uns“ Kassel am 31. Oktober


Bei der Aktionskonferenz von „Kürzen nicht mit uns Kassel“ haben am vergangenen Samstag, 31. Oktober, 75 Personen teilgenommen. „Kürzen nicht mit uns“ ist eine gewerkschaftliche Initiative, die vor Ort Sozialproteste organisiert. Siehe die Abschlussresolution:


„

Kürzen? Nicht mit uns! Wir machen weiter!


1) Wir als „Kürzen nicht mit uns“ organisieren mit Gewerkschaften und Betroffenen zusammen Sozialproteste gegen alle Kürzungen. Wir sind aktiv in betrieblichen und tariflichen Auseinandersetzungen, ob im Bereich Gesundheit, Bildung und Soziales oder bei VW. Dort setzen wir uns für einen kämpferischen Kurs ein. Rechten und autoritären Entwicklungen in der Gesellschaft treten wir entschieden entgegen.


2) Wir erklären uns solidarisch mit den (Jugend-)protesten international und unterzeichnen als Initiative den Aufruf zum Schulstreik am 20.11. (

www.schulstreikgegenwehrpflicht.com

).


3) Wir unterstützen aktiv Initiativen gegen Militarisierung und Aufrüstung, wie „Zivilklausel bleibt“ an der Uni. Wir wehren uns dagegen, dass Kassel zur „Rüstungshochburg Europas“ gemacht wird, wie es der grüne Oberbürgermeister Schöller möchte.


4) Am 2.12. wird es in Wiesbaden zur Arbeits- und Sozialminister*innen Protest vom Deutschen Gewerkschaftsbund (DGB) geben. Das unterstützen wir. Wir setzen uns darüber hinaus dafür ein, dass es spätestens im Januar 2027 eine große bundesweite Demo des DGBs in Berlin gibt. Hier sollten auch gewerkschaftliche Aktive von der Basis und Vertreter*innen der Sozialproteste mit eingebunden werden. Sollte es keinen neuen bundesweiten Aufruf geben, braucht es eine Initiative von der Basis hierfür.


5) Nötig ist eine starke bundesweite Mobilisierung, an der wir uns mit einem eigenen Aufruf für Nordhessen beteiligen wollen. Es braucht mehr Aufklärung über die Angriffe und persönliche Ansprache durch uns in unserem Umfeld. Mit Betriebs- und Personalversammlungen, sowie Versammlungen in Schulen, Unis und Nachbarschaften zum Thema können wir auch in der Breite Menschen ansprechen.


6) Wir bleiben in Kontakt mit den anderen Sozialprotest-Bündnissen bundesweit und behalten uns vor, mit diesen gemeinsam einen dezentralen Aktionstag zu organisieren.


7) Proteste auf der Straße alleine werden aber nicht ausreichen. Darüber hinaus braucht es auch zivilen Ungehorsam und politische Streiks gegen diese Politik. Das kann z.B. in Form von Betriebsversammlungen über mehrere Tage geschehen, um die Arbeit niederzulegen und weitere Schritte zu diskutieren. Wir wollen zusammen mit gewerkschaftlichen Gliederungen zeitnah eine Veranstaltung zum Thema „Politischer Streik“ organisieren.


8) Wir unterstützen die Idee des bundesweiten gewerkschaftlichen Ratschlags, betriebliche Aktionen wie diese an einem Tag oder einer Woche zu koordinieren und mit anstehenden Tarifrunden zu verbinden.


9) Tarifrunden der unterschiedlichen Branchen sollten – wo es möglich ist – zusammengeführt und politisch mit den Themen der Kürzungen und Sozialproteste verbunden werden. Gerade auch angesichts der Härte der Angriffe, brauchen wir Diskussionen in Betrieben und Gewerkschaften über längere wirkungsvolle Arbeitsniederlegungen bis hin zu Erzwingungsstreiks.


10) All diese Angriffe auf uns hängen zusammen. Ob lohnabhängig Beschäftigte, Erwerbslose, Kinder und Jugendliche, Frauen und queers, Rentner*innen, Menschen mit Behinderungen und Migrant*innen – wir leisten Widerstand und lassen uns nicht spalten! Nein zu allen Kürzungen! Nein zu Aufrüstung und Krieg! …

author: La Zarzamora
title: Octubre y Dominga
content:
I. Octubre: la Memoria de la Tierra

El calendario marca 31 de octubre de 2026. El ocaso de un mes jalonado por sangre, balas y gas lacrimógeno en esta oblonga franja de territorio que llaman $hile.

Hace 7 años, este mes nos hizo recordar porqué asociamos poéticamente el repunte de la primavera, con los intentos continuos y discontinuos por hacer de la Revuelta y la Insurrección algo más que fuego y humo de barricadas, sino un crisol en donde a través de sus cenizas, poder forjar y construir un terreno fértil de ideas, prácticas y relaciones nuevas.

Aquel 18 de octubre de 2019, podría decirse que significó una ruptura, una disrupción, un momento histórico de saturación con el Orden. Una coyuntura en donde se aglomeraron y articularon todas las luchas: estudiantes, feministas, jubiladxs, organizaciones sindicales, defensores del territorio clamando por Justicia Ambiental…Si bien aquella Revuelta fue instigada en primera instancia por el alza en los precios de la locomoción colectiva, con el devenir de los días de protesta y autoorganización se alzó con fuerza y visibilidad una problemática transversal a la clase, y a cualquier otra categoría que se quiera expresar: la usurpación de nuestros bienes comunes y la devastación territorial.

En dicho escenario de conflictividad social, la consigna “no son 30 pesos, son 30 años” emergió con rabia y fuego, entrelazando la compleja interrelación de todas las formas de opresión y malestar social, evidenciando asimismo las grietas de un modelo incompatible con nuestras necesidades vitales básicas, y frontalmente contrario a la continuidad y cuidado de la Tierra.

II. La Democracia es Extractivismo en favor de los ricos: la Herida abierta a tajo abierto

El modelo socioeconómico $hileno y toda la institucionalidad del Estado, durante las últimas décadas han actuado y operado en bloque para profundizar la precariedad socioambiental tanto de las poblaciones humanas como de otras especies endémicas. Así, tenemos la existencia de poblados enteros con acceso restringido al agua potable, como es el caso de la comuna de Contulmo en el Sur, producto de la imposición de zonas extensas destinadas al monocultivo de especies exógenas como el pino y eucalipto para la producción de celulosa; o, por ejemplo, sectores completos decretados en “zona de sequía” porque algún capitalista decidió con la venia de las autoridades entubar el agua para el regadío de parcelas privadas, como es el caso de la comuna de Petorca en la zona central. Toda esta realidad de despojo y precariedad, se impone con el lastre del Decreto Ley 701 (DL 701), promulgado el 15 de octubre de 1974, o en palabras sencillas, la ley infame de fomento forestal de la Dictadura de Pinochet, modelo de “desarrollo económico” (devastación territorial) que nos gobierna y somete hasta nuestros días.

No es una imagen exagerada definir todo el territorio nacional como una auténtica “Zona de Sacrificio”, aunque en las telepantallas y en las cifras oficiales quieran decirnos que somos una potencia a nivel sudamericano, en términos concretos este territorio que denominan $hile no es más que una pieza neocolonial tercermundista gobernada por los distintos capitales nacionales y transnacionales, entrelazados en cautos contubernios con la institucionalidad democrática-neoliberal burguesa local.

Y esta afirmación no es antojadiza, sino que lo demuestran, por un lado, la propia derrota de la Revuelta de 2019 (que cobró mutiladxs, presxs políticos y muertxs), con todo el posterior proceso de restauración de Normalidad democrática que salvaguardó el Orden político; y, por otro lado, no solamente la mantención del Orden socioeconómico, caracterizado y definido por su extractivismo y saqueo, sino que, por sobre todo, el remozamiento y persistencia de todos los nichos de explotación productiva, como son la megaminería y el modelo de monocultivo forestal, símbolos máximos de una economía destinada a la perpetuación grosera de la estratificación de clases, y NO a la satisfacción de nuestras necesidades y protección de los bienes comunes.

Esta vez ese remozamiento viene dado por la nueva retórica “verde y sustentable”, el GreenWashing de la nueva transición energética, pero que sabemos, no es más que la excusa capciosa y fraudulenta para perpetuar en las conciencias la reproducción social del Orden del Capital.

Una de estas heridas persistentes a …

Εκδήλωση και συζήτηση με θέμα “Καταστολή και Κοινοτισμός”. Θα συμμετέχουν δια ζώσης, η Κοινότητα Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών, η Κίνηση Χειραφέτησης Αναπήρων Μηδενική Ανοχή, η Επιτροπή Αγώνα Μεγάλης Παναγιάς και η Αυτόνομη Παρέμβαση Εστιακών.


Την προηγούμενη περίοδο η συνέλευσή μας, μαζί και με άλλες συλλογικότητες και ανθρώπους της Θεσσαλονίκης συντόνισε και προσπάθησε να δώσει ορμή και περιεχόμενο στον αγώνα αλληλεγγύης στα Προσφυγικά, όπως αυτός εξελίχθηκε στην πόλη μας. Το σκεπτικό μας, όπως το βάζαμε και στον δημόσιο λόγο μας, ήταν πως στα Προσφυγικά βρίσκουν έρεισμα όλοι οι αγώνες, γιατί όλοι οι αγώνες πηγάζουν και παίρνουν μορφή στην συλλογική ζωή των από τα κάτω. Μετά την πρώτη νίκη που κατάφερε ο αγώνας αυτός και με την επιθυμία να ανοίξουμε μία σειρά εκδηλώσεων για την αυτοοργάνωση πάνω στις βασικές συλλογικές μας ανάγκες, αποφασίσαμε να πραγματοποιήσουμε αυτήν την εκδήλωση. Στην κοινοτική συγκρότηση και την κοινωνική αυτοοργάνωση εντοπίζουμε την προοπτική συλλογικής επιβίωσης και αξιοπρεπούς ζωής μέσα στην συνθήκη εντεινόμενης καταστολής και μαζικής εξόντωσης που ζούμε σε πλανητικό επίπεδο.


Από τον κοινωνικό αγώνα των εστιακών ενάντια στην πλήρη υποβάθμιση του μοναδικού χώρου με στοιχεία κοινωνικής κατοικίας στην Θεσσαλονίκη, την κινηματική απάντηση σε μισαναπηρικές δολοφονίες και των εγκλεισμό των αναπήρων, την αντίσταση και την πολύμορφη καταστολή της Μεγάλης Παναγίας, ενός ολόκληρου χωριού, και το κοινωνικό μέτωπο που χτίστηκε με αιχμή τις απεργίες πείνας για την υπεράσπιση της Κοινότητας Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών, οι συμμετέχουσες συλλογικότητες εκφράζουν μια μεγάλη βεντάλια της αντίστασης των από τα κάτω, με μακρόχρονη εμπειρία απέναντι σε ευρύτατους μηχανισμούς και μεθόδους καταστολής.


Η Κοινότητα Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών έχει ξεκινήσει περιοδεία σε διάφορες γεωγραφίες στην ελλάδα και το εξωτερικό με τίτλο “Οι αγώνες νικούν όταν συναντιούνται”, με σκοπό τη σύνδεση και την ενδυνάμωση των αγώνων σε κάθε τοπικότητα. Θα παρουσιαστούν τα σκεπτικά και η θεμελίωση του αγώνα, τα μέσα που επιλέχθηκαν, ο απολογισμός της έκβασής του, καθώς και η προοπτική και οι προτάσεις για την επόμενη μέρα τόσο για την Κοινότητα όσο και ευρύτερα για το κίνημα και την κοινωνία.


Καλούμε τον κόσμο της πόλης να έρθει στην εκδήλωση και να συμμετέχει με τοποθετήσεις στην κουβέντα που θα ακολουθήσει.


– Ανοιχτή συνέλευση αλληλεγγύης στα Προσφυγικά –
