author: Unknown
title: Луиджи Фаббри - Анархическая Организация
content:
Автор

: Луиджи Фаббри

Название

: Анархическая Организация

Подзаголовок

: Доклад, представленный Итальянскому Анархическому Конгрессу в Риме (16-20 июня 1907) и Международному Анархическому Конгрессу в Амстердаме (24-31 августа 1907).

Дата

: 1907

Дополнительная информация

: Текст был разделен на 11 частей, только первая часть изначально была с названием. Названия для остальных частей придумал переводчик.


ПРЕДВАРИТЕЛЬНОЕ ЗАМЕЧАНИЕ


 В качестве заключения к следующему докладу об

индивидуальном и коллективном действии в анархическом движении

, представленному

Первому Итальянскому анархическому конгрессу

, состоявшемуся в Риме с 16 по 20 июня сего года (1907), была предложена эта резолюция:


 «

Конгресс,


принимая во внимание, что в борьбе против организованных сил капитализма и правительств необходимо единство анархических сил,


выражает пожелание, чтобы это единство становилось всё сильнее и обширнее на основе солидарности и сознательного участия всех индивидуальных воль;


вследствие чего полагает, что анархисты, уже согласные не только в идеях, но и в методах борьбы, объединят свои силы, повсеместно создавая группы и затем связывая эти группы между собой, при естественном сохранении автономии личности в группах и автономии групп в их объединениях;


заявляет, что, считая необходимым это объединение сил для коллективного действия, столь же необходимым остаётся и индивидуальное действие в его наиболее сознательных проявлениях, со стороны каждого соответственно его силам

».


 Конгресс единогласно, за исключением одного голоса, одобрил эту резолюцию теоретического характера; и принял, что касается Италии, следующее постановление практического характера:


 «

Конгресс рекомендует товарищам из разных местностей безотлагательное формирование групп, чтобы иметь возможность в кратчайший срок приступить к образованию


Итальянского Анархического Социалистического Альянса


на началах полнейшей автономии, поручив уже существующим группам подготовительную работу

».


 Представляя тот же теоретический и тактический доклад «Международному анархическому конгрессу» в Амстердаме, я надеюсь, что там будут приняты идентичные и ещё более точные резолюции, – и что вскоре от теоретических утверждений мы перейдем в область фактов к созданию Международной Анархической Ассоциации.


 Да здравствует Либертарный Интернационал!


 Рим, 20 августа 1907.


ЛУИДЖИ ФАББРИ


I. Вступление


Товарищи

.


 Уже много лет анархическое движение, – начавшееся столь блистательно внутри

Интернационала

, – бьётся в неразрешимом кризисе, и это происходит прежде всего из-за недостатка доброй воли среди нас.


 Мы, анархисты, должны признаться, если нас никогда не устрашали преследования, обрушивающиеся на нас извне, то мы всегда имели проклятый страх перед неким призраком, который сами же создали. Прежде всего мы смирились с тем, чтобы быть жертвами всех безумцев, всех чудаков, всех тех, кто впадает в крайности, которые под предлогом логики претендовали не только на то, чтобы оправдывать всё то, что находили непристойным и низким у буржуа, но и на то, чтобы препятствовать и разрушать всякую работу по восстановлению движения, которую пытались предпринять другие товарищи, постоянно выставляя напоказ призрак идейной непоследовательности.


 Анархическая идея имеет своей первой основой индивидуальную свободу; но те, кто стал бы утверждать, что индивидуальная свобода при анархии бесконечна и абсолютна, были бы утопистами в самом смехотворном смысле этого слова, ибо бесконечное и абсолютное – это абстрактные понятия, это умственные построения, не имеющие возможности практического осуществления. Ныне же, напротив, всегда во имя индивидуальной свободы некоторые анархисты, в зависимости от того, что им нравится, либо провозглашают право делать что угодно и даже посягать на свободу и право других, либо объявляют непоследовательным любую попытку революционного осуществления анархии и организации для пропаганды.


 Здесь мы намерены заняться возражениями, которые выдвигаются против идеи организации.


II. Организация и пропаганда


 Обычно говорят, что организация – это метод, а не цель; это ошибка. Принцип организации следует пропагандировать не только потому, что, организуясь сегодня, мы можем лучше подготовить революцию, но и потому, что принцип организации сам по себе является одним из главных постулатов анархической доктрины.

1. Defying the zio-global dictatorship

!


by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article 

here


I am sure you don’t need me to tell you that we are heading into a crucial period of history.


Not only is the shadow of a possible world war looming over us, but our freedom is coming under rapidly accelerating assault.


Here in France, for instance, the system started out by simply ignoring schoolkids protesting against the poor condition of their schools and their lives, then went on to

gas

 and

beat

 them,

smear

 their uprising in the media,

team up

 with far-right street gangs to attack the ever-broadening revolt,

ban protests

 in city centres,

pass a law

 to make demonstrators pay for windows they did not break on the basis of some kind of assumed collective responsibility, place protesters under

house arrest

 as “terrorists”, constantly

lie

 about the size of the turn-outs,

manipulate

 social media algorithms so that people did not know about the demos and threaten to pull that communication plug

altogether

.


I should add that there is also the possibility that at least some of the protesters and looters were

agents provocateurs

 working for the system to undermine public support for the youngsters’ cause, although I have not yet seen any hard proof of this.


In an article for

Le Monde diplomatique

 (November 2026 edition), Benoît Bréville describes how politicians were lining up on TV to demand a fascistic response to the protests, with many blaming the left-wing opposition party

La France insoumise

 – president of the French senate Gérard Larcher even suggested the party should be dissolved.


“Others suggested creating thousands of new places in prisons on the model of Nayib Bukele in El Salvador, of removing benefits from the trouble-makers’ families or of hardening the law against minors”.


Bréville notes that curfews were imposed in several cities, policed by drones and helicopters. “Gatherings are banned and in certain neighbourhoods it is even forbidden to walk around with a rucksack or hat”.


He adds that the French railways, SNCF, cancelled trains to prevent some people from attending demos and those arriving by road and rail were subject to police checks.


 “In Paris, the army was mobilised to supervise the demonstrators, along with the brigade of regional intervention, the RAID (

Recherche, assistance, intervention, dissuasion

) and the national gendarmerie’s intervention group (GIGN)”.


But in the face of all that, numbers on the protests across France did not drop away and the uprising is still going strong as I write!


All across Europe protests are

breaking out

 – including against what looks like an attempted

German-backed

 EU

coup d’état

 in Poland – and it seems that policing is increasingly being carried out by

Eurogendfor

 (European Gendarmerie Force), the European mercenary army deployed, as one

X

 user

put it

, “by the EUSSR to crush local uprisings, hijack demonstrations, and stage coups. They have no ties whatsoever to the local population (they don’t even speak the language) and will ruthlessly crush any form of civilian resistance with an iron fist”.


Meanwhile, hitherto unthinkable restrictions are being placed on people’s international travel on the basis of them not being appreciated by the zio-imperialist mafia (ZIM).


Take, for example, the way that veteran anarchist and co-founder of Food not Bombs

Keith McHenry

 was banned from entering Canada essentially on account of the decades of state violence and harassment  he has faced for feeding homeless people (

see below

).


Much of the repression centres, of course, around critics of Israel and its genocidal activities.


Swedish academic Andreas Malm was

refused entry

 to the UK, where he was due to headline an anti-imperialist and pro-Palestinian conference, on the grounds that his presence in the UK “may not be considered to be conducive to the public good”.


New York journalist Jeremy Loffredo has also

revealed

: “The UK is refusing to let me enter the country to report on and investigate the ongoing crackdown against elderly Palestine supporters because my ‘presence in the UK is not conducive to the public good’”.

content:
В поддержку анархиста Алексея Макарова создан канал Solidarity with Alexey Makarov / Солидарность с Алексеем Макаровым. Вот, что пишут его авторы:

Анархист Алексей Макаров больше двадцати лет борется с российским режимом. За участие в оппозиционной деятельности он прошёл через тюрьму, был вынужден покинуть Россию и в 2011 году получил убежище в Швеции.

Когда началось полномасштабное российское вторжение в Украину, Алексей не смог остаться в стороне. Летом 2022 года он покинул безопасную Швецию и отправился бороться за свободу и защищать народ Украины. Он воевал в составе 95-й десантно-штурмовой бригады, затем - Интернационального легиона и «Сибирского батальона». После двух тяжёлых ранений Алексей вернулся в Швецию для восстановления.

Там он столкнулся с тем, что страна, которая на словах заявляет о поддержке украинского государства, одновременно дискриминирует и подвергает репрессиям тех, кто защищал народ Украины. Сначала ему отказали в гражданстве, затем - в новом проездном документе беженца, фактически лишив возможности выезжать из страны. Основанием стало заключение шведской спецслужбы Säpo об «угрозе национальной безопасности». За этой формулировкой стоит его участие в вооружённом сопротивлении российской агрессии в Украине.

Сейчас ему нужна наша поддержка и помощь.

Этот канал создан друзьями и товарищами Алексея. Здесь мы будем публиковать новости по его делу, информацию о кампаниях солидарности и о том, как к ним присоединиться.

Just as the Franco-Italian anarchist miner Lawrence Storione imported revolutionary ideas to the Fife area of Scotland, so too did Spanish anarchist and socialist miners and steelworkers to South Wales in similarly little known circumstances.

The Orconero Iron Ore Company in northern Spain had been a subsidy of the Dowlais Iron Company in South Wales since 1873. In 1900 several hundred Spanish workers and their families were brought to Dowlais from northern Spain in what was seen as a way of undercutting wages for Welsh workers. A street was specifically built for them in Dowlais- King Alphonso Street after the then Spanish monarch Alfonso XII and two areas of the town were given over to them. However if the idea was to undercut the Welsh workers, it was a bad plan as most of those who came to South Wales were socialist or anarchist workers who had themselves been victimised for activity in Spain. They joined the local unions straight away. Shortly after, several Spanish families moved to the anthracite mining village of Abercrave in the Swansea Valle to work for a French mining company that had opened up the International Colliery there.

“Abercrave, a quiet little mining village of only a few thousand inhabitants at the top of the Swansea Valley, has now become one of the most cosmopolitan in the district. In addition to the Welsh, English, Scotch and Irish residing in the locality, there has been a strong influx during the past few years of Frenchman, Spaniards, Portuguese, Germans, Belgians &c, and employment has been found for them in the local collieries. The Spaniards form the strongest colony, and it is computed that there are over 200 in all” ( quoted in O’Leary). In Abercrave the Spanish settled on Davies Street and Brooklands Terrace, a line of single story two-room cottages. The area became known as Spanish Row or Espaniardos Row.

Among those who came to Wales was the anarchist Melchor Esteban. He had been a steel worker in Bilbao. Anarchist and atheist, he obtained work at the Dowlais Ironworks in 1907 and shortly after moved to the International Colliery at Abercrave. He had brought his family with him including his son Gregorio, born in 1887, who was to later to volunteer for the International Brigades during the Civil War.

The anarchist paper Freedom first mentioned the Spanish communities in Wales in June 1901, as the result of a visit to Dowlais by the Spanish anarchist Tarrida del Marmol and the London Welsh anarchist Sam Mainwaring (they were collaborating on an anarchist paper The General Strike). Mainwaring had conducted the first socialist tour of South Wales in alongside fellow Socialist Leaguer Frank Kitz in 1887 and had set up the South Wales Socialist Society in Landore in 1892. Through the use of Spanish by del Marmol and of Welsh and English by Mainwaring, they were able to sooth tensions between the different communities. Tensions once more came to the boil in 1913, when feelings …

Haben die Gewerkschaften nicht doch allerlei erreicht für die Arbeiter?

Kann man aber die Gewerkschaften nicht revolutionieren?

Wollen die Anarchisten eine eigene Organisation?

Wollen denn die Anarchisten gar keine Organisation.

Wie denken die Anarchisten sich den Zusammenschluss des Proletariats zum Klassenkampf?

Entspricht die B. O. den Kampfbedingungen unserer Zeit?

Wie vollzieht sich die soziale Revolution?

Sind die Betriebsorganisationen die Grundlage des Rätesystem?

Sie wollen den Wohlstand für alle. Darum müssen sie zu allererst gegen den Staat kämpfen, der nur den Wohlstand der Wenigen schützt auf Kosten der übrigen menschlichen Gesellschaft.

Die Anarchisten wollen eine Gesellschaftsordnung, in der die Produktionsmittel Gesellschaftseigentum sind, und alle Arbeiter den Ertrag ihrer Arbeit genießen können, eine Gesellschaftsordnung, in der produziert wird für den Bedarf aller, nicht mehr für den Profit einzelner. Sie wollen eine freie Gesellschaft, in der alles nur verwaltet wird, und wo niemand herrscht. Die Verwaltung sollen die Werktätigen selbst führen durch ihre Räte, die an den Arbeitsstätten gewählt werden und jeder Zeit abberufbar sind. Das ist: Die kommunistische Gesellschaftsordnung auf der Grundlage des Rätesystems.

Der Mensch ist weder schlecht noch gut. Schlecht aber sind die Verhältnisse der Menschen, ihre Gesellschaftsordnung, d. h. die Menschen werden sich wohler fühlen, wenn die Verhältnisse sich bessern. Eine falsche Betrachtungsweise sagt dann: „Die Menschen werden besser.“ Es ist durchaus natürlich, daß das Verhalten der Menschen in anderen Situationen sich ändert. Nicht weil wir die Menschen für besser halten, als sie sind, streben wir zur herrschaftslosen Gesellschaft — wenn es Engel unter uns gäbe, könnten wir es ertragen von ihnen beschützt und beherrscht zu sein, aber gerade weil wir die Menschen nehmen, wie sie sind, sagen wir: „Vertraut Euch ihnen nicht an.“ Der brutale Polizist könnte ein guter Mensch sein, wenn ihn nicht seine Gewalt und die Autorität seiner Uniform verführte. Das gleiche gilt sinngemäß auch von den Ausbeutern und Unterdrückern. Also, weil es keine Engel unter den Menschen gibt fordern wir:

„Ändert die verbrecherischen Verhältnisse, dann wird es keine Verbrechen mehr geben. Ändert die ausbeuterischen Verhältnisse, und es gibt keine Ausbeutung mehr. Ändert die schlechten menschlichen Verhältnisse und die „schlechten Menschen“ sterben aus.“

„Wohlstand für alle“ bedeutet Beseitigung einer Wirtschaftsordnung, in der der Reichtum Weniger auf der Armut der Vielen aufgebaut ist. Aber die Nutznießer dieses Zustandes sind mit Hilfe ihrer Gewaltorganisation bemüht, den jetzigen für sie günstigen Zustand zu erhalten, und das Proletariat gewaltsam zu geistiger Armut zu zwingen (denn Bildung ist nur gegen Geld erhältlich). So bleibt dem Klassenbewußten, d. h. dem zur Erkenntnis seiner Lage gekommenen Teile der proletarischen Klasse, nur ein Mittel übrig, das ist der Sturz der bestehenden Ordnung: Die Revolution.

Im Parlament wird verhandelt. Der Handel aber ist der Bourgeoisie geläufig, entspricht ihrer Wirtschaftsordnung und täglichen Übung. Diese heilige Grundlage der bürgerlichen „Ordnung“ findet ihren vollkommensten Ausdruck in der obersten Schacherinstanz: dem Parlament. Hier wird dem Handel der gloriose Mantel der sozialen Politik und der …

content:
Από το Πάσχα μέχρι και σήμερα, σε διάστημα 6 μηνών, έχουν πραγματοποιηθεί τρεις αστυνομικές εισβολές στη φιλοσοφική σχολή Αθηνών. Κράτος και πρυτανεία έστειλαν τους ένστολους δολοφόνους να εισβάλουν στη σχολή ενώ ήταν κλειστή κατά τη διάρκεια των διακοπών του Πάσχα, στη συνέχεια τους έμπασαν σαν τους κλέφτες ξημερώματα για να εκκενώσουν το Αναρχικό Στέκι Φιλοσοφικής, και την τελευταία φορά κατά τη διάρκεια της μαζικής συγκέντρωσης ανακατάληψης του Αναρχικού Στεκιού Φιλοσοφικής, την 1η του Σεπτέμβρη, εκμεταλλευόμενοι την ερημιά της σχολής εν μέσω εξεταστικής.

Μέσα στις σχολές πλειοψηφία είμαστε εμείς! Παράσιτα είναι οι μπάτσοι, οι εργολάβοι, οι πρυτάνεις και οι εισαγγελείς.

Όσο και άν η αστική ρητορική των εκάστοτε κυβερνώντων και τα δημοσιογραφικά «παπαγαλάκια» τους μιλάνε για παρασιτικές μειοψηφίες μέσα στις σχολές, η ίδια η πραγματικότητα των πανεπιστημίων αποδεικνύει ποιες είναι πράγματι αυτές οι παρασιτικές μειοψηφίες που λυμαίνονται τα πανεπιστήμια.

Από την άλλη πλευρά, η πλειοψηφία μέσα στις σχολές είμαστε εμείς: Οι φοιτητές και οι φοιτήτριες που παλεύουμε, κάτω από το βάρος της επισφάλειας και των αυξημένων απαιτήσεων διαβίωσης, να βγάλουμε τις σπουδές μας, και ταυτόχρονα να τα βγάλουμε πέρα στην καθημερινότητα· οι φοιτητές και οι φοιτήτριες που όταν αγωνιζόμαστε, ερχόμαστε αντιμέτωποι με την καταστολή και τα πειθαρχικά και το μόνο που μας επιφυλάσσουν είναι ένα αβέβαιο μέλλον μέσα στην εργασιακή ζούγκλα. Είναι οι εργαζόμενοι και οι εργαζόμενες στα πανεπιστήμια, είναι εκείνοι οι διδάσκοντες/ουσες που δεν θέλουν να βλέπουν τους φοιτητές τους να χτυπιούνται μέσα στις ίδιες τους τις σχολές. Και αυτή η πλειοψηφία πρέπει να δείξει πλέον τη δύναμή της!

ΣΤΟ ΑΣΥΛΟ ΔΕΝ ΜΠΑΙΝΕΙ Η ΑΣΤΥΝΟΜΙΑ ΟΙ ΦΟΙΤΗΤΕΣ ΘΥΜΟΥΝΤΑΙ ΤΟ ’73

ΕΞΩ ΟΙ ΜΠΑΤΣΟΙ ΑΠΟ ΤΙΣ ΣΧΟΛΕΣ ΜΑΣ

Ο ΑΓΩΝΑΣ ΔΕΝ ΥΠΟΚΥΠΤΕΙ ΣΤΗΝ ΚΑΤΑΣΤΟΛΗ

ΕΝΑΝΤΙΑ ΣΕ ΚΡΑΤΟΣ ΚΑΝΙΒΑΛΩΝ, ΙΔΙΩΤΙΚΟ ΚΕΦΑΛΑΙΟ, ΥΠΟΤΕΛΕΙΣ ΠΡΥΤΑΝΕΙΣ ΚΑΙ ΔΙΟΙΚΗΤΙΚΑ ΟΡΓΑΝΑ

Αναρχικό Στέκι Φιλοσοφικής https://steki-fls.espivblogs.net

Ο Φορέας Διαχείρισης του Πάρκου υπέγραψε πρόσφατα σύμβαση με τη «Νέα Μητροπολιτική Αττική Α.Ε.», προκειμένου η τελευταία να αναλάβει τη δρομολόγηση και επίβλεψη του έργου «Κατασκευή Περίφραξης και Αναβάθμιση Εισόδων στο Μητροπολιτικό Πάρκο “Αντώνης Τρίτσης”», συνολικού προϋπολογισμού 9.350.000 ευρώ. Το συγκεκριμένο έργο αναμένεται να ξεκινήσει άμεσα και θα πρέπει να έχει ολοκληρωθεί έως τις 31 Δεκεμβρίου 2029. Ως αιτιολόγηση για την ανάθεση προβάλλεται η τεχνική αδυναμία του Φορέα Διαχείρισης του πάρκου Τρίτση να υλοποιήσει το έργο. Και ενώ η «Νέα Μητροπολιτική Αττική Α.Ε.» θα αμειφθεί αδρά (122.763,47€) για τη σύνταξη των απαιτούμενων μελετών και των τευχών του διαγωνισμού, το έργο πρόκειται να υλοποιηθεί με τη μέθοδο της μελέτης-κατασκευής. Με άλλα λόγια, ο εργολάβος που θα το αναλάβει θα είναι εκείνος που θα εκπονήσει και τη μελέτη, με γνώμονα προφανώς τη μεγιστοποίηση του εργολαβικού του κέρδους. Γιάννης κερνάει, Γιάννης πίνει, λοιπόν…

Η δράση του Φορέα Διαχείρισης εντάσσεται στα ευρύτερα σχέδια κράτους και κεφαλαίου για τη μετατροπή των λιγοστών ελεύθερων χώρων που έχουν απομείνει, σε περίκλειστα, αποστειρωμένα, εμπορευματοποιημένα και απολύτως ελεγχόμενα περιβάλλοντα, όπως συμβαίνει ήδη σε αρκετά πάρκα (βλ. Πεδίο του Άρεως και τον χώρο του Ιδρύματος «Σταύρος Νιάρχος»).

Οι περιφράξεις δεν προστατεύουν· αποκλείουν. Δημιουργούν διαχωρισμούς ανάμεσα σε όσους και όσες «επιτρέπεται» να βρίσκονται μέσα σε έναν χώρο και σε όσους/ες/α περισσεύουν. Επιβάλλουν ωράρια, κανόνες και απαγορεύσεις, εγκαθιστώντας παράλληλα μηχανισμούς επιτήρησης, με στόχο τον περιορισμό της αυθόρμητης συνύπαρξης και κοινωνικής αλληλεπίδρασης.

Οι κυρίαρχες πρακτικές ελέγχου των ελεύθερων χώρων αποτελούν μέρος μιας ευρύτερης συνθήκης διαρκούς υποτίμησης των ζωών μας, μέσα στην οποία το κράτος επιδίδεται σε ένα κρεσέντο καταστολής. Από τον περιορισμό ή και την απαγόρευση των διαδηλώσεων, τις συλλήψεις και τις διώξεις όσων αντιστέκονται, τη συνέχιση των εκκενώσεων πολιτικών και στεγαστικών καταλήψεων, μέχρι τη συντονισμένη επίθεση μπάτσων και εργολάβων στους πανεπιστημιακούς χώρους και την ελεγχόμενη πρόσβαση σε αυτούς.

Στα πάρκα, στους δρόμους, στις πλατείες συναντιόμαστε, περπατάμε, αναπνέουμε, αντιστεκόμαστε στο καθεστώς της εξατομίκευσης, του φόβου και της ανασφάλειας που μας επιβάλλουν. Εκεί όπου δεν μεσολαβούν το εισιτήριο, η κατανάλωση, το κέρδος και ο έλεγχος, μπορούν να ανθίσουν σχέσεις αλληλεγγύης, συλλογικότητας και δημιουργίας. Να μην παραχωρήσουμε ούτε σπιθαμή τους. title: Halloween riots as youth uprising pushes on
content:
Photograph: Alain Jocard/AFP


from

Freedom News

, 2 November 2026


Against efforts by systemic forces to keep youth discontent in check, decentralised insurrection and autonomy continue to break through


Blade Runner


Halloween weekend saw mass protests throughout

France

,

Albania

,

Germany

,

Switzerland

 and

Portugal

, with riots erupting across multiple cities.


As Gen Z–led insurrections flare up globally, a neo-fascist surge has risen steadily alongside them. In the UK, the

assault on Freedom Bookshop

 sounds a clear warning and a reminder that the street-level provocations escalating across the country over the past few years are happening for a reason.


Systemic actors seek to keep the

youth’s insurgent tendencies

 in check, deliberately redirecting anger toward vulnerable groups such as

migrants

. This manufactured resentment is predictable amid ever-increasing housing and living costs for the working classes, pushing an increasing number of people to the margins.


At a time when Western superpowers engage in proxy wars and genocides abroad while leading an arms race at home, they ask their citizens to live with less and prepare for disaster.


This dynamic stems directly from the neoliberal restructuring of Western production in the 1980s. Designed to crush the advances of previous labour movements, it enforced the TINA (“There Is No Alternative”) dogma across politics and culture alike. Consequently, it has become increasingly difficult to imagine alternative ways of surviving, let alone navigating complex issues like personal liberty, identity, equality, and disagreement.


What mainstream news decries as a “shocking” resurgence of patriarchal misogyny among young people is often just youth mimicking adult behaviour—mirroring the brutality of genocidal wars and the competitive ethos of streaming media. Reproduced in schools and everyday life, hegemonic neoliberal ethics instil a worldview based on survival of the fittest, top-dog dominance, and “kill or be killed.”


Yet what this apparatus of indoctrination tries to suppress is the simple fact that when left to their own devices, most people naturally build networks of communal solidarity and mutual aid. In Serbia, following the Novi Sad canopy collapse and subsequent police violence,

student movements organised

 their resistance through confederated horizontal councils, effectively shifting the national political narrative. When elections arrived, they took the difficult decision to form an independent list that won national elections on 25 October 2026, ousting the Vu?i? regime after 15 years in power.


Representative democracy may not be a vehicle for social revolution, but this effort demonstrates the power of prefigurative politics. It proves that young people can mock authority, circumvent top-down structures, and channel the rage generated by class war into creative, radical action.


Where horizontal councils represent

organised prefigurative power

, the unguided unruliness of marginalised youth represents its raw, volatile foundation. Neofascist networks, nurtured by neoliberal centres, actively attempt to capture this untapped energy—redirecting class anger away from the ruling class to protect existing power structures. Yet as Gen Z leads insurrections worldwide, state attempts to enforce “law and order” inevitably generate contested spaces of disorder.


Radical left and anarchist currents meet the youth in these spaces, where bands of poor kids raised in the hinterlands of 21st-century capitalism disrupt the peace of petty bourgeois business owners. Their unguided discontent with the commodity society is a crude but authentic attempt to claim back autonomy. When survival is squeezed down to petty crime and syndicate work, roaming the streets at night with loot in hand becomes simultaneously alienating and liberating—an experiential truth of street-level autonomy that no top-down political theory can fully capture.


This reality explains the state’s aggressive attempts to criminalise and persecute horizontal protest structures, such as

Palestine Action in the UK

, which has not only struck major blows against domestic arms supply chains but has inspired offshoots across Europe and the US. The state relies on an old tactic: conflating separate legal cases to try activists together as members of an organised crime enterprise. The goal is to prevent the generalisation of dissent.

author: Wesley Whitman
title: လစ်ဘရယ်-မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ
content:
လစ်ဘာတေးရီးယန်း ဆိုရှယ်ဒီမိုကရေစီ သီအိုရီ


Wesley Whitman

. Original:

Liberal-Anarchism

, September 14, 2025. Translated into Burmese by Hein Htet Kyaw.


လစ်ဘရယ်ဝါဒ ဆိုတာ သေချာနားလည်အောင်ကြည့်ရင် လွတ်လပ်တဲ့ဈေးကွက် ဒါမှမဟုတ် လွတ်လပ်ခွင့် (negative liberty) အတွက်တင် အကြောင်းပြချက် ပေးတာမျိုး မဟုတ်ပါဘူး။ အခြေခံအားဖြင့်ကတော့ ဖိနှိပ်မှုတွေကနေ လွတ်မြောက်ရေးဆိုင်ရာ ဒဿနတစ်ခု ဖြစ်ပါတယ်။ အလားတူပါပဲ၊ မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ ဆိုတာ မင်းမဲ့စရိုက် ဆုတောင်းပွဲ မဟုတ်ဘဲ မည်သူမျှ စိုးမိုးခြယ်လှယ်ခြင်းမရှိတဲ့ ဆန္ဒအလျောက် ဖွဲ့စည်းထားတဲ့ လူမှုအဖွဲ့အစည်းကို ဖန်တီးဖို့ ကြိုးပမ်းတာ ဖြစ်ပါတယ်။ ဒီနားလည်မှု နှစ်ခုကို ပေါင်းစပ်ပြီး တွေးခေါ်မြှော်မြင်မှု ပရစ်ဇမ် (dialectical libertarian lens) နဲ့ ကြည့်လိုက်ရင်၊ အဲဒီအစဉ်အလာတွေကနေ ကျနော် “လစ်ဘရယ်-မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ” (liberal-anarchism) လို့ ခေါ်တဲ့ သီအိုရီသစ်တစ်ရပ် ဖြစ်ပေါ်လာပါတယ်။


အနုပဋိလောမ လစ်ဘာတေးရီးယန်း နည်းလမ်း


လစ်ဘရယ်-မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ ဟာ သဘောတရားအခြေခံ လစ်ဘာတေးရီးယန်းဝါဒရဲ့ ယုတ္တိပေါ်မှာ အခြေခံထားတာပါ။ ဒါဟာ သေသူလို ပုံသေကားချပ် မူဝါဒတစ်ခု မဟုတ်ဘဲ အခြေအနေပေါ်မူတည်ပြီး ကြည့်တတ်တဲ့ နည်းလမ်းတစ်ခု ဖြစ်ပါတယ်။ မူဝါဒ ဒါမှမဟုတ် အဖွဲ့အစည်း တစ်ခုခုကို “ပုံစံတကျ လစ်ဘာတေးရီးယန်း ဟုတ်မဟုတ်” ဆုံးဖြတ်မယ့်အစား၊ ဒီနည်းလမ်းက အဲဒီအရာဟာ သီးခြားလူမှုအခြေအနေတစ်ခုမှာ “တကယ်ပဲ လူတွေကို ဖိနှိပ်မှုကနေ လွတ်မြောက်စေသလား” လို့ မေးခွန်းထုတ်ပါတယ်။ ဥပမာ- ခွဲခြားဆက်ဆံမှု ဆန့်ကျင်ရေး ဥပဒေတွေဟာ စီးပွားရေးလုပ်ငန်းရှင် တစ်ယောက်ရဲ့ ပုံစံတကျ လွတ်လပ်ခွင့်ကို ကန့်သတ်နိုင်ပေမယ့်၊ သမိုင်းကြောင်းအရ ဖိနှိပ်ခံထားရတဲ့ လူမှုအသိုင်းအဝိုင်းမှာတော့ ဖိနှိပ်မှုကို လျှော့ချပေးပြီး ဖိနှိပ်ခံရသူတွေရဲ့ တကယ့်လွတ်လပ်ခွင့်ကို တိုးတက်စေတဲ့အတွက် တကယ်တမ်းကျ လစ်ဘာတေးရီးယန်း သဘောတရားနဲ့ ကိုက်ညီနေပါတယ်။


ဒီနည်းလမ်းကြောင့် အစိုးရရဲ့ ဝင်ရောက်စွက်ဖက်မှု တိုင်းကို ဖိနှိပ်မှုလို့ မမြင်တော့ပါဘူး။ တကယ်တော့ မြေယာတန်ဖိုးခွန် ဒါမှမဟုတ် လူမှုရေး အကျိုးအမြတ် ခွဲဝေမှု လိုမျိုး အစိုးရစွက်ဖက်မှုအချို့ဟာ လက်ဝါးကြီးအုပ် အခွင့်ထူးတွေကို ဖျက်ဆီးပစ်နိုင်ပြီး တစ်ဦးချင်းစီကို ပိုမိုလုပ်ပိုင်ခွင့် ပေးနိုင်ပါတယ်။ သမိုင်းဝင် အာဏာနဲ့ ကြွယ်ဝမှု စုစည်းမှုတွေ ကြောင့် ကစားကွင်းက မညီမညာဖြစ်နေတဲ့ လူအဖွဲ့အစည်းမှာ လွတ်လပ်ခွင့်ဆိုတာ ဝင်မစွက်ဖက်ဘဲ ဒီအတိုင်းကြည့်နေရုံနဲ့ မရဘဲ တက်တက်ကြွကြွ ပြန်လည်တည်ဆောက်ဖို့ လိုအပ်ပါတယ်။


ပြန်လည်ဖော်ထုတ်လိုက်သော လစ်ဘရယ်ဝါဒ


လစ်ဘရယ်-မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ ဟာ လစ်ဘရယ်ဝါဒရဲ့ သမိုင်းဝင် တိုးတက်ပြောင်းလဲမှု အပြည့်အဝကို လက်ခံထားပါတယ်။ အာဒမ် စမစ် (Adam Smith) နဲ့ ဂျွန် လော့ခ် (John Locke) တို့ရဲ့ တစ်ဦးချင်းစီရဲ့ လွတ်လပ်ခွင့်နဲ့ ပုဂ္ဂလိက ဦးဆောင်မှုကို အလေးပေးတဲ့ ဂန္ထဝင် လစ်ဘရယ်ဝါဒကိုရော၊ ဂျွန် ရောလ်စ် (John Rawls) ရဲ့ နိုင်ငံရေး လစ်ဘရယ်ဝါဒနဲ့ ဂျွန် မေးနဒ် ကိန်းစ် (John Maynard Keynes) တို့ရဲ့ စီးပွားရေး လက်တွေ့ဝါဒကိုပါ ပေါင်းစပ်ယူထားတာပါ။ ဒီတွေးခေါ်ရှင်တွေဟာ နိုင်ငံတော်ရဲ့ ဖိနှိပ်မှုပဲဖြစ်ဖြစ်၊ ဈေးကွက်ရဲ့ ဖိနှိပ်မှုပဲဖြစ်ဖြစ် ဖိနှိပ်ချုပ်ချယ်မှုတွေ ရှိနေသမျှ လွတ်လပ်ခွင့် ဆိုတာ ရှင်သန်လို့မရဘူးဆိုတဲ့ နားလည်မှုကို စေတနာတူ တူညီကြပါတယ်။


အာဒမ် စမစ် နဲ့ ဂျွန် လော့ခ် တို့လို ဂန္ထဝင် လစ်ဘရယ်ဝါဒီတွေဟာ မြေပိုင်ရှင် ဘုတ်ထိုင် စီးပွားရှာသူတွေရဲ့ အာဏာကို ကန့်သတ်ဖို့နဲ့ စီးပွားရေး သာယာဝပြောမှုကို ကျယ်ကျယ်ပြန့်ပြန့် မြှင့်တင်ဖို့အတွက် မြေယာတန်ဖိုး ခွန်ကောက်ခံတာကို ထောက်ခံခဲ့ကြပါတယ်။ ဂျွန် ရောလ်စ် က တရားမျှတတဲ့ လူအဖွဲ့အစည်းဆိုတာ အစဉ်အလာ ကင်းပီတယ်လစ်ဝါဒ ထက် ပိုင်ဆိုင်မှု ပစ္စည်းတွေကို လူထုကြား မျှမျှတတ ခွဲဝေပေးတဲ့ “ပိုင်ဆိုင်မှု-ပိုင်ဆိုင်သော ဒီမိုကရေစီ” ဖြစ်ရမယ်လို့ ဆိုပါတယ်။ ဒါ့အပြင် ရောလ်စ် က မညီမျှမှုတွေ ဖြစ်ပေါ်လာပြီးမှ ပစ္စည်းဥစ္စာတွေကို ပြန်လည်ခွဲဝေတာထက် မညီမျှမှုတွေ မဖြစ်ပေါ်အောင် အဖွဲ့အစည်းတွေကို ကြိုတင်ပုံစံထုတ်တာ က ပိုမိုထိရောက်ကြောင်း သဘောတရား ထည့်သွင်းခဲ့ပါတယ်။ တစ်ချိန်တည်းမှာပဲ ကိန်းစ် က အမှန်တကယ် ရှိနေတဲ့ ဈေးကွက်တွေရဲ့ မတည်ငြိမ်မှုကို အသိအမှတ်ပြုခဲ့ပြီး အလုပ်အကိုင် အပြည့်အဝရရှိရေးနဲ့ လူသားတွေရဲ့ သာယာဝပြောမှုကို ထောက်ပံ့ဖို့ သေချာစဉ်းစားထားတဲ့ စည်းမျဉ်းတွေ လိုအပ်တယ်လို့ အလေးပေးပြောခဲ့ပါတယ်။


ဒီသဘောအရ လစ်ဘရယ်-မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ ဟာ လက်ရှိ ဖြစ်ပေါ်နေတဲ့ အုပ်စုငယ်စု စီးပွားရေးစနစ် (ခရိုနီသဘော) ကို ငြင်းပယ်ပြီး၊ လစ်ဘရယ် ဒီမိုကရေစီနဲ့ ဈေးကွက်စနစ်တွေကို စည်းကမ်းချက်အချို့နဲ့ ထောက်ခံထားပါတယ်။ ဒါဟာ အာဏာရှင်ဆန်တဲ့ ကြွယ်ဝသူတွေရဲ့ စနစ် မဟုတ်ဘဲ ပိုင်ဆိုင်မှု-ပိုင်ဆိုင်သော ဒီမိုကရေစီကို ထောက်ခံပြီး၊ နိုင်ငံတော်ရဲ့ အတင်းအဓမ္မ ဖိနှိပ်ချုပ်ချယ်မှု ထိန်းချုပ်မှုကို သဘောတူညီချက်နဲ့ တာဝန်ယူမှုအပေါ် အခြေခံတဲ့ ဒီမိုကရေစီ အဖွဲ့အစည်းတွေနဲ့ အစားထိုးဖို့ ကြိုးပမ်းတာပါ။


အစွန်းရောက် လစ်ဘရယ်ဝါဒအဖြစ် မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ


လစ်ဘရယ်-မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ အခင်းအကျင်းမှာ မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ ဆိုတာ စည်းစနစ်ပျက်ပြားတာကို ငြင်းပယ်တာမဟုတ်ဘဲ ဖိနှိပ်ချုပ်ချယ်မှုကို ငြင်းပယ်တာ ဖြစ်ပါတယ်။ ပီးယား-ဂျိုးဇက် ပရူးဒွန် (Pierre-Joseph Proudhon)၊ ဖရက် ဖော့ဒ်ဗာရီ (Fred Foldvary) နဲ့ ပိုကျယ်ပြန့်တဲ့ အညမညသဘော နဲ့ ဂျီယို-လစ်ဘာတေးရီးယန်း အစဉ်အလာတွေကနေ ကူးစက်လာတဲ့ လစ်ဘရယ်-မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ ဟာ တရားဥပဒေနဲ့ စည်းစနစ်တွေဟာ ဆန္ဒအလျောက် ဖွဲ့စည်းထားတဲ့ အဖွဲ့အစည်းတွေကနေ ထွက်ပေါ်လာမယ့် လူအဖွဲ့အစည်းကို …

author: Matt Simmons
title: ‘Not at a distance’: listening and participating as decolonized journalism practice
content:
Stella Caruso records a video of drumming and singing led by Dúqva̓ísḷa William Housty. Photos by Matt Simmons


This story was produced in collaboration with

The Narwhal

.


I reach out to ​’Cúagilákv Jess Housty around the time of the Haíɫzaqv new year, when the wán̓ái (herring) return and harvesting season begins again after the long, dark winter.


We first connected six years ago, when Xenaksiala Elder Wa’xaid Cecil Paul left this world for the next and I was tasked with writing a

tribute

 to his life and legacy. I called ‘Cúagilákv and they told me stories about their interactions with him. Our paths have intersected a few times since — and before, unknowingly, in the neighbourhood I grew up in where they also spent time during their Youth. ‘Cúagilákv’s

poems

 are part of my love story, too, a thread of words and wild mint, mail and ferries. 


This time, I’ve reached out because I’m thinking about a tugboat called the Nathan E. Stewart, which ran aground near the village of Q’vúqvai in Gale Passage 10 years ago. Eight hours after it hit the rocks, it sank, spilling more than 100,000 litres of diesel and other pollutants. Grief and anger and trauma remain.


Much has been done since to protect Haíɫzaqv lands and waters from another tragedy. ‘Cúagilákv tells me how many others, including their brother, Dúqva̓ísḷa William Housty, are working on the technical and policy side of marine protections and stewardship. But ​’Cúagilákv is following a different path to care for Haíɫzaqv territory. 


“I’m going to deepen my commitment to land-based Youth programming so every kid in the community loves the territory and wants to protect it — and eventually they’ll be the system,” they explain.


Allisa Brown watches the other kids in λáλix̌sístala, the Big House at Kvai. Allisa joined me and Veda on the boat with ‘Cúagilákv

when we headed back to Wágḷísḷa the next morning.


Haíɫzaqv youth and camp staff Aria Reid and Norman Paul warm the drums by the fire before the 20th anniversary

celebration.


And they invite me and my daughter to attend the anniversary of the opening of λáλix̌sístala, a Haíɫzaqv Big House which was raised two decades ago on a beach in the Kvai watershed, around two hours by boat from the Haíɫzaqv capital of Wágḷísḷa (Bella Bella, B.C.) . I accept with gratitude, and following the words of Wa’xaid, I listen. I follow the Wedzin Kwa to where it meets K’sien, and from there follow the river to the ocean. 


In his house overlooking the bay at Wágḷísḷa, Ian Reid, a Haíɫzaqv artist and carver, tells me old stories of the animals and people, and some new ones too. We’re sitting together in his living room while our daughters play in the kitchen. Veda, my kiddo, and Hazel, theirs, met at Kvai and became fast friends. Eli, Hazel’s big brother, is in and out of the house, trying out some newfound freedom on his bike. Ian’s partner, Cayce, offers me a coffee. Cayce and I grew up a few blocks from each other and spent a year at the same elementary school — but we’re only meeting now. Ian’s brother, Garney, is outside the house fixing a water line in the street. I sat with Garney and his wife on the boat down to Kvai. We talked about movies.


I brought a blanket for Ian from the Unist’ot’en feast hall, delivering it for a friend. Ian, whose Haíɫzaqv name is ‘Nusi, meaning “Full Moon,” made a frog crest that was used by Dinï ze (Hereditary Chief) Nedïbïs of the C’ihlts’ehkhyu (Big Frog) Clan of the Wet’suwet’en Nation. Ian puts the blanket on “the way they would put it on me in the feast hall” and poses for a photo.


‘Nusi Ian Reid holds his abalone-adorned talking stick, wearing the blanket from the Unist’ot’en feast hall.


Why am I telling you all this? 


Because, as Opaskwayak Cree scholar Shawn Wilson says in

Research is Ceremony,

 “… it is important for storytellers to impart their own life and experience into the telling. When listeners know where the storyteller is coming from and how the story fits into the storyteller’s life, it makes the absorption of the knowledge that much easier.”


In a word: trust. 


I’ve been leaning into participatory journalism as a means of getting closer to stories that centre and prioritize the Indigenous communities where I’ve been welcomed and trusted, letting respect and reciprocity be my guides. In this practice, I’m not only finding deeper truths and more connection — I’m discovering richer, more nuanced stories.


Kim TallBear, in

Standing With and …

author: Unknown
title: Indigenous Action - Voting is Not Harm Reduction
content:
Author

: Indigenous Action

Title

: Voting is Not Harm Reduction

Date

: February 5, 2020

Source

: http://www.indigenousaction.org/voting-is-not-harm-reduction-an-indigenous-perspective/


 When proclamations are made that “voting is harm reduction,” it’s never clear how less harm is actually calculated. Do we compare how many millions of undocumented Indigenous Peoples have been deported? Do we add up what political party conducted more drone strikes? Or who had the highest military budget? Do we factor in pipelines, mines, dams, sacred sites desecration? Do we balance incarceration rates? Do we compare sexual violence statistics? Is it in the massive budgets of politicians who spend hundreds of millions of dollars competing for votes?


 Though there are some political distinctions between the two prominent parties in the so-called U.S., they all pledge their allegiance to the same flag. Red or blue, they’re both still stripes on a rag waving over stolen lands that comprise a country built by stolen lives.


 We don’t dismiss the reality that, on the scale of U.S. settler colonial violence, even the slightest degree of harm can mean life or death for those most vulnerable. What we assert here is that the entire notion of “voting as harm reduction” obscures and perpetuates settler-colonial violence, there is nothing “less harmful” about it, and there are more effective ways to intervene in its violences.


 At some point the left in the so-called U.S. realized that convincing people to rally behind a “lesser evil” was a losing strategy. The term “harm reduction” was appropriated to reframe efforts to justify their participation and coerce others to engage in the theater of what is called “democracy” in the U.S.


 Harm reduction was established in the 1980s as a public health strategy for people dealing with substance use issues who struggle with abstinence. According to the Harm Reduction Coalition (HRC) the principles of harm reduction establish that the identified behavior is “part of life” so they “choose not to ignore or condemn but to minimize harmful effects” and work towards breaking social stigmas towards “safer use.” The HRC also states that, “there is no universal definition of or formula for implementing harm reduction.” Overall, harm reduction focuses on reducing adverse impacts associated with harmful behaviors.


 The proposition of “harm reduction” in the context of voting means something entirely different from those organizing to address substance use issues. The assertion is that “since this political system isn’t going away, we’ll support politicians and laws that may do less harm.”


 The idea of a ballot being capable of reducing the harm in a system rooted in colonial domination and exploitation, white supremacy, hetero-patriarchy, and capitalism is an extraordinary exaggeration. There is no person whose life is not impacted every day by these systems of oppression, but instead of coded reformism and coercive “get out the vote” campaigns towards a “safer” form of settler colonialism, we’re asking “what is the real and tragic harm and danger associated with perpetuating colonial power and what can be done to end it?”


 Voting as practiced under U.S. “democracy” is the process with which people (excluding youth under the age of 18, convicted felons, those the state deems “mentally incompetent,” and undocumented folx including permanent legal residents), are coerced to choose narrowly prescribed rules and rulers. The anarchist collective Crimethinc observes, “Voting consolidates the power of a whole society in the hands of a few politicians.” When this process is conducted under colonial authority, there is no option but political death for Indigenous Peoples. In other words, voting can never be a survival strategy under colonial rule. It’s a strategy of defeat and victimhood that protracts the suffering and historical harm induced by ongoing settler colonialism. And while the harm reduction sentiment may be sincere, even hard won marginal reforms gained through popular support can be just as easily reversed by the stroke of a politician’s pen. If voting is the democratic participation in our own oppression, voting as harm reduction is a politics that keeps us at the mercy of our oppressors.

title: El suelo como espejo de la relación entre humanidad y naturaleza
content:
Por Patricia Fernández y Lourdes Gil Cardeza*


Somos muchas las personas, organizaciones e instituciones que reconocemos estar atravesando una crisis civilizatoria muy profunda. Hay tantísima evidencia que muestra cómo estamos sobrepasando los límites físicos que permiten nuestra existencia en el planeta Tierra. Hay un área específica de la economía que lo estudia: la economía ecológica. El estilo de vida que impone la sociedad occidental implica calentamiento global, una creciente y continua contaminación de suelos y aguas, y el constante despojo de tierras a pueblos indígenas y campesinos debido al avance del modelo económico, que pone en jaque a los procesos biológicos de la vida que han ido coevolucionando desde hace, al menos, 460 millones de años, cuando empezó a desarrollarse la vida fuera del agua.


El suelo es un espejo de los vínculos que lo conforman. Es la resultante de la convivencia evolutiva entre la roca madre, el clima y los seres vivos. En otras palabras, el suelo es parte de los procesos del planeta Tierra, el suelo es vida, el suelo está vivo. Tanto su color oscuro característico como ese olorcito que percibimos corresponden a la materia orgánica (componente fértil y vital del suelo), compuesta por los organismos vivos que lo habitan y por lo muerto en vía de descomposición que nutren de manera espiralada a los organismos y las plantas de las que nos alimentamos. El estilo de vida occidental pone en riesgo esa vitalidad.


El tipo de agricultura que domina al planeta no es un simple conjunto de técnicas para producir alimentos (y muchas veces commodities): es la materialización de una lógica de poder que entrelaza colonialismo, patriarcado y capitalismo. Así lo evidencian las voces críticas de pensadoras que ayer y hoy señalan cómo el avance sobre la tierra y la naturaleza es un reflejo de la misma lógica de dominación ejercida sobre los cuerpos de las mujeres y los territorios. Llegar a comprender la crisis o la degradación del suelo hoy, exige, en principio, desentrañar esta trama histórica y epistemológica que ha convertido a la naturaleza en un objeto de explotación ilimitada. 


Creemos que hacer el intento por desarmar esta trama (o trampa), es condición necesaria en el proceso de deconstrucción que elegimos, como dijo

Audre Lorde

, para transformar la ira en un proceso creativo. Con este texto buscamos traer a la actualidad, y a latinoamérica en particular, a Eve Balfour, una mujer de la aristocracia inglesa quien, con mucha claridad y simpleza, se atrevió a abordar temas invisibilizados en Europa y sus continentes colonizados, al publicar su libro

El Suelo Vivo

 (

The Living Soil

) en 1943. 


Foto: Matías sarlo - Minga


Esta tesis describe de manera sencilla los vínculos entre la salud humana y el cultivo de nuestros alimentos y pone la lupa en el suelo jerarquizando su rol como promotor de la salud toda. En palabras de Eve:

“La evidencia acumulada sobre la interrelación entre la vitalidad del suelo y la salud de las plantas, los animales y el ser humano es de tal importancia y de tan profundas implicancias que ya es hora de que el público en general tenga la oportunidad de estudiar y formarse su propio juicio al respecto”

.


La matriz del despojo


La crítica al modelo agrícola industrial debe partir de la constatación de que su origen no es meramente técnico, sino profundamente político. La antropóloga maya-kaqchikel

Aura Cumes

 sostiene que el patriarcado colonial llega desde Europa y se reconfigura en América para ejercer el sometimiento sobre las mujeres, las poblaciones indígenas y afrodescendientes convirtiéndolas en sujetos despojables y así validar la extracción del territorio y del cuerpo-territorio. Este proceso de dominación tuvo un pilar fundamental: la disociación del hombre respecto de la naturaleza, a la cual se feminizó para legitimar su conquista. "A partir de ello —explica Cumes— se atribuye la potestad de descubrirla, penetrarla, torturarla y convertirla en mercancía." 


Esta visión no es casual, sino que se fundamenta tanto en los textos bíblicos que otorgan al hombre el "señorío" sobre la creación como en el discurso científico que adoptó estos postulados como base de su conocimiento. En esta trama (o trampa), el capitalismo manifiesta la continuidad de las mismas lógicas que motorizaron al colonialismo al implementar la sustitución de ecosistemas enteros por una "biota mixta" europea (trigo, ganado vacuno, cerdos, malezas, microorganismos, personas) …

author: groundxero
title: The Twilight of Trumpism
content:
Contemporary Trumpism is not the conservative attempt to return US society back to the 1950s. It is the attempt to return US society back to the 1850s – an attempt which will fail completely, disastrously and totally.


 


By 

Dionysius


 


Between 2016 and 2026, the political system of the United States has been dominated by Trumpism, a.k.a. the US variant of billionaire fascism or plutofascism. Its domination was so complete that even when non-Trumpist politicians won elections, they did not question Trumpism’s single most compelling argument. This argument, in a nutshell, was that the United States could solve the 21st century problems of a

collapsing middle class

 and

an economy being looted by billionaire monopolists

 by a magical return to 19th century tariff walls, territorial imperialism and settler colonialism.


 


The year 2026 marks the moment when a majority of US citizens have stopped believing in 19th century magic. One of the most telling signs of this shift occurred on October 9, 2026, when Pete Hegseth, the Trumpist official in charge of the US military, announced that the US would broadcast the execution of a former US soldier on live television.


 


Hegseth had fully expected the announcement would create a wave of hurrah-patriotism. After all, the soldier in question, a former US Army major, had shot and killed 13 fellow soldiers and wounded 30 others at a military base in Fort Hood, Texas in 2009. The soldier also happened to be Muslim and the US-born son of Palestinian American immigrants, two groups which have been constantly scapegoated and persecuted by Trumpism.


 


Instead, the announcement triggered a firestorm of condemnation. Numerous former soldiers and Pentagon officials criticized the announcement as tantamount to a lynching, while human rights advocates pointed out that the only two countries which hold public executions are Taliban-ruled Afghanistan and theocrat-ruled Iran. Ten days later, overwhelming political pressure forced the Trump administration to back down and

call off the broadcast

.


 


To understand why Hegseth misread the situation so badly and why this moment is so significant, it is worth pausing for a moment to reflect on the group which forms the electoral core of Trumpism. This group consists of white males who are nostalgic for the settler colonial white masculinity which dominated US politics for almost two hundred years, i.e. between the creation of the US in 1783 and the civil rights and feminist struggles of the 1960s and early 1970s.


 


To understand why this group wants to return to the past, we must first understand that this white masculinity was responsible for 105 years of settler colonial land theft and genocide against the First Nations of North America. This period began with the 1785-1795 Northwest Indian War, and ended in the Wounded Knee Massacre in South Dakota committed by US soldiers against the Lakota people on December 29, 1890. Most of the surviving First Nations were confined to reservations thereafter, and none enjoyed full US citizenship rights until the Snyder Act of 1924.


 


This white masculinity was also crucial to perpetrating the horrors of 82 years of US chattel slavery (1783-1865) on African Americans and citizens kidnapped from Africa by slave traders. After the abolition of slavery in 1865, this white masculinity engineered systems of legal apartheid (commonly called “Jim Crow” laws) which privileged whites at the expense of African Americans. In addition to these laws, many US states had groups of white terrorists who regularly assaulted and murdered African Americans. The most notorious of these terrorists were the Klu Klux Klan, an organization so powerful that as late as August 12, 1925, an estimated 30,000 of their members marched openly through the US capital of Washington, DC without any legal repercussions whatsoever.


 


Official Jim Crow and unofficial racial terror ruled large parts of the US for 87 years (i.e. 1878-1965). They did not disappear until the 1965 Voting Rights Act granted African Americans the right to vote in all US states, and until Federal law enforcement agencies cracked down on white terrorist groups during the 1960s and 1970s.

author: winter oak
title: Calling on our ancestors!
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article

here


After I published my articles on the Druids and ancient Celtic culture this summer, Franklin O’Kanu wrote on his

Unorthodoxy

 blog about the parallels to his own ancestral culture.


He

said

: “What’s interesting about all of this is how two cultures, across the world, Nigerian and Celtic, have the same spiritual view of the world”. [1]


And he

commented

 on one of my posts: “From the Yoruba and Igbo perspective, what the Celts experience in one continent is what the practitioners of Ifa experienced in another continent: the same honor of the Divine”. [2]


I have now discovered similar echoes from a reverse direction, as it were, through reading

Of Water and the Spirit: Ritual, Magic, and Initiation in the Life of an African Shaman

 by Malidoma Patrice Somé (1956–2021).


Somé belonged to the Dagara, a million-strong people spread across the artificially-created nation-states of Ghana, the Ivory Coast and Burkina Faso – he came from the latter, which was still called French Upper Volta when he was born.


The environment and particular customs of this African people are, of course, very different from those of the ancient Celts – roasted monkey would not have been on the menu at a Beltane feast in Ireland!


But there are similarities as well. In the essay series I

cite

 Jean Markale’s account of how at their celebratory events the Celts drank copious amounts of alcoholic drinks, producing “drunkenness, in other words the trance thanks to which one can go beyond apparent reality and see the supernatural”. [3]


He adds: “For Greek and Roman writers, Celts already had a reputation for being passionate lovers of fermented drinks. Drunkenness is an oft-occurring theme in the epics, especially in Irish accounts.


“Gods and heroes compete in their unquenchable thirst for alcohol, in the form of beer, wine or mead. A religious festival never went by without a serious drinking session”. [4]


In

his

 book, Somé writes: “Millet beer has always been a part of major rituals. Our rituals are long, and one gets thirsty”. [5]


He explains that his tribe was said to have been taught how to make beer by the Kontomboli, mysterious otherwordly beings who introduced a woman to their astonishing brew: “When she drank it, she was delighted. She felt merry and wanted to sing”. [6]


I was also intrigued to learn that the Dagara use a twenty-based counting system, so that eighty-three would be expressed as “four times twenty plus three”. [7]


In France the same number is

quatre-vingt-trois

, “four twenties and three”, after the old Celtic system, and we used to have the same concept in English with a score, meaning twenty, using which eight-three is “four score and three”.


A more important connection between ancient European and African societies has been the effects of colonisation.


From an African perspective it must be strange to hear a white man claim to be the victim of colonialism, but such is the case.


Following the destruction of our indigenous culture by the Roman empire and its religious wing, we were then

colonised

 by the empire of usury and commerce and used as fodder for its insatiable industrial Leviathan. [8]


With our true identities further smothered, our vital energy was hijacked to allow that same empire to enslave and exploit other peoples across the world, including the Dagara.


Somé writes: “My own elders had experienced French colonialism and the culture of the West as a force that used violence as a means to eradicate traditional lifeways.


“They had seen their own youth stolen from them as they vainly struggled against the incursions of these intruders.


“During these years, in which my people were trying to make sense of a people whose every action seemed to go against the natural order of things, creating chaos, death, and destruction, the sense of unified community that sustained their tribal life was profoundly destabilized. These foreigners seemed to have no respect for life, tradition, or the land itself…


“In spite of the best efforts of all my people, the whites kept on coming; kept on doing whatever they pleased; and kept on taking more and more of our land, our beliefs and our lives”. [9]


“It is a sad thing to realize how much my people have lost and how much yet of our reality is to be buried in the pit of oblivion”. [10]


Although Upper Volta officially became independent in 1960 (it became Burkina Faso in 1984), this …

author: ROAPE
title: Africa on the map, but still off the table
content:
On 4 September 2026, the United Nations General Assembly adopted a non-binding resolution that might initially appear to belong to the relatively technical world of cartography. The resolution, “Correct the Map: Rebalancing Global Cartographic Representation and Promoting Equitable Representation of the World’s Regions, Particularly Africa,” was introduced by Togo on behalf of the African Group and adopted by 164 countries, with one country voting against and six abstaining.


In presenting the resolution, Togo’s Foreign Minister Robert Dussey argued that maps are not merely technical tools: their repeated use in schools, the media and digital platforms shapes how people understand and visualise the world. The African Group argued that the Mercator projection, designed for specific purposes—especially maritime navigation—had become a general-purpose image of the world that visually minimises Africa and other regions near the Equator.


The delegation framed the initiative around scientific and educational accuracy, cognitive justice, historical memory and the equal dignity of peoples. It also stressed what the resolution would not do: condemn the Mercator projection, impose a single map for every use, alter borders or take a position on territorial claims. Instead, it encouraged the use of projections such as Equal Earth when comparing the relative areas of continents, alongside better teaching about the strengths and limitations of different projections.


The resolution encourages the use of equal-area map projections, including Equal Earth, particularly when the relative size of regions matters. It also highlights the implications of existing representations for geographical and cartographic literacy. Importantly, however, it does not replace the Mercator projection, redraw international borders or alter the legal status of any territory. So why does a map matter? And why now?


These questions are more significant than the technical debate over which projection should be used. The UN resolution opens a much larger question about who has historically possessed the authority to represent the world, whose knowledge becomes universal knowledge, and what happens when previously marginalised actors begin to challenge that authority.


Mercator Map versus Equal Earth (wikicommons)


The map is not the territory—but it shapes how the territory is imagined


Gerardus Mercator’s famous projection was first published in 1569. It was developed primarily as a tool for maritime navigation, as its preservation of angles and constant compass bearings made it particularly useful for sailors plotting routes across oceans. The projection was never intended to provide an accurate comparison of the relative size of continents. Its distortion, however, has had a long afterlife.


Because the Mercator projection increasingly enlarges landmasses as they move away from the Equator, Greenland can appear comparable in size to Africa, despite Africa being approximately fourteen times larger.There is therefore an important distinction to make. Mercator was not invented as a deliberate attempt to make Africa smaller. Its original purpose was navigational. The political question emerges from what happened afterwards: how a projection designed for a particular technical purpose became normalised as a general image of the world.


A cartographic choice made for navigation became, through repetition, an educational and cultural convention. Maps entered classrooms, atlases, newspapers, television graphics, websites and digital platforms. In doing so, they did more than provide geographical information. They participated in producing a particular visual imagination of the world. This is where cartography becomes political. Can a two-dimensional map ever be neutral?


From geographical distortion to cognitive hierarchy


The significance of the new

UN resolution

 therefore lies less in replacing one map with another than in recognising that representation itself has consequences. The resolution’s language is striking. It connects cartographic representation to education, perception and collective understanding, framing the correction of historical distortions as a matter of equitable representation. The UN Office of the Special Adviser on Africa has presented the initiative as an African-led effort to challenge the symbolic minimisation of the continent. But the tension remains.


If representation contributes to how societies imagine the world …

author: Shannia Cabuello
title: Molbog community exposes agenda behind land-use projects
content:
They turned our ancestor’s burial sites into dumping grounds.

“They want to take everything so we insisted on coming here to express ourselves. We will embrace our land even if they harass us. We will not give it even if we get hurt.”

Molbog community member Anjilon Flores from Balabac Palawan stressed this point as Molbog indigenous peoples travelled to Metro Manila ahead of US President Donald Trump’s visit.

They aim to amplify their resistance against the Department of Environmental and Natural Resources’ Enhanced National Greening Program (E-NGP) and the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA).

Along with multi-sectoral groups and environmental advocates, they exposed the E-NGP and EDCA as tools of imperialist war and resource plunder, threatening the life, livelihood, culture, and ancestral lands of the Molbog people.

Long before Spanish colonial rule, the Molbog community have been the traditional stewards of Balabac island, depending on coconut farming, shifting cultivation, fishing, and harvesting seaweeds for livelihood.

“Palawan is a key biodiversity area and known to be the last ecological frontier of the Philippines,” Bianca Intia of Kalikasan Timog Katagalugan (TK) said at a press conference on October 26.

It shelters several endemic animal and plant species, including Philippine Mouse-deer which are exclusively found in Balabac and nearby islands.

Flores described their fields as prosperous with cassava, banana, corn, peanuts, and rice, making it their community’s main source of income for decades.

For them, lands are sacred that require ancestral permission before undertaking any activities like when entering the land, performing rituals, planting, harvesting, and cutting trees.

Born in Balabac, Flores cannot accept the prohibitions imposed by the E-NGP in using their resources. “They would restrict us from cutting trees which we use for firewood. This is also the livelihood for most of us. What will happen if they forbid us? Our livelihood will also be gone.”

Bangsa Molbog leader Emmanuel San Esteban lamented the encroachment of Balabac Air Base on their homes, sacred prayer grounds, and burial sites in Barangay Catagupan without any consultation with their tribal officials.

“They turned our ancestor’s burial sites into dumping grounds. The mountains where we do our rituals were flattened,” San Esteban said.

The local authorities said that the remains of their ancestors would be transferred to a different location. However, this is against the principles and culture of the Molbog tribe.

The indigenous residents dread the impact of both projects, as it begins to disrupt their peace, routines, and tradition.

They stressed that access to their land has been restricted, limiting the products they could gather from the forest.

According to DENR, the E-NGP was signed to rehabilitate the estimated 1.2 million hectares of the remaining unproductive, denuded, and degraded forestlands by 2022. It also aimed to maintain and protect existing forests.

This was already implemented by the DENR in several areas in Balabac where trees were planted in Barangay Catagupan, Agutayan, and Indalawan.

The communities worried about fines for damaging plants under E-NGP while clearing farmland. Cutting a tree must also be replaced with a hundred more trees and a Php 6,000 ($94) fine.

Kalikasan TK underscored that E-NGP did not aim to benefit communities but only to carbon offset the Ipilan Nickel Corporation’s deforestation and mining operations in Brooke’s Point, Palawan.

The Molbog people also expressed concerns that monocropping and fast-growing plant species under the E-NGP could affect forest biodiversity and native vegetation.

“The E-NGP is within our ancestral domain, for which we had applied for a Certificate on Ancestral Domain Title (CADT),” said San Esteban, questioning how the project progressed faster than their CADT application.

They first filed their CADT application in 2004 but the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP) only certified the application in 2019. To expedite the process, the NCIP required them to pay at least Php 1.6 million ($25,092.33). Their CADT remains pending.

San Esteban said that Balabac Air Base in Barangay Catagupan also pushed through because of the NCIP’s manipulation of the Free, Prior, and Informed Consent (FPIC) process.

author: anred
title: Trump bombardea Irán en la madrugada de su derrota electoral
content:
Tal como lo descontaban los sondeos electorales y hasta los “mercados”, Trump sufrió una derrota de carácter aplastante en los comicios de este martes. A

 nadie escapa que en el telón de fondo del rechazo electoral a Trump se encuentra la guerra contra Irán y sus consecuencias económicas. Pero al referirse al resultado electoral, los principales voceros del partido Demócrata -y también los de la democracia imperialista europea- han ocultado la cuestión de la guerra por abajo el felpudo. Un largo posteo oficial de Obama ni la menciona, después de varias invocaciones a la “unión nacional”. La guerra imperialista en desarrollo, que comenzó bajo el mandato de Biden, está en el horizonte estratégico de republicanos y demócratas.

Para Trump, la continuidad de la guerra con Irán es también un recurso para prevalecer sobre la Unión Europea, en medio del agravamiento de la guerra entre Ucrania y Rusia y los acuerdos por «separado» entre Putin y el propio Trump.

Un escenario de escalada militar, por un lado, y mayor autoritarismo, por el otro, agravará la crisis política y los estallidos populares al interior de los Estados Unidos, en medio de una crisis financiera en ciernes. El eje de la crisis mundial pasa por el corazón del imperialismo.

Por Marcelo Ramal (Política Obrera).


Tal como lo descontaban los sondeos electorales y hasta los “mercados”, Trump sufrió una derrota de carácter aplastante en los comicios de este martes. La victoria demócrata, que se consideraba segura en Representantes (diputados), también tuvo lugar en el Senado, donde la composición final sería de 52 o 53 escaños demócratas contra 48 o 47 de los republicanos. Los reveses de Trump abarcaron a estados con un dominio histórico de su partido, como Carolina del Norte y del Sur -en este último caso, ganaron los demócratas después de 25 años de mandatos republicanos; también en el bastión petrolero de Texas, donde se impuso un senador demócrata después de 38 años, y lo mismo en Kansas, después de casi un siglo de hegemonía republicana. En Florida, bastión del exilio derechista cubano y venezolano y corazón del movimiento MAGA, la candidata republicana María Salazar había tomado distancias de Trump para salvar el voto migrante. A pesar de ello, sólo se imponía por una diferencia del 0,1%, en un escrutinio voto a voto. En Michigan, la victoria del candidato de origen musulmán Abdul El Sayed lograba prevalecer después de una furiosa campaña en su contra de Trump y del sionismo.


Significado


Ningún observador reconoce un liderazgo o fisonomía política definida en la victoria demócrata: el hilo conductor del resultado electoral es el golpe asestado a Trump -los electores, que concurrieron masivamente a sufragar en un país donde el voto es voluntario- desplegaron una movilización política en rechazo a la carestía desatada por la guerra, la represión política y el “estado de excepción” impuesto por Trump contra la población migrante. Las redadas del ICE llegaron a convertirse en un factor de desorganización económica, al imponer una zozobra que afecta a una parte de la fuerza laboral del capitalismo americano. La tentativa de “reindustrialización” del país a costa de sanciones comerciales extendidas tuvo pobres resultados y acrecentó la inflación. La carestía fue también estimulada por la instalación de los centros de datos para la oligarquía tecnológica de la IA. En sus campañas electorales, los gobernadores electos de Texas, Ohio, Georgia y Pensilvania hicieron de la oposición a la instalación de estas infraestructuras un eje de campaña. 29 jurisdicciones votaron este martes medidas locales de restricción a estas instalaciones, con apoyo abrumador de la población. La política MAGA, en definitiva, sólo hizo grande a los negocios de la camarilla trumpista y la oligarquía tecnológica. Para la población explotada, sólo trajo inflación, salarios a la baja y mayor zozobra en el empleo.


Entre Mr. Veto y los acuerdos


“Con mi nombre en la boleta, ganábamos en todos lados”. Esto posteó Trump después de la derrota, desconociendo u ocultando que él mismo se había puesto al frente de las elecciones que acababa de perder. Pero la alusión a su figura apunta a lo que viene: la pretensión de erigir un régimen de poder personal, a costa de decretazos y de vetos. Las mayorías cosechadas por los demócratas no tienen la contundencia para desconocer esos vetos -tampoco para hacer avanzar hasta el final un juicio político contra Trump. author: Kodao Productions
title: Groups vow to hound Trump when he visits the Philippines next week
content:
Fresh from his resounding defeat in the US midterm elections, President Donald Trump would not be getting sympathy from Filipino groups who promised to hound the leader they blame for worsening the Philippines’ worst economic crisis in decades.


Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) and other groups and networks in the Philippines and abroad announced 12 days of protest starting this week against Trump’s visit to Manila on Nov. 16 and 17.


“Under the banner ‘Trump Out,’ we shall hold daily actions ranging from marches, rallies, indoor assemblies, public forums, pickets, concerts, teach-ins, camp-outs, and vigils aimed at expressing the Filipino people’s strong objection to Trump’s visit,” Bayan chairperson Teddy Casino said in the press conference on Wednesday.


Bayan said Trump will not come as a friend and has in fact caused untold hardships on the Filipino people and other peoples of the world.


Casino said they are raising many reasons to reject Trump’s visit for the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits

 hosted by the Philippines that currently chairs the regional formation.


Bayan said Trump is accountable for the war of aggression in Iran, his support for Israel’s genocide in Gaza, military escalation in the Philippines and Asia Pacific, sanctions and military interventions in Venezuela, Cuba, the Caribbean, and the entire Western Hemisphere, his unjust crackdown on immigrants and critics on the US mainland, and his many other actions that harm the global economy and undermine world peace.


Trump’s real objective in the Philippines


Trump has made the Philippines as the US’ “first island chain of defense” against China and as a staging ground for military intervention in the region, dragging us ever closer to war with its biggest neighbor, Casino said.


The former Bayan Muna Representative recalled that in his last visit in 2017, Trump called the Philippines the most valuable piece of military real estate. “Since then, the US has drastically increased the presence of its troops, military facilities, and weapons systems all over the country,” Casino said.


Bayan said they are opposing the Pax Silica Economic Security Zone in Tarlac, a project Trump promotes as US’ “defense-industrial and dual-use backbone.”


“Pax Silica threatens to displace thousands of Ayta people and farmers, gobble up water and energy resources, and cause massive environmental problems not only in Tarlac but in mining areas all over the country. With US demands for extraterritorial authority and virtual control of our critical and rare earth minerals, it is shaping into a total sell-out of our national sovereignty and patrimony,” Casino said.


Nationwide protests


Bayan vowed to hound Trump from his hotel to Malacañang and everywhere else he goes while in the Philippines.


Bayan said various groups from Southern Tagalog and Central Luzon will converge with protesters in Manila in the run-up to Nov. 16. A big rally will be held in the afternoon of the 16th and possibly the morning of the 17th until Trump leaves.


“[The protests are] to remind him that he is not welcome here and should be kicked out,” Casino said.


Protests abroad


The International League of Peoples’ Struggle (ILPS) said its country chapters, members and allies are organizing solidarity actions against Trump’s visit to the Philippines and expected signing of the Pax Silica agreement with Philippine counterpart Ferdinand Marcos Jr.


ILPS said protest rallies, public forums, and other solidarity activities will be held in Melbourne and Sydney, Australia; Canada; Berlin, Germany; Hong Kong; New Delhi and West Bengal, India; Indonesia; Iwakuni, Japan; Malaysia; the Netherlands; Auckland, New Zealand; Pakistan; Thailand; London, United Kingdom; and the U.S. (Honolulu, Los Angeles, New York, Oregon, and Washington, DC).


“The actions that our members and allies are organizing in different countries are a show of international solidarity and a united front against the common and biggest enemy of the world’s peoples today: U.S. imperialism as represented by the war criminal Donald Trump,” said Azra Sayeed, ILPS General Secretary. #

(Raymund B. Villanueva)

title: Eine Welt zu Gewinnen! – Interview zur Konferenz und dem Anspruch des Internationalismus im 21. Jahrhundert
content:

In Zeiten der Zuspitzung der globalen Systemkrise und im Angesicht ihrer direkten Auswirkungen auf uns hierzulande wollen wir eine neue Debatte über internationalistische Praxis und Ausrichtung hier in Deutschland anstoßen. Wir sprechen mit Ayşe vom Bund der Kommunist:innen

Lena:

 Die Konferenz wird einen ganzen Tag lang gehen und ist in drei Blöcke aufgeteilt: Zu Beginn haben wir Brigitte Studer eingeladen, die ihre Recherchen zur KomIntern vorstellen wird. Dabei werden wir natürlich Publikumsfragen stellen können, um zusammen herauszufinden, welche Lehren wir aus der Vergangenheit ziehen können. Im zweiten Panel teilt dann Torkil Lauesen seine Analyse des globalen Kapitalismus und seine Perspektiven mit uns. Was vor allem im Hinblick auf eine spezifische Praxis in den Zentren des Imperialismus sehr spannend wird.


Ay

ş

e

:

 Das Podium im Anschluss ist ein Ausdruck von dem, was wir mit der gesamten Konferenz versuchen: Wir schauen uns nicht nur die Geschichte der imperialistischen Epoche des Kapitalismus an, sondern auch, was die Bedeutung des Internationalismus in den imperialistischen Krisen war. Wie war unsere internationalistische Praxis in Deutschland in den letzten Jahrzehnten und wie muss eine zukünftige internationalistische Arbeit aussehen? Wir sehen die imperialistische Weltlage einerseits und haben viele internationalistische Erfahrungen. Wenn wir uns zum Beispiel Kurdistan anschauen, vollzieht sich ja ein Umbruch. Deshalb muss die konkrete Analyse, zu der wir gemeinsam an dem Tag kommen, auch dazu führen, dass die Art und Weise, wie unsere Praxis aussieht, sich sozusagen daran anpasst. Und das werden wir eben auf dem Podium gemeinsam, auch aus unseren verschiedenen Erfahrungen und Perspektiven, zusammenbringen.


Worin seht ihr die Herausforderung eines proletarischen bzw. sozialistischen Internationalismus in der heutigen Zeit?


Lena:

 Was wir vielleicht erstmal grundsätzlich zum Verständnis von Internationalismus sagen müssen: Aufgrund des global organisierten Kapitalismus brauchen wir auch eine internationale Strategie. Probleme dabei gibt es viele. Die subjektive Situation, also die Situation von uns organisierten Kräften, müssen wir dabei hervorheben: Auch wenn wir sehen, dass es einen Aufschwung bei den sozialistischen Kräften gibt, sind wir nicht so breit aufgestellt und stabil verankert. Es braucht eine gut organisierte gesellschaftliche Bewegung, um mit einer Relevanz tatsächlich in internationale Beziehungen zu gehen. Ein weiteres Problem ist die Trennung, die wir sowohl als Jugendliche, Frauen, als auch ArbeiterInnen anhand von nationalen Grenzen als auch anderen Machtgrenzen erfahren.


Ay

ş

e:

 Ja, viele Sachen, die Lena genannt hat, würde ich genauso teilen. Ich würde noch hinzufügen, dass, wenn man sich spezifisch die Arbeiterklasse anschaut, das Problem eben die extreme Heterogenität dieser ist. Nicht nur innerhalb der globalen Waren- und Produktionskette, sondern selbst hier in den Betrieben in Deutschland sehen wir: Okay, es gibt eigentlich verschiedene Stellungen in jedem Betrieb, es gibt Festangestellte, Subunternehmer, ganz prekär arbeitende Leute, die ja nicht mal in einem Betrieb ein gemeinsames Interesse formulieren können. Wenn man sich das über nationale Grenzen hinweg anschaut, ist es noch schlimmer.


In Deutschland haben wir das Problem, dass wir es tatsächlich großflächig mit einer Arbeiteraristokratie zu tun hatten. Gerade da, wo eigentlich ganz viel Macht bei der Arbeit liegt: Die Leute, die bei BMW und Mercedes und Volkswagen an den teuren Anlagen sitzen, wo ganz viel Mehrwert in wenigen Sekunden produziert wird, das sind natürlich auch die Leute, die am meisten befriedet sind, weil es einen super Kündigungsschutz gibt, die ein ganz gutes Gehalt bekommen und so weiter und so fort.

author: Unknown
title: 25 organizations in Europe seek to strengthen joint struggle and solidarity
content:
25 political and civil society organizations from Turkey and Kurdistan have agreed to establish a joint alliance for struggle and solidarity in Europe. The initiative aims to bring together different political currents and strengthen resistance against the rise of right-wing and fascist forces, imperialist war policies, and state repression. At the same time, the participating organizations intend to support the peace and democratic society process in Turkey and advocate for a democratic solution to the Kurdish question.


The agreement stems from a meeting held on October 17 at the Cologne headquarters of the Federation of Alevi Communities in Europe (AABK). Representatives from various political traditions and social movements gathered at the invitation of eight organizations. In a joint final declaration issued today, the participants reaffirm their determination to preserve their organizational independence while establishing a lasting foundation for joint political action.


Against militarism, fascism and imperialist war policies


In their declaration, the organizations describe a world marked by growing international tensions. They warn that wars and conflicts driven by imperialist centers of power are increasing the risk of a broader military confrontation, potentially escalating into a new global war over the redistribution of power and resources. While ever-greater resources are being devoted to armament and warfare, they say, poverty and social inequality are deepening. The consequences, they argue, are borne primarily by working and oppressed sections of society, women, and the natural environment.


The signatories view the growing strength of right-wing and fascist movements as part of this development. They argue that militarism, racism, sexism, hostility toward refugees and migrants, and the destruction of the natural foundations of life are interconnected. At the same time, social forces opposing these developments are increasingly being criminalized.


The organizations therefore call for stronger international coordination among movements of struggle. They remark that resistance movements from India to France and the United States, as well as Yemen and Rojava, must not remain isolated from one another. “Their experiences must be brought together and transformed into a shared framework of internationalist solidarity. Peace, democracy, and social justice cannot be expected from the very power structures responsible for war, exploitation, and oppression. Instead, the key lies in strengthening ties between working and oppressed populations across national borders.”


Joint resistance against AKP-MHP policies


Another key focus of the declaration is the political situation in Turkey. According to the organizations, the AKP-MHP government is exploiting the international shift to the right to consolidate its authoritarian system of rule on a permanent basis. They point out that repression against the political opposition, arrests, bans, and restrictions on democratic rights are aimed at suppressing social resistance and weakening organized opposition forces.


According to the organizations, those particularly affected include workers, trade unions, democratic organizations, intellectuals, artists, and opposition political groups. At the same time, the collective rights of the Kurdish and Alevi populations continue to be disregarded. Women face patriarchal violence and discrimination, while the protection of children and the right to life of animals, as well as the preservation of nature, are systematically neglected.


The organizations do not regard these policies as an isolated development in Turkey. Rather, they see them as part of a broader authoritarian offensive through which capitalist centers of power and reactionary governments are responding to social crises. This, they argue, makes it necessary to connect democratic and social struggles in Turkey with those in Europe and other regions of the world.


Democratic solution to the Kurdish question as a shared responsibility


The participating organizations explicitly address the peace and democratic society process, stating: “Although Abdullah Öcalan and the PKK have paved the way for political and democratic dialogue through their decisions to end the armed struggle, the AKP-MHP government and the Turkish state continue to refuse to take the necessary steps toward genuine progress.”
