author: Sophie Lemcke
title: So ist es, als weibliches Rind in der Milchindustrie zu leben
content:
Die Milchindustrie ist ein grausamer Kreislauf des Leids und endet mit einem gewaltvollen Tod.


Wie fühlt es sich an, in dieses System hineingeboren zu werden, ohne die Möglichkeit, dem zu entkommen?


Der einzige Grund, weshalb die Industrie dich „produziert“ hat: Auch du sollst Kinder gebären, immer wieder, damit du Milch produzierst. Milch, die dann von Menschen, statt von deinem Kalb konsumiert werden kann.


Du wirst fixiert, während jemand das Besamungsgerät in deine Vagina sowie seinen Arm in deinen Anus einführt. Wenn die Zwangsbefruchtung nicht beim ersten Mal zur Trächtigkeit führt – was oft der Fall ist –, wird dieser Vorgang mehrfach wiederholt.


Neun Monate – wie bei uns Menschen – wächst dein Kalb in dir heran. Du spürst eine Verbindung, merkst, wie es sich bewegt und immer größer wird. Je schwerer du selbst wirst, umso stärker werden deine Gelenkprobleme. Die rutschigen und harten Spaltenböden, auf denen du fast dein ganzes Leben verbringst, führen oft zu Verletzungen.


Dann bringst du dein Kalb zur Welt. Um dich herum riecht es extrem nach Kot und Ammoniak, von den Ausscheidungen der Tiere.


Endlich ist es da, noch ganz nass und schwach. Du leckst ihm über das Fell, um es zu wärmen. Es sucht deine Nähe und will an deinem Euter die für ihn so wichtige Erstmilch trinken. Sie stärkt sein noch schwaches Immunsystem und gibt ihm Kraft. Doch dann kommen die Arbeiter*innen.


Sie zerren dein noch ganz wackelig stehendes Kalb weg von dir. Es ruft nach dir. Du versuchst, bei ihm zu bleiben, aber du hast keine Chance. Die Menschen haben es weggebracht – du wirst es wahrscheinlich nie wiedersehen und nach nur zwei Monaten direkt wieder gewaltvoll befruchtet.


Du wirst nach der Geburt monatelang mehrmals täglich in den Melkstand getrieben – und die meiste Zeit davon bist du bereits wieder schwanger. Dein Körper muss gleichzeitig ein neues Kalb versorgen, das in dir heranwächst, und täglich über 22 Liter Milch produzieren. Dein Euter und deine Zitzen schmerzen. Aufgrund der extremen Überzüchtung produzierst du viermal so viel Milch, wie du es natürlicherweise für dein Kind tun würdest.


Die Prozeduren und Haltungsbedingungen zehren stark an deinem Körper. Dein Euter ist entzündet und schmerzt bei jeder Berührung. Andere Tiere humpeln, weil ihnen jeder Schritt wehtut. Viele sind schwach und ausgelaugt.


Wenn du nicht schon vorher stirbst oder getötet wirst, weil dein Körper nicht mehr kann, dann wirst du voraussichtlich nach nur fünf Jahren getötet – obwohl du unter natürlichen Bedingungen 25 Jahre alt werden könntest.


Dann kommt der Tag, an dem du als nicht mehr profitabel giltst. Du wirst aus dem Stall getrieben – das erste Mal nach Jahren verlässt du ihn, aber das ist kein Grund zur Freude.


Zusammen mit anderen erschöpften „ausgedienten Milchkühen“ wirst du auf einen Transporter verladen. Du hast Mühe, über die Rampe zu gehen. Deine Gelenke schmerzen vom jahrelangen Stehen auf Spaltenböden. Im engen Transporter stehst du dicht an dicht mit den anderen Tieren, der Lkw wackelt. Manche fallen hin und werden versehentlich getreten. Eure Fahrt in den Schlachthof dauert mehrere Stunden, ohne Wasser, ohne Nahrung, ohne Pause.


Angekommen erwartet dich ein brutaler Tod. Überall riecht es nach Blut, du bekommst Panik, aber es gibt keinen Ausweg. Dann ein Bolzenschuss in deinen Kopf. Wenn die Betäubung korrekt durchgeführt wurde und wirkt, brichst du zusammen. Wenn nicht, kann es sein, dass du bei Bewusstsein und unter extremen Schmerzen erlebst, wie dir deine Kehle aufgeschnitten wird und du verblutest.


Es ist unvorstellbar, was Mutterrinder in der Milchindustrie erleiden müssen.


Der wahre Preis von Milch


Ein Ermittler von Animal Equality hat mehrere Monate undercover in einem deutschen Milchgewinnungsbetrieb gearbeitet und den Alltag der Tiere dokumentiert. Was unsere Undercover-Recherche zeigt, ist der wahre Preis von Milch: Ausbeutung, Gewalt, Schmerz, Leid und Tod.


Auf unserer Webseite erfährst du mehr und kannst die Stellungnahme des Betriebs nachlesen:


Zur Undercover-Recherche


Unterstütze dieses grausame System nicht!


Entscheide dich konsequent für pflanzliche Lebensmittel. Im Supermarkt findest du zahlreiche Alternativen zu Milch, wie:


Hafermilch – mild, cremig, perfekt für Kaffee und Müsli (oft die günstigste Option!)


Sojamilch – proteinreich, ideal zum Kochen und Backen


Mandelmilch – leicht nussig, besonders lecker in Smoothies


Reismilch – süßlich und gut verträglich …

author: PETA-Team
title: Neue Aufdeckung: Kamele in Marokko für Tourismus missbraucht
content:
Recherchen von PETA Asien dokumentieren immer wieder wie

Kamele

 in der marokkanischen

Tourismusindustrie

 ausgebeutet werden. Die Tiere, die für Ausritte ausgenutzt werden, werden geschlagen und ohne Schutz vor der Witterung angebunden. Sobald sie keinen Profit mehr einbringen, werden sie im Schlachthaus getötet. Erfahren Sie hier, wie es den Kamelen in Marokko geht und was Sie dagegen tun können. 


PETA Asien deckt erneut auf: Missbrauch von Kamelen in Marokko  


PETA Asien hat 2026 erneut die Misshandlung von Kamelen am Rande der Sahara in Marokko aufgedeckt, wo die Betreiber:innen sie zwingen, Tourist:innen durch die trockenen Wüstendünen zu tragen:  


Die Tiere sind außerhalb ihrer Einsätze häufig angekettet und schutzlos extremer Hitze, intensiver Sonneneinstrahlung und Sandstürmen ausgesetzt. 


Viele Kamele verbringen einen Großteil ihres Lebens isoliert und haben kaum die Möglichkeit, sich frei zu bewegen oder Sozialkontakte zu pflegen.  


Die Kamele werden meist nur dann von ihren Ketten befreit, wenn sie kurz Wasser trinken dürfen oder um weitere Tourist:innen durch die Wüste zu tragen. Ein Kamel wurde dabei beobachtet, wie es nicht nur zum Trinken, sondern auch zu einem Pfosten rannte, um sich dort zu kratzen. Es wurde jedoch zurück zu seinem Anbindeplatz gejagt.  


Tierhalter:innen schlugen Kamele wiederholt mit Peitschen, traten sie und zerrten gewaltsam an ihren Schwänzen. 


Kamele sind intelligente, soziale Wesen mit eigenen Bedürfnissen, Wünschen und Interessen. Wenn sie frei in ihrem natürlichen Lebensraum umherstreifen, leben sie in Herden und kommunizieren miteinander durch Laute und Körperbewegungen. Als Zeichen der Freundschaft blasen sich Kamele manchmal gegenseitig ins Gesicht. In der Tourismusindustrie müssen diese Tiere ein Leben lang Elend und Leid ertragen.


 PETA Asien Recherche aus dem Jahr 2025


Bereits 2025

veröffentlichte

PETA Asien

 Videomaterial, dass die Ausbeutung und Misshandlung von Kamelen in Marokko dokumentiert.

Das beunruhigende Video zeigt Kamele, die an nur wenigen Meter langen Seilen angebunden sind. Ein Betreiber wurde dabei gefilmt, wie er ein gefesseltes Kamel wiederholt mit einem langen Stock schlug, während das Tier versuchte, den Schlägen auszuweichen. Ein weiterer Betreiber erklärte den

Ermittler:innen

, dass Kamele, die bis zu 40 Jahre alt werden können, in der Regel etwa fünf Jahre lang ausgebeutet werden, bevor sie getötet oder als

Fleisch

 verkauft werden.


Globales Muster der Grausamkeit


Frühere PETA-Untersuchungen von Kamel- und Pferdebetrieben in Ägypten offenbarten ähnliche Misshandlungen: Tiere wurden blutig geschlagen, gezwungen, Menschen in brütender Hitze ohne Zugang zu Schatten oder Wasser zu tragen, und wie Müll entsorgt oder ins

Schlachthaus

 geschickt, wenn sie zu alt, krank oder verletzt waren, um noch „nützlich“ zu sein. Airbnb, booking.com, Klook, Marriott und viele andere Unternehmen erklärten sich bereit, die Werbung für Tierfahrten bei den Pyramiden von Gizeh einzustellen, nachdem sie von PETA über das Leid der Tiere informiert worden waren.


So können Sie Tieren in der Tourismusindustrie helfen


Tourist:innen, die für Kamelritte bezahlen, halten diese herzlose, unmenschliche Industrie am Laufen. Wenn Sie einen Urlaub planen, vermeiden Sie Angebote mit Tieren und entscheiden Sie sich für tierfreundliche Alternativen. Unterstützen Sie unsere Petition, um das Leid der Kamele und Pferde bei den ägyptischen Pyramiden zu stoppen.  


		Jetzt unterschreiben!


The post

Neue Aufdeckung: Kamele in Marokko für Tourismus missbraucht

 appeared first on

PETA Deutschland e.V.

.

author: hsa_oryx
title: OCTOBER ROUND UP
content:
First conviction under Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023


October kicked off with

Glasgow Hunt Sabs

 reporting that Claire Bellamy, ex-huntswoman and former Master of the Lauderdale Hunt, was found guilty under the Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023. Footage which was obtained by sabs shows hounds chasing a fox outside the area covered by a licence that had been granted by NatureScot, and was described by the judge as “

gut wrenching

.” This is the first ever conviction under the new Scottish legislation and you can learn more about the legislation in Scotland and what led to Claire’s conviction

here.


Claire Bellamy found guilty of deliberately hunting a fox with dogs in January 2025.

Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs


Drone theft


On the 3

rd

 of October Dorset Borders Sabs reported that their drone had been stolen by The Cattistock Hunt as they hunted in Corscombe, Dorchester. The last image visible on the drone was a known member of the hunt running towards it in a field. The incident has been reported to the police and thanks to the generosity of supporters

Dorset Borders Sabs

 raised enough funds to replace the drone.


What do you do when you receive a CPW? If you’re a fox hunt then you break it as soon as possible of course


It didn’t take the Four Burrow Hunt long to break their Community Protection Warning (CPW) which had just been freshly issued by Devon and Cornwall Police. On the 10

th

 of October the hunt was caught breaking condition 7 of the CPW, by failing to give police 24 hours’ notice of their meet. As they had failed to give the details of the meet this means they won’t have provided a map of their “trail” meaning they will have broken more conditions that just number 7. It remains to be seen what action the police will take.

Read our recent article about CPW’s.


Four Burrow Hunt were issued with a CPW after years of trespass and livestock worrying.

Image:


Kernow Sabs, Monitors and Animal Rights Team-Cornwall


Stag hunting horror continues


The horror of stag hunting has continued to escalate in the south west. On the 12

th

 of October the Quantock Staghounds hunted a stag towards the A39 between Nether Stowey and Holford. This is a stretch of road where the hunt are continually causing chaos and putting people’s lives in danger.


This particular incident resulted in a

hunted stag running across the road and colliding with a car.

 A witness described how the terrified stag “

was flipped over the top of the car. Its leg kicked out smashing the rear nearside window. The Stag landed heavily on the verge.”

 Luckily the woman driving and her small child were not hurt but were badly shaken up.


The cruelty doesn’t end there. Two weeks later

North Dorset Hunt Sabs

 reported that the Quantock Staghounds had once again inflicted sickening suffering and pain on a stag. This particular large stag had a visibly infected wound on his side and it is also suspected he had a broken leg. These injuries unfortunately indicate that it is likely the stag that was hit by the car. Despite these injuries the hunt continued to torture him, subjecting him to a chase through thick gorse which no doubt would have caused him unbearable pain.


A stag hunted and terrorised by the Quantock Staghounds.

Credit: North Dorset Hunt Sabs


On the 22

nd

 of October hunt master of the Quantock Staghounds, Christopher Gibbons and huntsman Martin Watts, appeared at Taunton Magistrates Court. Gibbons is facing two counts of hunting a wild mammal under the Hunting Act, and Watts is facing one relating to the barbaric five-hour chase and ultimate

killing of a stag on the 23

rd

 of April 2026

. Both have pleaded not guilty and the case has been adjourned until the 18

th

 of January 2027 for a case management hearing; no trial date has been set. In the meantime, the Quantock Staghounds are continuing to commit abhorrent levels of animal cruelty whilst putting the safety of the general public at great risk.


This stag was tortured for five hours and ultimately killed on the 23

rd

 of April by the Quantock Staghounds.

 Huntsman and hunt master have both pleaded not guilty to charges under the Hunting Act.

Credit:


Mendip Hunt Sabs


They’re blatantly hunting foxes


Amidst the CPW’s, convictions, court hearings, road chaos and trespassing, foxes are still being chased, like the one pictured below.


Beds and Bucks Hunt Sabs

 along with

Peterborough Hunt Sabs

 have been keeping the pressure on …

author: L214
title: Enquête abattoir Cooperl
content:
L214 publie une enquête sur l’étourdissement des cochons au CO₂ dans l’un des plus gros abattoirs de France : l’abattoir Cooperl de Montfort-sur-Meu, en Ille-et-Vilaine (Bretagne).

Les images, commentées par l'écrivaine Marie Darrieussecq, montrent la cruauté de cette méthode d'étourdissement dont les instances scientifiques ont établi qu’elle est source de peur, de détresse et de souffrance.

Plus de trente vétérinaires signent un appel publié ce jour pour demander l’interdiction du gazage au CO₂ des cochons. L214 se joint à cette demande et entame un recours contre l’État pour faire interdire cette pratique. L’enseigne de supermarchés Carrefour fait fabriquer par son partenaire Cooperl ses produits à base de viande de porc sous ses marques distributeurs, notamment sa marque Filière Qualité Carrefour. L’association demande à Carrefour de refuser le gazage des cochons et de signer le Plant Protein Pact.

Le musicien Moby apporte son soutien et appelle à signer la pétition.

Chaque heure d’abattage, plus de 800 cochons sont gazés au CO₂ à l’abattoir Cooperl de Montfort-sur-Meu, en Bretagne. Plongés dans une fosse à haute concentration en CO₂, les cochons ont la sensation de se noyer : ils hurlent, paniquent, cherchent désespérément à fuir. Il leur faut entre 21 et 60 secondes pour perdre conscience…

Ce n’est ni instantané, ni sans souffrance. Les instances scientifiques européenne (EFSA) et britannique (AWC) l’affirment depuis 20 ans : cette méthode provoque douleur, peur et détresse respiratoire. Le Royaume-Uni envisage même d’y renoncer, et plus de trente vétérinaires demandent son interdiction.

Pourtant, l’abattoir Cooperl de Montfort-sur-Meu a investi en 2024 environ 5 millions d'euros dans cet équipement qui permet d’abattre un nombre gigantesque d’animaux, de conquérir de nouveaux marchés, d’augmenter les cadences et la productivité. L’enseigne Carrefour fait fabriquer par son partenaire Cooperl des produits à base de cochons gazés sous ses marques, dont la Filière Qualité Carrefour, tout en se disant « pionnier sur le bien-être animal »…

À l’État français : interdire le gazage au CO₂ des cochons ;

À Carrefour : ne plus s’approvisionner en produits issus de cochons gazés et participer à un changement collectif en s'engageant dans le Plant Protein Pact, pour prendre part à une réduction de moitié du nombre d’animaux tués d’ici 2030.

Plus nous serons nombreux et nombreuses, plus il sera difficile pour les responsables de fermer les yeux. Signez et partagez : les cochons ne peuvent pas parler pour eux-mêmes, mais nous, oui.

Contre la souffrance des animaux, agissez à nos côtés avec un don.

author: David Greene
title: EFF Submission to OHCHR Consultation on Child Rights and Safety in the Digital Environment
content:
“

The safety of young people in the digital environment cannot be assessed without also considering the safety of young people in offline environments. For millions of young people around the world, the digital environment is their safe place, their haven from an unsafe physical environment, community, or family situation. The digital environment may be the best, perhaps only, place for them to find critical safety information and community, to explore ideas that are controversial in their families and larger physical environments, and to otherwise nourish their personal autonomy.


“For these young people, regulatory efforts that limit their access to online services or to certain features they find valuable, make their lives, in total, less safe, even if there has been some marginal safety benefit to their digital environment.


“The OHCHR must thus consider the whole of young persons' lives in any recommendations that come out of this process and not treat ‘safety, physical or mental health, and rights in the digital environment’ as disconnected from safety, physical or mental health, and rights elsewhere.”


So begins

EFF’s submission

 to the global Call for Inputs on

Child Rights and Safety in the Digital Environment

 conducted by the United Nations Office of the High Commissioner on Human Rights. The OHCHR is preparing a report on the issue to be presented to the UN Human Rights Council at its 64th session in the first quarter of 2027. The Human Rights Council requested the OHCHR to solicit input from a wide range of stakeholders, including child and youth perspectives, and convene five regional consultations to assess the risks to the safety of the child in the digital environment and best practices to address these risks in different geographical areas, bearing in mind current and emerging business models. 


The OHCHR acknowledges that young people today navigate a digital environment with both “unprecedented opportunities” and “serious and evolving risks,” and sets out a rights-based framing whereby “Children's 'safety' is therefore addressed through the full framework of their rights — with freedom from violence (Art. 19) and protection from exploitation and abuse (Arts. 34–36) as clearly defined obligations, situated alongside privacy (Art. 16), access to information (Arts. 13 and 17), expression (Art. 13), participation (Art. 12), and development (Art. 6). Protection and the full range of children's rights are understood as reinforcing rather than competing imperatives, and measures taken in the name of safety must not be used to restrict the enjoyment of other rights, such as the right to privacy and the right to participate.”


In light of this, EFF’s

submission

 focused on the current general disregard for young people's speech and privacy rights by regulators around the world, all of whom seem far more interested in empowering parents rather than young people themselves, or meaningfully involving young people in the regulatory process. 

We emphasized the human rights-centered uses young people make of social media that were not specifically set out in the concept note. 

We also explained that too often, policy proposals aiming to remedy the issues of online safety for young people introduce limitations on access to online services and content rather than tackling the specific problems that people experience. 


More specifically, our submission looks at:


the most significant risks to young people’s safety in the digital environment


how digital product design and business models drive risks to children's rights online, including in AI-mediated services


the inclusion of young people’s views in the design, governance, and regulation of digital environments 


how equality and non-discrimination in access and protection can be ensured


the promotion of digital literacy, skills, and empowerment for young people 


the impact of legislative and regulatory measures from the United States to Indonesia and Australia 


importance of broader, more systemic interventions that can address address online harms


how global instruments and processes can protect young people online. 


The internet is where young people learn, find community, explore their identities, access important information, and express themselves. Curtailing these opportunities doesn't make them safer. And requiring everyone to hand over sensitive personal information just to access online spaces creates privacy risks for …

author: By L. Cam Anderson, Contributor
title: Hennepin County Surveilled Anti-HERC Activists Since 2023
content:
Minneapolis, MN — A report released by the Zero Burn Coalition documents years of surveillance conducted against activists pushing for clean air in Minneapolis. The revelations came from documents that the organization obtained through public information requests.


At the center of this is the Hennepin Energy Recovery Center (HERC), a nearly 40-year-old trash incinerator neighboring Target Field in Minneapolis permitted to burn 365,000 tons of garbage annually. Activists, including those with the Zero Burn Coalition, have advocated for its closure for years, citing the amount of pollution it produces and the disproportionate effect on marginalized communities.


A short walk to the west of the facility is historically Black and working-class neighborhoods of North Minneapolis, which bear the brunt of the plant’s pollution. 


Coinciding with the release of the report on Oct. 22, community members and Minnesota Environmental Justice Table (MNEJT) activists and leaders convened along Olson Memorial Highway in the Heritage Park neighborhood for a press conference, in full view of HERC’s foreboding smoke stacks on the other side of Interstate 94.


“Instead of addressing the concerns raised by residents, the county has devoted staff time and resources to tracking the people organizing for change,” MNEJT Associate Director Adina Black said. “This raises serious questions about accountability, transparency, and the county’s treatment of the communities it has a responsibility to serve.”


The

eight-page report

 details seven separate instances of the county surveilling activists and the role former environmental justice leader Joe Vital played in that. 


Hennepin-Co-Surveillance-Report-Zero-Burn-Coalition


Vital was a part of

the East Phillips Neighborhood Institute’s successful push

 to acquire the former Roof Depot site from the city of Minneapolis in 2023. Since then, he has become Hennepin County’s Environmental Engagement Coordinator and would attend activist meetings to feed his notes to other Hennepin County employees, such as the county’s Department of Environment and Energy Assistant Director David McNary.


The report alleges that Vital also attempted to learn the identity of a county whistleblower through conversation with Minnesota Environmental Justice Table’s co-founder Nazir Khan.


In emails acquired by the Zero Burn Coalition, McNary would forward alerts from the activists to Tim Steinbeck, the president of Great River Energy, the company operating HERC. McNary and Steinbeck both served simultaneously as the treasurer-secretary of Minnesota Resource Recovery Association, a group formed by leaders of the incinerator industry.


000124-000140


In March 2024, an amortization bill was introduced in the state legislature that would allow cities to phase out sources of pollution in vulnerable neighborhoods without requiring them to do so. The House committee considering the bill narrowed it to only the state’s largest cities.


Under Minnesota law at the time, amortization could only be used against adult-only stores and criminal nuisances.


While advocates rallied around the bill, McNary forwarded the private emails of activists to Steinbeck and other industry representatives, urging them to oppose it.


“They start with the big cities and before long it will be the entire state,” McNary wrote in the email thread while pushing the idea that the amortization process would come to affect other industries.


Read

all of the documents published to the public by the Zero Burn Coalition

.


HERC, which began operation in 1989, is a “waste-to-energy” facility, meaning it produces energy for the power grid by incinerating garbage. Since its construction, the population within five kilometers of the plant has grown to nearly 250,000.


Despite politicians and others

framing “waste-to-energy” as environmentally friendly

,

a peer-reviewed study published in 2023

 found that “incinerators emit more greenhouse gas emissions per unit of electricity produced … than any other power source.” The study also added that the inclusion of incinerators in “‘renewable’ or ‘clean’ energy standards is thus counterproductive, as they also divert more than $40 million in subsidies annually from cleaner energy sources.”


HERC, which has been operated by Great River Energy since 2018, annually produces roughly 350,000 million tons of carbon dioxide and 72,000 million tons of incinerator ashes, according to a report …

author: Maríangeles Guerrero
title: Las Tres Ecologías y la disputa por el espacio público en Rosario
content:
Por Laura Hintze


En la oferta gastronómica-cultural y del paisaje ribereño —por ahora accesible para todas y todos— en la costa de Rosario falta el Almacén de Las Tres Ecologías. Es un emprendimiento autogestivo donde, por más de una década, cooperativas, productores y organizaciones de la economía social de todo el país vendieron sus productos en un espacio público cedido a tal fin, en una zona codiciada por el negocio inmobiliario.

 Desde este año, por decisión unilateral de la Municipalidad, está cerrado.

 “El neoliberalismo es la práctica económica que, diciendo que está en contra del Estado, hace los mejores negocios con el Estado. Se apropia de sus recursos de infraestructura, de los recursos naturales o financieros para hacer negocios. Esto es lo que sucede. Es un proceso de profundización de la privatización”, reflexiona Roberto García, integrante de Las Tres Ecologías.


Durante años, quienes llegaban los fines de semana hasta el paseo ribereño podían encontrarse con un galpón de 25 metros por 10 donde había comidas, bebidas, artesanías, plantas, libros y textiles elaborados por cooperativas y organizaciones de distintas provincias

. Pero el Almacén no era solamente un lugar de venta. Aprovechaba su ubicación y el alcance a nuevos oídos y preguntas para abrir conversaciones a través de radios abiertas, presentaciones de libros, música en vivo, ferias y encuentros nacionales.

 Ese borde de la ciudad, a orillas del Paraná, se convertía en un lugar para producir, intercambiar y encontrarse.


El Almacén de las Tres Ecologías está cerrado desde enero. La Municipalidad de Rosario desocupó el galpón que había cedido once años antes a las organizaciones que lo gestionaban. Primero intentó hacerlo por la fuerza; después formalizó el cese del contrato por decreto. Desde entonces, quienes sostuvieron el proyecto se reorganizan fuera de ese espacio y buscan otro lugar en la ribera.

Detrás de esta disputa vuelve la pregunta que los rosarinos se hacen una y otra vez: ¿qué proyecto de ciudad se está construyendo frente al Paraná?


Foto: Las Tres Ecologías


El lujo es la organización comunitaria


El Almacén de las Tres Ecologías abrió sus puertas el 11 de febrero de 2015. “Ese día había muchísima alegría”, recuerda García. Habían trabajado todo ese verano para dejar el lugar a punto. El mobiliario, hecho con maderas recicladas, fue una de las marcas del espacio durante la década que funcionó: le daba un tono artesanal y luminoso que lo diferenciaba de lo que había alrededor. La inauguración reunió a amigos, organizaciones hermanas, ecologistas y autoridades municipales. “Fue el comienzo de una iniciativa única en todo el país”, resalta.


La apertura del comercio fue fruto de un acuerdo entre la Municipalidad de Rosario y tres redes de la economía social, solidaria y popular: la Red de Comercio Justo del Litoral, el Centro Ecuménico Poriajhú y la Cooperativa de Trabajo Encuentro Nacional. El Estado cedió a las organizaciones un espacio público sin cobrarles alquiler ni canon por su uso.


El galpón que recibió a las organizaciones cooperativas había pertenecido a empresas públicas vinculadas al puerto y al ferrocarril. Quedó abandonado después de las privatizaciones de los años 90. Según García,

mientras buena parte de esos espacios terminó destinada a proyectos inmobiliarios de lujo, otros quedaron en manos del Estado, municipal o provincial

. Ese fue el caso del galpón donde funcionó el Almacén, que quedó bajo la órbita de la secretaría de Economía Solidaria de la Municipalidad.


“La evaluación que hicimos hace 13 años fue que toda la costa se estaba privatizando y que solamente un galpón de 50 metros por 10 había quedado en manos de la Secretaría de Economía Solidaria. Entonces eso debía ser dedicado a prácticas relacionadas con la economía social y solidaria, una economía absolutamente emergente y débil frente a la economía de capital y del mercado. Nos pareció importante armar una propuesta en la que el municipio no hiciera algo estándar y llamara a licitación, que era lo que iba a hacer”, cuenta.


“Por eso no alcanza con decir que Las Tres Ecologías fue un proyecto cooperativo. Hubo una propuesta política muy fuerte: que estas organizaciones de la economía social, solidaria y popular pudieran gestionar un espacio del Estado de manera mancomunada, sin que el Estado aportara dinero ni les cobrara, sino que simplemente cediera el espacio.

Fue una experiencia de democracia participativa en el sentido más …

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Women on the frontlines defending land, life, and livelihood
content:
Across the Philippines, one of the world’s most disaster-prone countries, women are at the forefront of struggles to defend their communities against displacement, environmental destruction, and development aggression. From the mountains of Luzon to the coastal communities of the Visayas and Mindanao, they are fighting to protect the land and resources that make life possible.

In Kasibu, Nueva Vizcaya, about 300 women are actively involved in a long-running struggle against large-scale mining. They help maintain six community barricades that have blocked mining operations since 2007. Among the companies seeking to operate in the area is North Luzon Mineral Resources Corporation (NLMRC), whose government-issued exploration permit covers 4,456 hectares of land, threatening farms and watersheds that sustain thousands of residents. Click here to read their story.

Further south, the struggle takes a different form. In Tacloban, elderly women are protecting the coastal community they rebuilt after super typhoon Yolanda (international name: Haiyan) in 2013. The typhoon destroyed most of the area’s two-hectare mangrove forest, reducing it to just 2,000 square meters. Two months after Yolanda, they joined other residents in growing seedlings and restoring the mangroves of Cancabato Bay. Over the past decade, their efforts have helped the forest recover beyond its pre-Yolanda coverage, providing habitat for marine life and a natural buffer against storm surges.

Now, that recovery faces another threat. The multi-billion-peso Tacloban Causeway Project is a 2.55-kilometer road embankment and reclamation project intended to connect the airport to downtown Tacloban. Residents and environmental advocates have raised concerns about its effects on Cancabato Bay, particularly on water circulation, marine life, and livelihood. Click here to read the rest of the story.

Down south of the Philippines, in Balete Bay, Davao Oriental, women fisherfolk and farmers are confronting growing threats to the waters and land that sustain their livelihoods. Climate change, prolonged droughts, and rising sea temperatures are affecting fish catches and crops, making it harder for families to sustain their livelihoods. These challenges are compounded by the threat of large-scale mining in a province where around 80 percent of the land is covered by mining permit applications. Read the rest of the story here.

For the women of Kasibu, Tacloban, and Balete Bay, staying means knowing what is at stake when the land and resources their communities depend on are threatened. It affects how families earn a living and whether communities can continue to sustain themselves.

Women often bear much of this burden, even as they take an active role in resisting the forces that threaten their homes and livelihoods. They know what it takes to stay because they have lived through these struggles and continue to fight for the right to shape their own future. (AMU, RVO)

title: Karasu: The Republic must be democratised according to today's understanding of democracy
content:
Mustafa Karasu, a member of the KCK Executive Council, spoke about current affairs during a special programme broadcast on Medya Haber.


The first part of this interview can be read

here

.


The AKP government is entering into various alliances, particularly in the region. The benefits and drawbacks of these alliances continue to be debated publicly. Can the AKP secure its own position through such alliances?


After Devlet Bahçeli made his call, what did both Bahçeli and Erdoğan repeatedly say? They said that we needed to strengthen the domestic front. They also described this process as one of strengthening the domestic front. Yes, resolving the Kurdish question means strengthening the domestic front. This is because, from the Ottoman period onward, whenever Turkey has come into conflict with the Kurds, it has lost. Whenever it has maintained positive relations with the Kurds, it has achieved stability and strengthened its position.


Indeed, one of the most important factors in the decline of the Ottoman Empire was its failure to resolve its problems with the Kurds. From the nineteenth century onward, it entered into conflict with them. Once it became hostile to the Kurds, it began to decline rapidly. Had it resolved the Kurdish question and adopted the right approach, the Ottoman Empire might not have disintegrated to the same extent. Now, if the government claims to be pursuing a policy of strengthening the domestic front and repeatedly emphasises this objective, yet then assumes that it can secure its position through alliances formed abroad, I have to say that this is a misconception. No matter what alliances you form abroad, they will not achieve much if you do not first consolidate the domestic front. They may even produce the opposite results. In fact, the anxiety that has led to the formation of so many alliances stems precisely from the failure to strengthen the domestic front. This is preparation for war. The formation of so many alliances in the Middle East, which lies at the centre of ongoing wars, amounts to preparation for such wars—or to taking sides on the various war fronts.


If the domestic front were strong, if Turkey genuinely resolved the Kurdish question and took steps towards democratisation, it would not feel the need—or fall into the misconception—that it could save itself by forming one alliance with this party and another with that one. In this respect, let me be clear: the formation of so many alliances is also taking place under the direction of certain external powers. In his statement, Tom Barrack indirectly indicated that the alliances Turkey is forming are known to us, serve our interests and form part of our policy; they are not separate from it.


Thus, this alliance policy may be an attempt to secure Turkey's position, but it also creates antagonisms. Every alliance is, at the same time, directed against someone else. Of course, a state can form alliances and may need to do so. But because Turkey has failed to consolidate its domestic front, it feels weak. Consequently, it considers entering into various alliances necessary—or, more precisely, it feels compelled to create new enmities.


We do not believe that Turkey can resolve its own problems through alliance policies. The policy of strengthening the domestic front is correct, and this is what the government says it is pursuing. Yet instead of fulfilling the requirements of that policy and strengthening the domestic front, the government prefers to create its own fronts abroad and take sides in existing conflicts. This will not benefit Turkey very much. Turkey will suffer the consequences.


Abdullah Öcalan, the leader of the peoples, has described the process he initiated as one of change and transformation. In this context, efforts to organise a movement for a democratic republic are also on the agenda in the field of political struggle. What would you like to say about these discussions?


A republic was established in Turkey. Yes, a republic is a system of government in which those in power come to office through elections. Of course, a republic does not automatically mean direct democracy. There are many republics in the world that are undemocratic, even dictatorial. Conversely, there are countries without republics, where monarchies still exist, and certain offices are not filled through elections. Sweden, Norway and the Netherlands are examples, yet these countries do have certain democratic institutions, albeit …

author: Marianne Lavelle
title: Activists Hope Midterm Wins Set the Stage for Renewed Energy and Climate Policy
content:
Environmental advocates point out voters are angry at Big Oil, which is making record profits while families struggle.

Environmental advocates point out voters are angry at Big Oil, which is making record profits while families struggle.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Democrats on Tuesday won control of both houses of Congress and a decisive mandate to put a check on Donald Trump’s tumultuous presidency, a victory propelled by voter anger over high prices, corruption and the unchecked spread of data centers.

Some of the same concerns helped to lift Democrats to victories in statehouses, where they gained a majority of the country’s governorships for the first time in more than a decade.

Voters in Ohio, South Carolina and Texas — states Trump won by double digits two years ago — put Democrats over the top in the U.S. Senate. And the Democratic wave surmounted a seawall of money: the unprecedented spending the GOP’s tech industry allies poured into the races in recent weeks to protect the status quo and their freedom from regulation.

Activists believe the result sets the stage for renewed environmental and climate policy, even though candidates seldom mentioned those issues by name in their campaigns. They argue that any action Congress takes on voters’ top issues — soaring energy prices, undue industry influence and the surge of artificial intelligence infrastructure — will curb the upward trajectory of U.S. fossil fuel consumption that Trump has encouraged.

“Voters rejected the Trump administration’s failing energy policies, which have pushed electricity bills higher,” said David Kieve, president of EDF Action, the political arm of the nonprofit Environmental Defense Fund, which invested $18 million in the midterms. “Families know that blocking clean energy raises rates. Paying companies to abandon wind projects, canceling grants meant to lower rural utility bills, and using emergency orders to keep coal plants running when cleaner, cheaper options are available all moved us in the wrong direction.”

A president’s party typically loses seats in Congress in midterm elections, and in the face of that history, Trump urged voters to “pretend I’m on the ballot.” The results indicated that voters listened. Trump’s sagging approval became a millstone Republicans were forced to carry, as opponents attacked them for their complicity in an unpopular war that had caused U.S. energy prices to soar. (The decision to unilaterally join Israel in airstrikes against Iran on Feb. 28 resulted in “incalculable political damage for Trump’s party,” political pundit Charlie Cook wrote on the eve of the election.)

In unfortunate timing for Republicans, the U.S. oil industry last week reported its profits — $130 billion over the past six months, or triple the earnings of one year ago, all due to the war-related run-up in prices. On the campaign trail, Trump tried to frame the oil industry’s boon as a blessing for Americans.

“They’re making hundreds of billions of dollars — our country is — on oil,” Trump said at an Oct. 26 rally in Georgia. Trump said his advisers warned him not to mention that “because people are paying a little bit higher,” but he said he didn’t care how his words would be portrayed. “I don’t give a damn,” he said. “We’re making a freaking fortune!”

But Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-Ga.) seemed to better capture the mood of his state’s voters in his last days of campaigning for reelection: “Under failed president Donald J. Trump, it costs more than ever in American history to fill up your truck, stock your fridge, visit the doctor or power your home.” Ossoff coasted to re-election as expected, and former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms defeated Republican Rick Jackson to win the Georgia governor’s race.

Opposition to data centers helped Democrats in many races, such as in Ohio, where Democrat Sherrod Brown staged a political comeback and defeated Republican Sen. Jon Husted. Brown dubbed his opponent “the face of data centers,” and sought to tie Husted to tax breaks and other policies that have attracted the giant computing centers to Ohio.

Trump’s foes — including environmental groups — blanketed the airwaves in swing states and districts with ads tying the pain of high gasoline and electricity prices to cozy Republican relationships with oil and utility companies, tech giants and the insurance industry …

author: Fikayo Akeredolu
title: Nigeria's petrol subsidy was also an electricity policy
content:
As long as households and businesses in Nigeria depend on generators and cannot rely on the grid for electricity, some form of fossil fuel subsidy will always be necessary. Despite the costs, and despite what the World Bank, the International Monetary Fund (IMF), and the climate research community say. This is because fossil fuel subsidies, in my opinion, are the country’s largest and most decentralized electricity access program, and any attempt at reform without explicitly accounting for this will fail. This essay explains why.

As a starting point, I need everyone to read Dr. Neil McCulloch’s book

Ending Fossil Fuel Subsidies

. The book explains how subsidies are effectively a political prosthetic. Imagine you run a developing country with weak administrative capacity. You cannot reliably deliver schools or clinics, but you need to give citizens something that shows you are on their side and ensures you stay in power. Cheap energy through fossil fuel subsidies is the one thing you can deliver somewhat easily. Weak states, like Nigeria, lean on subsidies because a subsidy is a substitute for the public goods the state cannot otherwise provide.

Citing a Nigerian study, he shows that the subsidy mostly benefits the rich — the bottom 40 percent of households consumed only 3 percent of petrol, while the richest fifth captured around 27 times more benefit than the poorest fifth. By 2018, Nigeria was spending roughly $300 million a month on the petrol subsidy, more than its entire budget for basic education. Considering all of this, anyone can see that the subsidy is a bad political and economic deal.

Beyond the numbers, there is the climate change literature. McCulloch notes that fossil fuel subsidies are sometimes a key blockage to the wider development of renewable energy. Cheap petrol and diesel weaken the incentive to switch to cleaner alternatives. The reformist logic follows rationally — remove the subsidy, allow prices to reflect the true cost of fuel, and households and businesses should begin moving toward cleaner energy. And this logic from the literature is intuitive. But it makes assumptions that anyone who truly understands Nigeria will tell you just do not apply.

It assumes grid electricity already exists and the question is simply how it should be generated. But for many Nigerians, electricity means a petrol generator. Remove the subsidy and the choice is not necessarily dirty electricity versus clean electricity; it is instead between some electricity versus none.

The reformist logic also assumes a certain level of demand elasticity. The assumption here is that people can meaningfully reduce their demand when prices rise. But if petrol is running the generator that powers your home or business, there is only so much consumption you can cut before you have a bigger problem. It also assumes a substitute is readily available. A higher petrol price only pushes someone toward solar and electric vehicles if solar and electric vehicles are actually affordable, available, and accessible. It assumes subsidy removal mainly hurts a powerful fossil fuel industry. In Nigeria, it also hurts households and small businesses that rely on petrol generators because the grid does not work. And probably most importantly, it assumes a state government capable of capturing the savings from subsidy removal and redirecting them transparently, efficiently, and effectively into the transition.

If the assumptions do not hold, how exactly is the price signal of subsidy removal supposed to work? Post subsidy removal, what was the immediate short-term plan for providing electricity? If you make petrol for running generators more expensive, yes, the price signal should move people to cleaner sources, but are the cleaner sources within a price range that allows everyone to make the switch?

As someone who has lived in Nigeria, sat through more blackouts than I care to number and then gone on to do a PhD on this topic, I think that there was a key part of this debate that analysts, international financial institutions, and policymakers did not seem to fully reckon with. And it is this — on a not insignificant note, Nigeria’s subsidy was about generating electricity just about as much as it was a fiscal matter. Effectively, Nigeria’s petrol subsidy was a key part of its electricity policy.

And recommending and enacting its removal without explicitly accounting for this made the average Nigerian’s life worse. I say the average …

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: NTI has a plan to adapt to climate change but needs money to implement it
content:
Nunavut Tunngavik Inc. has set a new vision for responding to climate change in the territory.


The plan – Anijaarniq Strategy: An Inuit Approach to Addressing Climate Change in Nunavut – identifies 15 goals based on engagement sessions with Nunavummiut. 


Nunavut’s three Inuit associations, the Kitikmeot Inuit Association, Kivalliq Inuit Association, and Qikiqtani Inuit Association hosted the workshops over 2024 and 2025. 


“This is one of the most intensive processes I believe that we’ve gone through in terms of the development of a strategy,”

 said NTI research director Cheryl Wray, who oversaw the development of the

Anijaarniq Strategy

.


The plan calls on the territorial and federal governments to commit money to achieve the goals identified in it, which include building more climate-resilient housing; transitioning to renewable energy systems; and creating Inuit-led climate research and adaptation programs. 


“We require funding for this plan to be actionable,” Wray said.

“This is a plan which requires all partners to come to the table.”


She said NTI has yet to decide how much to ask for from each government.


Those consulted as part of the plan said their top concerns are rapid changes in sea ice, harms to wildlife, unsafe travel, permafrost thaw and extreme weather events.


“One of the key issues that we’re facing up here is the delay in the sea ice freezing, especially for the migrating animals like caribou,” said Derek Elias, a business development officer with the Kitikmeot Inuit Association who organized the engagement session in Cambridge Bay. “We’ve had animals drown when trying to cross.”


He said the sea ice between Victoria Island and the mainland forms later each fall and isn’t as thick as it used to be. 


“We’re just hoping that the territorial government is going to take climate change seriously and [provide] the appropriate funding, tools and resources for us to be able to tackle climate change and its effects,” Elias said. “It’s for our future generations.”


GN Environment Department spokesperson Estęla Aguilar declined to answer questions about how the department intends to work with NTI.


In a statement to Nunatsiaq News, Carolane Gratton, spokesperson for Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada,

said the department recognizes the importance of “predictable, long-term climate funding.”

She noted that it helped fund the development of the action plan.


She also said that since 2016, the department has provided NTI with over $8 million to support climate adaptation initiatives and policy development.


Over the same time frame, she said, the department also committed $90 million into infrastructure vulnerability assessments, clean energy and emergency preparedness in Nunavut.

author: Kavita Naidu
title: Kavita Naidu: You cannot destroy the Global South for the Global North’s renewable transition
content:
Kavita Naidu is an international human rights lawyer and feminist climate activist from Fiji. She delivered this speech at the No Cop-Outs at COP31: Climate Action Now rally at Sydney Town Hall on Gadigal Country, on October 24.

For the Pacific, going above 1.5 degrees is a death sentence we will not be quiet about.

The 1.5 degree threshold is not only anchored in the International Court of Justice (ICJ), it was also what the Pacific pushed for in the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea and the Inter-American Court of Human Rights.

For the first time we have a very powerful legal floor, and you can see in Australia there are legal cases which will establish what these advisory opinions mean in practice.

Pacific rejects false climate solutions

Pacific community service organisations met in Tuvalu ahead of Pre-COP in Fiji to issue the Funafuti Call for Climate Justice, which speaks for Pacific peoples. The rallying cry was “Lose Tuvalu, Lose our World”.

The Pacific is calling for an immediate phase out of coal, oil and gas and an end to new exploration, licensing, expansion and subsidies, with developed states phasing out first and fastest.

We are rejecting all false solutions, including carbon capture and storage, nuclear energy, offsetting, geoengineering and “managed transition pathways” as substitutes for cutting production.

We reject deep-sea mining, we reject a “just transition” based on green and blue colonialism, opening frontiers of dispossession of land and oceans to sate the need for developed states to transition.

A transition for who? And a transition for what? We are not questioning the consumption of energy as a problem, we are simply looking at the source of energy and we need to beyond this.

You cannot destroy and extract from the Global South to suit the transition needs of the Global North, that is not just and equitable.

We do not understand, because so much of it is greenwashed, but the rush for critical rare earth minerals is not just for solar panels, it is tied to the militarisation of this region. It is tied to missiles and drones.

You just need to see the billions the Australian government is putting into militarisation, because they want to go for our land and oceans and they need a military to protect those resources.

The Funafati Call rejects a securitised, militarised and nuclearised Pacific. It names AUKUS, the Papua New Guinea–Australia Mutual Defence Treaty (Pukpuk Treaty) and the Vuvale Union as attempts to seize control of our economic resources and make us beholden to what the Australian government demands of us.

We condemn all missile testing in our waters and we condemn any future weapons testing in our waters.

We assert our right to remain on our islands with dignity. We reject mobility deals traded against the sovereignty and security of our people.

The Pacific is a region that is still occupied. Struggles for self-determination continue in West Papua, Guam, Kanaky and Tahiti.

We cannot talk about climate justice without recognising self-determination of the indigenous people who continue to be on the frontlines of the worst climate impacts in this region.

This is why we must call out our Pacific leaders for endorsing Zionism by supporting Israel at the United Nations, opening Israeli embassies in the region and signing “development cooperation” deals.

We reject endorsing a genocidal state and commit to tackling the scourge of Zionist fundamentalism on our islands.

The other thing about the Pacific that people don’t understand is that we have among the highest rates of violence against women in the world. We recognise that we must incorporate gender justice into our climate justice campaigns.

That includes recognising and redistributing unpaid care, social protection guarantees and attention to gender-based violence and sexual and reproductive health rights.

The Pacific has also been very progressive in recognising how artificial intelligence and data centres are coming for us. We already have data centres being built, subsea cables and other digital infrastructure in the region, but their energy, water and emissions footprints are not being disclosed.

The Pacific asserts data sovereignty and the protection of indigenous knowledge from AI. We also question the duality of purpose of AI and its use for military surveillance and intelligence.

We will not be complicit in killing people in other parts of the world by providing the infrastructure in …

author: Mong Palatino
title: The thrill of group bike rides
content:
Bikers have been bonded by the daily commute or the frequent group rides, and this ritual of biking together can be turned into an advocacy action. This should not be a surprise since the tribe of bikers who regularly ride together suffers from the same grave inefficiencies that plague our roads and communities.


Biking brings calm and exhilaration at the same time, and these feelings are amplified during a group ride.


Planning a group ride takes time and patience, and it is deservedly celebrated when it happens.


It is usually done for leisure, a chill time with fellow bikers. It can be a training session for a scheduled race. Or it can become the power of many if organized to promote a cause.


Whatever the intent that pedals the ride, it is necessary to have trust, coordination, and the unity to move forward in one direction.


Safety measures are learned, relearned, enforced, and adopted during the ride. Newbies take cues from fellow riders, hand signals are introduced, and road rules that apply to cyclists are highlighted in real time. The grounding experience allows bikers to map out routes, rediscover a place from a new perspective, and become familiar with the local scenery. If field trips immerse travelers in history and the tourism value of a town or institution, a group bike tour provides the same allure and they cover even the remote corners that cars and buses cannot reach. A bike tour always offers new ways of seeing and experiencing the peripheries in our communities.


The group ride is an educative activity for all – riders, motorists, commuters, and pedestrians. It makes the bikers more visible, and this is deliberate. A lone biker wishes to be seen for his or her safety, a group ride ensures it and compels the people on the road to acknowledge the space reserved for cyclists. And if a protected bike lane is missing, the bikers crowding the street effectively become the mobile barrier that serves as a reminder not just of the presence of two-wheeled vehicles but also the right of others (non-car drivers) to use the taxpayer-funded road infrastructure.


This is the principle guiding critical mass rides which have become a global movement. An intentional biking of the many to normalize the idea of biking, encourage people to go out and bike, and destigmatize the use of roads by bikers. It is through these collective efforts that a community of bikers is formed. Bikers sharing the joy of biking and pedaling together to remove the perils of the supposedly mundane human act of travelling on a non-motorized vehicle.


There is no single community of bikers, and the diversity of these networks highlights the power that can be harnessed to deliver a message to broader segments in society. Bikers have been bonded by the daily commute or the frequent group rides, and this ritual of biking together can be turned into an advocacy action. This should not be a surprise since the tribe of bikers who regularly ride together suffers from the same grave inefficiencies that plague our roads and communities. They all see, hear, and experience the same daily evils of bad governance that propel citizens to speak out and mobilize. 


Imagine a long line of bikers occupying a road, this scene repeated several times until it becomes normal. It is an attempt to rewire our perceptions of what a car-dominated street should look like. Then imagine this determined group of citizens on the move who by their mere presence reveal the glaring inadequacies in urban planning. They can be rallied to challenge car centrism and its morbid manifestations in policymaking, public works, traffic regulations, and toxic road mindset and habits.


The potential of tapping bikers to be active advocates of sociopolitical causes is confirmed by their actual participation in protest actions against controversial issues from the flood corruption scandal in 2025 to Pax Silica this year. Frequent bike rides have been organized to raise public awareness of pressing social concerns such as the critical conditions of rivers, coastal habitats, and watersheds. Both young and old bikers have shown enthusiastic participation in rides that explore historical landmarks and celebrate the opening of parks and green spaces.


Biking alone will not change the world, but it is a brave individual defiance of the norms in our motorized megapolis. Every pedal is a plea for consideration, recognition, and basic kindness. Biking together provides greater …

title: Ejército Zapatista de Liberación Nacional - Don’t Forsake Us!
content:
Author

: Ejército Zapatista de Liberación Nacional

Title

: Don’t Forsake Us!

Subtitle

: Zapatista Women in ’94

Date

: 1994

Notes

: Originally published by Ediciones OnA, València-Chiapas: 1

st

 edition May 2018, 2

nd

 edition January 2019, 3

rd

 edition July 2019, 4

th

 edition January 2020.

 English translation by Ediciones Bloodfruit/Malvivientes, 2026.

Source

: Retrieved 10/30/26 from https://www.patreon.com/bloodfruit/posts/dont-forsake-us-173797846


 The money raised from the this first volume are going to the benefit of Compañera M. Mother,

 Social Warrior, Multiply Employed, Indigenous.


 The best way to understand the path of the women who struggle is through their own words. These brief texts, interviews and declarations of the women of the Zapatista Army for National Liberation in the first months of the armed uprising of 1994 showcase the situation of indigenous women in Mexican territory, and are a mirror of the dignity that has kept the Zapatista struggle alive despite male chauvinism, racism and capitalism.


 This edition was part of a mutual aid initiative to redistribute the

funds of the circulating texts and “Independent” editions among

the struggles’ female protagonists


Words From Comandanta Ramona and Major Ana María


Another concern that indigenous

women have is the free choice of partners.


“The dowry custom still exists,

the girl is never taken into account,

she is sold off (in this region,

the average price of nuptial dowry is

two thousand pesos). The idea of

having a boyfriend doesn’t exist; it is sin.”


 Ana María, Infantry Major: “Don’t Forsake Us!” is the desperate plea of the women of the Zapatista Army for National Liberation so that their hopes of being heard within and without their communities may not die. “We ask all women to fight alongside us” is what Comandanta Ramona and Major Ana María say in Tzotzil and Spanish. Their call to Mexican women is not one to take up arms, but rather so that, within their spaces, they may support the changes proposed by the Revolutionary Law of Women, as well as their extensive list over equality, justice, health, education and housing. That night, the penultimate they would spend at the Cathedral, they arrived through the back of the altar, accompanied by Subcomandante Marcos.


 He, dressed in his unmistakable military uniform. Some steps behind, the only two women of a group of the 19 delegates of the Indigenous Clandestine Revolutionary Committee. “I’ll leave them with you so that you can speak to them about anything you wish,” he said in a joking tone as he bid his farewell to the group of five female reporters and two photographers intent on interviewing the women of the Zapatista Army. Ramona’s wide and sharp eyes revealed weariness. The black wool skirt, the beautifully embroidered loom-woven blouse, and her short stature contrasted with Ana María’s gray

ruana

 and sturdy frame. Alongside them, Comandante Javier remained behind (to translate Ramona’s Tzotzil’s words into Spanish). The words of the Comandanta, even if in Tzotzil, flow smoothly from her indigenous heart.


 I left my community in search of work because of necessity itself, there was no longer anything to live off of. When I arrived someplace else I began to learn that it wasn’t the same situation as that of women in the countryside. I learned there to understand and gain conscience of the differences, that’s how I learned of the organization (EZLN), and that it was also necessary to organize women.


 Within EZLN women’s participation in key. Ramona belongs to the political group that works in the communities; Ana María is part of the approximately 30% of female combatants/insurgents who voluntarily refuse to form a family in order to engage in armed struggle.


 “I am an insurgent. I’ve dedicated my entire life and time to the cause,” affirms Ana María, a 26 year old Infantry Major who, when speaking of displacement and suffering endured, furrows her brows in sadness, the only sign of expression able to be seen beneath her balaclava. “It’s a long story,” she says,


 Ever since I was eight years old I took part in peaceful struggles, in marches, in meetings. My family was one that fought, that always organized in order to have a dignified life, but that never achieved it through that route. We were in an organization —won’t say which— with other persons, with other peoples. We would go there, the children too, and that’s how we went began …

title: La UNSa y su trabajo con los Pueblos Originarios
content:
Recordando que el reciente 12 de octubre, el Día del respeto a la Diversidad Cultural, en todo el país hubo actividades llevadas a cabo por organizaciones y comunidades originarias.


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Pastrana-david.-Pueblos.mp3


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Pastrana-david.-Pueblos.mp3


Descargar archivo


Y uno de esos lugares fue la Provincia de Salta, en donde la Universidad Nacional de Salta reunió a referentes de pueblos originarios, autoridades, realizadores audiovisuales y miembros de la comunidad en una jornada de diálogo, memoria y reconocimiento de las realidades territoriales.


Esa actividad se llamó “Voces del Territorio: Memoria, Identidad y Continuidad” en donde se proyectó la Película “Senda India”, con la presencia de la directora Daniela Seggiaro.


Esto dio lugar a espacios de intercambio y debate sobre la situación territorial de los pueblos originarios y la agenda legislativa vinculada a sus derechos.


Cabe destacar que la película se hizo tomando como base las filmaciones realizadas por el joven wichí Miguel Ángel Lorenzo, quien filmó con una cámara de video Hi8, con humor, sensibilidad y junto a sus paisanos, recorridos por el monte, por casas vecinas, en actos escolares, pericias arqueológicas y visitas de un juez, como parte de las pruebas para un juicio que llevaba adelante su comunidad desde 1986.


Esta jornada fue organizada de manera conjunta por la Universidad Nacional de Salta, a través de la Coordinación de Pueblos Originarios de la UNSa, el Instituto Provincial de Pueblos Indígenas de Salta (IPPIS), el C.I.P.I., el MinPPi y EIB Salta.


Por eso, contamos ahora con el testimonio de David Pastrana, Coordinador de Pueblos Originarios de la UNSa, quien comenta con más detalles acerca de las reflexiones que tuvieron lugar en esa oportunidad. Agradecemos al programa Protagonistas de la Mañana de la Radio Universidad de Salta por este material.


El Micro Kay Pacha se realiza con el apoyo de la organización Otto per Mille-Chiessa Valdense


La entrada

author: Stelinsky
title: Μπέικον και δουλεία
content:
Το σημερινό άρθρο είναι επετειακό. Πριν από 350 χρόνια διαδραματίστηκαν στην αγγλοκρατούμενη ακόμα Αμερική τα γεγονότα που επιτάχυναν την εδραίωση της δουλείας στην αμερικανική ήπειρο, και η αφορμή ήταν στην περιοχή της Βιρτζίνια, και συγκεκριμένα στην πόλη του Τζέιμς Τάουν, και αυτή θα παρουσιάσουμε σήμερα.

Ας τα πιάσουμε όμως από την αρχή. Υπάρχει μία εύλογη ερώτηση στην ατμόσφαιρα· πριν από το 1676 δεν υπήρχε δηλαδή δουλεία στην Αμερική; Υπήρχε, απλά αποτελούσε εκείνη την περίοδο τη μειοψηφία στις εργασιακές σχέσεις. Η πιο διαδεδομένη όμως εργασιακή σχέση ήταν κάπως διαφορετική. Για να μπορέσει η Βρετανική Αυτοκρατορία να αποικίσει την ανατολική ακτή των σημερινών Ηνωμένων Πολιτειών, πρόσφερε στους μεγαλοκαλλιεργητές κάποια κίνητρα για να προσελκύσουν Άγγλους υπηκόους. Μέσω μίας σύμβασης με έναν τσιφλικά μπορούσες να προσληφθείς για 3 με 7 χρόνια, και να εργαστείς στις αμέτρητες εκτάσεις καπνού που είχε στην προκειμένη περίπτωση η Βιρτζίνια, και μετά το πέρας του συμφωνημένου χρόνου δικαιούσουν μία μικρή έκταση για να γίνεις και εσύ από μεριάς σου ένας αγρότης με το δικό του χωράφι. Ο «εργοδότης» σου από την άλλη, για κάθε έναν νέο άποικο που ερχόταν για λογαριασμό του, έπαιρνε 50 εκτάρια γης, και μόνη του έγνοια ήταν να σου πληρώσει ένα εισιτήριο για να έρθεις μέχρι την Αμερική, και αρκετό φαΐ ώστε να επιβιώνεις. Αυτή η σύμβαση ήταν καλύτερη από την απόκτηση ενός δούλου για τον εξής λόγο: Εάν εσύ που είχες υπογράψει τη σύμβαση πέθαινες, είτε κατά τη διάρκεια του ταξιδιού, είτε εξαιτίας των ασθενειών ή των συνθηκών που επικρατούσαν στην άλλη μεριά του Ατλαντικού, τότε ο τσιφλικάς είχε αποκτήσει τα 50 εκτάρια, και για την αντικατάστασή σου απλά θα έβρισκε κάποιον άλλον φουκαρά που θα ήθελε να ξεφύγει από την ανέχεια. Αντιθέτως για τους τσιφλικάδες η αγορά από τα σκλαβοκάραβα, που έφερναν σωρηδόν κόσμο από την Αφρική, ήταν μια μπίζνα ριψοκίνδυνη καθώς αγόραζαν ανθρώπους σε μία εποχή που η θνησιμότητα βάραγε κόκκινο.

Η δεκαετία του 1670 όμως δεν είναι και τόσο καλή για τον κόσμο που έρχεται στην Αμερική από το Ηνωμένο Βασίλειο. Κυβερνήτης της Βιρτζίνια είναι ένας από τους αγαπημένους του στέμματος, ο ηλικιωμένος Μπέρκλεϊ, ο οποίος έχει δημιουργήσει μια σταθερή κατάσταση στην περιοχή. Οι εχθροπραξίες με τους ιθαγενείς είχαν περιοριστεί, αλλά ο Μπέρκλεϊ είχε και σοβαρές εμπορικές δραστηριότητες μαζί τους. Έτσι και έσοδα έρχονται και δεν είναι υποχρεωμένοι να πληρώνουν για σοβαρά έξοδα για τη φύλαξη της περιοχής. Το πρόβλημα πού βρίσκεται λοιπόν; Κόσμος έρχεται στην Βιρτζίνια, δουλεύει στα καπνά, αλλά δεν υπάρχει η απαραίτητη γη για να τους δοθεί ως αντάλλαγμα. Έτσι έχουμε στα περίχωρα του Τζέιμς Τάουν ένα μείγμα λευκών δυσαρεστημένων που θέλουν περισσότερα από αυτά που τους δίνει η εξουσία. Και για αυτή την κατάσταση φταίνε φυσικά από τη μία ο Μπέρκλεϊ και από την άλλη οι ιθαγενείς. Και εδώ εμφανίζεται ο ήρωας της σημερινής ιστορίας· το όνομα αυτού Ναθάνιαλ Μπέικον. Ο Μπέικον δεν είναι κάποιος τυχαίος. Τον έστειλε ο πατέρας του από την Αγγλία στη Βιρτζίνια, αγόρασε εκεί εκτάσεις και έγινε τσιφλικάς στα περίχωρα κοντά στα νοητά σύνορα με τους ιθαγενείς. Φαινομενικά στην όλη κατάσταση ο Μπέικον δεν είχε κανέναν λόγο να εμπλακεί. Ήταν ένας γενικά κλειστός άνθρωπος, χωρίς κάποιο ιδιαίτερο ενδιαφέρον για τα κοινά. Όμως μία σειρά αντεγκλήσεων με ιθαγενείς στην περιοχή, οι οποίες δεν αφορούσαν καν τον ίδιο, τον έκαναν να αναλάβει δράση. Χαρακτηριστικό παράδειγμα είναι η σύλληψη από μέρους του κάποιων ιθαγενών οι οποίοι, σύμφωνα πάντα με τον Θάνο μας, έκλεψαν καλαμπόκι το οποίο δεν ήταν καν δικό του. Ταυτόχρονα η συμβιβαστική στάση του Μπέρκλεϊ τού δημιουργεί την εικόνα μίας διεφθαρμένης κλίκας στο Τζέιμς Τάουν που δεν νοιάζεται να αντιμετωπίσει τα προβλήματα των κατοίκων της.

Έτσι, λοιπόν, ο Μπέικον αποφασίζει να πάρει την κατάσταση στα χέρια του. Δημιουργεί μία πολιτοφυλακή με άλλους κατοίκους (λευκούς και Αφρικανούς) και μπαίνει σε εδάφη των ιθαγενών και ξεκληρίζει χωριά. Ο κυβερνήτης Μπέρκλεϊ κρατάει μία αρκετά συμβιβαστική στάση και προσπαθεί να ηρεμήσει τα πράγματα, αλλά ο Μπέικον είναι ανένδοτος, αναγκάζοντας τον πρώτο να τον κηρύξει στασιαστή. Έτσι τον Ιούλιο του 1676 ο Θάνος γράφει τη Διακήρυξη του Λαού· ένα δριμύ κατηγορώ απέναντι στον κυβερνήτη που του επιρρίπτει ευθύνες για τον κίνδυνο που διατρέχουν οι κάτοικοι της περιοχής, για τη βαριά φορολογία και τον αποκλεισμό του κόσμου από τα κέντρα λήψης αποφάσεων. Ένα μανιφέστο αρκετά ωραίο στα αυτιά, αλλά που επ’ ουδενί δεν επιδιώκει να δώσει κάποια πιο δημοκρατική …

author: Peter C. Gøtzsche, MD
title: Winning Norwegian Lawsuits about Forced Drugging with Antipsychotics
content:
I

t is very difficult to win lawsuits about psychiatric malpractice, particularly about forced drugging with antipsychotics.

1

 One reason is, as lawyer Jim Gottstein, has observed in Alaska,

2

 and which I have also seen on several occasions, that psychiatrists routinely misrepresent the evidence in court: About how ill their patients are; what wonders they can achieve with antipsychotics; and saying that the patients have tolerated them well, which the patients disagree with.

3


When I studied 30 consecutive cases from Denmark

3

 and 30 consecutive cases from Alaska,

4

 where the patients had appealed forced treatment orders, I found that the legal procedures were a sham where the patients were defenceless, and that the law had been violated in every single case.


Another reason why lawsuits are difficult to win is that judges have so much respect for authority that they didn’t care the least when I, other expert witnesses, and lawyers for the plaintiffs like Gottstein demonstrated in court that professors of psychiatry and other experts were lying.

1,2,5


A third reason why it is so difficult to obtain justice is that Ombudsman and Supreme Court decisions are consistently being ignored.

1

 In Norway, the Ombudsman concluded in 2018 that forced treatment with an antipsychotic in a concrete case had violated the law.

6

 The law stipulates that forced drugging can be used when, with “high probability, it can lead to recovery or significant improvement in the patient’s condition, or if the patient avoids a significant worsening of the disease.” Referring to science, the Ombudsman noted that the probability of achieving the intended improvement is very low.


Despite the Ombudsman’s ruling, the unethical practice just continued. It is therefore very significant, also in an international context, that four court cases in Norway—three of them related to antipsychotics—were recently won.


In 2024, I was an expert witness in a lawsuit against the Norwegian State at the Oslo District Court.

5

 It was lost because of an incompetent judge, but the Court of Appeal, which corresponds to the Superior Court in other countries, ruled in 2026 that the human rights were violated when Inger-Mari Eidsvik was subjected to forced treatment with antipsychotics and in a case of solitary confinement.


It had been very difficult to get there. Inger-Mari’s lawyers had been fighting

pro bono

 for over three years for the right to sue the state for multiple violations of the European Convention on Human Rights, the UN conventions, and the Norwegian Constitution. After having lost in two inferior courts, they won at the Supreme Court and were allowed to go ahead with the first case ever to challenge coercive treatment in psychiatry.


I describe here three other Norwegian cases. I met the three women involved at the Mad in Norway film festival in September 2026 where my filmmaker and I showed our documentary, “The Illusion of Psychiatry.”

7

 My account is based on court documents and personal information.


Helen Wesnes


Helen’s story is so gruesome that it is hard to believe that this could happen in a civilised country. She was sexually assaulted in her late teens and struggled with insomnia and nightmares. In the end, she agreed to a two-week stay at a psychiatric hospital, which a psychologist had suggested.


Two weeks turned into nine years. Helen spent nine years continuously in Reinsvoll Hospital from 2000 when she was only 20 years old. NINE YEARS!


Then, from 2009 to 2015, she stayed at an assisted living residence where she was subjected to forced medication. In total, she was under forced treatment for 15 years.


From day one, she was put on an antidepressant, and shortly thereafter she also received antipsychotics, benzodiazepines, an antiepileptic, a stimulant, and lithium. She was misdiagnosed with hebephrenic schizophrenia, but lithium doesn’t work for schizophrenia.

8,9

 It was also medical malpractice to treat Helen with Leponex (clozapine) and Abilify (aripiprazole) simultaneously. National

10

 and international guidelines recommend against using two antipsychotics at the same time and there are very good reasons for this. The benefit is not increased by increasing the dose

11

 but the risk of death from these highly toxic drugs is of course dose-related.

12


Leponex is a particularly toxic drug, which is not more effective than other antipsychotics,
