author: daniel
title: Ableistisches journalistisches Versagen
content: Dieser wurde aber weitgehend totgeschwiegen. Es gab kaum Presseberichte. Selbst über die Besetzung eines Bundesministeriums berichtete einzig die Frankfurter Rundschau. Journalist*innen schreiben lieber über Einzelschicksale. Mitleid-erweckende Berichte generieren online Klicks und gefallen Leser*innen. Die Berichte bleiben oberflächlich und die systemischen und politischen Hintergründe werden nicht beleuchtet. Betroffene als Objekte einer bequemen Berichtserstattung. Sobald Betroffene als Akteur*innen auftreten und das System, das sie behindert, anprangern, werden sie unsichtbar gemacht. Die Redaktionen stehen offenbar zu dieser ableistischen Linie. Der Lüneburger Behindertenbeirat kritisierte die Nicht-Berichtserstattung der Landeszeitung (LZ) über eine Kundgebung am europäischen Protesttag für die Gleichstellung von Menschen mit Behinderung. Die Redaktion antwortete am 22. Mai 2026 wie folgt: „Anm. d. Red.: Am Protesttag selbst hat die LZ tatsächlich nicht berichtet. Wir stellen hingegen regelmäßig Schicksale von Menschen mit Einschränkungen in den Mittelpunkt von Geschichten – unabhängig von Protest- oder Gedenktagen. So haben wir beispielsweise am 9. Mai von der 16-jährigen Lotti berichtet, die trotz Unterstützungsbedarf ihren Traumberuf lernen will.“ Selbst die verwendete Sprache ist hier ableistisch. Das Wort „Behinderung“ wird gemieden, obwohl dies kein Schimpfwort ist, sondern eine neutrale Eigenschaft. Das ist ein journalistisches Versagen. Die Graswurzelrevolution wird dagegen über die Proteste und ihre Hintergründe ausführlich in der GWR 514 berichten. Seid auf den Schwerpunkt der Dezemberausgabe gespannt!

author: Sarah Hughes
title: Members Alarmed by End-Run around Democracy at Buffalo Health Care Local
content:
Things had been tense for some time inside the leadership of Communications Workers (CWA) Local 1168, a 4,800-member health care union based near Buffalo, New York. Still, it was a high-functioning local with a busy calendar of events, stewards handling grievances, organizers pursuing leads, and leaders organizing at work.


So it was a surprise to members in June when their parent union, CWA, put the local into trusteeship, at the request of the local’s president and seven of the nineteen executive board members.


Trusteeship meant the union’s bylaws and elected leaders were suspended, and most of its work temporarily ground to a halt. The appointed Director of Organizing and Mobilizing Mary Nowocien and elected Vice President Patrick Weisansal II found themselves locked out of their group chats, email, and union hall, and facing an internal union prosecution.


A staffer of CWA District 1, Erin Spaulding, was assigned as trustee—tasked with maintaining the functioning of the local, setting up and overseeing judicial processes for the charges against officers, and making a plan to return the union to local control.


Nowocien and Weisansal saw the sudden trusteeship as an escalation of a long-running conflict and a deliberate undermining of the upcoming union elections. Weisansal had just announced his intention to run against incumbent President Cori Gambini.


Now the elections are on hold until the trials are over, whenever that is. And lately, the employer has been taking advantage of the turmoil in the union.


While the allegations are serious, members are concerned that the trusteeship was a nuclear option for an internal financial matter and that it has torn apart relationships at the local, weakened opposition to management’s schemes and denied democratic processes to an active, engaged union membership.


ALLEGED TIMECARD ISSUES


The trusteeship filing lists the cause as “serious allegations of financial misconduct” from officers and “dueling charges” between leaders.


Gambini and Executive Vice President Robert Andruszko had accused Nowocien and Weisansal of defrauding the local of thousands of dollars, by getting paid by both the union and their employer for the same hours worked, and by falsifying records. These issues came to light during a timecard audit in the fall of 2025 by their employer, Kaleida Health.


Nowocien and Weisansal acknowledged there were significant errors on old timecards and paychecks, but said it was the product of the employer’s faulty timekeeping and payroll system, and human error. The majority of other officers also had issues, they pointed out, but only some were being singled out for discipline by the local and the employer.


Spaulding, the trustee, interviewed all the suspended officers and allowed the majority to return to their paid positions—with the exception of Nowocien, Weisansal, and three others not facing any charges: the Communications and Political Directors and one of the Area Vice Presidents. Also fired were two longtime staff organizers, on the grounds that there was no work for them to do, according to one, Ann Converso, who had recently helped organize a new unit of substance use disorder counselors and was gearing up for their first contract fight.


Many current leaders on both sides of this schism were part of a reform caucus in Local 1168, the Caucus of Rank-and-File Healthcare Employees (CORHE), which dissolved when they won their positions in 2020.


Since winning, Gambini and a few others have butted heads with Weisansal, Nowocien, and others over how to tackle problems. The latter camp frequently organized their facility—Buffalo General Hospital, the union’s largest unit—to push back against management’s changes and violations. Gambini and leaders aligned with her argued that that wasn’t the right approach—that they had to pick their fights and not overextend the membership, according to Weisansal.


One Buffalo General steward, who asked to not be named, said members were appalled that the trustee had removed elected officers. “If our employer treated one of our members in a similar fashion,” the steward said, “union leadership would rally around them and fight to return them to their position!”


Spaulding wrote in a public FAQ posted on the local’s social media that the temporary administration “is not intended to be punitive or find guilt against any individual in the Local. It is intended to stabilize the Local while issues are …

author: Solarpunk Magazine
title: Solarpunk Horror, Lunarpunk Submissions, and 2027 Magazine Submissions
content:
We’ve got some exciting announcements to share! There’s a brand-new lunarpunk anthology seeking submissions, our special horror-themed issue of Solarpunk Magazine is available for preorder, we’re going to start publishing solarpunk novellas and novels, and our complete 2027 submissions schedule is now up on our website’s submissions page.

So whether you’re a reader looking for your next great story or a writer dreaming up better futures, here’s what’s coming.

Submission Window: November 1 – December 31, 2026

Android Press is preparing to venture into the shadows with What Blooms in Darkness: A Lunarpunk Anthology, edited by our co-editor-in-chief, Justine Norton-Kertson, and scheduled for publication in autumn 2027.

Lunarpunk shares solarpunk’s commitment to ecological regeneration, social justice, community, and liberatory futures, while exploring the possibilities that emerge in darkness, mystery, privacy, dreams, and the hidden corners of our world.

What Blooms in Darkness asks some fascinating questions: What kinds of communities thrive beyond the reach of surveillance? What knowledge survives underground? What forms of liberation become possible when people are free to remain unseen?

Android Press is seeking stories about everything from nocturnal ecosystems and underground communities to secret mutual-aid networks, hidden cultures, rituals, and resistance movements. The anthology welcomes imaginative interpretations of lunarpunk, especially stories that challenge the assumption that darkness is inherently dangerous or frightening.

Genre: Lunarpunk, climate fiction, and related speculative fiction

Eligibility: Original, unpublished fiction by human authors worldwide

Expected publication: Autumn 2027

Whether you’re a writer or a reader, you can easily sign up to get a notification when the anthology’s crowdfunder launches in March 2027!

We’ve spent years exploring what better futures might look like. Now we’re inviting some monsters into the garden. We’re thrilled to reveal the cover and complete table of contents for Solarpunk Magazine Issue #30, our special Solarpunk Horror issue, arriving November 10, 2026!

Horror and solarpunk might seem like an unusual combination, but we think they have a lot to say to each other. What happens when the ghosts of ecological destruction refuse to stay buried? What kinds of monsters might haunt societies struggling to heal centuries of exploitation? And how do things like fear, grief, survival, and resistance fit into our visions of better futures?

This extra large special issue brings together fiction, poetry, essays, and artwork that explore the darker edges of solarpunk imagination. We’re especially excited about the lineup of writers and artists contributing to this issue.

“The Unrooted Sea” by Seiba Rosario

“Bottles, Bones, Skein” by Marisca Pichette

“A Sweetness On The Breeze” by John Leahy

“Blood of the Town, Veins of the Earth” by Katharine Tyndall

“Beneath the Absorbent City” by Joy Donnell

“Bombarding Bloom of Another Disintegration” by CP Nwankwo

“I Carry My Hauntings Into a Stranger’s House” by Sarah Titus

“The Kingdom of Rot Is Within You” by Josh Pearce

“The Monsters Have Entered the Garden” by Justine Norton-Kertson

“The Ordinary Was Extraordinary All Along: A reflection on loss, appreciation, and radical hope from Gaza” by Aya Al-Hattab

“Reemergence of the Past” by Victoria Black

We’re incredibly grateful to all the contributors who helped bring this experiment in solarpunk horror to life.

Issue #30 releases November 10, 2026, and is available for preorder now for $6.

Planning to send us something in 2027? Here are the dates to remember! Our regular magazine submission windows for short stories, poetry, essays, and art will be the same as they were in 2026:

We also have two special themed issues planned for 2027!

Our sixth annual Colorful Roots issue will publish in July and continue our commitment to celebrating the voices and imaginations of Black, Indigenous, and other writers and artists of color. Colorful Roots has become an important part of our publishing calendar, and we’re excited to continue creating space for the diverse perspectives and experiences that are essential to solarpunk’s vision of collective liberation. BIPOC authors and artists can submit work for this issue during any submission window by using the tag #BIPOC in the submission cover letter.

author: Tam Saavedra
title: WEI and UN Women Co-Launches Guide for Disability-Inclusive
content:
Across Asia and the Pacific, 350 million women and girls with disabilities navigate conflict, crisis, and climate instability. While they are frontline peacebuilders, community leaders, and human rights defenders, they remain systematically excluded from formal peace and security decision-making.

To break down these barriers, Women Enabled International (WEI) and the UN Women Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific have officially launched a landmark publication today: the Guidance Note on Disability-Inclusive National Action Plans on Women, Peace and Security in Asia and the Pacific. Released ahead of the annual UN Security Council high-level debate in New York, this first-of-its-kind guide provides a practical, policy-oriented blueprint for governments, policymakers, and civil society.

Read the full Guidance Note on Disability-Inclusive NAPs on WPS in Asia and the Pacific

Historically, women with disabilities in peace policies have been viewed narrowly as victims or passive recipients of protection. Co-drafted through consultations with 26 women and gender-diverse people with disabilities, in collaboration with Women Enabled International and the UN Women Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific, this guide directly challenges that narrative. It grounds its framework in a human rights model of disability and the core movement principle: “Nothing about us without us”.

As WEI Executive Director Maryangel García-Ramos Guadiana stated during the launch:

“The true value of this Guidance Note is that it exists, not as a siloed document, but as a means to ensure we, as feminist disabled change-makers, are not left out of the agenda, but we are the ones who get to set the agenda.”

UN Women Regional Director for Asia and the Pacific, Christine Arab, added:

“National Action Plans on WPS that include everyone lead to peace that lasts.”

The publication was shaped by participatory research, drawing on focus groups and surveys with 26 grassroots leaders with diverse disabilities across the region. It addresses critical ground-level hurdles—including digital exclusion, inaccessible evacuation infrastructure, and ableism in mainstream spaces—ensuring that the voices of women, girls and gender-diverse people with disabilities form the foundation of the guidance.

The publication urges stakeholders to align National Action Plans (NAPs) with international standards—including the CRPD, CEDAW, and UN Security Council Resolution 2475—across all four WPS pillars:

Participation: Reserve seats for organizations of persons with disabilities (OPDs)—especially women-led OPDs—on NAP steering committees with full accessibility support.

Participation: Reserve seats for organizations of persons with disabilities (OPDs)—especially women-led OPDs—on NAP steering committees with full accessibility support.

Prevention: Recognize women and gender-diverse people with disabilities as active peacebuilders and integrate intersectional early-warning indicators.

Prevention: Recognize women and gender-diverse people with disabilities as active peacebuilders and integrate intersectional early-warning indicators.

Protection: Address unique forms of violence (such as caregiver abuse or institutionalization) and guarantee accessible shelters and evacuation procedures.

Protection: Address unique forms of violence (such as caregiver abuse or institutionalization) and guarantee accessible shelters and evacuation procedures.

Relief & Recovery: Ensure transitional justice mechanisms, reparations, and post-conflict upskilling actively include women with disabilities.

Relief & Recovery: Ensure transitional justice mechanisms, reparations, and post-conflict upskilling actively include women with disabilities.

The guide also features a practical Disability-Inclusive WPS NAP Checklist to help stakeholders evaluate progress at every stage of policy implementation.

This Guidance Note was made possible with the generous support of the Government of the Republic of Korea (through the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family) as part of the project “Promoting Leadership of Future Generation Peacebuilders and Change-makers in Asia and the Pacific”, and of the Australian Government under the Regional Framework Towards Peaceful, Inclusive Societies (2023–2027).

author: Anne-Marie Cicala
title: How My Body Rejected Lithium After 25 Years
content:
I

t was two o’clock in the morning on our first night out of town in New Orleans, and I woke up suddenly in the dark hotel room feeling horribly sick and needing to run to the bathroom. What ensued was messy and lasted for two hours. I kept waking up with my head in the toilet to do it again. I used most of the towels in the bathroom to clean up both myself and the mess I had made on the floor. At 4am, exhausted and beyond tired, not knowing exactly how to handle the situation, I opened my hotel room door completely naked, threw the armful of soiled towels into the hallway and went back to bed.


The next morning, I woke up extremely nauseous. I was thankful we had packed a decent amount of THC gummies, as they proved to be a savior for the next few days. The gummies took the nausea down to a level where I was able to function throughout the day, but I was still not feeling right or well. I didn’t know if it was from the previous night’s events, but I felt subdued by a heavy brain fog.


The day progressed slowly, as I was not feeling 100%, but I made it through, enduring other would just get a good night’s sleep and be better in the morning. Yet, without fail, I once more woke up in the middle of the night, more prepared this time, and got sick several times.


I really had no idea what was going on. Once again, I woke up with severe nausea but thought maybe a good breakfast would set me straight.


At the hotel restaurant, I could not tolerate the smell of the food. I could barely drink my coffee. My husband, looking at me searchingly, kept asking if I was okay. I tried to assure him that I would be fine, although I wasn’t sure I believed that myself. He finally said, “I don’t know what to do when my wife looks like she’s about to vomit at any moment.” Remembering how much the gummies had helped me the day before, I decided it was going to have to be another day like that, so I asked him to go up to the room to retrieve one for me. He happily obliged. I ate the gummy and was feeling relief within about 40 minutes. I could finally breathe and begin to perform as a person on vacation.


At restaurants, I noticed that the menus would shake furiously in my hands, as well as my fork and my drinking glass. I brushed it off as my usual lithium tremor combined with low blood sugar. I also noticed that my thirst was unquenchable. At one restaurant, as soon as the waiter set the water on the table, I chugged the glass immediately and instructed him to keep them coming, that I was extra thirsty. My husband looked at me with concern and kept the gummies coming, which were still keeping the nausea at a manageable level. My additional stomach ailments continued, but I pushed through them and tried to make the best of it, still under the spell of a heavy brain fog.


After another night of vomiting and immediately popping gummies as soon as I woke up, my husband and I put our heads together. We ran through the list of symptoms I had been experiencing, coming up clueless. Next, we thought back on anything that had changed recently. Aha! Indeed, my psychiatrist had increased my lithium right before we left for vacation.


Only knowing that connection, we began to research my symptoms plus the keyword ‘lithium’. Immediately, tons of links popped up about lithium toxicity, something neither one of us knew anything about. It seemed serious, but some of the stories I read seemed a lot graver than mine, so I figured I wasn’t in need of emergency care. I simply discontinued the lithium, and we went home the next day. Not getting back until later in the evening, it was the following day before I could go in for an emergency blood draw to check my lithium levels, something that had been done frequently throughout my nearly 25-year history of being on the medication.


I had been put on lithium for my early bipolar (then later schizoaffective) diagnosis when I was 18 years old, after spending the previous year psychiatrically hospitalized seven times for depression, anxiety, psychosis and unstable mood. I was promised mood stability and less suicidal ideation. It was supposedly the leading option, my best line of defense. That is what I was told for the next 25 years, but I was never told about lithium toxicity.


From the start, the side effects were horrible. So much GI distress and unquenchable thirst, which I know now was my kidneys urgently trying to rid my body of the essential poison of the drug. I learned to deal with it. Every …

content:
Le 31 octobre, c'est Halloween – la fête des morts. Généralement ils reviennent exiger des bonbons ou des sorts. Le 17 octobre, le gouvernement a choisi les sorts. Résultat : on vient de quitter l'époque contemporaine et, depuis, Bismillah, c'est les ténèbres. Mais ces ténèbres, elles sont super drôles.


Jamais autant de créatures multiformes n'avaient déferlé dans nos insurrections. Il nous a fallu analyser cet étrange phénomène. Alors on a invité deux experts des ténèbres joyeuses : le philosophe Norman Ajari et l'essayiste Pacôme Thiellement. La brèche entre les mondes vient de s'ouvrir, elle n'est pas près de se refermer. C'est la première fois que la révolution s'apparente à la chorégraphie du Thriller de Michaël Jackson. Si le Gilet Jaune de 2018 s'est ajouté au k-way noir de 2016, désormais : c'est l'intégralité du multiverse qui se fait costume. author: Tam Saavedra
title: ¡Las Directrices de la CDPD de la ONU sobre Interseccionalidad están aquí!
content:
Read in English


Las Directrices de la CDPD de la ONU sobre Interseccionalidad acaban de cambiar las reglas del juego para los derechos de las personas con discapacidad: Esto es lo que necesitas saber

 


¡Grandes noticias para las mujeres con discapacidad y para todas las personas defensoras, aliadas y organizaciones feministas y con discapacidad en todo el mundo!

 


Durante su 35º Período de Sesiones en agosto de 2026, el

Comité de las Naciones Unidas sobre los Derechos de las Personas con Discapacidad

 (CDPD de la ONU)

 adoptó oficialmente las

Directrices sobre la Identificación y Abordaje de la Discriminación Interseccional Contra las Niñas, Adolescentes, Mujeres y Mujeres Mayores con Discapacidad

.

 


Este hito representa un paso gigante para los derechos de las personas con discapacidad. Por primera vez, los Estados Partes cuentan con orientación explícita y accionable para respaldar sus obligaciones en la intersección entre género y discapacidad.

 


Lee las Directrices oficiales de la CDPD de la ONU aquí

 


¿Qué son las Directrices de la CDPD sobre Discriminación Interseccional?

 


Las Directrices constituyen un marco internacional autorizado, desarrollado por la CDPD de la ONU, para ayudar a los Estados a prevenir, supervisar y abordar de mejor manera la discriminación interseccional.

 


A lo largo de años de procesos de revisión de países por parte de la CDPD de la ONU, el Comité identificó una brecha persistente y crítica:

los derechos humanos específicos de las mujeres con discapacidad y la discriminación interseccional y compleja que experimentan, rara vez son comprendidas o abordadas por los gobiernos.

 


Al celebrar el 20º aniversario de la CDPD de la ONU

, e

stas Directrices fueron emitidas para cerrar esa brecha, garantizando que la convención se aplique a favor de

todas

las mujeres y niñas con discapacidad, y las personas de género diverso con discapacidad a lo largo de sus vidas.

 


¿Por qué estas Directrices cambian las reglas del juego?

 


Los documentos internacionales rara vez se centran de forma explícita en las experiencias de vida y los derechos de las mujeres con discapacidad. Estas Directrices nombran y explican las barreras sistémicas que las mujeres y personas de género diverso con discapacidad enfrentan a diario en todo el mundo, incluyendo:

 


Salud y Derechos Sexuales y Reproductivos (SDSR):

 Abordar y prevenir la esterilización forzada, la anticoncepción forzada, la falta de atención médica accesible, las restricciones al aborto y la falta de atención perinatal, menstrual y menopáusica.

 


Violencia de Género y Basada en la Discapacidad:

 Exponer la violencia institucional, el abuso digital/en línea y la falta generalizada de servicios de apoyo para las víctimas.

 


Reconocimiento de las labores de cuidado:

 Validar a las mujeres con discapacidad como cuidadoras activas y madres, en lugar de tratarlas únicamente como receptoras de cuidados.

 


Exclusión económica y educativa:

 Destacar las barreras en el mercado laboral y la exclusión de la educación durante la pubertad.

 


Respuesta a crisis y cambio climático:

 Combatir la exclusión agravada durante desastres ambientales, emergencias climáticas y esfuerzos de ayuda humanitaria.

 


Por nombrar sólo algunas.

 


7 avances clave en el enfoque de las Directrices

 


Lo que hace que este documento sea un instrumento transformador único es su enfoque estructural y progresista:

 


Inclusión explícita de la diversidad de género:

 Las Directrices abarcan explícitamente los derechos de las personas transgénero, intersexuales, no binarias y de otras diversidades de género con discapacidad, y solicitan una interpretación inclusiva de la diversidad de género de todas las obligaciones descritas.

 


Reconocimiento de las raíces históricas:

 El Comité aborda explícitamente el legado y los impactos continuos del colonialismo y la esclavización, estableciendo que los Estados que se benefician de estos sistemas históricos tienen la responsabilidad particular de reparar sus efectos actuales.

 


Un catálogo abierto de diversidad:

 El texto reconoce que las mujeres con discapacidad pertenecen a comunidades multimarginalizadas —incluidos grupos indígenas, afrodescendientes/negros, dalit, adivasi, refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, minorías religiosas, pastoriles o personas que viven en asentamientos informales, entre otros— dejando espacio para todas las identidades interseccionales.

author: Robert Whitaker
title: Dangerous Gifts: Rethinking Madness, Healing, and Human Connection – A Conversation With Sascha DuBrul
content:
H

ello, my name is Robert Whitaker, and today I have the great pleasure of having as my guest on Mad in America Radio Sascha DuBrul. Sascha will be well-known to most Mad in America listeners. He’s been a leading activist in psychiatric circles for more than two decades now.


He co-founded The Icarus Project and worked closely with the Institute for the Development of Human Arts. His interests lie at the intersection of the public mental health system and the Mad Underground.


The transcript below has been edited for length and clarity. Listen to the audio of the interview here.


Robert Whitaker: Sascha, welcome to Mad in America Radio.


Sascha DuBrul

: I’m so happy to be here, Bob.


Whitaker: I’d like to tell a little story about how I first discovered you and the Icarus Project. I had come out with a book,

Mad in America

, in 2002, and at that time, I wrote about MindFreedom, David Oaks, and the psychiatric survivor movement. Then all of a sudden, the Icarus Project popped up on my screen, and I could see that it was different in its orientation from the psychiatric survivor movement, and yet it was user-led. Sascha, can you tell us what led you to co-found the Icarus Project?


DuBrul:

 First of all, it’s great to have this conversation with you after all these years, because one thing that just occurs to me is when you started the Mad in America website, I was one of the first people

blogging

 on it.


When we started the Icarus Project, there was the psychiatric survivor movement that you were talking about, and then there was biological psychiatry. There were the NAMI meetings that my mom had gone to when I had been hospitalized and diagnosed with bipolar disorder, but there was nothing really in between. There was no space to say, Hey, you know what? These things that we’re talking about, mental illness if we want to call it that, or the extreme states that we’re experiencing, or these hard times that we’re going through, we don’t have language to talk about it.


The psychiatric survivor language never really resonated with me or with the other people that were originally part of Icarus, and part of that was a generational thing. The psychiatric survivor movement came of age in a time when people were getting locked up in institutions for long periods of time. We were the biomedical generation, where we were getting diagnosed and put on drugs, but not having these long, extended stays in the hospital.


Icarus started because I wrote an article in the

San Francisco Bay Guardian

. I was 27 years old, and I was asking questions like, I don’t trust the pharmaceutical industry, but the drugs that they’re giving me seem to actually be helping me. I’m looking for other people out there that are just trying to figure this stuff out. That’s the context in which Icarus started.


Whitaker: The Icarus Project is often referred to as a radical group. Yet on the one hand, you’re finding the drugs helpful; many members did. I presume you were in a position of choice, right? People like the drugs, that’s great. If they don’t like the drugs, that’s good too.


DuBrul:

 When we started, we said very clearly, if you take the psychiatric drugs or you think they’re poison, you’re welcome to be a part of the Icarus Project. If you use diagnostic categories, like bipolar disorder or schizophrenia, or you think all those categories are ridiculous, you’re welcome to be a part of the Icarus Project. We opened up a lot of space for people who wouldn’t necessarily agree with each other to be in the same room.


Whitaker: But you shared the experience of having been diagnosed, of having some exposure to the psychiatric system, and in some ways finding it unhelpful. Isn’t that correct?


DuBrul:

 For sure, but I think what that actually means is for people to say, yeah, that was really horrible the way those doctors treated me. They treated me like I couldn’t even make decisions for myself. But what is that language they use? The language of harm to self or harm to others. Maybe I actually was going to hurt myself if they didn’t put me in the hospital. Maybe I was actually going to hurt somebody else if I wasn’t put in the hospital.


We opened up space for all kinds of questions like that, that I think the traditional psychiatric survivor movement really didn’t have language or space for in the way they were thinking.

author: Donald Zrebiec
title: She Was Here: Finding My Grandmother After Willard
content:
I

 often mention that I was the only one of Catherine Smoral’s grandchildren to see her alive. I was six years old, and the visit to Willard State Hospital was a bad experience for all four of us who were there: my mother Anna, my Uncle Tony, me, and my grandmother Catherine. The three of us who came from Syracuse were all shocked at the physical and mental condition of our mother and grandmother. Our visit upset her, and we spent a very short time there before being asked to leave.


My grandmother was born in Poland in 1884. She emigrated to the U.S. in 1900, and in 1902 she married my grandfather, Karol Smoral. They were married at Sacred Heart, a beautiful Polish church that still stands on the west side of Syracuse. They were a happy couple who went on to have nine children, a happy and healthy brood. Karol bought his own home on Morgan Avenue, and a family burial plot at Sacred Heart Cemetery not far from it. In the early 1920s, disaster struck the household.


I received, I believe from Ancestry.com, a copy of an article from the Syracuse Herald from the early 1920s. This is how it read:


SMORAL FAMILY WOES CULMINATE IN COMMITTAL OF EIGHT TO INSTITUTIONS. Mother and Son Are Sent to Willard. Six Younger Children to Various Orphanages. Father Died in December.


Mrs. Catherine Smoral and son Stephen, 15, were committed to Willard. Until death delivered its first blow at 107 Morgan Avenue, the family of Karol had something resembling happiness. The mother, who had been in a State Hospital before, had been returned to her family apparently cured. Stephen, then the oldest child, was of working age at 16. The children were sufficiently nourished and progressing. When Karol died, his wife became melancholic, and their son Stephen succeeded her as both mother and father of the household. The burden of being both mother and father broke him down. An investigator from the International Institute found the family nearly destitute. The son Stephen had been employed in a laboratory, but conditions for work were made impossible.


Awaiting his transfer to his new home, Chester drugged himself [he was a year and a half old at the time] with some chocolate he was given by someone in the courtroom. He smeared himself with the chocolate . . . Welfare workers are working to find him a home in a Polish family. The four girls had been all dressed up for the trip and were quiet. They had been weeping.


No matter how many times I see or read this article, I get emotional. It encapsulates the reason I wrote the book. I have a lot of trouble with it. First, it is inaccurate, and it tries to make those kids into clowns instead of marveling at their courage. Perhaps what bothers me most is the comment early on that the family had “something resembling happiness.” Who in the hell was that reporter to make a judgment like that? That’s my family he is talking about. How did they make this family tragedy a front-page story, and why did they try to turn it into some semi-comic farce? Every time I reread it, I would like to hit that reporter right in the face. But at the time, maybe mental illness and sudden death were subjects for fun and light-heartedness.


His name was never Chester. His given name was Vincent, and his nickname was Chet. I get upset about his “drugging himself” on chocolate when he was a year and a half old. He may never have had chocolate until that day. I always admired him. He became a scholarship athlete who went to college and was the first member of the Smoral family to graduate, and he was an excellent role model for his children.


Then there is the way they described the girls, all dressed up but weeping. Those girls were about six, eight, and ten years old. They had just lost both parents, their home, and probably each other, and the newspaper noticed that they had been crying. This was my family they were talking about. They should have had the sense to commend those children for holding up so well. A lot of children could not have, and I wouldn’t have blamed them. This article encapsulates all of the sadness in this whole story.


Zrebiec family photo. Courtesy of Don Zrebiec


I got over the visit to Willard pretty quickly. My picture of my grandmother faded after a short time, and I became immersed in the process of growing up. I talked to my mother about her mother at times, but she always seemed reluctant to go very deep in these conversations and often changed the subject. She had been hurt by …

author: Hilde Marie Rekstad
title: The Process: Helen Wesnes Fights for Her Rights
content:
Editor’s Note: This piece was originally published on our affiliate site,

Mad in Norway

.


Helen Wesnes took control of her own case from the beginning and has already won several victories in the legal system. She does this for all those who lose their lives in psychiatry. Photo: private


H


elen Wesnes was 19 when she sought help from the health care system. It cost her 15 years, followed by a 12-year legal process. She has already won millions in damages and is ready for the next round. Now she explains how she built her case.


Few people know that in Norway there is a society within a society, full of paradoxes and with no known way out. This is the Norway offered to psychiatric patients once they fall under the Mental Health Care Act. “Someone must have slandered Josef K., for one morning, without having done anything wrong, he was arrested,” writes Franz Kafka in his world-famous

The Trial

, and what follows is a nightmare about the individual’s powerlessness against the arbitrariness of bureaucracy. Josef K. and Helen W. don’t have a great deal in common, since she walked out alive and victorious. Otherwise, the process was much the same.


“The media are failing their mission when they don’t raise this case to a systemic level. The practice itself is the problem, not whatever diagnosis the patient may have.”


Helen Wesnes speaks out about her 15 years of confinement, and the legal process that followed


I have invited Helen Wesnes to a conversation in which she shares reflections on the 15 years she was locked up in psychiatry, cut off from both physical and emotional contact with other people. This was the consequence of seeking medical help after a collapse brought on by a critical life event. Her story is an almost unbelievable process, and so is the battle Helen is now fighting in the Norwegian legal system. It is a battle she is fighting for everyone who loses their lives to psychiatry. She holds hard-won experience of what health care should have been, but isn’t, for those who need it most.


There has been limited media interest in covering the legal process Helen Wesnes has pursued for 12 years, and which is still ongoing. This despite the fact that it is historic for a psychiatric patient in Norway to be awarded damages for human rights violations. The articles that have been written have focused on the fact that she was misdiagnosed. Helen says the media are failing their mission when they don’t raise this case to a systemic level. The practice itself is the problem, not whatever diagnosis the patient may have.


Helen has unique expertise in how to prevail against the system once mistakes have been made. She has acquired these skills through what has so far been a more than twelve-year war against state bodies, along with insight into what goes on behind closed doors. In this in-depth interview you can read about a Norway that very few people know exists. She is now asking for deeper understanding from the media and others. “They tend to focus on how terrible it is that I was misdiagnosed, back when trauma was interpreted as schizophrenia. They don’t ask the fundamental question: Should any human being be treated like this?”


Above the entrance to Reinsvoll hospital, the sign reads “Emergency care.” When Helen needed two weeks of rest after a crisis, the consequence was 15 years of confinement and inhumane treatment. Photo: Helen Wesnes


There are events in this story that reveal eugenics thinking, and this is Norway in the 2000s. The sum of what she has been subjected to can also be understood as misogyny. The mechanisms meant to detect and correct problems in the many locked wards in our country have proven to fail. Helen herself says she believes she got out at the last minute, when medical tests showed alarming values.


What began as a patient injury case in 2015 has become an insane process in which the State is doing everything to crush a patient, where the hospital had admitted its mistakes even before the case began. This shameful story should have been compensated many years ago. Instead, the state has dared to appeal.


A brief outline of the Norwegian system


Patients subjected to compulsory treatment must turn to the Control Commission to complain, or to the County Governor (Statsforvalteren) if the complaint is unsuccessful. Once treatment has ended, patients can claim compensation from NPE (the Norwegian System of Patient Injury Compensation). If the claim is rejected …

title: Lois Waisbrooker - A Sex Revolution
content:
Author

: Lois Waisbrooker

Title

: A Sex Revolution

Date

: 1894

Notes

: Second Edition

Source

: <

http://www.pierssen.com/misc/treasures/asr.htm

>


Preface.


 Dear Reader:—The history of the past shows us that nations rise, go through a longer or shorter period of prosperity and then decay. The ruling motive in the life of nations, so far, has always been the same, the aggressive or masculine. Self-aggrandizement,

our

 nation right or wrong, all to be laid upon the national altar in the name of patriotism, a centralizing of wealth and power in the hands of the few at the expense of the many, and the result has always been what? Go, gather together the human wrecks of any one nation and you have your answer.


 Now will not this latest and brightest of nations perish also unless methods are changed, unless the social lever is reversed? Already the seeds of decay are taking root; is there not some law through which we may take a new lease of life, and what is that law, if there be such, if it be not that


 “woman, take the lead?”


 True, woman is already quite prominent, is becoming more so, but she does not seem as yet to realize that with man’s methods she will succeed no better than man has done. She must formulate her own methods before her true work can appear. Woman must be free, must refuse to be led, must believe in herself, before the evils attendant upon imperfect motherhood can be eliminated, and as I see things, the only hope of our nation lies in this direction.


 Let us once rise above the necessity of armies, navies, prisons, almshouses, asylums, etc., then the future will stretch out before us with ever increasing brightness. The first step toward this desirable consummation is to believe that it

can

 be done; the next is that it

will

 be done, and lastly to determine to do it

ourselves

.


 L. W.


Chapter I.


 First, a little something about myself. I, Margaret Mulgrove, am a childless widow. My husband, Richard Mulgrove, went into the Union army at the beginning of our last war and never came out alive. My only child, little Bessie, took the scarlet fever in the second year of my widowhood, and though employing the most skillful physician in the whole country around, I could not save her. To say that I was desolate does not begin to express the feeling I had.


 An aunt, my father’s only sister who lived in another State, hearing of my bereavement, decided to come and stay with me awhile and wrote me to that effect. Now my father and mother had in their lifetime (I forgot to say that I was an orphan also) had been good orthodox Christians and had brought me up to walk in the same path, so when Aunt Belinda wrote me she was coming I was a little troubled, for I had been told that she was an Infidel.


 I believed infidelity to be something awful, and as our community was a very respectable one, to have a woman of that character come among us, and as my relative was an affliction I had not counted on, but it could not be helped; aunt would be there the next day and I must make the best of it. So the next morning I went to work to put things in the best order possible to receive my expected relative.


 She came about ten o’clock, a pleasant faced, white haired lady toward whom my heart instinctively went out, and in spite of my prejudices I felt that I should love her. She stayed with me several months during which time nothing was said or done which brought up the subject of beliefs. True, I had purposely avoided everything that could lead in that direction, but she did not seem at all inclined to be aggressive.


 The Sunday, and in fact the day before she left, our minister’s sermon called out some remarks from her that surprised me very much.


 “Why aunt,” I exclaimed, “I thought you were an Infidel!”


 “And so I am to church theology.”


 “And yet you have just affirmed your belief in the underlying principle of all church theology.”


 “How is that?” she asked.


 “You said you believe in God manifest in the flesh.”


 “I said I believed God manifest in the flesh was necessary to the salvation of the race, but I did not say I believed it had already taken place.”


 “Not taken place! do you then look for a coming Christ?”


 The old lady smiled. “Before you can understand me,” she said, “you must learn that a narrow personal application of a general principle is, must be false. The universal spirit of life can never be manifest in its fullness through, or be embodied in …

 Сегодня революционная борьба страдает от недостатка способностей на индивидуальном, организационном и социальном уровнях. Нашим крупнейшим социальным движениям, как и нашим самым страстным индивидуальным усилиям необходим милитантский импульс, способный стратегически соединять разрозненные действия. Милитантность позволяет массовым движениям испытывать обоснованную гордость и ощущать свою причастность к наиболее успешным революционным действиям. Она также даёт активному меньшинству чёткую цель и место в формировании социальной силы. Однако стойкая милитантность — это акт свободы, но сегодня большинство людей оказываются «втянуты» в неё не из сознательного выбора, а в силу обстоятельств. Мы, люди, борющиеся за социальную революцию, хотим иметь возможность самим решать, как развивать нашу милитантность. Мы требуем возможности сознательно участвовать в милитантской практике, поскольку так революционный потенциал наших движений будет обеспечен свободой людей.


 И всё же, даже при наличии свободы выбрать милитантскую деятельность остаётся вопрос:


 Куда революционерам направить свои усилия, чтобы их деятельность была связана с той реальностью, в которой в конечном счёте будет жить народ, пробуждала в людях чувство субъектности в Истории и принятие ответственности за этичность своих действий в настоящем?


 Наш ответ следует искать во взрослом образовании, которое представляет собой особенно благоприятную почву для долгосрочного участия в судьбе народных движений. Людям всегда будет необходимо учиться. Поэтому мы предлагаем создать, поддерживать и защищать революционное образовательное направление, которое станет местом встречи и обмена опытом для людей, стремящихся учиться и учить других, — в том числе членов сообщества, активистов, организаторов, диссидентов и милитантов.


 Стремление учиться, которое обычно связывают с молодёжью, новичками, студентами и теми, кому недостаёт опыта, не следует отвергать как стихийную форму организации. Нередко люди, «научившись», переходят к «действиям»: применяют полученные знания, но покидают пространство обучения, в котором они развивали свои способности, не заботясь о том, чтобы сохранить прочную связь с его методами и целями.


 Однако мы настаиваем на том, что это пространство нуждается в целенаправленной защите, если оно должно оказывать долговременное влияние на социальные преобразования. Прежде всего, защита этого пространства со временем будет способствовать коллективному становлению милитантов, которые смогут использовать общий образовательный опыт как основу для единой стратегии и политической программы. Кроме того, сохранение этого пространства будет способствовать пониманию значимости милитантов в социальной борьбе и осознанию того, насколько милитантность необходима для успеха революционных движений.


 Стремление учиться должно выполнять две функции: с одной стороны, служить пространством, где люди получают инструменты и обретают сообщество, необходимые для становления милитантами; с другой — знакомить более широкое сообщество с понятием милитантности и её теорией. Таким образом, наша цель едина, но включает два самостоятельных аспекта, которые необходимо развивать одновременно:


 Мы должны создать образовательное пространство для становления милитантов, а наше регулярное участие в его жизни должно обеспечивать надёжные пути как к милитантской деятельности, так и обратно — к образованию.


 Таким образом, стремление учиться станет пространством, где люди с большим и меньшим опытом смогут встречаться и учиться друг у друга.


 При столь ясных целях нас, несомненно, будут оценивать по нашим же критериям — приверженности делу и стойкости. Ясное определение того, что представляет собой стремление учиться, сможет воплотиться в жизнь лишь благодаря нашей приверженности ему, а его эффективность можно будет оценить лишь по тому, насколько долго оно сохраняется и насколько верно остаётся своим целям.

Es drängt uns, eine Frage von eminenter Wichtigkeit und folgenschwerer Bedeutung unter das Secirmesser der Kritik zu bringen, die Organisationsfrage nämlich. Es ist dieser Gegenstand von weit grösserer Wichtigkeit und Tragweite, als es bei einer flüchtigen Betrachtung den Schein haben mag: denn die Organisation ist das wichtigste Werkzeug des obschwebenden geistigen Riesenkampfes, und ist von grosser Wichtigkeit, ob eben dieses Instrument scharf und spitzig oder schartig und stumpf ist: die Organisation kann aber auch, wenn sie tauglich geformt wird, zur wirksamen Triebkraft, zum zweckdienlichen Sauerteige für die künftige Kulturform werden, sowie andererseits zum Geiste, der beschworen wurde und sich nicht zähmen lässt, wie der von Goethe’s Zauberlehrling.

Dem Wesen nach unterscheiden wir zwei Systeme der Organisation, und zwar den Centralismus und den Föderalismus. Beide sollen nun untersucht werden.

Was zunächst den Centralismus anbelangt, so ist derselbe nichts Anderes wie ein misslungener Abklatsch des despotischen oder absoluten Regierungssystems und zeigt uns, dass nicht allein der Affe, sondern auch der Mensch den Nachahmungstrieb besitzt.

Die Despotie zeigt uns den Centralismus in seiner vollendetsten und ausgebildetsten Form.

Caligula und Nero, Philipp der Zweite von Spanien und Richard III. von England, sowie Ludwig XI. von Frankreich: sie Alle waren Centralisten, die unser Augenmerk fesseln, denn sie waren gross, wenn auch als Tyrannen, wenn auch im Schlechten, sie ragen über die Mittelmässigkeit hoch empor: sie waren Verbrecher an der Menschenwürde, aber sie waren es voll Kraft und Mut, voll Kühnheit und Energie. Was sind aber die Tyrännchen, die sich die Arbeiter durch den Centralismus erzeugen, indem sie sich von Mauldreschern bethören lassen? Erbärmliche Jammergestalten im Vergleiche mit jenen Titanen, deren Andenken glühenden Hass in unserer Seele weckt? Sie sind armselige Zwerge, Liliputaner, und thun wohl daran, sich spreizen und viel und laut von der Redner-Tribüne herunter zu deklamiren und zu kreischen, denn sonst würde man sie gar nicht wahrnehmen. Sie zu verachten, wäre zu viel Ehre für sie, nein, ein mitleidiges Bedauern ist Alles, was ihnen zugewendet werden kann. Sie sind der Vergessenheit geweiht und haben dereinst zwecklos gelebt: das alleinige Ziel ihres Strebens ist das Wohlleben, und dafür treten sie das Heiligste, Erhabenste, die himmlische, ewige Idee in den Kot: sie unterscheiden sich in nichts von einem Mastschwein, das auf nichts denkt wie auf vielen und guten Mais und einen trefflichen Stall, nur erstreben sie beides in einer anderen Form. Ärmliche, kleinliche Menschlein! – Und sie wären vielleicht fähig, ihr ephemeres Sein an die ewige unvergängliche Kette von Ursachen und Wirkungen, Grund und Folge zu knüpfen und ewig zu sein im Erlösungswerk der Menschheit durch ihr fruchtbringendes Wirken, sie wären vielleicht befähigt zu schaffen, so dass sie darin das reinste Glück, ein Gefühl von Seligkeit empfänden im Glücke und Paradieses-Sein Aller, dass sie für künftige Generationen anzubahnen helfen würden.

Der Centralismus vernichtet die individuelle Selbstständigkeit und Freiheit vollständig, wie wir es im despotischen Staat antreffen. Hier ist der Wille des Autokraten Gesetz, dort der Wille des Parteigötzen, den man auf das Piedestal emporhob: der Druck ist ärger noch als im despotischen Staat, denn in einem solchen soll nur eine gesetzwidrige Handlung gerichtet werden; die Spitze der centralistischen Pyramide aber richtet nicht allein die Handlungen, sondern sogar die Meinungen, sie erforscht Herz und Nieren der Menschen wie Jehova, und es sollte auch der Wille solcher Parteigötzen unter Donner und Blitz zeitweilig verkündet werden, wenigstens hätte das Colophonium stärkeren Absatz und die Spängler fänden bei der Anfertigung von Donnerblechen vielleicht lohnende Arbeit.

En svensk förf. Fredrik Lindholm, har någon gång år 1909 "gjort" en skrift om anarkismen, vari han åtagit sig att framställa anarkismens uppgifter. Skriftens huvudsakliga innehåll har blivit ett upprepande av de kungamord och tsarmord, som anarkisterna anklagats för, och i vissa fall väl även utfört.

Den omfattar en period då despotismen, liksom nu i många länder, intog högsätet, då folket var helt rättslöst, då anarkisterna och andra motståndare till stats- och utsugningsmonopolen, behandlades som förbrytare och fördrevs ur landet. Ofta fanns det blott en utväg att väcka uppmärksamhet för dessa ohyggliga förhållanden: Bombens detonation.

Bomben var avsedd eller träffade en herre som i sitt dagliga liv, kanske tanklöst, undertecknat hundratals dödsdomar och förvisningar, som framställde sig vara i kompani med gud, innehade kontroll över alla kanaler till det existerande rättsväsendet, befallde över polis och militär, följaktligen utövade ensam härskarmakt eller representerande sådan makt.

Jag anser mig inte i detta sammanhang ha någon befogenhet att diskutera huruvida det var rätt eller inte. Det skulle bli en alltför vidlyftig avhandling, att framställa vad man talar för och emot i ett sammanhang som detta. Våldet har alltid karaktäriserats som ultima ratio, en sista utväg.

I anarkismens politiska och sociala tankevärld har våldet ingen plats. Såväl de politiska som sociala uttrycksformerna skapar en miljö och atmosfär, som avlägsnar ifrån våldet och främjar inbördes hjälp. Dessa förändringar bygger anarkisterna inte på en sinnets förändring som grundlag, men på fakta som att möjligheterna för det sociala välståndets fördelning uppnåtts och herraväldets och förtryckets förverkligande avlägsnats.

Den fulländning som anarkismens samhällsideal företräder bygger på orsakernas upphävande, orsakerna till våldsmentaliteten.

De invändningar som göras, bygga på helt andra förutsättningar. Den ägande som fruktar för att tjuvar och rånare skola tillägna sig hans egendom, vinkar indignerat bort pratet om att våldet skulle bli överflödigt, noggrant förbiseende att människorna under kommunistiskt-anarkistiska samhällsformer inte ha någon anledning att stjäla eller med våld försvara sig mot stöld.

Militären, som tränat in sin yrkesmentalitet och den fanatiske chauvinisten komma med sina argument! Skola vi inte försvara oss mot utländska fiender?

Här är en fråga som redan nuet borde taga klar ställning till. Finns det någon mening i att försvara sig mot utländska fiender? Vad är det man kan och vill försvara? Marken, naturen, sjöarna, kan inte försvaras, kan inte erövras. Under ett krig kan man däremot förstöra dem. Ja, måste förstöra. Fransmän och belgare förstörde stora delar av sina egna områden, direkt, när tyskarna trängde fram under världskriget, förstörde för att inte tyskarna skulle få nytta av det. Franska och belgiska sprängämnen och volymkulor träffade fransk och belgisk natur - och förstörde kanske lika mycket som "fienden", tyskarna, förstörde.

Krigets mekanisering är ett kapitel som vilar tungt på vågen när det gäller att mäta våldets uppgift i nuet. Förr, när en hord människor dreva mot varandra med pikar och muskedunder, var det hela ett farligt äventyr, som begränsades av vapnens räckvidd. Nu finnes det inte längre någon sådan begränsning. Brand-, gift- och spränggaser ha förverkat varje tanke på "försvar" och mobiliserat angreppstanken som enda möjlighet i en våldskonflikt mellan staterna. De långskjutande kanonerna understryka denna utveckling. Ett krig blir blott ett fruktansvärt förgörande av allt levande.

Enda synpunkten som talar för att med krigets våld lösa de mellanfolkliga konflikterna, är den, att vapenfabrikerna och sprängämnestillverkarna behöva experimentera och måste ha stora dividender.

author: John Lost
title: Anarcho-communist politics of autonomy
content:
Selection from Eibisch, Jonathan (2024): Politische Theorie des Anarchismus, transcript Verlag: Bielefeld, S. 187-208. (open access: https://www.transcript-verlag.de/978-3-8376-7183-4) machined translated text from German to American English.

Anarchist communism was developed as a departure from and further development of mutualist and collectivist approaches, which were criticized, on the one hand, for being too reformist and, on the other hand, for failing to resolve fundamental problems of the state-capitalist social order. This concerned, above all, debates regarding the remuneration of labor and the handling of property relations. Communist anarchists advocate for the decoupling of labor and remuneration, as well as the abolition of private ownership of the means of production and the socialization of wealth. They can be considered radical insofar as they aim to transform social relations as a whole (Turcado 2019: 237f.). Furthermore, they replaced earlier anarchist references to “the people” as a subject with a broad concept of class. In contrast to other communists, they emphasized that the goal of an anarcho-communist social system is the full development of individuals, which is reflected in the debates between them and individualist anarchists (→ 4). Davide Turcado traces the origins of anarchist communism to the year 1876, based on Malatesta and Cafiero’s critique of collectivism (ibid. : 238), although James Guillaume also played a significant role (Cahm 1989: 36 –43). This approach places particular emphasis on education and propaganda, since the development of class consciousness is regarded as an essential prerequisite for the emancipatory orientation of social-revolutionary processes, while avant-garde claims are rejected with reference to the self-organization of the proletarianized classes. As the best-known theorist of anarchist communism, Kropotkin emphasized that desirable communist and anarchist conditions can exist in parallel with the existing capitalist and state-based systems of domination (→ Fig. 4). Thus—in contrast to Marxism—capitalism would by no means be a precondition for socialism, and a state-led introduction of socialism would not only be impossible but would also undermine itself. Furthermore, communism cannot be implemented against the will of the people; rather, it must be realized by the people themselves. The focal point of anarchist-communist aspirations is the vision of a federation of decentralized, autonomous communes.[1] Wilhelm Weitling can be considered a pioneer of anarchist communism. In his 1838–39 work *Guarantees of Harmony and Freedom* (Weitling 1974), he develops “ideas for the reorganization of society.” This theoretical framework bridges the gap between the earlier early-socialist concepts of Charles Fourier, Robert Owen, and Henri de Saint-Simon and modern communist understandings of social transformation and organization. Weitling oscillates between a messianic hope for redemption (ibid., 256f.) and the notion of continuous historical progress (ibid., 7), as well as between, on the one hand, a reluctance to establish fixed plans and programs for the desired social order and, on the other hand, a desire to formulate precisely such proposals in detail. These are ambivalences which anarcho-communism also seeks to convey. With regard to the pursuit of autonomy, the three-step process—the dismantling of state-mediated relations, the establishment of social-revolutionary class power, and finally the self-organization of a libertarian-socialist society—is carried out. The selection of texts refers to Kropotkin (1892/1973) , Malatesta (1892–1932/2014), and Most (1884/2006A, 1899–1905/2006B) with regard to classical anarchism, and is continued with Bookchin (1982, 1990), Graeber (2004, 2007, 2009, 2011, 2012, 2014) and Milstein (2013) with regard to contemporary anarchist thinkers.[2]

3.3.1 Abolition of State-Mediated Relations

In the essay *The Conquest of Bread*, the foundations of anarchist communism are clearly outlined. Kropotkin’s aim is to provide a rational analysis of society, from which he sketchily derives the programmatic foundations of a libertarian-socialist form of society. ¿QUÉ es el patriotismo? ¿Es el amor por el lugar donde uno nació, el lugar de los recuerdos y las esperanzas de la infancia, de los sueños y las aspiraciones? ¿Es el lugar donde, con ingenuidad infantil, contemplábamos las nubes fugaces y nos preguntábamos por qué nosotros tampoco podíamos correr tan rápido? ¿El lugar donde contábamos los miles de millones de estrellas centelleantes, aterrorizados ante la idea de que cada una de ellas fuera «un ojo» que traspasara lo más profundo de nuestras pequeñas almas? ¿Es el lugar donde escuchábamos el canto de los pájaros y anhelábamos tener alas para volar, como ellos, hacia tierras lejanas? ¿O el lugar donde nos sentábamos a los pies de nuestra madre, embelesados por maravillosos relatos de grandes hazañas y conquistas? En resumen, ¿es el amor por ese lugar, donde cada pulgada representa recuerdos queridos y preciosos de una infancia feliz, alegre y juguetona?

Si eso fuera patriotismo, pocos hombres estadounidenses de hoy en día podrían considerarse patriotas, ya que el lugar de juego se ha convertido en fábrica, molino y mina, mientras que los sonidos ensordecedores de la maquinaria han sustituido a la música de los pájaros. Tampoco podemos ya escuchar las historias de grandes hazañas, pues las que cuentan hoy nuestras madres no son más que historias de dolor, lágrimas y aflicción.

¿Qué es, entonces, el patriotismo? «El patriotismo, señor, es el último recurso de los sinvergüenzas», dijo el Dr. Johnson. León Tolstói, el mayor antipatriota de nuestro tiempo, define el patriotismo como el principio que justifica la formación de asesinos en masa; un oficio que requiere mejor equipamiento para el ejercicio del asesinato que para la fabricación de artículos de primera necesidad como zapatos, ropa y viviendas; un oficio que garantiza mejores beneficios y mayor gloria que el del trabajador medio.

Gustave Hervé [1], otro gran antipatriota, califica acertadamente el patriotismo de superstición —una mucho más perjudicial, brutal e inhumana que la religión—. La superstición de la religión tuvo su origen en la incapacidad del hombre para explicar los fenómenos naturales. Es decir, cuando el hombre primitivo oía un trueno o veía un relámpago, no podía dar una explicación a ninguno de ellos y, por lo tanto, concluía que detrás de ellos debía de haber una fuerza mayor que él mismo. Del mismo modo, veía una fuerza sobrenatural en la lluvia y en los diversos cambios que se producen en la naturaleza. El patriotismo, por el contrario, es una superstición creada artificialmente y mantenida a través de una red de mentiras y falsedades; una superstición que despoja al hombre de su autoestima y dignidad, y aumenta su arrogancia y vanidad.

De hecho, la vanidad, la arrogancia y el egoísmo son los elementos esenciales del patriotismo. Permítanme ilustrarlo. El patriotismo parte de la base de que nuestro planeta está dividido en pequeños rincones, cada uno rodeado por una verja de hierro. Quienes han tenido la suerte de nacer en un rincón concreto se consideran mejores, más nobles, más grandiosos y más inteligentes que los seres vivos que habitan en cualquier otro rincón. Por lo tanto, es deber de todo aquel que vive en ese rincón elegido luchar, matar y morir en el intento de imponer su superioridad sobre todos los demás.

НАКОНЕЦ-ТО!

Что такое "диктатура пролетариата"


 Наконец-то появился тот, кто говорит ясно!


 До сих пор, когда мы говорили, что то, что социалисты называют

диктатурой пролетариата

, на самом деле есть не что иное, как диктатура некоторых людей, которые с поддержкой партии становятся над пролетариатом и навязывают себя ему, нас за это называли чуть ли не клеветниками.


 Вопреки всякой вероятности и всем установленным фактам утверждалось, что в России разрешена та квадратура круга, которой было бы правительство, действительно представляющее интересы и волю управляемых.


 Соответственно, Москва стала Меккой пролетариата: оттуда исходил свет, а вместе со светом – и категорические приказы относительно идей, которых должны придерживаться, и линии поведения, которой должны держаться те, кто с разрешения вышестоящих хотел называть себя коммунистами.


 Вследствие этого изумительного открытия, сделанного в России, – правительства, созданного по образу народа и для блага народа (или пролетариата, как угодно называть), – всё, что приходило из России, казалось обладающим чудотворной силой; и достаточно было назвать по-русски

советом

 любое собрание или комитет, чтобы он был возведён в верховный фактор революции.


 Но вот очарование разрушено.


 На этот раз не мы раскрываем секрет: мы, анархисты, злоязычные и непочтительные по убеждению. На этот раз это официальная газета Итальянской социалистической партии, до сих пор наиболее авторитетный орган московского слова.


 Это

Avanti!

 от 20-го числа текущего месяца, которая говорит:


 «....

В России при советском режиме Партия действительно направляет всю политику Государства, и вся общественная деятельность как отдельных лиц, так и коллективов подчинена решениям Партии, так что

 В САМОМ ДЕЛЕ ДИКТАТУРА ПРОЛЕТАРИАТА ЕСТЬ ДИКТАТУРА ПАРТИИ И, СЛЕДОВАТЕЛЬНО, САМОГО ЦЕНТРАЛЬНОГО КОМИТЕТА».


 Итак, теперь мы знаем, чего нам следует ожидать: диктатуры Руководящего органа Социалистической партии, или диктатуры нарождающейся Коммунистической партии, или даже диктатуры Д'Арагона и компании!


 Но руководители Социалистической партии, претендующие ввести Диктатуру, должны понять, что это, по крайней мере в Италии, невозможно: невозможно, потому что есть мы, анархисты и синдикалисты.


 Если бы мы находились в том же соотношении сил с социалистами, в каком, возможно, оказались наши товарищи в России, дело было бы простым: диктаторы избавились бы от нас средствами, дорогими всем диктатурам, – виселицами и тюрьмами, – и шли бы вперёд, пока не были бы свергнуты революцией или реакцией.


 Но мы уже сила, с которой необходимо считаться, и мы быстро развиваемся, чему благоприятствуют обстоятельства и то, что

Avanti!

 называет

необузданным темпераментом трудящихся масс

. И мы твёрдо решили не подчиняться.


 Не то чтобы мы верили, что массы всегда правы и что мы хотим всегда следовать за массами в их изменчивых настроениях. У нас есть программа, идеал, который мы хотим привести к победе, и поэтому мы отличаемся от массы, – мы люди определенного направления. Мы хотим воздействовать на массу, подталкивать её по пути, который считаем лучшим; но поскольку наша цель – освобождение, а не господство, мы хотим приучать массы к свободной инициативе и свободному действию.


 Мы верим, что свобода учит свободе и солидарности, и поэтому питаем отвращение к любому авторитарному устройству – как в обществе в целом, так и в любой отдельной партии или объединении.


 Социалисты хотели бы подготовить народ к свободе посредством власти.


 Но если бы, по предположению, которое мы отвергаем, было верно, что для торжества революции и устройства нового общества необходимо сосредоточить в немногих руках государственную власть, если бы было верно, что кто-то обязательно должен командовать, – тогда, пусть социалисты хорошенько поймут, – командовать хотели бы мы и не подчинились бы, разве что силой, командованию того, кто, по нашему мнению, заблуждается.


 Следствием чего было бы то, что революция, совершённая по авторитарным меркам и с диктаторскими целями, неизбежно привела бы в Италии к войне между одними революционерами и другими.


 Этого не хотели бы мы; этого не должны хотеть социалисты.


 Поэтому, оставив в стороне теории и судя о вещах реалистично, социалистам следовало бы отказаться от всяких диктаторских притязаний и принять либертарную …

title: Antimilitarismus und Revolution
content:

Mehr Kontakt Material Sticker, Plakate, etc.

In einem Briefe an „Les Temps Nouveaux“ (seinerzeit als „Le Revolté“ von Kropotkin und seinen Freunden gegründet) und in einem zweiten an den bürgerlichen „Temps“, der aber nicht veröffentlicht wurde, nimmt Peter Kropotkin Stellung zur antimilitaristischen Propaganda. Es handelt sich in erster Linie um die Frage, wie sich die Revolutionäre im Falle eines Krieges zu verhalten hätten, und hier nimmt Kropotkin eine gerade entgegengesetzte Stellung zu der antimilitaristischen Richtung, die in letzter Zeit in dem Professor Hèrvé einen energischen Vertreter gefunden. Während diese Letztere für die vollständige Unterdrückung des Militarismus eintritt und selbst im Falle eines „Verteidigungskrieges“ mit dem Streike der Militärpflichtigen antworten will, tritt Ersterer für eine bedingte Beibehaltung des Militärs ein, welches Frankreich, das daran ist, die Grundlagen seiner Gesellschaftsform zu ändern, gegen Angriffe von reaktionären Feinden, unter welchen er hauptsächlich die Deutschen versteht, zu schützen hätte.

Nach unserer Ansicht beruhen die Schlüsse, welche Kropotkin zieht, auf einer allzustarken Unterschätzung der Deutschen, was man ihm aber wahrlich nicht übel nehmen kann; waren es doch die „Germanen“, welche stets wie ein Bleigewicht auf den Gang der internationalen Arbeiterbewegung wirkten. Ganz so pessimistisch denken wir jedoch nicht, vielleicht eben weil wir „Deutsche“ sind, sonst hätten wir es schon längst aufgegeben, unter einer solchen elenden Schafherde Propaganda zu machen.

Nun ist zu sagen, dass, seitdem Russland aufgehört hat, eine stete Bedrohung der freiheitlichen Bewegung in Westeuropa zu sein – was man heute schon mit Bestimmtheit sagen kann – ist es auch Deutschland nicht mehr in dem Masse, weil es an „Rückgrat“ verloren hat. Es wird bald damit genug zu tun haben, die „eigenen Völker“, namentlich die Polen in der Zucht zu halten, dass es sich nicht mehr erlauben kann, ein grosses Volk, das sich zudem noch im Befreiungskampfe befindet, zu unterjochen.

An die Ausführungen von Kropotkin knüpfen sich eine Reihe von Auseinandersetzungen, und es ist auch für uns Schweizer nicht unnützlich, der Sache näher zu treten und sich darüber gründlich auszusprechen, weil es das beste Argument der Bourgeoisie und Sozialdemokraten gegen die antimilitaristische Propaganda ist, dass wir „Freiheiten“ gegen lüsterne Räuber zu verteidigen hätten.

Nachbringend bringen wir die charakteristischsten Ausführungen Kropotkins zum Abdruck, und in Fortsetzung eine Entgegnung von Charles Albert auf dieselben, ebenfalls in „Les Temps Nouveaux“ veröffentlicht.

Dies schreibt unser Peter Kropotkin in einem Briefe an „Les Temps Nouveaux“:

„Wenn Frankreich durch einige Militärmächte überfallen wird, so ist die Pflicht der Revolutionäre nicht, die Arme zu kreuzen und dem eindringenden Feinde freies Spiel zu lassen. Sie ist: die Revolution anzufangen und das Territorium der Revolution zu verteidigen, um sie fortzusetzen.

Die Formel „Streik der Conscrits“ (der militärpflichtigen jungen Leute, D. Ueb.) sagt nicht genug. Sie hat die Unannehmlichkeit, sich auszuschweigen über den eigentlichen Zweck der Propaganda, und gibt Anlass zu falschen Deutungen desselben. Sie sagt nichts von der Revolution und sagt nichts von der Notwendigkeit, in welche die Revolutionäre versetzt werden, diese, jeden Zoll französischer Erde, der sich in Revolution befindet, mit den Waffen in den Händen zu verteidigen gegen die bürgerlichen und kaiserlichen Horden deutscher, englischer oder vielleicht russischer Räuber.“

Und weiter in seinem Briefe an den „Temps“: „Aber wenn die Deutschen Frankreich überfallen, an der Spitze – wie sie es ohne Zweifel machen werden – einer mächtigen Koalition, und die Hände der kleinen Grenzstaaten (Belgien und Schweiz) binden, alsdann wird der Streik der Conscrits nicht genügen. Man müsste machen, was die „Sanscullotes“ im Jahre 1792 getan haben, welche in ihren Sektionen die revolutionäre Kommune vom 10. August konstituierten, das Königtum und die Aristokratie über den Haufen warfen, gewaltsam Steuern von den Reichen erhoben, die Legislative (die gesetzgebende Körperschaft der grossen Revolution) zwangen, das erste wirkliche Dekret zur Vernichtung der feudalen Rechte zu erlassen und deren Zurücknahme durch die Bauern des kommunalen Bodens, und die marschierten, um die französische Erde zu …

author: Joakim
title: Landmark Collective Agreement for Migrant Workers
content:
Article from Znetwork. More articles by the author here. Photo above: migrant workers after the agreement was signed. Photographer: Valeriia Eltarenko.

Workers at the construction of a Microsoft data center in Sweden secured a collective agreement under threat of strike action through the syndicalist union SAC.

A trade union victory at a Microsoft construction site has attracted attention from a large number of European media outlets. The workplace is situated outside the city of Gävle in Sweden.

The Guardian has published a five-month investigation into conditions for migrant workers on data center sites across Sweden, Norway, Belgium and the Netherlands. The investigation uncovers evidence of dangerous conditions and unpaid wages, including at the Microsoft site outside Gävle.

“Days before publication of this investigation, the syndicalist union, representing 70 Romanian workers at Microsoft’s site in Gävle, brokered a settlement with BenBau, which it says will give workers back pay and allow unions access to sites,” reports the Guardian. The back pay amounts to 15 million Swedish kronor (roughly 1, 5 million US dollars).

On October 25, this group of workers voted unanimously for a collective agreement with BenBau AB, one of the companies building Microsoft’s server halls, reports the Swedish newspaper Arbetaren. The deal raises wages to 260 kronor an hour (26,46 US dollars), includes a time bank for longer leave periods in the workers’ home countries, and allows the workers to elect health-and-safety delegates from their own ranks.

The agreement opens with the statement: “This collective agreement is the first Swedish collective agreement written by and for migrant workers.” Since the deal was struck, even more workers have joined the union at the construction site.

This outcome is the latest result of the syndicalist union’s years of organizing among migrant construction workers, particularly those from post-Soviet countries who use Russian as a common language. Freelance journalist Volodya Vagner has reported extensively on these efforts. “By confronting exploitative employers with aggressive litigation and long-forgotten methods of struggle, like blockading the construction sites of contractors with wage debts, the union has managed to redistribute millions of dollars in unpaid wages and damages,” writes Volodya Vagner.

The collective agreement at the Microsoft site is consistent with SAC’s new collective agreement-strategy articulated in 2020. This strategy is a response to a Swedish anti-strike law that entered into force in 2019. The strategy was presented on the Counterpunch news site: “According to our assessment syndicalists can still fight lawfully for both collective agreements and alternatives to such agreements”, SAC representatives stated.

Yet collective agreements are nothing new for Swedish syndicalists. During the 20th century, Swedish syndicalists entered into hundreds of collective agreements.

SAC was founded in 1910. Fittingly, the vote on the 2026 collective agreement took place in the childhood home of the legendary Joe Hill.

This rewrite was made by Rasmus Hästbacka, labor lawyer and member of SAC
