author: Dennis Ward
title: SCO grand chief given a ‘reprieve’ from a vote that could have ousted him
content:
The grand chief of an organization that represents 33 Anishinaabe and Dakota Nations in southern Manitoba will carry on in his leadership role until at least June 2027.

This past summer, a former ally of Jerry Daniels brought forward a motion seeking a vote to remove him as leader of the Southern Chiefs Organization (SCO).

“Chiefs have raised numerous concerns regarding governance, leadership, accountability, transparency, organization decision-making and the confidence of member Nations in the current leadership of the Organization,” said a resolution at the time tabled by Lake Manitoba Chief Cornell McLean.

A response, at the time, attributed to the SCO Chiefs Executive Committee, cited the financial cost of a summit, among other reasons, and called for the motion to be brought forward at an ordinary summit

That meeting, SCO’s Chiefs-in-Summit gathering, got underway on Wednesday in Brokenhead Ojibway Nation, where a vote on Daniels’ leadership was expected.

According to an SCO spokesperson, “the Chiefs withdrew the proposed non-confidence motion at today’s SCO Chiefs-in-Summit, and no vote was held.”

McLean told APTN News that “it wasn’t a win for him, it’s more like a reprieve. We decided to wait until his term is over in June.”

Daniels has previously faced two non-confidence votes.

Those came shortly after a fight involving the grand chief outside of a bar in Ottawa in December 2024, on the eve of an Assembly of First Nations gathering.

The SCO Chiefs-in-Summit is closed to the media.

Dennis is Métis from southern Manitoba. After spending a decade working in TV in Alberta and Ontario, Dennis returned to Manitoba to join APTN. In 2016, he won a Canadian Association of Journalists award for his story A Soldier Scorned for APTN Investigates. In 2017, he became a host/producer for APTN National News and Face to Face.

author: LCM-Redaktion
title: The Kids Are All Riot – Gen Z gegen Zeitenwende und Staatsräson
content:
Nachdem die Social Media-Algorithmen wochenlang voll waren von einem Mix aus aufständisch-revolutionär wirkenden Szenen und TikTok-Tänze tanzenden Teenagern vor überforderten Bullen aus Frankreich, Albanien und Co., war es am Samstag endlich so weit: Nachdem zunächst anonyme KI-generierte Aufrufe online den 31. Oktober als Stichtag dafür ausgerufen hatten, den Funken der Revolte endlich auch nach Deutschland überspringen zu lassen, wurden in über 30 Städten Demonstrationen organisiert. Mit Blick auf die Entwicklungen im Ausland wurde dieser Tag von verschiedenen Seiten mit großer Anspannung erwartet. Während die revolutionäre Linke zu großen Teilen damit zu rechnen schien, dass die online entfachte Stimmung auch eher online bleiben würde, warnten Politik und Presse davor, dass der Untergang unserer zivilisierten Ordnung an diesem Halloween eingeleitet werden würde und in den Klassenräumen deutscher Großstädte wurde darüber diskutiert, was man sich zuerst aus den Media-Markt Regalen holen würde, wenn „die Revolution losgeht“.


So ganz scheint sich keine dieser Prognosen bewahrheitet zu haben. Tatsächlich ist es nicht übertrieben davon zu sprechen, dass die „Gen Z regelt“ Proteste die größten organischen Jugenddemonstrationen seit Fridays for Future auf die Straße gebracht haben und der Auftakt für eine relevante neue Bewegung mit wesentlich größerer Bedeutung werden könnten. Und auch wenn nun mit aller Macht versucht wird, die Bilder aus Frankfurt, Hamburg und Köln heranzuziehen, um zu beweisen, dass die vorangegangene Panikmache völlig berechtigt gewesen sei, blieben die völlig unangetasteten Spanholzfassaden, die auf einmal in großen und kleinen Städten überall auftauchten und kleinlaut wieder abgenommen wurden, um den alltäglichen Konsum am Montag wieder freien Lauf zu lassen, mehr Grund für Belustigung im Netz und bei vorbeigehenden Passanten als nötige Schutzmaßnahmen gegen den revolutionären Mob.


Panikmache oder reale Angst?


Doch die Angst, die im Vorhinein angeheizt wurde, ist echt. Es ist nicht die Angst einer Bevölkerung, die um die eigene Sicherheit und Innenstädte bangen muss, auch wenn mit aller Macht versucht wird, das zu behaupten. Es ist die reale Angst einer herrschenden Klasse davor, dass sich tatsächlich eine Stimmung in der deutschen Jugend breitmacht, die sich gegen die Verhältnisse richtet, in denen sie in zunehmend kaputt gesparten Schulen darauf vorbereitet wird, Nachwuchs für die Klasse zu sein, aus der jetzt auch noch der letzte Tropfen Lebens(=Arbeits)kraft ausgepresst wird, um den Krieg zu finanzieren, in dem sie außerdem als Kanonenfutter verheizt werden soll. Denn mit einer solchen Jugend wären Deutschlands aktuellen imperialistischen Bestrebungen tatsächlich nur schwer zu machen. Dementsprechend ist nicht nur die Angst der Herrschenden sehr real, sondern auch ihr Wille, eine solche Bewegung gegen ihre Politik zu verhindern.


Auch die Repression steht erst am Anfang


Diesen Willen bewiesen sämtliche großen Medienhäuser bereits im Vorfeld des Aktionstags, die die Proteste so schnell wie möglich gesellschaftlich zu delegitimieren versuchten. Das massive und aggressiv auftretende Polizeiaufgebot ist ein weiterer Beleg dafür, wie ernst es dem deutschen Staat mit seinem Willen ist, eine echte neue Jugendbewegung nicht aufkommen zu lassen. Bei aller Freude darüber, wie stark sich der Widerwille gegen die Politik dieses Staates am Samstag gezeigt hat, dürfen wir nicht darüber hinwegsehen, dass die Reaktion der herrschenden Klasse noch deutlich stärker werden wird. Historisch waren erstarkende und in Teilen militante Widerstandsbewegungen immer auch Grund für eine eskalierende Reaktion. Das ist kein Argument, als Bewegung die Spaltung, die durch die mediale Hetze erzeugt werden soll, zuzulassen, aber wir müssen ehrlich einschätzen, wie bereit wir dafür sind, die sich zuspitzende Dynamik von wachsender Repression und sich radikalisierenden Protest auszutragen. Andernfalls droht eine weitere Verschärfung des deutschen Repressionsapparats, ohne dass wir als Bewegung unseren Zielen wirklich näherkommen.


Es wäre ein Fehler, zu unterschätzen, wie wirksam die BRD bereits darin ist, radikalen Protest zu unterdrücken. Dass für eine Eskalation oft juristische Konsequenzen drohen, die das gesamte weitere Leben einschränken und nicht nur primär körperliche Gewalt durch die Cops, führt bereits jetzt dazu, dass solche Eskalationen vor allem von denjenigen Jugendlichen ausgehen, die diese Konsequenzen …

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Angie Nixon Hints at Another Senate Run in 2028, After Being Heavily Outspent
content:
Nixon, Democrats’ candidate for US Senate in Florida, didn’t receive any funding from the party’s Senate PACs.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Democratic candidate Angie Nixon has suggested she could run again in 2028 after being narrowly defeated in her race for U.S. Senate in Florida on Tuesday, falling to Republican opponent Ashley Moody by roughly 3 points after being massively outspent in the race written off by the Democratic establishment.

Moody received 50.9 percent of the vote to Nixon’s 48 percent, still overcoming a 10-point swing toward Democrats compared to 2024. Nixon got roughly the same proportion of the vote as Florida governor candidate David Jolly, a former Republican member of the House who left that party in 2018 and registered as a Democrat last year.

The race was a special election to fill the Senate seat left vacant by Marco Rubio, who won the seat in 2022 but left to become Secretary of State. Moody was chosen by Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis as a temporary replacement, and has now been officially elected to serve the rest of the term.

This means that the seat will be up for grabs again in 2028 — and Nixon, who has already defied the odds in her race, has left the door open for another run.

In her concession speech on Tuesday, Nixon struck a positive tone despite the loss, touting the movement built by her campaign. “When we started this campaign, people told us it could not be done,” she said. “They told us we couldn’t compete with the political establishment.”

“I need y’all to stay in this fight. The war is not over. 2028 is around the corner. So Ashley Moody, you better get it right. Cause we’re coming for you,” Nixon said. Let’s go win y’all.”

Indeed, it is extraordinary that a member of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) could come so close to a win in the red state. Though Nixon has rejected the socialist label, the DSA has been relentlessly vilified by conservatives and liberals alike, and Nixon has embraced left-wing stances like rejecting assistance to Israel and supporting Medicare for All.

Nixon’s primary race was already historic. She won despite being outspent by roughly 13 to 1, and raised just under $1 million compared to $16 million raised by opponent Alex Vindman, a former national security official in Donald Trump’s first administration.

The Democratic establishment, however, seemingly wrote off her race — or potentially actively opposed her bid. Neither the Senate Majority PAC nor the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC) spent any money supporting Nixon’s race, The American Prospect points out.

According to AdImpact data, Republicans spent $28.7 million on TV ads supporting Moody, while Democrats only spent $7.9 million. Nixon’s campaign says that support and fundraising from Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vermont) was an enormous help.

“Bernie’s impact on our campaign was immeasurable. He was one of our most important partners, by far,” said Kevin Lata, Nixon’s deputy campaign manager, on X on Tuesday evening. “I can almost guarantee that the democrats who are blaming Bernie did very little themselves to help, and should instead be looking inward, not at him.”

Some politicians chalked the lack of support from the main arms of the Democratic Party as racism as well as pro-centrist bias. Last month, Rep. Ayanna Pressley (D-Massachusetts) called out the DSCC for this disparity.

“It is shameful that we are not seeing an equitable investment in progressive and diverse candidates like Abdul El-Sayed, like Angie Nixon, like Scott Colom,” said Pressley. Nixon and Colom, whose Senate race in Mississippi is too close to call as of Wednesday afternoon, are Black, while progressive Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed is Arab American.

“They have earned and need the investment so that we can have a majority,” Pressley said, as Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-New York) nodded beside her.

Nixon added on Wednesday, after sweeping Democratic wins even across traditionally red states in the South, that Democrats must not write off the region.

“Invest In The South,” Nixon wrote.

author: Maria Martha Bruno
title: Derrota dos Republicanos nos EUA tem mais a ver com economia que democracia, diz socióloga
content:
Com a vitória avassaladora do Partido Democrata nas eleições de meio de mandato dos Estados Unidos (as chamadas

midterms

), o “recado das urnas”, na opinião da socióloga e cientista política Gisele Agnelli, foi a economia.

A promessa central que elegeu Donald Trump em 2024 — a

affordability

, ou recuperação do poder de compra — “não se materializou na percepção de grande parte dos eleitores”.


Membro do Hoosier Women Forward, um dos movimentos de lideranças femininas do Partido Democrata, ela afirma que o resultado não aponta para um alinhamento da população com o partido. Para Agnelli, os eleitores reprovaram o mandato do presidente republicano e cobraram o não cumprimento da principal promessa de campanha, a redução do custo de vida das famílias norte-americanas.


Por isso, antes de apontar semelhanças entre a vitória de Lula e a derrota de Trump, ela ressalta que os motivos que moveram os eleitores em ambos os países foram distintos, embora a ameaça antidemocrática estivesse em jogo nos dois pleitos:

“Não acredito que a defesa da democracia tenha sido o fator decisivo das

midterms

“.


No futuro, ela vislumbra oportunidades para o Brasil e um cenário exige “reflexão estratégica do governo Lula e, particularmente, do PT”. Com os canais diplomáticos oficiais quase monopolizados pelo bolsonarismo instalado nos EUA, ela aponta a chance do governo estabelecer contato com o próprio Congresso norte-americano, agora com maioria democrata no Senado e na Câmara dos Representantes (equivalente à nossa Câmara dos Deputados).


“A esquerda brasileira precisa distinguir a crítica histórica ao intervencionismo dos EUA da capacidade de construir alianças institucionais dentro da própria democracia americana”, analisa.


E antes de que muitos se empolguem com os resultados, Agnelli destaca que as dificuldades para Trump não necessariamente se traduzirão no desmonte da poderosa estrutura administrativa e política montada por ele. Gisela também não acredita “que veremos menos agressividade” por parte do presidente. “Um presidente com menos espaço no Legislativo pode recorrer ainda mais aos instrumentos unilaterais no Executivo”, aponta.


Qual sua avaliação geral sobre as

midterms

?


O grande derrotado foi Trump, mas não necessariamente o vencedor foi o Partido Democrata. O presidente acabou se tornando o principal alvo do descontentamento expresso nas urnas.


As eleições confirmaram, de forma contundente, uma máxima clássica da ciência política: as

midterms

 funcionam como um referendo sobre a popularidade presidencial, a percepção do desempenho econômico e o desejo do eleitorado de contrabalançar o poder do partido que ocupa a Casa Branca.


Embora Trump também tenha se consolidado como um fator de desestabilização institucional,

o recado mais significativo das urnas foi econômico.

 A promessa central de sua campanha de 2024 — a

affordability

, ou recuperação do poder de compra das famílias americanas — não se materializou para grande parte dos eleitores.


Os democratas exploraram essa frustração com uma campanha essencialmente pragmática, concentrada no custo da alimentação, da moradia, dos combustíveis e dos serviços de saúde.

Em vez de restringir a disputa à defesa abstrata da democracia ou à condenação moral do trumpismo, conseguiram traduzir o descontentamento em questões concretas do cotidiano.


A contradição entre promessa e governo foi agravada pelas próprias escolhas da administração Trump. A guerra contra o Irã, com seus efeitos sobre os preços da energia, e a política tarifária, que pressionou custos, contribuíram para alimentar a percepção de perda de poder aquisitivo.


Há também uma contradição política fundamental: Trump foi eleito prometendo “America First”, a priorização dos interesses domésticos e o fim do envolvimento americano em guerras externas custosas. No entanto,

seu governo dedicou enorme energia política e recursos à agenda internacional, em detrimento das promessas econômicas para o eleitor americano.

 Essa ruptura desgastou sua popularidade e também aprofundou divisões dentro do próprio campo republicano.


Que aspecto da eleição mais chamou sua atenção?


O primeiro é o

limite do redistritamento eleitoral

 como instrumento de preservação do poder. Mesmo diante de mapas distritais redesenhados para favorecer candidaturas republicanas, em alguns casos com consequências especialmente negativas para a representação de minorias,

a insatisfação do eleitorado mostrou capacidade …

author: Chris Walker
title: Democrats Finally Have the Votes to Make the Electoral College Obsolete
content:
“Blue wave” wins have produced enough Democratic state governments to pass the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Several statewide and state legislative contests in this week’s midterm elections have resulted in new Democratic Party “trifecta” governments — places where the party is now in control of both houses of the state legislature as well as the governor’s office.

With these new wins, Democrats have the opportunity to do something once considered nearly impossible: implement a popular vote model for electing future presidents of the United States, to replace the archaic and unpopular Electoral College.

Due to the mechanics of the Electoral College, five presidential “winners” in U.S. history have taken office who did not win the approval of most voters, including twice over the past three decades. While a constitutional amendment would be needed to formally abolish the Electoral College — which is unlikely to happen anytime soon, even after this week’s “blue wave” — there is a workaround called the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact, which doesn’t require such an amendment.

Per Article II of the U.S. Constitution, each state is mandated to appoint, “in such manner as the Legislature thereof may direct, a number of electors, equal to the whole number of Senators and Representatives to which the State may be entitled in the Congress.” These electors end up voting for president and vice president.

All states today direct their electors to vote based on their own results in presidential races. If a Democratic candidate wins in California, for example, all 54 of its electors are people chosen to support that candidate in the Electoral College.

But under the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact, that would change. States that have agreed to abide by the compact would direct their electors to support the candidate who won the national popular vote, not who their state alone voted for. For example, if a Republican candidate won the national popular vote but California voters preferred the Democrat, the state’s electors would be directed to the Republican under the compact.

Such a move would not be unconstitutional, as it complies with the Article II rule that allows states to determine for themselves how to distribute electors.

The compact doesn’t come into play until it is joined by enough states, totaling a majority of all Electoral College votes (at this time, 270 votes of the 538). Currently, only 18 states plus Washington, D.C. have signed on to the compact, totaling 222 Electoral College votes, which means the old, undemocratic system of selecting the president remains in place for now.

Before Tuesday’s elections, multiple paths were under consideration for attaining the remaining 48 electoral votes needed. However, the midterm results have produced one such path.

Democrats have won new trifecta governments in Wisconsin, Michigan, Nevada, and Pennsylvania. Democrats in Arizona are also claiming to have won a trifecta. In total, those five states, which have not yet passed the compact, make up 61 electoral votes. Even without Arizona, the 50 electoral votes the other four states have are more than enough to implement the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact.

The question is no longer if Democrats can pass a popular vote model for president, but whether they have the will or determination to do so. If those states opt to join the compact, it could go into effect as soon as the 2028 presidential election.

Notably, an Economist/YouGov poll this past summer found that 56 percent of Americans would approve of a Constitutional amendment to implement a popular vote model in presidential elections, rather than the Electoral College. Only 23 percent opposed the idea, while 21 percent were unsure.

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. As Trump attempts to silence dissenting voices, we have no choice but to ask for your help.

We are fundraising today to fund our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference — we appreciate your support.

author: Lilli Akpaleeapik
title: Tuberculosis documentary shows healing through sharing stories
content:
Iqaluit’s Astro Theatre was filled with people Tuesday evening for the première of a documentary that follows a group of tuberculosis survivors and youth as they find closure over their forced relocations decades ago.


Between the 1940s-1960s, the federal government transported thousands of Inuit to southern sanatoriums for tuberculosis treatment without their consent or without informing them about what was happening.


Many Inuit never returned home.


Taqqut Productions joined hands with The SeeChange Initiative to create

Our Elders are so Important to Us: A Tuberculosis Sanatorium Healing Journey

, a 29-minute documentary that follows youth and survivors as they connect over these relocations, in an effort to provide healing and closure.


“If we value our elders as much as we say we do as Inuit, why not listen to their stories,” asked Naomi Tatty, the intercultural health lead at SeeChange, a non-profit and one of the leads for the documentary.


“Why not put their words out there and help us younger generations, and the generations ahead of us, understand what our families went through?”


She was on site for the screening and to help facilitate discussion afterwards, at the Storehouse.


Tuberculosis is an airborne bacterial disease characterized by a cough, weight loss, night sweats, and a fever. Without treatment, it can cause serious complications and death.


In 2025, a group of TB survivors who had been relocated while sick, alongside others who were affected by the relocation of family members, made a journey to the former Mountain Sanatorium site in Hamilton, Ont. While there, they shared their history with youth and discussed how tuberculosis continues to affect people to this day.


Astro Theatre was filled with survivors, youth, health-care workers and community members to view the film and participate in the discussion afterward.


The idea for the healing journey was sparked by former prime minister Justin Trudeau’s 2019

apology

 over TB sanatoriums, and his subsequent announcement of the The Nanilavut Initiative, a collaborative project that helps Inuit locate family members who never came home.


Tatty told Nunatsiaq News that her mother, or anaana, Ida Atagoyuk, was a TB survivor who spent three and a half years alone in treatment. She was present when the apology was given. But she wondered, Tatty said, what else was being done for healing. The 2025 healing journey was a product of that question, and the documentary followed.


Tatty also highlighted the importance of youth for facilitating healing how important it is to share stories.


“Hopefully there’s a ripple effect of the younger generation to be able to have a mindset of understanding and to gain that knowledge and more understanding towards their upbringing and their homes,” she said to Nunatsiaq News.


Tuberculosis is still a crisis within Inuit Nunangat, and Nunavut has the highest rate of active tuberculosis of any province or territory in Canada.


So far this year, there have been 32 tuberculosis cases reported in seven communities.

author: Lisa Xu
title: Reform Candidate Says UFCW Rep Tailed Him for 300 Miles to Thwart Petition Effort
content:
In a union that has been headed by one family with no competitive elections since 1984, a group of grocery workers is organizing for change. But this week, they say, union staff who back the incumbent administration went to outrageous lengths in an attempt to make sure there’s no election this year either.


On Monday afternoon, Eric Marcuz, a veteran Northern California Safeway worker, stopped at the union office to pick up blank petitions to get on the ballot in the union’s upcoming election. Marcuz is running for president on the

At What Cost

 slate in the 23,000-member United Food and Commercial Workers (UFCW) Local 8-Golden State, one of the largest locals in the union.


To get on the ballot, Marcuz and his slate-mates have to collect 443 petition signatures—2 percent of the local’s active members—in the next two weeks. If they don’t get enough signatures, no election will be held.


After Marcuz picked up the petitions from the local’s Roseville office, he got in his car to drive three hours south to Fresno, to start collecting signatures with another candidate on his slate at a Save Mart store there. (The local spans a 10-hour stretch from Bakersfield up to the Oregon border).


When Marcuz stopped for gas, he said he noticed that a black Dodge Ram pickup stopped as well. When he got back on the freeway, so did the truck.


At the next gas stop, Marcuz spoke to the man driving the truck. It was Jeff Berns, a staff representative for Local 8-GS. His brother, Mark, is also a rep for the union—and the local’s election chair, responsible for overseeing the election.


Marcuz asked Jeff Berns why he was following him. According to Marcuz, Berns said he wanted to make sure that all the members got the “accurate information” that Marcuz’s slate was going to “divide” the union. He said he was going to follow him the entire time Marcuz was out, all the way back to Marcuz’s house in Redding, several hours north. Marcuz jokingly asked him if he needed a place to stay. Berns said he didn’t—because he’d been staying a lot in the Redding area lately himself, which Marcuz said he thought was “creepy” because that’s where Marcuz lives with his family (and is not where Berns lives).


Berns would live up to his promise—following Marcuz for the next 300 miles, through every stop, exit, and U-turn. He even followed him inside the Fresno Save Mart, and camped out for an hour with another union rep while Marcuz ate dinner at a supporter's house 100 miles north in Modesto.


NO COMPETITIVE ELECTIONS


At the gas station, Berns repeated the mantra, “Solidarity works!” That’s the motto of the incumbent president, Jacques Loveall, who is heading the

Solidarity Works Team

 slate in this election.


Loveall was appointed to lead the union in 2004, when his father, Jack Loveall, stepped down. The elder Loveall had held the top office since 1984; when he retired he was one of the highest-paid union officers in the country, earning the equivalent of $1 million today. (The

Contra Costa Times

 reported that he had a $28,000-a-year country club membership and “two pilots on staff to chauffeur him in a private jet.”) Neither father nor son has ever faced a competitive election in the local.


Back on the freeway, Marcuz called a Department of Labor agent whom he had already been in touch with. They had previously spoken about the local’s apparent attempt to

cancel the election

 by merging with a mysterious organization called the Staffing Agencies Federated Employees, an entity which listed one of Loveall’s relatives as its president on its initial filing. The agent told him to report the intimidation to the election chair and tell him to get the rep to back off.


Marcuz then called Mark Berns, the election chair, who he said told him he would talk to staff about acting in a professional manner.


MORE REPS


However, when Marcuz arrived at the Save Mart store in Fresno to begin collecting petition signatures, he and another slatemate, Mike Romero, said that three union reps were waiting for them, including Jeff Berns. One of the others was John Micheletti, a longtime Local 8 vice president. Far from being called off, they said, the intimidation had actually intensified.


Marcuz and Romero said the reps interfered with every conversation they attempted to have with workers about signing their nomination petition. The very first worker they engaged about signing, a longtime acquaintance of Romero’s, fled once a rep entered the …

author: groundxero
title: পশ্চিমবঙ্গে সংখ্যালঘুদের উপর বাড়তে থাকা আক্রমণ, এসআইআর, ডিটেনশন ক্যাম্প-এর বিরোধিতায় সাংবাদিক সম্মেলন
content:
ভোট পরবর্তী সময়ে এ রাজ্যে একের পর এক ঘটে চলা সংখ্যালঘু খ্রিষ্টান গীর্জার উপর হামলা, SIR প্রক্রিয়ায় ভোটারদের নাম বাদ দেওয়া, রাজ্যের বিভিন্ন প্রান্তে ডিটেনশন ক্যাম্প তৈরি ও বেআইনি ভাবে সাধারণ মানুষদের সেখানে আটক করার বিরূদ্ধে ৩ নভেম্বর, মঙ্গলবার কলকাতার প্রেস ক্লাবে এক সংবাদিক সম্মেলন ডাকা হয়ে।

মৈনাক দত্ত

-র প্রতিবেদন।


 


কলকাতা, ৩ নভেম্বর ২০২৬


 


নতুন সরকার পশ্চিমবঙ্গে ক্ষমতায় আসার পর কেটেছে মাত্র পাঁচ মাস। ভোট পরবর্তী সময়ে এ রাজ্যে ৪৮টি খ্রিষ্টান উপাসনালয়ে হামলা চালিয়েছে হিন্দুত্ববাদী দুষ্কৃতিরা। কিন্তু এফআইআর হয়েছে মাত্র ১৫ টি। এমনকি বহু জায়গায় পুলিশ এফ.আই.আর নিচ্ছে না। ‘কারওয়ানে মহব্বত’, ‘সবর ইনস্টিটিউট’ ও ‘আমরা এক সচেতন প্রয়াস’ নামক সংগঠনগুলির মিলিত তথ্যান্যসন্ধানে উঠে এসেছে এমনই বাস্তবচিত্র।


 


ভোট পরবর্তী সময়ে এ রাজ্যে একের পর এক ঘটে চলা সংখ্যালঘু খ্রিষ্টান গীর্জার উপর হামলা, SIR প্রক্রিয়ায় ভোটারদের নাম বাদ দেওয়া, রাজ্যের বিভিন্ন প্রান্তে ডিটেনশন ক্যাম্প তৈরি ও বেআইনি ভাবে সাধারণ মানুষদের সেখানে আটক করার বিরূদ্ধে ৩ নভেম্বর, মঙ্গলবার কলকাতার প্রেস ক্লাবে এক সংবাদিক সম্মেলনের ডাক দেয় এই সংগঠনগুলি। সংবাদিক সম্মেলনে বক্তা হিসেবে উপস্থিত ছিলেন প্রাক্তন আইএএস অফিসার জহর সরকার, প্রাক্তন আইএএস অফিসার ও সমাজকর্মী হর্ষ মন্দার, প্রাক্তন আইএএস ওয়াজাহাত হাবিবুল্লাহ, সংবাদিক আকার প্যাটেল, মানবাধিকার জন দয়াল এবং মানবাধিকার কর্মী বিদ্যা ডিঙ্কার।


 


জহর সরকার নিজের বক্তব্যে সরাসরি বলেন, “পাড়ার কিছু গুণ্ডারা পার্টির নাম ব্যবহার না করে ‘বিশ্ব হিন্দু পরিষদ’, ‘হিন্দু জাগরণ মঞ্চ’ এসব সংগঠনগুলোর নাম করে একের পর এক হামলা চালাচ্ছে। চারিদিকে যেন একটা কম্পিটিটিভ কমিউনালিজম চলছে। এই নতুন নতুন গুন্ডারা এসব ঘটাচ্ছে পার্টির তরফ থেকে একটু নজর যাতে তাঁদের উপরে পরে।” SIR প্রসঙ্গে তিনি যোগ করেন “সারা ভারতে ১৩ কোটি ভোটার বাদ দিয়েছে। বাংলায় প্রায় ১ কোটি মানুষকে লাইনে দাঁড় করানোর পর সম্প্রতি একটি আরটিআই-এর জবাব দিতে গিয়ে নির্বাচন কমিশন জানিয়েছে মাত্র ১৬০০ জনকে তাঁরা বিদেশি হিসেবে সন্দেহ করছেন। মাত্র ১৬০০ জনকে খুঁজতে গিয়ে তাঁরা সারা ভারতবর্ষে তাণ্ডব চালিয়েছে।”


 


এদিনের সাংবাদিক সম্মেলনে স্পষ্ট করা হয় SIR প্রক্রিয়া যে সংখ্যালঘু সম্প্রদায়, মুসলিম সম্প্রদায়কে বাদ দেওয়ার জন্য করা হয়েছিল তা সবর ইনস্টিটিউট তাঁদের প্রকাশিত রিপোর্টের মাধ্যমে প্রমাণ করে দিয়েছে। যেভাবে রাজ্যের বিভিন্ন প্রান্তে ডিটেনশন ক্যাম্প গড়ে উঠছে এবং বিভিন্ন মানুষকে রাতের অন্ধকারে বেআইনিভাবে আটক করা হচ্ছে তাঁর বিরুদ্ধেও প্রশ্ন তোলা হয়।


 


প্রাক্তন আইএএস অফিসার ও ভারতের সংখ্যালঘু কমিশনের চেয়ারম্যান ওয়াজাহাত হাবিবুল্লাহ বক্তব্যের শুরুতেই মনে করিয়ে দেন – ভারতের সংবিধানের ধারণা কেবল একটি লিখিত দলিলের মধ্যেই সীমাবদ্ধ নয়। এটি একটি গভীর আধ্যাত্মিক ধারণা, যার শিকড় হাজার হাজার বছরের ইতিহাসে বিস্তৃত।


 


আলোচনায় যে গুরুত্বপূর্ণ প্রশ্ন তিনি তোলেন তা হল – “ভারতের সংবিধান কেবল একটি সাংবিধানিক দলিল নয়। এটি আমাদের কাছে ভারত নামক দেশটির অস্তিত্বের সংজ্ঞা নির্ধারণ করে। ভারত কী? এর উত্তর হল— ভারতের সংবিধান। এই রাষ্ট্র কি এখনও ভারতের সংবিধানের কাঠামোর মধ্যে থেকে পরিচালিত হচ্ছে? যখন আমরা লিখিতভাবে ভারতের সংবিধানকে সংজ্ঞায়িত করেছি, তখন একজন ভারতীয় হিসেবে, আপনাদের সকলের মতো আমিও এই প্রশ্ন তুলতে বাধ্য— যাঁরা আমাদের দেশে ক্ষমতায় নির্বাচিত হয়েছেন, তাঁরা কি সেই সংবিধানকে রক্ষা করার দায়িত্ব পালন করছেন? তাঁরা কি ভারতের এই ধারণাটিকে সুরক্ষিত রাখছেন?”


 


তিনি তুলে আনেন আরটিআই প্রসঙ্গ। ভারতের সংবিধানের ১৯ নম্বর অনুচ্ছেদে বাক্‌স্বাধীনতা ও মতপ্রকাশের স্বাধীনতার অধিকার স্বীকৃত হয়েছে, যা বাস্তবায়নের অন্যতম প্রধান হাতিয়ার হল তথ্যের অধিকার আইন বা RTI Act। এই প্রসঙ্গেই তিনি বলেন, “তথ্যের অধিকার আইনকে কি যথাযথ সম্মান জানানো হচ্ছে? আইনটি মেনে চলা তো দূরের কথা, তাকে কি আদৌ গুরুত্ব দেওয়া হচ্ছে? সম্প্রতি SIR-সহ বিভিন্ন ঘটনাবলি নিয়ে আমরা যে অনুসন্ধান করেছি, তার উত্তর হল— না।”


 


বেআইনি নির্বাসন নিয়ে তাঁর বক্তব্য, বাংলাদেশি হিসাবে চিহ্নিত করা ব্যক্তিদের  শনাক্ত করার জন্য যে পদ্ধতি ব্যবহার করা হচ্ছে, তার কোনও নির্ভরযোগ্য ভিত্তি নেই। বাস্তবে কোনও প্রমাণ ছাড়াই দাবি করা হচ্ছে, তাঁরা বাংলাদেশ থেকে এসেছেন। এক্ষেত্রে যে জরুরি প্রশ্নগুলো উঠে আসে তা হল – কীভাবে তাঁদের বাংলাদেশ সরকারের হাতে তুলে দেওয়া হচ্ছে? তাঁদের অধিকার ও স্বাধীনতা রক্ষার জন্য কি কোনও পদক্ষেপ নেওয়া হচ্ছে? সংবিধানের অংশ হিসেবে আমাদের যে দায়িত্ব রয়েছে, তার ভিত্তিতে কি তাঁদের সুরক্ষা নিশ্চিত করা হচ্ছে?”


 


প্রাক্তন আইএএস অফিসার ও সমাজকর্মী হর্ষ মন্দার তাঁর বক্তব্যে এই বিষয়ের উপরেই জোর দেন যে প্রত্যর্পণ একটি আইনি প্রক্রিয়া, যারজন্য অন্য দেশটির সরকারের সঙ্গে আনুষ্ঠানিকভাবে যোগাযোগ করতে হয়। সরকার দাবি করছে সন্দেহভাজন ব্যক্তিদের চিহ্নিত করে দেশ থেকে ফেরত পাঠানো হচ্ছে। “অথচ এখানে যা ঘটছে, সেই মানুষগুলির বাংলাদেশি হওয়ার কোনও প্রমাণ সরকারের হাতে নেই। আপনাকে অন্য দেশের সরকারের কাছে নিজের প্রমাণ পেশ করতে হবে। তারপর সেই সরকার ওই ব্যক্তিকে নিজেদের নাগরিক হিসেবে গ্রহণ করে ফিরিয়ে নেবে। এখানে তেমন কোনও আইনি …

author: Anikibawal
title: Festival MANOJO – INFANCIAS Y ARTES ESCÉNICAS. Una experiencia enfocada en la primera infancia donde se reúnen las artes escénicas, mediación y juego libre en la ciudad de Temuco este 6 y 7 de noviembre.
content:
Durante esta semana, los días viernes 6 y sabado 7 de noviembre, desde las 12:00 a las 19:00 hrs, se realizara la Primera Version del

Festival Manojo – Infancias y artes escénicas

, un festival enfocado en la primera infancia (de 0 a 7 años) el cual tendra lugar en el Museo Regional de la Araucanía, en especifico en el parque que alberga el lugar, conversamos con Brenda Lizama Farfán, psicóloga, bailarina de danza contemporánea y directora del Festival Manojo, quien nos cuenta en sus palabras

“Manojo es un festival de primeras infancias, dirigido también hacia esas edades, de 0 a 7 años y a sus cuidadores y cuidadoras, es una propuesta en el exterior, por lo tanto permite otras experiencias en relación a la exhibición de obras y a la apreciación de artes vivas.”


En su primera versión, el festival trae como impronta ser una de las primeras iniciativas de artes escénicas enfocadas de forma exclusiva en las primeras infancias, sus familias, cuidadores y cuidadoras en Temuco, entrelazando diversas disciplinas tales como la danza, circo contemporáneo, títeres y narración oral, junto con instalaciones de mediación y juego libre pensadas para la estimulación de las niñeces.


El festival desde su propuesta curatorial viene a buscar la recuperación de espacios naturales dentro de la comuna de Temuco principalmente, como lo es el Museo Regional de la Araucanía, desde la dirección del festival reflexionan respecto a “

el museo regional es un espacio que no abre por ejemplo, los domingos o que no abre después de las 5:30 hrs, donde sabemos que la mayoría de las personas trabajamos en ese horario, entonces, ¿En qué momento llevamos a nuestras niñeses a esos espacios? habitarlos, conocerlos explorando, y ¿De qué manera también les invitamos a explorar? ¿Pueden tocar lo que existe en ese lugar? Entonces, esas son las preguntas también que nos hicimos al momento de seleccionar este espacio para realizar nuestro festival”.


El festival cuenta con una parrilla programática qué incluye 6 obras de artes escénicas, a continuación Brenda, su directora, nos habla sobre las actividades y los fundamentos qué dieron vida al festival

“Manojo cuenta con una parrilla programática de 6 obras de artes escénicas, además contamos con una experiencia que es un laboratorio de exploración de juego y movimiento libre para bebés de entre 10 y 36 meses que se llama Danzas Sensibles, que es un proyecto que vengo investigando ya hace cuatro años aproximadamente, y además va a estar la Tribu Reverdecer de danza porteo, que también es un proyecto que da inicio también a toda esta propuesta de festival, fue mi primer trabajo después de ser madre. Desde ahí también vienen todas estas preguntas que les he comentado respecto a cómo las madres habitamos estos espacios: ¿dónde somos bienvenidas y dónde podemos criar en comunidad? Entonces, esta tribu fue un proyecto de acompañamiento psicocorporal y psicoemocional a madres, mujeres puerperas junto a sus bebés desde los 3 meses después del parto y desde ahí surge la danza en movimiento libre… , gracias también al poeta bebé nuestras piernas nuestros cuellos para poder danzar con nuestros bebés… eso también se va a presentar ese día del festival, somos nueve mujeres danzando con nuestros bebés. Creo que también es una propuesta reivindicadora de la maternidad, que visibiliza también a las madres, el puerperio, en un espacio y en un contexto territorial que muchas veces no es tan visto, no es tan visible y que creo que es muy importante tener ese gesto político dentro de este festival, que ya es una gran propuesta política que va a remover ciertas maneras de ver la danza en particular y también las artes escénicas y las artes vivas en el territorio»

, de esta forma, el festival invita a las niñeces, sus familias, cuidadores y cuidadoras, a pasar la tarde en el parque que antecede al Museo Regional de la Araucanía, incentivando a llevar alimentos para consumo propio y/o una manta qué permitan a las infancias ocupar los jardines del lugar.


Esta información se publicó en

Radio Kurruf

.

author: Andrew Crocker
title: We’re Asking the Ninth Circuit to Hold Reverse Location Warrants Categorically Unconstitutional
content:
Yesterday, along with the ACLU, EFF filed an

amicus brief

 in the Ninth Circuit court of appeals in

United States v. Spurlock

, a case involving a “tower dump” warrant. These overbroad warrants require cellular providers to turn over location data about every phone in a given area at a given time. This is the first such case to be heard by a federal appeals court since the

US Supreme Court ruled this summer

 that highly similar “geofence” warrants are searches under the meaning of the Fourth Amendment.


Spurlock

involves an investigation into two murder victims discovered on the side of a rural California highway. Police also found a car belonging to one of the victims several miles away on the same highway. They quickly sought a tower dump warrant for an area covering this stretch of road, which eventually revealed location data on nearly 1,700 unique phones. Faced with a motion to suppress, the district court relied on a

Fifth Circuit court of appeals decision

 about geofence warrants to hold that tower dumps are similarly categorically unconstitutional “general warrants” that violate the Fourth Amendment. However, the court refused to suppress evidence on the basis of the “good faith doctrine.”


Our amicus brief on appeal makes several key arguments.


First, we point out that the Supreme Court’s decision in the geofence case

Chatrie v. United States

this summer only strengthens the arguments that tower dumps are unconstitutional general warrants. Tower dumps are a somewhat older technique than geofence warrants, but they are both “reverse location searches,” in which police “tap into an all-encompassing database, allowing them to undertake nearly perfect, retrospective surveillance of countless persons and places.” This is the sort of untargeted “general warrant” the framers of the Fourth Amendment wanted to prevent. As we write in the brief, “Searching all people in an area without probable cause to believe they were all involved in the criminal activity under investigation reproduces the evils of general warrants and is not constitutionally permitted.” It’s this rule of law that prevents police from searching the houses of a hundred, or even a thousand people in the vicinity of a crime.


Second, we note that even if high courts continue to allow tower dump and geofence warrants in any cases, core Fourth Amendment law requires strict limits to protect the privacy of innocent bystanders, including limits on the scope and duration of the warrants, as well notice to affected individuals and after-the-fact deletion and minimization of irrelevant data.


Finally, we argue that the Fourth Amendment requires the court to set aside the good faith doctrine in cases like these and actually decide the constitutional issue. Too often courts pass the buck in cases involving novel surveillance techniques, leading to situations where police can continue using the technique for years or even decades without a definitive ruling.

title: Kurdish writer Gülazer Akın released after 30 years in prison
content:
Kurdish political prisoner and writer Gülazer Akın has been released from Bünyan Women’s Prison in Turkey’s Kayseri province after 30 years of imprisonment. She was welcomed outside the prison by family members, representatives of the prisoners’ solidarity association TUHAYDER and numerous supporters. Akın, who had been imprisoned since November 1996, endured numerous health problems during her decades behind bars, completed a university degree and wrote several literary works.


Upon her release, Akın said she had not believed until the very end that she would actually be able to leave prison. The release of a fellow prisoner had previously been postponed by a decision of the Prison Administration and Observation Board. She therefore feared that her own release might also be blocked.


“As long as even one of our friends remains in prison, I will not feel that I have truly been released,” Akın said. She also welcomed the peace process that had begun: “We have matured and returned. A new process has begun. I said this before the board as well. A new process has begun, and I support it. There is probably nothing more beautiful than freedom.”


Following her remarks, Akın released a white dove as a symbol of peace.


TUHAY-DER calls for the release of political prisoners


During the welcome gathering, the prisoners’ solidarity association TUHAY-DER criticized the continued imprisonment of seriously ill prisoners and the repeated postponement of scheduled releases. Representatives of the association stated that genuine freedom could only be achieved when all political prisoners and Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan were released.


The decisions of Prison Administration and Observation Boards have faced criticism from human rights and prisoners’ rights organizations for years. These organizations accuse the boards of delaying the release of long-term prisoners for political reasons, despite their having met the necessary requirements for release.


Three decades behind prison walls


Gülazer Akın was born in 1975 in Ahlat, in the province of Bitlis. She joined the Kurdish freedom movement in 1993. On November 3, 1996, she was arrested in Istanbul and placed in pretrial detention. A Turkish State Security Court later sentenced her to life imprisonment on charges of separatism.


During her imprisonment, Akın was held in various prisons across Turkey. Despite health problems, she continued her education and graduated with a degree in public administration from Anadolu University.


At the same time, she devoted herself extensively to literature. Her experiences of imprisonment, social exclusion and women’s lives became central themes in her writing.


Writing against oblivion


Akın’s first novel,

Tencerenin Dibi

 (

The Bottom of the Cooking Pot

), was published in 2013. The book was introduced by Turkish writer Adil Okay, who drew attention to the extraordinary circumstances under which she produced her literary work in an accompanying text.


Okay quoted from a letter Akın had written after 18 years of imprisonment. In it, she described how an entire generation had grown up behind prison walls while life continued outside:


“We were still almost children when we entered prison. Many of us grew up and matured while staring at walls. As the walls deteriorated, we grew more mature.”


Akın offered a particularly poignant account of her encounters with family members whose growth she could witness only during prison visits:


“When we entered prison, our siblings, nieces and nephews were still babies. Today, they are adults. We could only watch all of this through the small window of the prison. With every visit, we were amazed all over again and asked: When did you grow so big?”


According to Akın, this experience created an almost unbearable sense of injustice. Adil Okay praised her novel as a work written under conditions in which even colored pencils had reportedly been prohibited. Despite these restrictions, the writer developed her own literary voice to bring attention to experiences that were barely acknowledged beyond the prison walls.


Confronting patriarchal social structures


With her 2017 book

Cinsiyetçiliğin Yaratımı

 (

The Creation of Sexism

), Akın also turned her attention to theoretical questions concerning women’s liberation. In the book, she examines sexism as a system of social domination and explores the significance of women’s self-determination in transforming social structures.

title: Ecocide continues in Şırnak: Hundreds of oak trees cut down
content:
Environmental destruction continues in the Kurdish province of Şırnak. Footage recorded by local residents yesterday in the Besta region shows hundreds of oak trees cut down across a vast area, leaving large sections of the forest stripped of trees.


While activities carried out under the guise of mining exploration on Mount Cudi and oil exploration on Mount Gabar for nearly a decade have already caused significant environmental damage, tree felling continues in the Besta region under the pretext of commercial activity.


According to reports, oak trees, some of them up to a century old, have been cut down by village guards under military supervision. Footage recorded in the Kaniya Kolanan and Dergê Gêzna areas showed numerous trees being cut down at their bases with chainsaws. The logging site is reportedly accessible only through a military checkpoint, and around ten people were said to be operating in the area with vans and chainsaws.


DEM Party Şırnak MP Mehmet Zeki İrmez shared the footage on his social media account, condemning the tree felling and tagging the Şırnak Governor’s Office and the Provincial Directorate of Agriculture.


https://twitter.com/zekiirmez/status/2117663598902161603


İrmez stated that deforestation continued despite previous assurances that it would end. He accused public institutions of turning a blind eye to the destruction and said that the activities of local collaborators were making ecocide a permanent reality in the region.


Emphasizing that social peace could not be approached from a single perspective, İrmez stressed that protecting nature was also an essential component of peace. He called for an immediate halt to the tree felling and demanded that those responsible be held accountable.


Meanwhile, deforestration work is also reported to be continuing in rural areas around the villages of Cilbiya and Biliga in Silopi.


According to reports, village guards have been transporting the felled trees by tractor to the towns of Şêxan (Hilal) and Sêgirk (Şenoba). A local resident recorded footage of the trees being transported by tractor near the İnceler Dam.

title: Vigil in Geneva enters its 69th month: ‘Öcalan’s status must be officially recognized’
content:
A vigil by the Democratic Kurdish Community in Switzerland has been taking place in front of the UN headquarters in Geneva since 25 January 2021. Every Wednesday, activists stage a protest in front of the United Nations building to demand the release of Kurdish people’s leader Abdullah Öcalan. The action is carried out as part of the 'Dem dema azadiye' [Time for Freedom] campaign and is directed against the isolation of the Kurdish leader on the Turkish prison island of Imrali, the Turkish occupation attacks on Kurdistan, the massacres committed in Kurdish territories and the silence of the UN. Demonstratos call on international institutions to fulfill their responsibilities to secure Öcalan’s physical freedom.


This week's demonstration, which is held at a tent set up in Nations Square where the UN Office is located, began with a moment of silence in memory of those who lost their lives in the Kurdish freedom struggle.


During this week’s demonstration, participants from Kurdistan once again called on international institutions to fulfill their responsibilities in securing the physical freedom of Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan, who has been held in Imralı Island Prison since 1999.


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/079bead5_20261104154836_2026-11-04-cenevre-onder-apo-icin-ozgurluk-nobeti-bm-ofisi-onunde-69-aylinda-devam-ediyor-1.mp4


Xebat Veysel Kuşkanadı, spokesperson for the “Freedom for Abdullah Öcalan, A Democratic Solution to the Kurdish Question” campaign committee, spoke about the ongoing peace process launched in Turkey following Öcalan’s February 27, 2025 ‘Call for Peace and Democratic Society.’ He expressed respect and appreciation for the Kurdish leader’s intensive efforts and work toward peace.


Stating that Öcalan sought an end to the conflicts in Turkey and the Middle East and a democratic resolution to the Kurdish question, Xebat Veysel described this approach as an important demonstration of political will and goodwill toward peace.


Veysel accused the Turkish state of deliberately prolonging the process without taking concrete steps, emphasizing that the Kurdish people did not accept this approach.


Xebat Veysel outlined their demands as follows: “The Turkish state must take genuine and serious steps, and Leader Öcalan’s status must be clearly defined and officially recognized. Leader Öcalan must be provided with conditions that allow him to work freely.”


Osman Tekin, Co-Chair of the Geneva Democratic Kurdish Community Association, then took the floor, emphasizing that the Kurdish question was fundamentally an issue of rights.


Tekin stated that autonomy for local administrations, constitutional guarantees for the Kurdish language and securing Öcalan’s physical freedom were key elements of a resolution.


Stressing the need for new legislation and reforms, Tekin said that Öcalan must be allowed to communicate with members of the press, civil society representatives, the Peace Mothers and his comrades.


Tekin stressed that only if these steps were taken could they believe in the Turkish state’s sincerity regarding the process.

title: Rojhilat Alliance: Member parties in favor of continuing dialogue
content:
The Rojhilat Kurdistan Union Group issued a written statement regarding its meeting with representatives of four member parties of the Alliance of Political Forces of Eastern Kurdistan.


The statement said: “In order to activate the Alliance of Political Forces of Eastern Kurdistan, which was established more than eight months ago, and to identify the obstacles preventing it from functioning effectively, the Rojhilat Kurdistan Union Group invited the Alliance’s six parties to a consultative meeting.


The Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK), the Kurdistan Freedom Party (PAK), the Organization of Struggle of Iranian Kurdistan (Sazmana Xebat a Kurdistana Îranê), the Democratic Party of Iranian Kurdistan (KDP-I), and the Association of Kurdistan Toilers attended the meeting.


Only the Komala Party stated that it was not prepared to attend the meeting. In addition, a few days before the meeting, the Democratic Party of Iranian Kurdistan (KDP-I) withdrew without providing any explanation.


On Sunday (1 November 2026), a three-hour meeting was held between the Rojhilat Kurdistan Union Group and representatives of four parties belonging to the Alliance of Political Forces of Eastern Kurdistan.”


The statement noted that the four parties regarded the political alliance as an important and long-term necessity. It added that the Political Alliance could become more active and effective in the near future by adopting a charter, defining roles and responsibilities, and establishing mechanisms for joint work.


Regarding the possibility of dialogue with the Iranian state, the statement said that the parties had agreed that, should an opportunity for dialogue arise and the need for negotiations emerge, no member party of the Alliance should independently enter into negotiations with the Islamic Republic of Iran without the Alliance’s participation and coordination.


The statement described the meeting as a positive step, noting the willingness to discuss directly the challenges facing the Political Alliance—an initiative that deserved support and further development. It added that representatives of all the parties had expressed positive assessments of the meeting.


The statement also emphasized that the parties should refrain from accusing one another in order to avoid undermining trust between them and jeopardizing the continuity of their joint work.

author: Daron Letts
title: ‘Government-wide effort’ needed to fix broken foster system: premier
content:
One day after the federal auditor general’s office published its latest

report

 on the state of Nunavut’s foster care system, Premier John Main pledged his government will do better.


“This report is upsetting,” Main said during a news conference at the legislative assembly Wednesday.

“The responsibilities that lie with our government are serious and we need to live up to the duties that have been entrusted to us.”


Deputy auditor general Andrew Hayes tabled the report,

Foster Care in Nunavut,

 in Nunavut’s legislative assembly on Tuesday. The federal auditor general has the authority to review the effectiveness of Government of Nunavut programs.


The document outlines the Family Services department’s failures to maintain regular contact with children in care, to screen and monitor foster homes, and to maintain reliable information on the number of children in the system and where they had been placed — a problem that was highlighted in the auditor general’s

2023 report

.


“The Department of Family Services did not provide timely and effective foster care services to protect and support the safety and well-being of children,” Hayes said during a news conference Tuesday afternoon. “It could not consistently demonstrate that basic safeguards intended to protect children and place them in safe environments were being followed.”


The department’s failure to solve the lapse in data stems from the department staff’s lack of training on its

centralized reporting system

, known as Matrix, Hayes said.


“We saw differences between the manual lists that the department is working with and the information in Matrix. That is a problem,” Hayes said.


Family Services Minister Gwen Healey Akearok said that is changing.


“The Matrix training has been unrolling throughout the territory,” she said at the news conference. “There’s another one happening this month.”


She said 90 per cent of front-line staff and 80 per cent of other staff have been trained so far.


“We know we need that evidence. We need strong documentation. We need excellent records,” Healey Akearok said.

“Every foster file is now in one system.”


She said that

97 per cent of home studies have been completed and, as of October, 82 per cent of annual reviews had been completed.


“There’s still work to be done,” she added.


The auditor general will release another report in the spring of 2027, on the department’s “quality assurance work,” Hayes said. 


Nunavummiut will see improvements in that report thanks to “a government-wide effort,” Main said.

“Our sincere hope is that future audits will show real improvement.”


Asked if any staff will lose their jobs over the report’s findings, Main said he will not share that publicly.


“From the upper management on down, there is an expectation that you will fulfill your duties, and if not, you’ll face the consequences,” he said.

author: Katharine Trendacosta
title: Google Summaries Aren't About AI, They're About Lock-In
content:
Whether they call it AI summaries, knowledge panels, or AMP, Google takes actions that are less about functionality and more about locking you into its own ecosystem. Knowing that makes it possible for all of us to choose better services than Google's, defeating their anticompetitive goal. In this case, as it is so often, knowledge is power.

 


In the old days, when dinosaurs roamed the earth and getting online involved your computer making eldritch shrieking, Google was a website that took whatever you typed in and gave you a list of links that best matched what you were searching for. As it's grown beyond that, however, the core function of Google Search has moved from giving you the best answer to your query to a number of other things, most of them about making money for Google.

 


This is obviously not a new observation. It's at the core of what EFF Special Advisor Cory Doctorow named "

enshittification

." But it's important to remember that whatever shiny new name or technology is wrapped around these tools, it's not about the wrapping, it's about the monetization.

 


In the case of Google Search, the company has a history of rolling out new "features" that are less helpful to the searcher and more designed to keep you and your data within the Google ecosystem. One easy example of enshittification is putting sponsored links and ads at the top of search results, forcing you to scroll down past a bunch of not relevant links to get to your answers. Or, in some cases, accidentally clicking on sponsored links that might be designed to give you the opposite information of what you're looking for or for a competitor to the product you intended to buy.

 


The other clumsy version of this is Google's self-preferencing, where Google's own services—say YouTube if you're looking for a video—are weighted so that they appear at the top of a search over a competitor's. Similar to this was Google's push for websites, particularly news ones, to be made available via what it called

"Accelerated Mobile Pages" or AMP

, which in theory stripped out features that might make loading a page on mobile too slow, but also handed over control of how webpages looked on mobile to Google and turned mobile links, often by default, into Google links.

 


But the other way that Google has historically kept your—and your valuable eyeballs—on its website has been to just obviate the need to even click on a link and leave Google at all. The first version of this was what Google calls "knowledge panels." These are snippets of information shown on the results page of a search that purport to answer your question. Knowledge panels predate the AI push and haven't always been what you could call

accurate

.

 


Knowledge panels are extremely similar to the AI summaries we now see at the top of Google Search results, except that instead of pulling quotes from specific linked sources, it's the AI doing the summarizing, though also sometimes with links. They are basically the same thing, mostly changed only in branding, because AI is now the cool kid on the block. The goal is essentially the same—it's less about providing you with the best answer to your query and more about making you think it's unnecessary to click a link and leave Google's ecosystem. And, more importantly, it keeps you on Google's pages longer to read the content. More time on the page is more time exposed to ads and sponsored links and more money for Google. 

 


The biggest irony here is that

it didn’t even work

. People choosing to use “AI mode”—and possibly made accustomed to getting information as text instead of links through the knowledge panels and the AI summaries at the top—has caused

“lower monetization”

 via ads. Ads, remember, are Google’s main source of revenue. Like newspapers before them, Google is finding that counting on a monopoly on ad space maybe isn’t the most sound strategy in a shifting technological landscape. And to get out of the hole it has made for itself, it is lighting cash on fire to try to get back on top. Perhaps they should consider pivoting to video.

 


Every time you see a feature like this, no matter what it is called or what "new" technology they claim fuels it, remember that it is Google's monetary incentives that drive the decisions and not necessarily the tech itself. And you can always choose to ignore it, scroll past, disable it, or even

go to another service entirely

.

author: Daniel Hunter
title: The Midterms Repudiated Trump. Grassroots Momentum Will Shape What Comes Next.
content:
We can exhale — and celebrate — and then we need to sustain movement energy for the long-haul pressure campaigns ahead.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

The broad strokes of the midterms are clear: A massive repudiation of MAGA’s fascist wave has ended the Donald Trump 2.0 era of congressional complicity with his authoritarian takeover. Trump’s lame duck presidency now begins.

This lopsided electoral rejection is historically rare: Flipping control of both the House and Senate in a midterm has only occurred three times since World War II (in 1946, 1994, and 2006). The breakthroughs are astounding: the first Native American governor and senator, five Black governors, the first majority of Democratic governors in 16 years, and critical down-ballot wins like the first Democrat to win as Texan oil regulator since 1990 and the first openly transgender state legislator in Alabama.

Authoritarians do not do well when trapped — and with a famously norm-busting president, anything is possible. But, critically, election deniers like Darline Graham and Greg Abbott are conceding their races. Trump is already saying he’s “absolutely willing” to accept the results and told CBS, “Congratulations to the Democrats, and I look forward to working with you for the good of our country.”

These midterms have left me, like many, with abundant free-floating anxieties. The “what if” scenarios have been abundant — and while some of the most extreme versions did not happen, the federal government was weaponized against the election system like never before.

Because the times have been so rough, it can be hard to exhale and accept a win, especially since elections are not material changes — they are promissory notes that the future may be different. Until January 3, we live under the same dangerous authoritarian government, even if the atmosphere has changed.

Before I advocate for you to breathe, let’s affirm all the many hard reasons to not exhale. The wins were not universal, as some big losses cut deep. There’s a reality that all of this is ephemeral if Democrats cannot govern a policy of change — if we only manage an economic status quo it will disillusion and likely result in yet another whiplash election in the other direction. And it’s hard to breathe in a dizzying moment.

The country looked at fascism and fully rejected it.

Further, the attacks on elections were treasonous. I won’t list the complete litany of federal assaults — but we have a Department of Justice captured by authoritarian forces using its power nakedly for partisan goals. The far right openly prepared sham legal theories to refuse certification of Democratic representatives. While we did not get systematic federal law enforcement terror at polls, we saw National Guard throughout Washington, D.C. We still have too many election officials committed to the Big Lie. And ongoing structural impediments to a fair election are consequential: In Mississippi, the Senate margin remains tiny while any win may be marred by equipment trouble, poll changes, and voters unexpectedly removed by data purges from the voting rolls.

Notably, the election maps themselves have been gerrymandered by racists to ensure power — though their greed led to multiple losses in these redistricted seats. (Groups like Black Voters Matter deserve a huge shout-out for fighting in the South and in races Democrats had abandoned.)

Despite all that, we managed a pro-democracy win that was too big to rig. The country delivered a shellacking to MAGA politics — an encouraging sign for all of us who are hoping for a better future. Ultimately, the election proceeded with voters refusing to be intimidated.

Buddhists remind me we can take a breath anytime. But this moment seems as good a moment as any, especially when we remind ourselves that exhaling isn’t signaling that things are over. Exhales are how our body gets in tune with this moment and releases the latest tension. Bracing doesn’t make us wiser, just tenser.

So really, take five breaths right now. As you breathe, read in a poem by Jarod Anderson:

You can be still while the world is whirling.

You can be silent while your heart is thundering.

You can be alone while your memory is teeming.

You can live forever in the span of a moment.

You can grow kindness in the soil of hatred.

You can decide purpose. You can decide victory.

As we breathe in — exhale and inhale — …

author: Sharon Zhang
title: “Donald … Call Me Senator”: Abdul El-Sayed Wins by 7 in Triumph Over GOP Bigotry
content:
“Donald, I know you struggled with my name. So after JD swears me in … call me senator,” El-Sayed said.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Abdul El-Sayed walloped his Republican opponent, Mike Rogers, in Michigan on Tuesday, marking a massive triumph over the strategy of flat-out Islamophobic bigotry that Donald Trump, the GOP, and even many liberals embraced in the months of fierce campaigning against the progressive pro-Palestine senator-elect.

“They went all in on one of the ugliest campaigns we’ve seen in our lifetimes,” said El-Sayed in his victory speech early Wednesday morning. “They weren’t just attacking me. They were targeting and attacking you. They were targeting and attacking the very idea of America.”

With over 95 percent of votes counted, El-Sayed had 52.5 percent of the vote compared to Rogers’s 45.5 percent — matching the exact margin that El-Sayed predicted he would win back in May.

This is despite Trump and Republicans making him one of their primary targets this midterm cycle, with Trump spewing Islamophobic hate and incitement to violence against El-Sayed nearly every time he spoke at a rally or with the media. At a rally in Michigan in late October, Trump said El-Sayed is a “jihadist” and that the Senate should install a metal detector just to screen him.

He and others like Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) suggested that El-Sayed was violent with no evidence, pointing only to his faith. After winning the primary in August, Rogers’s first statement suggested that El-Sayed was a terrorist. “I spent years hunting terrorists and bringing Osama bin Laden to justice,” he said.

Liberal pundits and politicians, too, joined in on the bigoted pile-ons; El-Sayed’s AIPAC-backed primary opponent, Haley Stevens, used hateful tropes against him during the bitter primary race, and she ultimately issued a surprise endorsement of Rogers two days before the election.

El-Sayed often spoke out against the hate, hammering people like Trump and Vice President JD Vance. He also kept a laser-focus on his agenda: Medicare for All, banning corporate money in politics, and opposing further assistance to Israel.

On Wednesday night, El-Sayed said that his win was for “all the parents who struggled to explain why the president openly mocked” people like him.

“Mike, enjoy your retirement…. You chose hate, and Michigan chose hope. May we never have to see the likes of you in this state ever again,” he said.

“JD, habibi. There is this delicious irony that you’re constitutionally obligated to swear me in in January,” El-Sayed went on, to raucous cheers from the crowd. “Donald, I know you struggled with my name. So after JD swears me in in January, you can just go on and call me senator.”

El-Sayed also spoke out against the pro-Israel lobby, with AIPAC pouring a record amount into the election to defeat him. He espoused the “love” that he has for the Palestinian people, drawing a sharp contrast to the hatred levied against him.

“To AIPAC who spent $42 million against us: Thank you for giving me the opportunity to beat you twice,” he said. “They try to call you hateful if you believe that Palestinian kids should get to grow up in the land of their forefathers, to not be murdered by our tax dollars. If you believe in equal rights to peace, dignity, and self-determination, that’s not hate, it’s love.”

The corporate media waged an all-out attack on El-Sayed, in part due to his stances on Israel. Outlets like The New York Times ran stories about him losing Jewish voters and accusing him of antisemitism, without evidence. Corporate outlets also spread a narrative that he had “struggled to win over Black voters” in the state, as Politico wrote on Sunday, or that many Democrats were peeling off from him to vote for Rogers.

But Tuesday’s result shows that these narratives were overblown. Exit polls suggested that Jewish people overwhelmingly went for El-Sayed, and data from VoteHub finds that El-Sayed won majority-Black districts by a whopping 81-point margin. The “Democrats for Mike Rogers” PAC, which poured millions into the race, was revealed by Truthout in October to be a Republican front group.

author: Sasha Abramsky
title: The Egg on Elon Musk’s Face Cost More Than $440 Million
content:
Musk’s astronomical campaign contributions were no match for outraged voters across the US.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Elon Musk, the world’s wealthiest man, went on a spending spree in the weeks leading up to the midterms. By Election Day, he had invested — and I use that word deliberately — more than $440 million into propping up the GOP to try to make its message and its candidates more palatable with voters during an election cycle in which their brand had become increasingly toxic.

Astoundingly, nearly half of that money — more than $190 million — was spent on one campaign: Ken Paxton’s effort to make the leap from an impeached state attorney general to being U.S. senator for Texas. Musk was, in broad daylight, like the gilded age oligarchs of the late-19th century, essentially trying to buy himself a senator.

Many rich candidates have in recent years self-funded their candidacies or intervened in initiative campaigns — Michael Bloomberg put in more than $1 billion into his go-nowhere presidential campaign in 2020, Tom Steyer spent upwards of $200 million in his recent futile attempt to become the California governor, and a cluster of billionaires, led by Google’s Sergei Brin, put obscene amounts of money into opposing the billionaires’ wealth tax initiative before voters in California this election. This year, the Texas race seems to be the first time a single non-candidate donor has put this much money into a particular marquee contest.

Musk — who relocated to Texas during the pandemic in a fit of pique against California’s public health mandates — has a large and growing business footprint in Texas, and a desire to take over more land both for his space launch business and his data centers; he therefore needs political figures from the state not only on his side but in his pocket, as Democrats began gleefully pointing out in the final month of the campaign.

The SpaceX titan isn’t, of course, alone in his mega-donations. The Brennan Center for Justice has reported that in the 2026 election cycle, 40 mega-donors altogether ponied up an astounding $2.5 billion, the large majority for GOP candidates. But the scale of Elon Musk’s financial outlay does put him in a league of his own. Individually, in 2026 Musk gave more than twice as much to candidates as did the entire cryptocurrency industry — which has also not been shy about buying political loyalties as its footprint has increased in size.

Most of Musk’s money was channeled through the Senate Leadership Fund, the coordinating fund the GOP ran for its Senate candidates. This move allowed Paxton, whose entire career has been a pinball exercise caroming from one corruption scandal to the next, to flood the vast Texas media market with attack advertisements in the weeks leading up to the election. The Republican candidate’s campaign promptly used this money to lean ever further into anti-trans messaging, saturating the airwaves with ads accusing Democratic candidate James Talarico of being an extremist for transgender rights.

Then, as the governor’s race in Texas tightened, with Democrat Gina Hinojosa making an unexpectedly strong run to break the GOP stranglehold on the state’s top office, Musk also began injecting millions of dollars into Greg Abbott’s re-election campaign.

But Musk’s ambitions weren’t limited to the Lone Star State. In this election cycle, the oligarch gave tens of millions of dollars to super PACs supporting vulnerable GOP candidates in House races around the country and funneled millions more to gubernatorial and attorneys general campaigns, recognizing that a Democratic victory would likely harm his corporate ventures and reduce the flow of money from government contracts.

In New Hampshire, Musk’s super PAC, America PAC, pumped $1 million into supporting Republican candidate John Sununu for a Senate seat that the GOP identified early in the campaign season as a possible pick-up. In New York, the trillionaire’s PAC put hundreds of thousands of dollars into efforts to salvage GOP Congressman Mike Lawler’s campaign in the competitive 17th congressional district. Singlehandedly, Musk seemed intent on showing, throughout election season, just how much financial sway the oligarchy can have on U.S. politics. author: David Swanson
title: Taxpayers Mobilize in Washington, D.C., to Protest $1.5 Trillion Military Budget
content:
Economic Cost, Immorality, Nonviolent Activism, North America, What to do

By CODEPINK and a large coalition of advocacy groups, November 4, 2026

Taxpayers from across the U.S. will gather in Washington, D.C., from November 10 to 12, 2026, to protest the proposed $1.5 trillion 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). Organized by CODEPINK and a large coalition of advocacy groups, the demonstration aims to put the country’s excessive and harmful military spending at the forefront of the national conversation after the midterms.

“The midterm elections were a nationwide condemnation of Trump and Hegseth’s horrible war in Iran. The Taxpayer Uprising is about creatively and beautifully making sure this current Congress doesn’t forget about it – because passing Trump’s war budget would mean green-lighting his reckless wars for the remainder of his presidency,” explained CODEPINK’s national co-director Danaka Katovich.

The three-day event will feature office visits with elected officials and visual demonstrations. Tentative schedule as follows:

Tuesday, November 10: Senate Office Visits from 10 am- 4 pm: The group will kick off the first day of action at the Dirksen Cafeteria at 10 am. They will break off into specific advocacy groups and visit senators’ offices.

Wednesday, November 11: Victims of the War Budget Processional, 10–2 pm, starting at Peace Monument.

Thursday, November 12: House of Representatives office visits, 10 am-4 pm. The group will meet at the Rayburn Cafeteria at 10 am, then break into groups to visit their representatives’ offices. There will also be an Ice Cream Social with Ben & Jerry’s own Ben Cohen at 2pm at the Intersection of First Street SE and Independence Avenue SE.

Constituents from various states, including California and Texas, will join organizations like CODEPINK, World BEYOND War, RootsAction, National Priorities Project at the Institute for Policy Studies, Doctors Against Genocide, Climate Defenders, CAIR National, Eisenhower Media Network, National Iranian American Council, Fellowship of Reconciliation, American Muslims for Palestine, Veterans For Peace, DSA International Committee, and more in demanding a reallocation of funds towards domestic needs.

“We’ve tried voting our way to represent our overwhelming public preference for less war funding and more funding of human and environmental needs. Now let’s add the powerful tool of nonviolent activism. Now let’s make it harder to defy the people of this country than it is to defy the war profiteers.” – David Swanson, Co-Founder and Executive Director, World BEYOND War.

“Americans are increasingly recognizing the connection between funding the genocide in Gaza, the ongoing ethnic cleansing in the West Bank, Israel’s escalating aggression across the region, and the illegal war on Iran, and their own struggles to make ends meet and achieve economic mobility. Our lawmakers appear more concerned with appeasing the Israel lobby and war profiteers than listening to the majority of Americans, who do not want endless, unjustified wars and instead support greater investment in social welfare, education, healthcare, and workers’ rights. The Taxpayer Uprising is our way of continuing to build the political power necessary to secure a future that prioritizes people over war and invests in the well-being of our communities.” AMP executive director, Dr. Osama Abu Irshaid

The Trump Administration’s proposal marks the largest increase in military spending in modern history, prioritizing the war budget over human needs like healthcare, education, and housing. The proposed budget allocates about $116.43 million per hour to US warfare, ranging from illegal boat bombings in the Americas to the disastrous war in Iran. Half of that will go directly to contractors in the arms and AI industries. Meanwhile, nearly 45,000 Americans die annually due to lack of health insurance. Shifting even a small share of military spending to healthcare and social programs would save countless lives in the US and worldwide.
